## Reports & lessons

```bash
mushi reports list [--status new] [--severity critical]
mushi reports show <id>
mushi reports triage <id> --status acknowledged --severity high
mushi reports resolve <id>
mushi reports reopen <id>
mushi reports dismiss <id>
mushi reports reply <id> "Thanks — we're on it"
mushi reports search "checkout button"
mushi reports file --title "…" --description "…" [--severity high] [--component checkout]

mushi lessons list
mushi lessons show <id>
mushi sync-lessons              # pull promoted rules → .mushi/lessons.json
```

### Sentry issues already open

The Sentry webhook only sees new issues. `mushi sentry import` brings in the
ones already open, so they get the same diagnosis. Running it twice is safe: an
issue already imported links to its report.

```bash
mushi sentry import                                  # newest unresolved issues
mushi sentry import WEB-1A2 WEB-1A3                  # by id or short id (up to 10)
mushi sentry import --query "level:error" --since-days 7
mushi sentry import --query "level:error" --cursor <next>   # next page, printed after each import
```

It needs the Sentry org slug, project slug and an auth token with `event:read`
and `project:read` (console: **Integrations → Sentry**).

### File a report yourself

For a bug you found yourself, or a backlog item you want an agent to fix,
`mushi reports file` adds a report to the app's queue. It goes through the same
triage as a user report, so it gets a diagnosis and can be sent to `mushi fix`.

```bash
mushi reports file --title "Checkout adds tax twice" \
  --description "Cart with 2 items shows the tax line twice on /checkout. Done when the total matches the cart."
mushi reports file --title "Bump sharp to 0.34" --description "..." --severity low --component build --project <uuid>
```

`--severity` (critical, high, medium, low) and `--component` are hints that
triage may refine. It needs a key with the `mcp:write` scope; each app takes at
most 30 filed reports an hour. The MCP tool is `file_report`.

### Reporter updates held for review

When reporter updates are in review mode, each status message waits in the
outbox until you send it. Sending and discarding reach a real person, so both
need `--yes`.

```bash
mushi outbox list
mushi outbox edit <messageId> "Fixed in 1.4, thanks for the report"
mushi outbox release <messageId> --yes
mushi outbox release <messageId> --text "Fixed in 1.4" --yes
mushi outbox discard <messageId> --yes
```

---

## Agentic fixes

### `mushi fix `

Dispatch an agentic fix for a classified report.

```bash
# Default agent (from project settings)
mushi fix 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000123

# Cursor Cloud Agent — wait for PR
mushi fix <reportId> --agent cursor_cloud --wait

# A project with a frontend and a backend repo: send the fix to the backend
mushi fix <reportId> --repo acme/app-backend

# CI: fail the pipeline if the fix errors
mushi fix $REPORT_ID --agent cursor_cloud --wait && echo "Fix PR opened"
```

| Flag | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `--agent ` | `claude_code` (default), `cursor_cloud`, `codex`, `mcp` |
| `--model ` | Model override for `cursor_cloud` (e.g. `composer-latest`) |
| `--no-auto-pr` | Skip automatic PR creation for `cursor_cloud` |
| `--wait` | Poll until terminal state; exits non-zero on failure |
| `--repo <repoId\|owner/name>` | Linked repo to open the fix PR against, for a project with several repos. Defaults to the primary repo. A name is looked up among the project's linked repos |

### `mushi fixes`

Headless fix lifecycle; pairs with `mushi fix --wait`.

```bash
# Stream dispatch SSE events (no browser)
mushi fixes tail --report-id <reportId>

# Pull latest GitHub Actions status (same as console "Refresh CI status")
mushi fixes refresh-ci <fixId>
mushi fixes refresh-ci <fixId> --json

# Squash-merge the draft PR and mark the report Fixed
mushi fixes merge <fixId>
mushi fixes merge <fixId> --method squash   # default
mushi fixes merge <fixId> --method merge
mushi fixes merge <fixId> --json

# The verified-merge gates for the PR's current head (ADR 0035)
mushi fixes verify <fixId>
mushi fixes verify <fixId> --rerun   # re-check now, then show
mushi fixes verify <fixId> --json
```

**Merge prerequisites:** the fix attempt must be `completed` with an open PR (`pr_url`
+ `pr_number`). Draft PRs are auto-readied via GitHub GraphQL before merge (same as the
console). Requires GitHub App or PAT connected and an API key with `mcp:write`.

When merge succeeds, the report moves to **Fixed**, the reporter gets notified, and
`fix.applied` webhooks fire, the same as merging on GitHub or via the admin console.

### `mushi work`

Fix reports with a coding agent on your own machine instead of a cloud agent.
The agent (the Cursor CLI, `cursor-agent`, signed in to any Cursor account)
only edits a worktree of your repo; `mushi work` commits, pushes and opens the
draft pull request with **your** local credentials. So you can spend a Cursor
account's allowance without that account's GitHub ever touching your repo.

```bash
# Show which reports it would take (worst first, none with a run or PR already live)
mushi work --repo-dir ~/code/my-app --dry-run

# Fix up to 3 reports, one at a time
mushi work --repo-dir ~/code/my-app --max 3

# One report, a chosen model
mushi work --repo-dir ~/code/my-app --report <reportId> --model gpt-5
```

For each report it:

1. Reads Mushi's fix packet and what earlier attempts did (their Opus review
   findings), as data the agent must not take as instructions.
2. Creates a worktree from `origin/` on
   `bugfix/MUSHI--local-cursor` and runs `cursor-agent -p` in it
   (30 minutes at most), after installing the worktree's dependencies from
   its lockfile (pnpm, npm or yarn) so the agent can run the tests and your
   commit hooks work. The agent's environment has no credentials, and
   version control inside it cannot reach the remote.
3. With changes: commits, pushes, opens a draft PR with `Mushi report: `,
   registers the fix attempt (like the MCP tool `submit_fix_result`) and
   queues the Opus review, so the PR follows the same review and release
   train as a cloud agent's. Without changes: records the agent's
   `Mushi verdict:` on the attempt.

A report whose local run ended without a pull request in the last 7 days
(a timeout, no change, or a verdict) is skipped; pass `--report ` to run
it anyway. The agent has 30 minutes, so a report that names several pages is
fixed one page at a time: split broad reports into one page or cause each.

When Opus says "fix first" on one of these pull requests, run
`mushi work --followups`. Mushi checks the round (the reviewed commit is still
the PR's head, at most 2 rounds per PR), sends only the findings that pass its
safety screen, and the agent fixes them in a worktree of the PR's branch.
`mushi work` commits and pushes to that branch, and Opus reviews the new
commit. Cloud-agent pull requests get the same follow-up from Mushi itself.

```bash
# Which pull requests are waiting for a follow-up
mushi work --repo-dir ~/code/my-app --followups --dry-run

# Run them
mushi work --repo-dir ~/code/my-app --followups --model grok-4.7-xhigh
```

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--repo-dir ` | A clone of the app repo; only worktrees are created in it |
| `--max ` | Reports per run (default 3, at most 10) |
| `--report ` | Work on this report only |
| `--followups` | Fix the Opus "fix first" findings on pull requests `mushi work` opened, and push to them |
| `--model ` | Model for the agent (`cursor-agent --list-models`) |
| `--keep` | Keep the worktree afterwards |
| `--dry-run` | Show the plan; change nothing |

Needs `cursor-agent` and `gh` signed in, and an API key with `mcp:write`.

### `mushi worker`

`mushi work --daemon` runs `mushi work` for you, all the time, as a local
worker the console can see and steer (Pipeline → Workers). One process serves
every lane on the machine. A lane is one app and one clone of its repo.

Every minute it sends a heartbeat. The answer holds each lane's settings, set
in the console: its model, mode, how many reports at once, paused, drain and a
stop date, plus the machine's guards (agents at once, a free-memory floor, a
GitHub API floor). The daemon then works by each lane's mode:

| Mode | What the lane does |
| --- | --- |
| `fix` | Runs review follow-ups first, then claims reports: the lane's queue first, then the worst open reports |
| `followups` | Review follow-ups only |
| `conflicts` | Merges the base branch into a merge-queue PR of the clone's repository at the commit Mushi saw; the agent may change only the conflicted files; refused on a leftover marker or any other change; commits with your hooks and pushes the merge, fast-forward only |
| `audit` | A model (read-only) proposes bugs for one screen with the line, the code there and a check; the machine runs the check itself and files only what reproduces; a second model may only veto |
| `skill` | Only the rounds of skill runs started with this lane on Spend credits |

Whatever its mode (except `followups`), a lane first takes a **first-time user test**
someone started with Run now in the console: it runs `mushi-ux fresh-eyes` on this
machine and the console follows it live. The heartbeat tells the lane within a minute.

While a lane holds a report, no cloud agent is sent to it. Every outcome goes back to
Mushi; a failure of the machine (a clone permission, the network, a hook that
timed out under load) is kept apart from a failure of the code and never
counts against the report.

```bash
# One lane: print what it would write, then write it after you say yes
mushi worker install --lane my-app --project <projectId> --repo-dir ~/code/my-app --dry-run
mushi worker install --lane my-app --project <projectId> --repo-dir ~/code/my-app

# Import an existing lanes.conf (columns: name profile clone projectId model mode)
mushi worker install --lanes-conf ~/lanes.conf --clone-root ~/.cache/mushi-work

# A worker key made in the console instead of with your CLI login
mushi worker install --lanes-conf lanes.conf --key-stdin --yes < worker.key

# This machine's lanes and service, then every worker the console sees
mushi worker status

# Run it in the foreground (the service runs exactly this)
mushi work --daemon

# Revoke this machine's key and stop the service
mushi worker revoke
```

`install` writes the lanes to `~/.config/mushi/worker.json` (the clone paths
stay on your machine), stores a worker key in the OS keychain (or
`~/.config/mushi/worker.key`, mode 0600, where there is none), and writes the
service: a systemd user unit (`mushi-worker.service`) on Linux and WSL2, a
scheduled task that starts at logon on Windows. From `lanes.conf`, `queue` and
`fix` become `fix`, `followups`, `conflicts`, `audit` and `skill` stay as they
are, `off` becomes a paused lane, and the profile column is dropped: one worker
key serves every app. The heartbeat names each lane's repository (`owner/name`
from its `origin` remote) so a conflicts lane takes only that repository's
PRs; the clone's path never leaves the machine.

The worker key has the scope `worker:run`: it can take reports for its lanes,
record their fixes and file reports, and nothing else. It cannot merge, change
settings or read keys. `install` makes one with your CLI login (which needs
`mcp:write` on every lane's app), or takes one from stdin. The daemon refuses
your CLI key. The agent gets neither key.

`mushi worker status` starts with what stops your workers from fixing bugs, the
same list as the console's Workers tab, worst first: a run stuck in a repo's
commit or pre-push hook (with its stage and last log lines), an offline
machine, a Cursor account check that failed or timed out, lanes waiting for an
agent space (one coding agent at a time; each machine allows a set number),
`gh` signed out, idle credits. Each comes with what to do. It exits with code 2
while one of them needs you now. The worker sends the stage and log lines with
its heartbeat; keys, tokens and paths are removed and e-mail addresses masked
before anything leaves the machine.

| Command | Flags |
| --- | --- |
| `mushi work --daemon` | `--worker-config ` (default `~/.config/mushi/worker.json`) |
| `mushi worker install` | `--lanes-conf `, `--clone-root `, or one lane: `--lane`, `--project`, `--repo-dir`, `--model`; `--stop-at ` (every lane's stop date on first registration), `--cursor-account ` (spend only that Cursor account), `--endpoint`, `--key-stdin`, `--no-service`, `--yes`, `--dry-run` |
| `mushi worker status` | `--project `, `--json` |
| `mushi worker revoke` | `--yes` |

Operator guide (service, logs, moving existing lanes): [Local workers](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/docs/operators/local-workers.md).

### `mushi verify`

The `mushi-verify` workflow that proves an agent's fix with a test that fails
without it, filled in with your project's runner labels and test command. Full
guide: [Verified merge](/admin/verified-merge).

```bash
mushi verify workflow                                           # print it
mushi verify workflow --out .github/workflows/mushi-verify.yml  # write it
mushi verify workflow --project <projectId> --json
```

### `mushi runner`

Where your tests run and why a fix waits to land. Full guide: [CI runners](/operating/ci-runners).

```bash
mushi runner status [--days 7] [--refresh] [--all] [--json]   # machines, runners, wait times, test machine vs code failures
mushi runner compare [--days 30] [--all] [--json]             # what CI costs and how fast it runs: GitHub-hosted vs your machines (estimated)
mushi runner bill [--month 2026-10] [--owner login] [--push] [--json]  # what GitHub actually charged, read with your own gh login; --push shows it in the console
mushi runner placement show|preview|request|revert          # where each repo's CI runs; change one runner variable with approval (ADR 0037)
mushi runner fix --repo <owner/repo> --workflow <path> --kind <kind>  # draft PR with one CI cost fix (ADR 0047)
mushi runner fix-status [jobId]                              # the fix, its PR, and after the merge the measured saving
mushi runner key                                  # a runner key (can only report runner health), saved, never printed
mushi runner heartbeat [--once] [--dry-run]       # send this machine's memory, swap, load and runner services
mushi runner hooks install --dir <runner folder>  # per-job memory peak and out-of-memory kills
mushi runner add --repo owner/name --dry-run      # set this machine up as a runner, safe defaults
mushi runner audit [--repo owner/name | --all]    # list self-hosted runners and flag the odd ones
```

## QA coverage & TDD

```bash
# Live crawl → inventory proposal
mushi stories map --url https://your-app.com --wait
mushi stories map --url https://app.com --provider browserbase --cursor-refine

# TDD test generation
mushi tdd gen <storyId> --mode review
mushi tdd pending
mushi tdd approve <qaStoryId>
mushi tdd improve                    # PDCA on failing tests
mushi tdd run <qaStoryId>

# QA story ops
mushi qa stories
mushi qa runs <storyId>
mushi qa run <storyId>
mushi audit                        # full-stack project health audit
```

### UX pass over every screen

`mushi ux` runs [`@mushi-mushi/ux`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/ux) on your machine. It maps every page, tab and dialog of your running app, then hands one screen at a time to the coding agent you choose, in a separate git worktree. An edit is kept only if accessibility, layout and console measurements don't get worse. Exploring the app never sends a write request.

```bash
mushi ux ui                                              # studio: pick agent, model and skill; start; watch every attempt
mushi ux models --agent cursor                           # the models your account can use
mushi ux skills                                          # skill names from kensaurus/skills
mushi ux discover --url http://localhost:5173            # list the screens; edits nothing
mushi ux login --url http://localhost:5173               # sign in once, by hand, for signed-in screens
mushi ux run --dev "pnpm dev --port {port}" --agent claude-code
mushi ux run --dev "pnpm dev --port {port}" --agent cursor --model <id> --skill enhance-mobile-native-feel --base origin/main
mushi ux run --dev "pnpm dev --port {port}" --agent cursor-cloud --model grok-4.7   # edits run in Cursor Cloud
mushi ux open <runId>                                    # dashboard for a past run
```

The run ends with a branch, `mushi-ux/`, for you to review and open as a draft PR. Nothing is merged.

With `--steps` (on by default in `mushi ux ui`), the agent first plans each screen as 2–5 small, separate improvements without editing, then makes one per attempt; each step is measured and kept or rolled back on its own, so one bad step never costs the rest.

A run that stops for any reason (Stop, a closed terminal, a killed process) can be resumed with **Resume** in `mushi ux ui`, or with `mushi ux run --resume `: it carries on from the first unfinished screen with the settings it started with.

A run first checks, in about a minute, that the agent can read a file, and tells you what to fix if it cannot (`--no-preflight` skips it). On Windows, start the Cursor agent from PowerShell or cmd: the Cursor CLI also runs your Claude Code hooks, which can fail under Git Bash. Pass `--ignore ` (repeatable) for elements that are not your app's UI, such as a dev badge; dev overlays, build stamps and the Mushi widget are skipped already.

To run it on your repo's GitHub Actions instead, add the [`mushi-ux.yml` workflow](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/docs/templates/mushi-ux.yml) and use **Run in the cloud** on the console's [UX runs](/admin/ux-runs) page. It uses `cursor-cloud` and opens one draft PR.

### Gate findings

`mushi audit findings` lists each finding from the recent gate runs with its
file and line. `mushi audit explain` says why one fired, what it prevents and
how to fix it. `--gate` takes any gate name: one this CLI version does not list
is still sent to the server, with a warning.

```bash
mushi audit findings
mushi audit findings --gate code_health --severity error
mushi audit findings --all                      # include allowlisted findings
mushi audit explain <findingId>
```

### Code health

Oversized files and bundle size that your CI posts to `POST /v1/ingest/metrics`.

```bash
mushi code-health show [--days 30]
mushi code-health stats
```

## Your repo

These read the GitHub repo connected to the project. Mushi reads it through
the GitHub connection and does not clone it.

```bash
mushi repo digest > digest.txt                  # one token-budgeted text for an LLM; summary goes to stderr
mushi repo digest --report <reportId>           # start from the files in that report's stack trace and fixes
mushi repo digest --path src/auth --budget 40000 --out digest.txt

mushi repo diagram show                         # the architecture diagram as an outline
mushi repo diagram generate [--force]           # draw it for the latest commit
mushi repo diagram publish --yes                # make it a public page (owners and admins)
mushi repo diagram unpublish --yes
```

`publish` shows where the page will go before it publishes. It sends the hash
of exactly what the preview showed, so a diagram that changed in between is
refused. A private repo can only be published from the console.

### Clean up branches and pull requests

```bash
mushi repo cleanup show [--stale-days 14]       # branches and fix PRs Mushi opened that can go, with why and the commit
mushi repo cleanup request delete-branches --repo owner/app [--keys branch:a,branch:b]
mushi repo cleanup request close-prs --repo owner/app [--keys pr:12]
mushi repo cleanup request auto-delete --repo owner/app   # turn on GitHub's "Automatically delete head branches"
mushi repo cleanup restore <itemId>…            # bring back a branch Mushi deleted, at the commit it kept
```

Only branches and pull requests Mushi itself opened are listed: a branch whose
pull request merged or closed and that still points at that pull request's last
commit, or an open fix PR that a newer fix replaced, that the Opus review held,
or that got no new commit for 14 days. The CLI only asks. A team owner or admin
approves the exact list in the console (Repo → Clean up) within an hour, and
Mushi checks every item again before it deletes or closes anything.

## App recipe

```bash
mushi recipe init                    # write a starter mushi.recipe.json from what the repo shows
mushi recipe check                   # validate it and its token files; run Mushi's deviance rules and print the 0–100 score
mushi recipe check --max-score 30    # also fail when the score is above 30
mushi recipe check --push            # send the recipe and the scan from your existing CI job; fails above the project's limit when that gate is on
mushi recipe show                    # each part of the recipe and its state
```

For `--push`, give CI a `mushi login` key (it carries `mcp:read`). A push with
the SDK key (`report:write` only) keeps its findings and the CI gate, but never
sets the score the console shows or dispatches a design fix, because that key
ships inside your app.

## Hole checks (radar)

Checks that catch a problem before a user hits it. `scan` runs in your own CI
job; Mushi never clones your repo.

```bash
mushi radar scan                     # storage deletes done in SQL, secret keys in the built app; lists the build files the store rules read
mushi radar scan --push              # send results to Mushi (one extra step in your existing CI job, after the build step)
mushi radar scan --bundle-dir web/dist   # scan only these built client folders (repeatable), e.g. to leave out a server dist
mushi radar show                     # every hole check for this project and what it found
```

Run `scan` **after your build step**: it also reads the built app (`dist`,
`build`, `out`, `.next/static`, `.output/public`, `.svelte-kit/output/client`,
`.vercel/output/static`, native JS bundles) for secret keys. A `dist` that holds
server code counts too; name the client folders with `--bundle-dir` to leave it
out. With no build output, that check is left out and reads "Not checked",
never a pass.
Only the file, the line and the kind of key are sent, never the key itself.
The Supabase anon key and the Mushi SDK key are public by design and are not
flagged.

### One CI step for both checks

`radar scan --push` and `recipe check --push` belong in a job you already
run, so they cost no extra job. Both need `@mushi-mushi/cli` 0.29.0 or later;
an older CLI answers "unknown command", and the packaged action stops with
that version in its error instead. Store a project key as a repo secret first.
The SDK ingest key works; an account-level (org) key does not. Both commands
read the checked-out repo, so the job needs `actions/checkout` before them,
and `radar scan` also reads the built app, so put the step after your build.

**Copy-paste `run:` step**, for any CI system:

```yaml
- name: Mushi checks
  run: |
    npx --yes @mushi-mushi/cli@latest radar scan --push
    npx --yes @mushi-mushi/cli@latest recipe check --push
  env:
    MUSHI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MUSHI_INGEST_KEY }}
```

**Packaged GitHub Action**, the same CLI with the inputs spelled out:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: kensaurus/mushi-mushi/packages/cli@master
  with:
    api-key: ${{ secrets.MUSHI_INGEST_KEY }}
    upload-sourcemaps: 'false'   # set 'true' (the default) to also upload source maps
    radar-scan: 'true'
    recipe-check: 'true'
    # working-directory: apps/web   # if the app is not at the repo root
    # fail-on-error: 'false'        # warn instead of failing the job
```

| Input | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `radar-scan` | `false` | Runs `mushi radar scan --push`. Findings do not fail the job; they show on the hole checks. |
| `recipe-check` | `false` | Runs `mushi recipe check --push`. An invalid `mushi.recipe.json` (or none) fails the step. |
| `fail-on-error` | `true` | `false` turns a failed check or an unreachable Mushi into a warning. |
| `working-directory` | `.` | The repo root both checks read. |
| `upload-sourcemaps` | `true` | The action's original source-map upload. Uses `release`, `sourcemaps-dir`, `dry-run`. |

Run it on pushes to your default branch. `recipe check --push` records the
commit SHA and branch from `GITHUB_SHA` and `GITHUB_REF_NAME`, and on a pull
request the branch is the merge ref.

## Store listings

Copy the live App Store and Google Play listings into the repo once, so the
listing lives as code. It runs with your own keys and sends nothing to Mushi.
Your own CI publishes listing changes after that.

```bash
mushi store pull --asc-key-id <id> --asc-issuer-id <id> --asc-key-path AuthKey.p8 \
  --play-key-path play-service-account.json
```

It reads `store.listingDir`, `store.ios.appleId` and `store.android.package`
from `mushi.recipe.json`. The keys can also come from `MUSHI_ASC_KEY_ID`,
`MUSHI_ASC_ISSUER_ID`, `MUSHI_ASC_KEY_PATH` and
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. Review the files before you commit them.

## Integrations, keys & Slack

```bash
mushi integrations list
mushi integrations test slack
mushi integrations test sentry
mushi integrations test github

mushi keys list
MUSHI_BYOK_KEY=sk-ant-... mushi keys add --provider anthropic --label "Backup"

# Spend down a Cursor key's expiring credits on open bugs (draft PRs only)
mushi keys spend-down                                   # status of every Cursor key
mushi keys spend-down <keyId> --on --expires 2026-10-31 \
  --model 'grok-4.7?reasoning_effort=xhigh&context=500k' --per-day 20

mushi slack status
mushi slack test
```

Spend-down mode starts `--window-days` (default 14) before the credits expire
and dispatches the best open reports of the apps the key already pays for,
inside each app's auto-fix limits. A key shared by the whole organization is
changed by an owner or admin in the console (Settings, AI keys, Cursor).
It pauses an app on its own when that app's recent agent pull requests review
poorly, then sends one test fix a day until they recover
([agent PR review](/concepts/agent-pr-review#spend-down-and-its-safety-stop)).

## Several apps

For a team with more than one app. These read team-wide data, so they need an
account-level key (console: **Connect → MCP → account key**), not a key bound
to one project. If you belong to several teams, the error lists each one with
the `--org ` to pass.

```bash
mushi portfolio show                 # each app: health, open reports, holes, SDK version, last release
mushi portfolio findings             # the same problem repeated across apps, SDK skew, integration holes
mushi portfolio resources            # domains, accounts and buckets shared between apps
mushi connectors list                # connectors with status and last error (read-only)
mushi connectors status <id>
mushi connectors actions             # requested connector actions and whether they ran
mushi funnel show                    # one funnel, every app side by side
mushi funnel set --steps signup,first_report,fix_merged --window 7d
mushi releases calendar              # what is waiting to ship in each app, and one suggested batch
```

Adding, probing or editing a connector takes credentials, so it stays in the
console.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Purpose |
| -------- | ------- |
| `MUSHI_API_KEY` | Admin or ingest API key (prefer env over `--api-key` flag) |
| `MUSHI_API_ENDPOINT` | API base URL |
| `MUSHI_PROJECT_ID` | Project UUID |
| `MUSHI_CONSOLE_URL` | Admin console base for CLI hints + browser opens |
| `MUSHI_BYOK_KEY` | BYOK key value for `mushi keys add` (keeps key out of shell history) |
| `MUSHI_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` | Skip npm registry version nudge in `mushi init` |
| `MUSHI_ASC_KEY_ID`, `MUSHI_ASC_ISSUER_ID`, `MUSHI_ASC_KEY_PATH` | Your App Store Connect key for `mushi store pull` (read on your machine, never sent to Mushi) |

### Config file

The CLI keeps credentials in one `config.json`. The first match wins:

1. `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mushi/config.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, on any platform
2. `%APPDATA%\mushi\config.json` on Windows
3. `~/.config/mushi/config.json` otherwise (macOS, Linux)

On macOS and Linux the file is mode `0o600`; on Windows the CLI restricts its
ACL to your account (and SYSTEM) instead. A legacy `~/.mushirc` auto-migrates
on first load. `mushi setup --help` prints the path it resolved on your
machine.

## @mushi-mushi/core

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/core

---
title: '@mushi-mushi/core'
description: Reference for @mushi-mushi/core, the MushiConfig shape, widget options, PII scrubbing helpers and region resolution shared by every Mushi Mushi JavaScript SDK.
---

# `@mushi-mushi/core`

Shared types, HTTP client, offline queue helpers, and config used by every
Mushi Mushi framework SDK. It is framework-agnostic, and you rarely install it
directly.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @mushi-mushi/core
```

## API

### `Mushi.init(config)` (web) / `MushiProvider` (React Native)

```ts
interface MushiConfig {
  projectId: string   // UUID from the console Projects page
  apiKey: string      // report:write key — shown once at project creation
  apiEndpoint?: string // override for self-hosted deployments
  /** Automatic error reports only (0–1). User feedback always sends. Default 1. */
  sampleRate?: number
  /** Session-replay sampling (0–1). Decision at init. Default 1. */
  replaySampleRate?: number
  /** Drop or mutate any report after PII scrub. Prefer over beforeSendFeedback. */
  beforeSend?: (report: MushiReport) => MushiReport | null | Promise<MushiReport | null>
}
```

Get both values in one step by running `mushi login` or by creating a project in
the [Mushi Mushi console](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/admin/projects). The ID and
key are shown together on the success screen after project creation.

Sampling + `beforeSend` examples: [`@mushi-mushi/web`](/sdks/web#sampling--beforesend).

### `MushiWidgetConfig` (selected keys)

```ts
interface MushiWidgetConfig {
  position?: 'bottom-right' | 'bottom-left' | 'top-right' | 'top-left'
  theme?: 'auto' | 'light' | 'dark' | 'inherit'
  trigger?: 'auto' | 'banner' | 'edge-tab' | 'attach' | 'manual' | 'hidden'
  /** 1.19+ — privacy caption under screenshot preview */
  screenshotSensitiveHint?: boolean | string
}
```

See [`docs/SDK_SCREENSHOT_PREVIEW.md`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/docs/SDK_SCREENSHOT_PREVIEW.md)
for the full preview + consent flow.

### `captureEvent(input)`

Send a report from code through the SDK instance (`Mushi.getInstance()` on
web). The input is `MushiCaptureEventInput`:

```ts
interface MushiCaptureEventInput {
  description: string
  category?: 'bug' | 'slow' | 'visual' | 'confusing' | 'other'
  severity?: 'critical' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'
  component?: string
  tags?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>
  source?: string
  error?: { name?: string; message?: string; stack?: string }
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>
}
```

The full wire shape the SDKs build for you is `MushiReport` (environment,
console and network logs, `screenshotDataUrl`, reporter token, and more).

### Offline queue

`createOfflineQueue()` is the IndexedDB queue the web SDK uses. Queued
reports send automatically when the connection returns; there is no manual
flush call to make.

### PII scrubbing utilities (1.27+)

The redactor that every SDK uses at capture time is exported so you can reuse
it in your own `beforeSend` hook, server code, or logs. It runs entirely in
your process, so scrubbed values never leave the client.

```ts
import { scrubPii, scrubUrl, createPiiScrubber } from '@mushi-mushi/core'

// Free text → typed placeholders
scrubPii('email jake@x.com or call +1 415 555 0100')
// → 'email [REDACTED_EMAIL] or call [REDACTED_PHONE]'

// URL query values → redacted; keys and path preserved for debuggability
scrubUrl('/articles?tag=dragons&token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.payload.sig')
// → '/articles?tag=dragons&token=[Scrubbed]'
```

**`scrubPii(text, config?)`** replaces sensitive substrings anywhere in free
text. **`scrubUrl(url, config?)`** redacts only query-string *values* (both the
standard `?…` part and any `?…` inside a hash-router fragment, `#/path?…`) and
leaves keys and path segments intact. `scrubUrl` redacts values under
known-sensitive keys (any key containing `token`, `jwt`, `passw`, `pwd`,
`secret`, `api_key`/`apikey`, `auth`, `session`, `signature`, `email`, `phone`
or `ssn`, case-insensitive, plus the exact keys `key` / `code` / `sig`)
to `[Scrubbed]`, then pattern-scrubs the remaining values so a JWT hiding under
an innocent key (`?next=eyJ…`) is still caught. Both accept absolute or relative
URLs and never throw.

Patterns and their placeholders (all matched case-sensitively unless noted):

| Data | Placeholder | Default |
|------|-------------|:-------:|
| Email | `[REDACTED_EMAIL]` | on |
| Phone number | `[REDACTED_PHONE]` | on |
| US SSN | `[REDACTED_SSN]` | on |
| Credit-card PAN | `[REDACTED_CC]` | on |
| JWT (`eyJ….….…`) | `[REDACTED_JWT]` | on |
| AWS access key | `[REDACTED_AWS_KEY]` | on |
| AWS secret access key (case-insensitive key name) | `aws_secret_access_key=[REDACTED_AWS_SECRET]` | on |
| Stripe secret / restricted key | `[REDACTED_STRIPE_KEY]` | on |
| Stripe publishable key | `[REDACTED_STRIPE_PK]` | on |
| Slack token | `[REDACTED_SLACK_TOKEN]` | on |
| GitHub personal access token | `[REDACTED_GITHUB_PAT]` | on |
| OpenAI key | `[REDACTED_OPENAI_KEY]` | on |
| Anthropic key | `[REDACTED_ANTHROPIC_KEY]` | on |
| Google API key | `[REDACTED_GOOGLE_KEY]` | on |
| IPv4 address | `[REDACTED_IP]` | **off** |
| IPv6 address | `[REDACTED_IPV6]` | **off** |

IP scrubbing is off by default because IPs are frequently load-bearing for
debugging (rate-limit keys, geo). Toggle any pattern via `PiiScrubberConfig`:

```ts
interface PiiScrubberConfig {
  emails?: boolean       // default true
  phones?: boolean       // default true
  creditCards?: boolean  // default true
  ssns?: boolean         // default true
  secretTokens?: boolean // default true — JWTs + vendor API keys
  ipAddresses?: boolean  // default false — IPv4
  ipv6?: boolean         // default false
}

// e.g. also redact IPs, keep everything else on
scrubPii(text, { ipAddresses: true })
```

`createPiiScrubber(config)` returns `{ scrub, scrubObject }` when you want to
build the scrubber once and reuse it across many strings or object fields:

```ts
const { scrub, scrubObject } = createPiiScrubber({ ipAddresses: true })
scrub(logLine)
scrubObject(record, ['description', 'url']) // scrubs only those string keys
```

The pattern set is the single source of truth shared with the Flutter SDK's
generated copy, so the two scrubbers can't drift.

### Region resolution

```ts
import { resolveRegionEndpoint, REGION_ENDPOINTS } from '@mushi-mushi/core'

const url = await resolveRegionEndpoint({
  projectId: 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID',
  apiEndpoint: REGION_ENDPOINTS.us,
  region: 'eu',
})
```

`REGION_ENDPOINTS` contains the canonical URLs:

```ts
const REGION_ENDPOINTS = {
  us: 'https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api',
  eu: 'https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api',
  jp: 'https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api',
}
```

## eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/eslint-plugin

---
title: 'eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi'
description: eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi, the Mushi Mushi ESLint plugin. Its no-dead-handler and no-mock-leak rules and preset flag empty handlers and mock data in production.
---

# `eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi`

The Mushi Mushi ESLint plugin has two lint rules for bugs AI coding tools often ship: **`no-dead-handler`**
flags event handlers that do nothing (`onClick={() => {}}`, a body that only
logs) and **`no-mock-leak`** flags faker / placeholder data left in
production paths. They run wherever ESLint runs: your editor, `pnpm lint`,
and CI.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi
```

## Turn on the two rules

```js filename="eslint.config.js"
import mushi from 'eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi'

export default [
  // …your other configs
  {
    plugins: { 'mushi-mushi': mushi },
    rules: {
      'mushi-mushi/no-dead-handler': 'error',
      'mushi-mushi/no-mock-leak': 'error',
    },
  },
]
```

For legacy `.eslintrc`:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["mushi-mushi"],
  "rules": {
    "mushi-mushi/no-dead-handler": "error",
    "mushi-mushi/no-mock-leak": "error"
  }
}
```

## The recommended preset

`mushi.configs.recommended` (and `plugin:mushi-mushi/legacy`) turns on the
two rules above plus `no-allowlist-jsx-textnode`, which catches an allowlist
comment written as JSX text (it would render on the page) and nothing else.

```js filename="eslint.config.js"
import mushi from 'eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi'

export default [mushi.configs.recommended]
```

The plugin's other 16 rules check the Mushi console's own design system
(tokens, ``, ``, page posture, the widget theme) and
are only in the Mushi monorepo's `internal` preset. Turn one on by name if
it fits your app.

## Rules

### `mushi-mushi/no-dead-handler`

Flags inline event handlers (`on*` props, and `onClick` / `onSubmit`-style
object keys) whose body is empty, returns `null`, holds only `console.*` calls in a
block, or throws "not implemented", including inside `useCallback`. It checks inline
functions only: a handler passed by name, such as `onSubmit={noop}`, is not
followed. Files named `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` and `*.stories.*` are skipped.

```jsx
// ✗ caught
<button onClick={() => {}}>Submit</button>
<button onClick={() => { console.log('clicked') }}>Save</button>

// ✓ allowed
<button onClick={() => mutate()}>Submit</button>
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}><button type="submit">Submit</button></form>

// ✓ allowed in tests + stories
<button onClick={() => {}} />        // foo.test.tsx, *.stories.tsx
```

### `mushi-mushi/no-mock-leak`

Flags mock-library imports (`@faker-js/faker`, `faker`, `msw`, and
similar), arrays of placeholder objects (`John Doe`, `Jane Doe`), and
`lorem ipsum` or `placeholder@example.com` strings in production files. It
skips files under a `__tests__`, `test`, `tests`, `spec`, `stories`,
`fixtures`, `mocks` or `__mocks__` folder, and files named `*.test.*`,
`*.spec.*`, `*.stories.*` or `*.mock.*`. The intent is to catch the
moment a developer leaves their seed data wired up in a real page.

```ts
// ✗ caught — apps/web/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx
const projects = [
  { name: 'John Doe', tasks: 12 },
  { name: 'Jane Doe', tasks: 7 },
]

// ✓ allowed — apps/web/src/__mocks__/projects.ts
export const projects = [
  { name: 'John Doe', tasks: 12 },
]
```

## In CI

Run ESLint as its own step (for example `npx eslint .`) so a PR fails when
either rule reports. To record the findings in Mushi Mushi as well, write a
JSON report (`npx eslint -f json -o mushi-eslint.json src/`) and pass it to the
[`@mushi-mushi/mcp-ci`](/sdks/mcp-ci) `gates` command as `eslint-report`. That
command does not run ESLint itself, and its `dead_handler` and `mock_leak`
gates fail when no report is given.

# `mushi_mushi` (Flutter)

The Mushi Mushi Flutter SDK, written in Dart, for iOS and Android: `RepaintBoundary` screenshot capture, shake
detection via `sensors_plus`, a Material bottom sheet, and a byte-capped
offline queue.

  **Preview, not on pub.dev yet.** Install it as a `git:` dependency from the
  repository until the first release is published.

```yaml
# pubspec.yaml
dependencies:
  mushi_mushi:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi.git
      path: packages/flutter
      ref: master
```

See [Quickstart → Flutter](/quickstart/flutter) for the full setup walkthrough.

## API surface

| Member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Mushi.instance.configure(MushiConfig)` | Boot the SDK; call once in `main()` before `runApp()` |
| `Mushi.instance.report(description:, category:, metadata:)` | Submit a report from code |
| `Mushi.instance.captureError(error, [stackTrace])` | Report a caught error with its type and stack trace |
| `Mushi.instance.showWidget(context)` | Present the bottom sheet from any screen |
| `Mushi.instance.screenshotBoundaryKey` | `GlobalKey` of the `RepaintBoundary` screenshots are taken from |
| `Mushi.instance.rootContext` / `setRootContext(context)` | Context used by shake-to-report to present the sheet |
| `Mushi.instance.onReportSubmitted` | Callback after each successful submission (use it to mirror reports into Sentry) |

## Configuration

`MushiConfig` requires `projectId`, `apiKey` and `endpoint` (the hosted API is
`https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api`). Optional fields:
`triggerMode` (`shake`, `button`, `both`, `none`; default `shake`),
`captureScreenshot`, `minDescriptionLength` (default 20),
`offlineQueueMaxBytes` (default 2 MB), `theme` and `triggerInsets`.

## Submitting a report

```dart
await Mushi.instance.report(
  description: 'The checkout button does nothing.',
  category: 'bug',
  metadata: {'screen': 'checkout'},
);
```

## Screenshot capture

The SDK captures the widget tree under `screenshotBoundaryKey` into a PNG
before submission. No boundary key, no screenshot; set
`captureScreenshot: false` to turn it off entirely.

## Offline queue

Reports that fail to send are written to a file in the app's support
directory and retried every 30 seconds and whenever connectivity returns. The
queue is capped by `offlineQueueMaxBytes`; the oldest entries are trimmed
first.

## @mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/inventory-auth-runner

---
title: '@mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner'
description: "@mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner logs in with Playwright from your inventory.yaml auth script so the Mushi Mushi crawler can reach pages behind a login."
---

# `@mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner`

A small Playwright runner that signs in to your app with the login script
in your [`inventory.yaml`](/sdks/inventory-schema), picks the session
cookie, and saves it to your Mushi Mushi project so the crawler and synthetic
monitor can reach pages behind a login wall.

## When you need it

If your `inventory.yaml` describes any path that requires a session
(`/dashboard`, `/settings/*`), the crawler and synthetic monitor will
get redirected to `/login` until they have valid auth. This package
gives you the bootstrap step that hands them a session.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner
npx playwright install chromium   # once, if Playwright has no Chromium on this machine yet
```

## Usage

Add a scripted `auth` block under `app` in `inventory.yaml`. The script is
the body of an async function that receives Playwright's `page`, an `env`
object for your secrets, and `context`; the runner has already opened
`base_url` + `login_path`:

```yaml filename="inventory.yaml"
app:
  id: acme-web
  name: Acme web
  base_url: https://app.acme.test
  auth:
    type: scripted
    config:
      login_path: /login
      script: |
        await page.fill('[data-testid=email]', env.TEST_USER_EMAIL)
        await page.fill('[data-testid=password]', env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD)
        await page.click('[data-testid=login]')
        await page.waitForURL('**/dashboard')
```

Inline scripts may not use `require(`, `import(`, `process.`, `eval(` and
similar escapes, and are capped at 8 KB. For anything longer, set
`script: 'js:./scripts/login.js'` to a module that default-exports an
async `(page, env, context)` function. The path resolves against the folder
of your local `inventory.yaml` (`--inventory ` or
`MUSHI_INVENTORY_FILE`; default `./inventory.yaml`, so the working
directory).

Then run:

```bash
TEST_USER_EMAIL=user@acme.test \
TEST_USER_PASSWORD=… \
MUSHI_API_KEY=mushi_… \
MUSHI_PROJECT=<project-uuid> \
npx mushi-mushi-auth refresh
```

Without installing, use
`npx --yes -p @mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner mushi-mushi-auth refresh`.
`MUSHI_API_KEY` needs the `mcp:write` scope. `MUSHI_API_ENDPOINT` is only
for self-hosting.

The runner signs in in a fresh headless Chromium, picks the session cookie
set for your app's domain, and saves it with
`PATCH /v1/admin/inventory/:projectId/settings`. The crawler and synthetic
monitor read it from there on every run.

## In CI

Cookies expire. Rebake them on a schedule (e.g. nightly) so the
synthetic monitor never falls back to an unauthenticated walk:

```yaml filename=".github/workflows/mushi-auth-bootstrap.yml"
name: Mushi auth bootstrap
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  refresh:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      # The runner launches Chromium; a fresh runner has no Playwright browser.
      - run: npx --yes -p @mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - uses: kensaurus/mushi-mushi/packages/mcp-ci@master
        with:
          api-key:    ${{ secrets.MUSHI_API_KEY }}
          project-id: ${{ secrets.MUSHI_PROJECT_ID }}
          command:    auth-bootstrap
        env:
          TEST_USER_EMAIL:    ${{ secrets.MUSHI_TEST_USER_EMAIL }}
          TEST_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MUSHI_TEST_USER_PASSWORD }}
```

The `auth-bootstrap` command in [`@mushi-mushi/mcp-ci`](/sdks/mcp-ci)
is a convenience wrapper that calls this runner (with `MUSHI_PROJECT` set
from `project-id`); use it from CI. It does not install a browser itself.

## @mushi-mushi/inventory-schema

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/inventory-schema

---
title: '@mushi-mushi/inventory-schema'
description: "The Zod schema, JSON Schema and TypeScript types for inventory.yaml: your app's pages, the buttons and forms on each, what they do, and the tests that prove it."
---

# `@mushi-mushi/inventory-schema`

Validate an `inventory.yaml`: the file that lists your app's pages, the
buttons and forms on each one, what each should do, and the test that
proves it. Zod schema, JSON Schema and TypeScript types, matching what the
Mushi Mushi console accepts when you upload the file.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @mushi-mushi/inventory-schema
```

Add it when you write a tool that produces or checks `inventory.yaml`
files, or to validate the file in your own CI. Mushi's CLI, ESLint plugin
and GitHub Action do not depend on it.

## What `inventory.yaml` looks like

```yaml filename="inventory.yaml"
schema_version: '2.0'          # a string starting with "2"; quote it
app:
  id: acme-web
  name: Acme web
  base_url: https://app.acme.test
  # Optional: how the crawler signs in (see inventory-auth-runner).
  auth:
    type: scripted
    config:
      login_path: /login
      script: |
        await page.fill('[data-testid=email]', env.TEST_USER_EMAIL)
        await page.fill('[data-testid=password]', env.TEST_USER_PASSWORD)
        await page.click('[data-testid=login]')
user_stories:
  - id: signup
    title: New user signup
    pages: [signup]
pages:
  - id: signup
    path: /signup
    auth_required: false
    elements:
      - id: signup-submit
        type: button             # button, link, form, input, list, toggle, menu, image, media, other
        action: Creates the account and opens the dashboard
        user_story: signup
        testid: signup-submit
        backend:
          - { method: POST, path: /signup }
        db_writes:
          - { table: users, operation: insert }
        verified_by:
          - { file: e2e/signup.spec.ts, name: signs up a new user, framework: playwright }
        # Machine-readable success contract. Threaded into the
        # fix-worker LLM prompt and asserted by the synthetic
        # monitor after every probe.
        expected_outcome:
          summary: 'POST /signup returns 200 and creates a user row'
          response:
            status_in: [200, 201]
            json_path:
              - { path: 'user.id', op: 'exists' }
          database:
            table: 'users'
            expect: 'row_exists'
          ui:
            route_change_to: '/dashboard'
            visible_text: 'Welcome'
```

`app` and at least one page are required; `user_stories`, `dependencies`
and `extensions` are optional. Each element needs `id`, `type` and
`action`. `auth` can also be `cookie`, `bearer` or `oauth`.

See [Concepts → Inventory and gates](/concepts/inventory-and-gates) for
the conceptual model and a walkthrough of the gates.

## Programmatic use

```ts
import {
  inventorySchema,
  parseInventory,
  type Inventory,
} from '@mushi-mushi/inventory-schema'

const result = parseInventory(yamlString)
if (!result.ok) {
  for (const issue of result.issues) console.error(`${issue.path}: ${issue.message}`)
  process.exit(1)
}
const inventory: Inventory = result.inventory!
```

`inventorySchema` is the canonical Zod schema. `parseInventory` loads the
YAML and runs `safeParse`; `validateInventory` does the same for an object
you already parsed. `computeStats` counts pages, elements, actions, stories,
API and database dependencies, and tests.

## JSON Schema

For editor completion, point your YAML extension at the published JSON
Schema:

```yaml filename="inventory.yaml"
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/schemas/inventory-2.0.json
schema_version: '2.0'
# …
```

The same schema is exported as `inventoryJsonSchema` from
`@mushi-mushi/inventory-schema/json-schema`.

# `MushiMushi` (iOS / macOS / tvOS)

The Mushi Mushi native Swift SDK, with no third-party dependencies.

  **Preview.** Not on CocoaPods and no release tag yet. Add the package with
  Swift Package Manager on the `master` branch.

```swift
// Swift Package Manager: Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi.git", branch: "master")
```

See [Quickstart → iOS](/quickstart/ios) for the full setup walkthrough.

## API surface

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Mushi.shared.configure(with: MushiConfig(...))` | Boot the SDK; call in `App.init()` or `application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:)` |
| `Mushi.shared.report(description:category:metadata:)` | Submit a report from code, no UI |
| `Mushi.shared.captureError(_:context:)` | Report a Swift `Error` with its name, message and cause |
| `Mushi.shared.showWidget(category:metadata:)` | Present the bottom-sheet widget |
| `Mushi.shared.setUser(_:)` | Attach app user identity to subsequent reports |
| `Mushi.shared.setMetadata(_:value:)` | Attach or clear a metadata key on subsequent reports |
| `Mushi.shared.addBreadcrumb(category:level:message:data:)` | Add to the 50-entry breadcrumb ring buffer |
| `Mushi.shared.attachTo(_:)` | Open the widget when a `UIControl` is tapped |

## Setup

`MushiConfig` requires `projectId`, `apiKey` and `endpoint`. Everything else
has a default.

```swift
import MushiMushi

Mushi.shared.configure(with: MushiConfig(
    projectId: "YOUR_PROJECT_ID",
    apiKey: "mushi_...",
    endpoint: "https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api",
    triggerMode: .shake,       // .shake | .button | .both | .none
    captureScreenshot: true,
    minDescriptionLength: 20
))
```

## Identifying users

```swift
// After sign-in
Mushi.shared.setUser(["id": user.id, "email": user.email])
```

## Offline queue

Reports that fail to send are appended to
`Application Support/MushiMushi/queue.ndjson`, capped by
`offlineQueueMaxBytes` (default 1 MB; oldest entries trimmed first), and flushed on a timer
and when the network comes back.

## Screenshot capture

Screenshots are taken with `UIGraphicsImageRenderer` when `captureScreenshot`
is `true`. Turn it off for flows that show sensitive data.

## Sentry

There is no Sentry bridge in the Swift package. Keep initialising Sentry in the
host app and pass context to Mushi with `setMetadata` or
`report(..., metadata:)`.

## mushi-mushi (launcher)

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/launcher

---
title: 'mushi-mushi (launcher)'
description: npx mushi-mushi detects your framework, installs the matching Mushi Mushi SDK, writes your project ID and API key to .env.local, and prints the snippet.
---

# `mushi-mushi`: the one-command launcher

`npx mushi-mushi` is the single Mushi Mushi entry point on npm: it auto-detects
your framework, picks the right `@mushi-mushi/*` SDK, writes your project ID
and API key into `.env.local` (or an existing `.env`) as `MUSHI_PROJECT_ID` and
`MUSHI_API_KEY` with your framework's env prefix, and prints the snippet to
paste into your app.

## Try it

```bash
npx mushi-mushi
```

Equivalent commands. All three run the same wizard from
[`@mushi-mushi/cli`](/sdks/cli):

```bash
npx mushi-mushi              # the launcher (this package)
npm create mushi-mushi       # via the npm-create convention
npx @mushi-mushi/cli init    # the scoped name
```

## What it detects

The wizard reads the dependencies in your `package.json` first, in this
order, and takes the first match:

| Framework (`--framework` id) | Detected from |
| --- | --- |
| Next.js (`next`) | `next` dependency |
| Nuxt (`nuxt`) | `nuxt` dependency |
| SvelteKit (`sveltekit`) | `@sveltejs/kit` dependency |
| Angular (`angular`) | `@angular/core` dependency |
| Expo (`expo`) | `expo` dependency |
| React Native (`react-native`) | `react-native` dependency without Expo |
| Remix (`remix`) | `@remix-run/react`, `@remix-run/node` or `@remix-run/serve` |
| Astro (`astro`) | `astro` dependency |
| Solid (`solid`) | `solid-js` or `@solidjs/start` |
| Capacitor (`capacitor`) | `@capacitor/core` (with `react` it is treated as React) |
| Svelte (`svelte`) | `svelte` dependency |
| Vue (`vue`) | `vue` dependency |
| Create React App (`cra`) | `react-scripts` dependency |
| React (`react`) | `react` dependency |
| Express, Fastify, Hono (`express`, `fastify`, `hono`) | the server framework's dependency (`hono` or `@hono/hono` for Hono) |
| Vanilla (`vanilla`) | fallback |

With no matching dependency it falls back to config files
(`next.config.*`, `nuxt.config.*`, `svelte.config.js`, `angular.json`,
`remix.config.*`, `astro.config.*`). Pass `--framework ` to skip
detection.

The package manager is detected from the lockfile (`bun.lockb` or
`bun.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`). Env-var
prefixes are chosen by framework: `NEXT_PUBLIC_…`, `NUXT_PUBLIC_…`,
`EXPO_PUBLIC_…`, `REACT_APP_…` (Create React App), `PUBLIC_…` (Astro) and
`VITE_…` for the other browser frameworks. Server frameworks, bare React
Native and Remix get plain `MUSHI_…` names.

## Running it again

Running the wizard a second time is safe:

- If `MUSHI_*` vars already exist in the env file, the wizard asks before
  replacing them. With `--yes` (and in non-interactive shells) it replaces them.
- The install step runs again; pass `--skip-install` to print the install
  command instead. When an `@mushi-mushi/*` package is already a dependency,
  the wizard suggests `npx mushi-mushi --audit`, which runs health checks
  instead of the setup.
- After writing the env file it warns if that file isn't gitignored, so
  secrets don't accidentally end up in source control.

## When to use the launcher vs the CLI directly

Use **the launcher** when you want one command to give a teammate
("`npx mushi-mushi` and you're done"). Any other command is forwarded to
`@mushi-mushi/cli`, so `npx mushi-mushi setup --ide cursor` or
`npx mushi-mushi reports list` works without a global install.

Install **`@mushi-mushi/cli`** globally (`npm install -g @mushi-mushi/cli`)
when you use it every day and want the short `mushi` command, for example
`mushi reports list`, `mushi reports triage `, or the `mushi migrate`
migration helper.

## Bug report MCP server for Cursor & Claude Code

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/mcp

---
title: Bug report MCP server for Cursor & Claude Code
description: Reference for @mushi-mushi/mcp, the Mushi Mushi MCP server for Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code and Windsurf. stdio and hosted HTTP transports, scopes and setup.
---

# `@mushi-mushi/mcp`

The Mushi Mushi MCP server for Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, Claude, Zed,
and other MCP clients: reports, plain-English reads, and fix briefs in the editor.
**[→ Connect](/connect)** for a one-click install. Full walkthrough:
[Quickstart → MCP](/quickstart/mcp).

Speaks **JSON-RPC 2.0** with `tools/call` semantics. The hosted endpoint also
supports the MCP **Tasks** extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`), so a
client on the 2026-07-28 revision can follow a long-running fix as a task.

## Quick start

```bash
npx mushi-mushi setup --ide cursor   # or: claude, continue, zed
```

Restart the editor and ask "what's broken in prod?". For Cursor and Claude
Code, `setup` writes the hosted server entry
(`https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/hosted-mcp/`, URL only): the editor opens a
browser sign-in on first use and no API key is stored on disk. Pass
`--stdio` for a local server instead. Continue and Zed always get the stdio
entry.

## Two transports

- **stdio (local)**: `npx -y @mushi-mushi/mcp@0.30.0`. This is what
  `mushi setup --stdio` writes, and what `setup` always writes for Continue and
  Zed. Use it for any client that only runs local servers. Your client launches
  the server as a subprocess and pipes JSON-RPC over stdio.
- **Streamable HTTP (hosted, 2026-05-09 release)**: single endpoint
  at `/functions/v1/mcp`, dual-era (MCP 2024-11-05 … 2025-11-25 with `initialize`, and the current 2026-07-28 revision with `server/discover`). POST returns
  `application/json` or `text/event-stream` per content negotiation,
  GET opens an SSE stream for server-pushed notifications, DELETE
  terminates the session. Use this when you want to skip the local
  subprocess (typical for OpenAI Agents SDK, ChatGPT Agent, hosted
  CrewAI, or any orchestrator that talks remote MCP).

For browser sign-in, use the URL-only entry `mushi setup` writes. To pass a
key yourself instead (for an orchestrator that cannot open a browser), send
it as a header. A static key header turns the client's sign-in off:

```jsonc
// .cursor/mcp.json: Streamable HTTP with an API key
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mushi-mushi-hosted": {
      "url": "https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Mushi-Api-Key": "mushi_…",
        "X-Mushi-Project-Id": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Auth on both transports is the same dual-mode (API key with
`mcp:read|write` OR JWT) used everywhere on `/v1/admin/*`.

## Spec traceability for `dispatch_fix`

The `dispatch_fix` tool now accepts `inventoryActionNodeId` so callers
that already know the inventory `Action` they want repaired can pin the
fix directly. The complementary `get_fix_context` tool surfaces the
linked Action (with `expected_outcome`) so an external orchestrator can
read the contract before drafting a fix.

```jsonc
// dispatch_fix tool inputSchema (excerpt)
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["reportId"],
  "properties": {
    "reportId": { "type": "string" },
    "projectId": { "type": "string" },
    "inventoryActionNodeId": { "type": "string" }
  }
}
```

See [`@mushi-mushi/mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/mcp)
on npm for the full **130-tool** catalog and
[Connecting your orchestrator](/concepts/orchestrator-interop) for the
non-MCP surfaces (REST, A2A, AG-UI SSE).

Discoverable via the [A2A Agent Card](/concepts/architecture#a2a-agent-card).

## @mushi-mushi/mcp-ci

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/mcp-ci

---
title: '@mushi-mushi/mcp-ci'
description: "@mushi-mushi/mcp-ci is the Mushi Mushi GitHub Action: fail a PR while reports await triage, dispatch a fix, run pre-release gates and refresh crawler sign-in."
---

# `@mushi-mushi/mcp-ci`

The Mushi Mushi GitHub Action. It calls the same API the MCP server uses, from a
short CI job: fail a PR while bug reports sit untriaged, have an agent open
a fix PR for one report, run the pre-release gates on a commit, or refresh
the crawler's signed-in session.

## Quick start

```yaml filename=".github/workflows/mushi-gate.yml"
name: Mushi gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  coverage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: kensaurus/mushi-mushi/packages/mcp-ci@master
        with:
          api-key:      ${{ secrets.MUSHI_API_KEY }}
          project-id:   ${{ secrets.MUSHI_PROJECT_ID }}
          command:      check-coverage
          min-coverage: '0.9'
```

`check-coverage` fails the step when fewer than `min-coverage` (default
`0.8`) of the project's reports are classified. Classification runs on its own
when a report arrives; `trigger-judge` does not classify reports.

### Gates on every PR

```yaml filename=".github/workflows/mushi-gates.yml"
name: Mushi gates
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gates:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      # Gates 1 + 2 read your ESLint report (eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi rules).
      - run: npx eslint -f json -o mushi-eslint.json src/ || true
      - uses: kensaurus/mushi-mushi/packages/mcp-ci@master
        with:
          api-key:       ${{ secrets.MUSHI_API_KEY }}
          project-id:    ${{ secrets.MUSHI_PROJECT_ID }}
          command:       gates
          eslint-report: mushi-eslint.json
          commit-sha:    ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          pr-number:     ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
```

## Commands

| `command:`           | What it does                                                          |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `check-coverage`     | Fails when the classified share of reports is under `min-coverage`; sets the `coverage` output. |
| `trigger-judge`      | Starts the judge, which grades the AI classification of up to 50 classified reports not yet graded (projects with the judge turned on). It does not classify new reports. |
| `dispatch-fix`       | Queues an agent fix for `report-id` (optionally pinned with `inventory-action-node-id`). |
| `query`              | Runs a plain-English `question` against your reports and prints the answer. |
| `gates`              | Runs the gates for `commit-sha` (`all` = `dead_handler`, `mock_leak`, `api_contract`, `status_claim`, `orphan_endpoint`, `unknown_call`) and fails the step when one fails, errors or returns no result. |
| `discover-api`       | Walks your repo for Next.js route handlers and OpenAPI files (plus optional Supabase introspection) and sends the routes to Mushi for the `api_contract` gate. |
| `spec-drift`         | Gate 6: runs `oasdiff breaking` between `base-spec` and `head-spec`, records the findings and sets the `findings` output; fails on a breaking change unless `fail-on-breaking: false`. |
| `discovery-status`   | Reads what the SDK has observed; sets `ready_to_propose`, `total_events` and `route_count` outputs. |
| `propose`            | Asks the LLM proposer for an `inventory.yaml` draft and sets `proposal_id`. It does not open a PR. |
| `auth-bootstrap`     | Runs [`@mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner`](/sdks/inventory-auth-runner) (`npx --yes -p @mushi-mushi/inventory-auth-runner mushi-mushi-auth refresh`) to refresh the crawler's sign-in cookie. |

The action fails the step; it does not post a separate GitHub commit status.
`dead_handler` and `mock_leak` judge the findings in `eslint-report` (an
ESLint JSON report made with [`eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi`](/sdks/eslint-plugin)).
A run that asks for them without a report fails, so a missing lint step can
never pass as "no findings". `crawl` is not run by this command: start a crawl
with **Reconcile** on the Inventory page; `api_contract` reads its result. A
skipped gate prints its reason.

## In your IDE

The same commands are exposed as MCP tools via [`@mushi-mushi/mcp`](/sdks/mcp).
Cursor, Claude Code, and Copilot can run them on your behalf when the MCP
server is configured. Inside the admin console you can also click
**Run gates** / **Run crawler** directly on each row of the User stories
page; see [Admin → User stories · Inventory](/admin/inventory).

## Inputs

`action.yml` is the source of truth; a test keeps it in step with the CLI.

| Input         | Required | Default       | Description                                          |
| ------------- | :------: | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `api-key`     | ✓        | —             | Project API key (`mushi_…`). Store it as a repo secret. |
| `project-id`  | ✓        | —             | Project UUID.                                        |
| `command`     | ✓        | —             | One of the commands listed above.                    |
| `api-endpoint` |         | hosted Mushi Mushi API | Override for self-hosted deployments.          |
| `report-id`   | for `dispatch-fix` | —   | Report UUID.                                         |
| `inventory-action-node-id` |  | —     | For `dispatch-fix`: the inventory action to pin the fix to. |
| `question`    | for `query` | —          | The question to ask.                                 |
| `min-coverage` |         | `0.8`         | For `check-coverage`: the share of reports that must be classified. |
| `fail-on-quota` |        | `true`        | Set `false` to warn instead of failing on `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`. |
| `commit-sha`  |          | `GITHUB_SHA`  | For `gates` and `spec-drift`: the commit to check.   |
| `pr-number`   |          | —             | For `gates` and `spec-drift`: the PR the findings belong to. |
| `gates`       |          | `all`         | For `gates`: a comma-separated subset; `crawl` is refused. |
| `eslint-report` | for `gates` with `dead_handler` / `mock_leak` | — | ESLint JSON report (`eslint -f json`) made with `eslint-plugin-mushi-mushi`. |
| `repo-root`   |          | the workspace | For `discover-api`: where to look for routes. For `gates`: the root `eslint-report` paths are made relative to. |
| `openapi-file` |         | `openapi.yaml` in `repo-root` | For `discover-api`: an explicit OpenAPI file. |
| `supabase-url`, `supabase-anon-key` | | — | For `discover-api`: optional Supabase introspection. |
| `base-spec`, `head-spec` | for `spec-drift` | — | Base and head OpenAPI specs (path or URL). |
| `fail-on-breaking` |     | `true`        | For `spec-drift`: fail on a breaking change.         |

## Outputs

| Output             | Set by             | Description                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `result`           | most commands      | JSON returned by the Mushi API.                          |
| `coverage`         | `check-coverage`   | Observed classified ratio.                               |
| `findings`         | `spec-drift`       | JSON array of the oasdiff findings.                      |
| `ready_to_propose` | `discovery-status` | `"true"` once there is enough discovery data to propose. |
| `total_events`     | `discovery-status` | SDK discovery events recorded.                           |
| `route_count`      | `discovery-status` | Routes discovered.                                       |
| `proposal_id`      | `propose`          | Inventory proposal to review on `/inventory`.            |

More workflow examples are in the
[package README](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/mcp-ci).

## Read tools (`mcp:read`)

| Tool | Title | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `get_recent_reports` | Recent bug reports | List recent bug reports for a project, newest first. Returns \{ reports: [\{ id, status, category, severity, summary, component, created_at, processing_error }], total }; includeRaw=true returns every list column instead. Reporter identifiers (end-user id, reporter token hash, session id, display name) are never returned. Optional filters: status (new\|classified\|grouped\|fixing\|fixed\|verified\|reopened\|dismissed\|…), category (bug\|slow\|visual\|confusing\|other), severity (critical\|high\|medium\|low), limit (default 20, max 100). Use to survey open reports; for one report use get_report_detail, to find a bug by text use search_reports. |
| `get_report_detail` | Report detail | Fetch the full record for one bug report by id: description, console logs, network requests, screenshot URL, classification (stage 1/2), fix history, the paste-ready fix packet and the inventory action it is filed against. Returns \{ report } with the documented fields; includeRaw=true returns every column the detail route has instead. Reporter identifiers (end-user id, reporter token hash, session id, display name) are never returned. Read-only. Use when you have a reportId and need everything about it; for evidence only use get_report_evidence, for the activity thread use get_report_timeline, for a one-call fix bundle use get_fix_context. |
| `get_report_timeline` | Unified report timeline | Return the ordered activity timeline for one report (oldest to newest), merging reporter comments, fix events, QA runs, skill-pipeline steps, and Ask Mushi turns into one lane. Returns \{ events: [\{ ts, kind, actor, summary }] }. Read-only. Use to see what happened end-to-end on a report thread; use get_report_detail for the static record or get_fix_timeline to debug one fix attempt. |
| `search_reports` | Search reports | Search reports by meaning and keyword (pgvector similarity server-side; falls back to summary/description substring if embeddings are unavailable). Returns ranked \{ results: [\{ id, summary, similarity }] }. Read-only. Use to find reports by free text ("checkout flakiness"); use get_similar_bugs to dedupe a known component/bug, or get_recent_reports to list without a query. |
| `get_similar_bugs` | Similar bugs | Find existing bugs similar to a component, page, or description via pgvector nearest-neighbour search (same backend as search_reports, tuned for "have we seen this before?"). Returns ranked \{ reports: [\{ id, summary, similarity }] }. Read-only. Use to dedupe before filing or group regressions; use search_reports for general free-text search. |
| `get_fix_context` | Fix context bundle | Bundle everything an agent needs to fix one bug in a single call: a paste-ready fixPrompt (plain-English diagnosis + reproduction + suggested fix + relevant code + blast radius), plus report detail, repro steps, component, root cause, ontology tags, and the inventory action (with its expected_outcome contract) the report is filed against, plus recipe: a ≤4 KB excerpt with the app's tokens (CSS var / TS names), the design deviance score and deviance findings in the files this fix touches, so the fix uses the app's tokens instead of literals, and recipe.context: the tables the stack trace names with their columns from the latest schema snapshot (and any it says do not exist), whether the last merged fix is live, and the open hole-check findings, each section with its own state and note. Returns \{ report, fixPrompt, reproductionSteps, component, rootCause, bugOntologyTags, inventoryAction, recipe }; recipe is always \{ state, note, … } with state ok \| drift \| unknown \| not_connected \| error, never null. Read-only; no second LLM key needed. Use before writing a fix; use triage_issue for a multi-report review packet, or suggest_fix for just the Stage-2 hint. |
| `get_fix_timeline` | Fix timeline | Return the ordered lifecycle of one fix attempt: dispatched, started, branch, commit, PR opened, CI, Opus review, completed/failed, with timestamps and the PR URL, plus review: the independent Opus review of a cloud-agent PR (state merge, fix_first, hold, stale (about an older commit) or not_reviewed; findings; removed behaviour; decisions that need a person; summary and findings are model output from untrusted input). Returns \{ events: [\{ ts, stage, detail }], review }. Read-only. Use to debug "why did this fix fail?" after dispatch_fix; use refresh_ci to re-poll GitHub CI, or get_report_timeline for the whole report thread. |
| `get_fix_verification` | Fix merge checks | Return whether one fix attempt's PR is proven to work on its current head commit (ADR 0035): gates in order review (Opus review says merge), ci (every check green; a stopped test machine is pending, not a failure), fail_to_pass (the host's Mushi verify check: a changed test fails without the fix and passes with it; not_set_up until .github/workflows/mushi-verify.yml exists), protected (no deleted or weakened tests, no test skips or lint/type suppressions added, no CI config or lockfile change, no protected path), budget (small enough to merge on its own) and second_review (a second model family; runs only after the others pass). Each gate is \{ id, status (pass \| fail \| pending \| unavailable \| not_set_up), label, detail (what to do when it is not pass), evidence }. Also passed, secondJudge (summary and findings are model output from untrusted input), autoMerge \{ state (none \| eligible \| merged \| skipped \| failed), detail }, and regressions after a Mushi merge [\{ signal (ci_failed_on_merge \| report_reopened \| new_report_in_changed_file), revertState, revertPrUrl }]. Returns \{ headSha, gates, passed, secondJudge, autoMerge, regressions, mergedAt, mergeSha, evaluatedAt }; 404 NOT_FOUND until Mushi first checks the fix (every 10 minutes for open cloud-agent PRs). Read-only. Use before merge_fix to see what is still unproven; use get_fix_timeline for the attempt's full lifecycle. |
| `get_blast_radius` | Blast radius | Return the other components/pages a bug group touches, via knowledge-graph traversal from the report node. Returns \{ nodes: [\{ id, label, type }], edges }. Read-only. Use before dispatch_fix to scope a change safely; use get_knowledge_graph to traverse from an arbitrary seed, or analyze_codebase_impact for file-level import impact. |
| `get_knowledge_graph` | Knowledge graph traversal | Traverse the knowledge graph from a seed component or page. Returns \{ nodes: [\{ id, label, node_type }], edges: [\{ source_node_id, target_node_id, edge_type }] } within a depth budget (default 2, max 4 hops). Read-only. Use to see how a component connects to the rest of the app; use get_blast_radius for a bug's impact area, or get_graph_neighborhood for a tighter BFS around one node. |
| `run_nl_query` | Ask your data (NL → SQL) | Answer a natural-language question about your project data by generating and running a read-only SQL query (no privileged schemas, rate-limited to 60/hour). Returns \{ sql, rows }. Use for ad-hoc analytics ("which components had the most critical bugs this week?"); use get_recent_reports/search_reports for plain report lookups, or search_mushi_docs for documentation questions. |
| `get_inventory` | Inventory snapshot | Return the current inventory.yaml snapshot for a project: latest ingest, validation errors, and a per-action status summary. Returns \{ snapshot, validationErrors, actions: [\{ id, status }] }. Requires the inventory_v2 plan. Read-only. Use for the full current state; use diff_inventory to compare two commits, or list_gate_findings for the latest gate results. |
| `diff_inventory` | Inventory diff | Diff two ingested inventory commits (fromSha to toSha): added/removed nodes and edges. Returns \{ added, removed, changed }. Requires inventory_v2. Read-only. Use before merging a PR that touches inventory.yaml to see what changed; use get_inventory for the current snapshot. |
| `list_gate_findings` | Gate findings | List recent inventory gate runs and their findings for a project, newest first. Returns \{ runs: [\{ id, gate, status, findings_count, … }], findings: [\{ severity, rule_id, message, file_path, node_id, … }] }. Filter by gate (dead_handler \| mock_leak \| api_contract \| crawl \| status_claim \| spec_drift \| orphan_endpoint \| unknown_call \| schema_drift \| code_health \| design_drift \| ci_drift \| deploy_drift \| env_drift \| radar \| portfolio_radar \| portfolio_radar_ci \| portfolio_radar_vulns \| store_review) or finding severity (info \| warn \| error). The *_drift gates are the App Recipe checks: design_drift is code that drifts off the design tokens, ci_drift / deploy_drift / env_drift are CI, deploy and env vars that drift from the recipe; radar is the Mushi setup checks (a rejected provider key, no spend cap or AI budget, a webhook that never delivered, a stale code index), each with a suggested_fix (a spend-cap fix is applied in the console by a signed-in project admin, not through an API key); portfolio_radar / portfolio_radar_ci / portfolio_radar_vulns / store_review are the app hole checks (prefer get_radar). | `get_app_recipe` | App recipe | Return the App Recipe for a project: one card per element (schema, design, routes, gates, ci, deploy, env, integrations), each with a state, a plain-English reason, key facts, a findings count and console links, plus the worst state overall and the mushi.recipe.json manifest status. Every element is exactly one of ok \| drift \| unknown \| not_connected \| error. unknown means configured but not observed recently and never means healthy; not_connected means nothing is configured. Returns \{ projectId, worst, elements: \{ \: \{ state, reason, facts, findingsCount, lastCheckedAt, links } }, manifest, snapshotHash }. Read-only. Use to see how the app is put together and which part is drifting; use get_design_tokens for the token values, get_design_deviance for code that drifts off them, or list_gate_findings for gate detail. |
| `get_design_tokens` | Design tokens | Return the app's normalized design tokens (DTCG: path, type, resolved value, hex / px, alias, CSS var, TS and RN names, description, defining file) for the active token set, plus nameMap (CSS var or TS name → token path). This is the tool that makes a fix use the app's tokens instead of hard-coded literals: look up the token for a colour, spacing, radius or font before writing one. Optional filters: group (first path segment, e.g. color, space), type (color \| dimension \| fontFamily \| …), direction (a named token set instead of the active one). Returns \{ projectId, set, tokens, nameMap, total }; at most 500 tokens. Read-only. Use get_design_deviance to see where code drifts off these tokens, or get_app_recipe for the overall state. |
| `get_design_deviance` | Design deviance | Return how far the code drifts off the design system: the latest 0–100 deviance score (lower is better; null means not scored yet), its per-rule breakdown, the score trend, a scan still running if any, the top findings (file, line, literal value, rule, and the nearest token to use instead), and the active rules (off_token_color, off_token_font, off_scale_spacing, off_scale_radius, contrast_below_aa, raw_interactive_element). | `get_store_status` | Store review status | Return the latest store review of an app: listing text in the repo vs what is live on the App Store and Google Play (listing_drift, a language out of sync, store length limits), listing claims checked against the code (listing_claim_contradicts_code: for example "never leaves your phone" while the code uploads, or "open source" for a private repo), privacy labels vs data-collecting SDKs, iOS screenshots that look Android-shaped or older than recent releases, and a pre-submission checklist with a risk per item.
