## Shake → Mushi Mushi

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/shake-to-mushi

---
title: 'Shake → Mushi Mushi'
description: Replace the Shake bug-reporting SDK with Mushi Mushi and keep shake-to-report on mobile. Config mapping, identity, and a cut-over checklist.
---

# Shake → Mushi Mushi

 

Shake (shakebugs.com) is a hosted bug-reporting service built around
shake-to-report. This guide swaps it for Mushi Mushi and keeps the same
trigger on mobile.

  Shake-to-report is available in the Mushi React Native and Capacitor
  SDKs. The Mushi web SDK has no shake trigger: on the web, users open the
  widget from its launcher (a floating button on desktop, an edge tab on
  phones), or you open it from your own button.

## Why switch

- **Open-source server.** Mushi's SDKs are MIT and its server and admin
  console are AGPLv3, so you can run all of it yourself. (Shake's SDKs are
  MIT on npm; its backend is a hosted service.)
- **Self-host.** Mushi runs on your own Supabase / Postgres.
- **AI triage.** Mushi's two-stage classifier and judge loop ship in the box.
- **Pricing.** Self-hosting is free. The cloud is free for one app and 100
  diagnoses a month; paid plans are priced by number of apps (see
  [pricing](/pricing)).

## API mapping

Mushi calls are on the SDK instance: `useMushi()` in React Native, or
`const mushi = Mushi.init({...})` on the web.

| Shake | Mushi Mushi |
|-------|-------|
| `Shake.start(apiKey)` | `` (RN) / `Mushi.init({ projectId, apiKey })` (web) |
| `Shake.show()` | `mushi.open()` |
| `Shake.registerUser(id)` + `Shake.updateUserMetadata({ email, name })` | `mushi.setUser({ id, email, name })` |
| `Shake.setMetadata(key, value)` | `mushi.setMetadata(key, value)` |
| `Shake.setInvokeShakeOnShakeDeviceEvent(true)` | RN: `config.widget.trigger: 'shake'` (needs `expo-sensors`) |
| `Shake.setShowFloatingReportButton(true)` | RN: `config.widget.trigger: 'button'` (or `'both'` with shake); web: the default launcher (a floating button on desktop, an edge tab on phones) |
| `Shake.addPrivateView(viewRef)` | Web: add `data-mushi-redact` to the element, or list selectors in `privacy.redactSelectors`. RN: the reporter sees the screenshot and can remove it before sending. |

## SPA → SSR (Next.js / Nuxt / SvelteKit)

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/spa-to-ssr

---
title: 'SPA → SSR (Next.js / Nuxt / SvelteKit)'
description: Move a Vite SPA to Next.js, Nuxt or SvelteKit. Env var prefix changes, where to mount Mushi Mushi so it survives navigation, and hydration gotchas.
---

# SPA → SSR (Next.js / Nuxt / SvelteKit)

 

Move a Vite SPA (React, Vue, or Svelte) onto a server-rendered framework
(Next.js, Nuxt, or SvelteKit respectively) for SEO, faster TTFB, and
real route-level data loading.

The Mushi Mushi bits are: env-var prefix changes, where to mount the
provider so it survives navigation, and what to do about hydration
warnings. The framework-level migration mechanics are upstream:

- React SPA → **Next.js** App Router: [Next.js: migrating from Vite](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/from-vite)
- Vue SPA → **Nuxt**: [Nuxt installation](https://nuxt.com/docs/4.x/getting-started/installation)
- Svelte SPA → **SvelteKit**: [creating a SvelteKit project](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/creating-a-project)

## Env-var prefix mapping

This is the change that most often breaks the SDK after a move:

| Vite SPA | Next.js | Nuxt | SvelteKit |
|----------|---------|------|-----------|
| `VITE_MUSHI_PROJECT_ID` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_MUSHI_PROJECT_ID` | `NUXT_PUBLIC_MUSHI_PROJECT_ID` | `VITE_MUSHI_PROJECT_ID` (unchanged) |
| `VITE_MUSHI_API_KEY` | `NEXT_PUBLIC_MUSHI_API_KEY` | `NUXT_PUBLIC_MUSHI_API_KEY` | `VITE_MUSHI_API_KEY` (unchanged) |
| `import.meta.env.VITE_*` | `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_*` | `useRuntimeConfig().public.*` (declare the keys in `nuxt.config`) | `import.meta.env.VITE_*` |

SvelteKit runs on Vite, so `VITE_` variables keep working; if you prefer
SvelteKit's own `PUBLIC_` prefix, read them from `$env/static/public`
instead. Rerunning `npx mushi-mushi init` in the new project writes the
prefix the CLI uses for that framework into your `.env.local`.

## Migration checklist (generic, picks the right framework as you go)

React SPA → Next.js (App Router). Vue SPA → Nuxt. Svelte SPA → SvelteKit. Don't switch UI framework AND rendering model in the same migration — it doubles the risk.</> },

npm create nuxt@latest            # Nuxt
npx sv create                     # SvelteKit`} },
    { id: 'design-system', label: 'Port shared design tokens / global CSS first', content: <>If you use Tailwind, the config carries over almost as-is. CSS-in-JS users on emotion/styled-components need to wire up the SSR adapter for their library before any components move.</> },

## Where the Mushi Mushi widget lives across SSR vs CSR

The Mushi visual widget mounts client-side, in a Shadow DOM child of
`document.body`, after `Mushi.init()` runs. Because it doesn't render in
the server-side HTML, you'll see:

- ✅ No hydration warnings caused by the widget itself
- ✅ Crawlers don't see the widget (it's not in the initial HTML)
- ⚠️ The widget appears only after the client-side JavaScript runs, so on
  slow networks the page shows briefly without it (intentional, to keep
  server HTML lean)

## Common gotchas

- **`useMushi()` in a Server Component** (Next.js App Router): build
  error. Add `'use client'`. See the
  [Next.js Pages → App Router guide](/migrations/nextjs-pages-to-app-router#server-components-and-usemushi)
  for the recommended pattern.
- **Calling `Mushi.init()` as well as the framework adapter.** Since 1.0,
  `MushiPlugin` (Vue/Nuxt) and `initMushi()` (Svelte) initialise the SDK
  themselves; a second `Mushi.init()` only logs "Already initialized".
  Remove it.
- **Env-var prefix typos.** The SDK throws an error saying `projectId`
  and `apiKey` are required. Run `npx mushi-mushi init` to regenerate the
  env section.

- [Creating a SvelteKit project](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/creating-a-project)

## Vue 2 → Vue 3

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/vue-2-to-vue-3

---
title: 'Vue 2 → Vue 3'
description: Upgrade a Vue 2 app to Vue 3 and move from the plain Mushi Mushi web SDK to the @mushi-mushi/vue plugin, with an interactive migration checklist.
---

# Vue 2 → Vue 3

 

Vue 2 reached end-of-life on 2023-12-31. This guide covers the upgrade
and the Mushi Mushi pieces.

The Mushi Vue adapter (`@mushi-mushi/vue`) supports **Vue 3.3 and later**
(its peer dependency is `vue >=3.3`). Apps still on Vue 2 use the plain
`@mushi-mushi/web` SDK; this guide brings you onto the adapter.

  **Vue 2 is no longer receiving security patches.** The Vue team's official
  recommendation is to migrate. If you cannot, [HeroDevs ships a paid LTS](https://www.herodevs.com/support/nes-vue)
  for Vue 2.7 with security backports.

## What changes (high level)

- `new Vue({...}).$mount(...)` → `createApp(App).mount(...)`
- Options API still works in Vue 3, but the **Composition API** is the
  recommended style. You can mix both during the migration.
- Filters are gone. Methods or computed properties replace them.
- Functional components are plain functions in Vue 3; the `functional`
  option and `` are gone.
- `v-model` on a custom component changed semantics; see the
  [Vue 3 migration guide](https://v3-migration.vuejs.org/breaking-changes/v-model.html).
- Vue Router 3 → 4. Vuex 3 → 4 (or Pinia, recommended).
- Mushi: `@mushi-mushi/web` direct usage → `@mushi-mushi/vue` adapter.

## API mapping (Mushi Mushi)

| Vue 2 (with @mushi-mushi/web) | Vue 3 (with @mushi-mushi/vue + @mushi-mushi/web) |
|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `Mushi.init({ projectId, apiKey })` in main.js | `app.use(MushiPlugin, { projectId, apiKey })` only; the plugin calls `Mushi.init()` itself |
| Manually attach `Vue.config.errorHandler = ...` to forward to Mushi | The adapter chains onto Vue 3's `app.config.errorHandler` automatically |
| Use the instance from `Mushi.init()` in components | Use the `useMushi()` composable inside `` / `setup()` |

## Migration checklist

{`# Vue 3 ships a compat build that runs Vue 2 code with deprecation warnings:
npm install vue@^3
# Then in your build config, alias 'vue' to '@vue/compat'
# This lets you migrate incrementally without flag-day risk`} },
    { id: 'fix-warnings', label: 'Fix every Vue 2-style deprecation warning', content: <>Each warning links to its migration page. Common ones: filters removed, $on/$off/$once removed, functional: true removed. Work through them all before removing the compat alias.</> },
    { id: 'remove-compat', label: 'Remove @vue/compat alias once warnings are zero', content: <>Now you're on real Vue 3.</> },
    { id: 'router', label: 'Upgrade Vue Router 3 → 4', content: {`npm install vue-router@^4

// router.js
- import VueRouter from 'vue-router'
- Vue.use(VueRouter)
- export default new VueRouter({ routes })
+ import { createRouter, createWebHistory } from 'vue-router'
+ export default createRouter({ history: createWebHistory(), routes })`} },
    { id: 'state', label: 'Decide: Vuex 4 or Pinia', content: <>Vuex 4 is a Vue-3-compatible drop-in. Pinia is the new recommended state library — better TS, smaller, simpler. If you're touching state code anyway, Pinia is worth the switch.</> },
    { id: 'install-mushi-adapter', label: 'Install the Mushi Vue adapter', content: {`npm install @mushi-mushi/vue
# @mushi-mushi/web comes with it as a dependency`} },
    { id: 'wire-mushi', label: 'Replace direct Mushi.init usage with the adapter', content: {`// main.ts

The adapter chains its own app.config.errorHandler that reports to Mushi.</> },
    { id: 'verify', label: 'Smoke-test: throw an error, verify it lands as a Mushi report', content: <>Throw inside a Vue lifecycle hook. The adapter sends it to Mushi with source vue-error-handler. Confirm it appears in the admin console.</> },

/>

## Common gotchas

- **Calling `Mushi.init()` as well as `app.use(MushiPlugin, ...)`**. Since
  `@mushi-mushi/vue` 1.0 the plugin initialises the SDK itself; a second
  `Mushi.init()` only logs "Already initialized". Remove it.
- **`` and Options API mixing**. Both work in Vue 3, but
  `useMushi()` is a composable, so call it inside `setup()` /
  ``. In an Options API component, add a `setup()` option
  that returns it, or use `Mushi.getInstance()` from `@mushi-mushi/web`.
- **Stale Vue 2 plugins**. Check each Vue plugin you use (error
  reporting, logging, UI kits) for a Vue 3 version.

## Mushi Mushi during the migration

You can run **just `@mushi-mushi/web`** in compat mode and it works. The
adapter is purely additive: it gives you a nicer composable API and
auto-wires the error handler. Migrate Mushi to the adapter only after
your app is on real Vue 3 (compat alias removed).

- [Pinia (recommended state)](https://pinia.vuejs.org/)
- [`@mushi-mushi/vue` SDK reference](/sdks/vue)

## index

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins

---
description: Send Mushi Mushi events to the tools you already use as HMAC-signed Standard Webhooks, with 13 first-party plugin packages and an SDK to build your own.
---

# Plugin marketplace

Mushi Mushi sends events out as **HMAC-signed JSON webhooks** with [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) headers (`webhook-id` / `webhook-timestamp` / `webhook-signature: v1,…`) to any tool you wire up. There are **13 first-party plugin packages**, and you can build your own with `@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk` (signature checks, duplicate-delivery handling, typed events, a retry helper for your own outbound calls, and a small client for calling back into the Mushi Mushi API).

## Works with Sentry, or without it

You don't need Sentry. If you already use it, keep it: its errors land in the same list as user reports, each explained in plain English.

Bugs come in from users, monitoring tools and even your voice. Fixes and updates go out to your editor, coding agents, tracker and team chat.

## Available plugins

Six plugins are listed in the console's **Marketplace** today: PagerDuty, Linear, Sentry, Zapier, Cursor Cloud Agent and Claude Code Agent. Slack, Discord, Teams, GitHub Issues and Jira also work without a plugin, from the **Integrations** page. The other packages are for running the plugin on your own server.

| Plugin              | What it does                                                                 | In Marketplace | Doc |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | --- |
| **Cursor Cloud Agent** | Starts a Cursor agent on critical triaged reports; no server needed       | Yes | [Cursor Cloud](/plugins/cursor-cloud) |
| **PagerDuty**       | Pages on `report.classified` at or above a severity (default critical); resolves on `fix.applied` or a report marked fixed | Yes | [PagerDuty](/plugins/pagerduty) |
| **Linear**          | `report.created` opens an issue, `report.classified` updates it              | Yes | [Linear](/plugins/linear) |
| **Sentry**          | Copies triaged reports at or above a severity (default high) into Sentry; resolves on fix | Yes | [Sentry](/plugins/sentry) |
| **Zapier**          | All events                                                                   | Yes | [Zapier](/plugins/zapier) |
| **Jira Cloud**      | `report.created` opens an issue; `report.status_changed` transitions it; comments on `fix.applied` | No  | [Jira Cloud](/plugins/jira) |
| **Slack app**       | Report cards with buttons and the `/mushi` command (built in via Integrations) | No  | [Slack](/plugins/slack) |
| **Discord**         | Embeds for `report.classified`, `fix.proposed`, `fix.applied`, `report.status_changed` | No  | [Discord](/plugins/discord) |
| **Microsoft Teams** | Adaptive cards for `report.classified`, `fix.proposed`, `fix.applied`        | No  | [Teams](/plugins/msteams) |
| **GitHub Issues**   | `report.classified` opens a labelled issue; `fix.applied` closes it          | No  | [GitHub Issues](/plugins/github-issues) |
| **Bugsnag**         | Copies triaged reports into Bugsnag; marks them fixed on `fix.applied`       | No  | [Bugsnag](/plugins/bugsnag) |
| **Rollbar**         | Copies triaged reports into Rollbar items; resolves them on `fix.applied`    | No  | [Rollbar](/plugins/rollbar) |
| **Crashlytics**     | On `fix.applied`, sets a Firebase Remote Config flag (it does not create Crashlytics issues) | No  | [Crashlytics](/plugins/crashlytics) |

Browse and install from the admin console: **Marketplace**. A plugin receives only the events in its **Subscribed events** list (empty or `*` means all).

## Webhook delivery contract

Every dispatch is:

- **POST** to your configured webhook URL with `Content-Type: application/json`.
- Body: `{ event, deliveryId, occurredAt, projectId, pluginSlug, data }`.
- **Standard Webhooks headers** ([standardwebhooks.com](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/)):
  - `webhook-id: `
  - `webhook-timestamp: <unix-secs>`
  - `webhook-signature: v1,<base64-hmac-sha256>` over `${id}.${ts}.${rawBody}`
- The HMAC key is your signing secret's raw bytes. Standard Webhooks libraries base64-decode the secret by default, so pass it raw (for example `new Webhook(secret, { format: 'raw' })` in the `standardwebhooks` npm package) or use the plugin SDK, which does this for you.
- Legacy headers are sent too: `X-Mushi-Event`, `X-Mushi-Signature: t=<unix-ms>,v1=` (HMAC-SHA256 over `${t}.${rawBody}`), `X-Mushi-Project`, `X-Mushi-Plugin`, `X-Mushi-Delivery`, and `X-Mushi-Retry-Attempt` on retries.
- Your endpoint has 8 seconds to answer. Any non-2xx answer, timeout or network error is retried: up to 5 attempts in all, about 30 s, 2 min, 10 min and 1 h apart (±20%). A retry keeps the same `webhook-id` and body, with a fresh timestamp and signature. After the fifth failure the delivery is marked `error`.
- Each delivery is logged with status, HTTP code, latency and the first 512 characters of your response, on the **Marketplace → Deliveries** tab.

## Build your own

See [Building a plugin](/plugins/building) and [Webhook events](/plugins/events).

`@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk` exports `createPluginHandler` (checks the signature, drops duplicate deliveries and routes events to your handlers), `verifyStandardWebhooksSignature` and `verifySignature` if you want to check signatures yourself, and `withRetry` for retrying your own calls to other APIs.

## Bugsnag

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/bugsnag

---
title: Bugsnag
description: Copy triaged Mushi Mushi bug reports into Bugsnag and mark the error fixed when the fix merges. A self-hosted plugin with a Data API token.
---

# Bugsnag plugin

Copies each bug Mushi Mushi triages into Bugsnag as an error, and marks it
`fixed` when the fix merges.

**Not in the Mushi Cloud Marketplace yet.** The console has no Bugsnag
listing, so you can't install it from there. On a Mushi server you run
yourself, add a `plugin_registry` row for it and install it like any listed
plugin.
To bring Bugsnag errors *into* Mushi, use `@mushi-mushi/adapters` instead.

## Setup (self-hosted Mushi Mushi)

```bash
npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-bugsnag
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...      # the signing secret set when the plugin is installed
export BUGSNAG_API_KEY=...          # Bugsnag Data API token
export BUGSNAG_PROJECT_SLUG=...     # from your Bugsnag project URL
export ADMIN_BASE_URL=https://...   # optional: console URL for report links
npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-bugsnag mushi-plugin-bugsnag
```

Point the plugin's webhook URL at `https://<your-host>/mushi/webhook`.

## Package

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-bugsnag`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-bugsnag)

## Events

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `report.classified` | Create a Bugsnag error (grouping hash `mushi--`) with a link back to the report, through `POST /v2/projects//errors` on the Data Access API |
| `fix.applied` | Set the error's status to `fixed` |

The report → error mapping is kept in memory unless you pass your own cache
to `createBugsnagPlugin(cfg, cache)`, so after a restart `fix.applied` is
skipped for older reports.

We have not confirmed the create call against a live Bugsnag account, and
Bugsnag documents its SDKs as the usual way to record errors. Check your
server log after the first `report.classified` before you rely on it.

## Building a plugin

---
title: Building a plugin
description: Build your own Mushi Mushi plugin, an HTTP endpoint that receives HMAC-signed webhook events and checks them with @mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk in a few lines.
---

# Building a plugin

A Mushi Mushi plugin is an HTTPS endpoint that receives HMAC-signed webhook events and does something useful with them. `@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk` gives you a handler that checks the signature, drops duplicate deliveries and routes each event to your code, plus typed event shapes.

```bash
npm install @mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk hono
```

`hono` (or `express`) is an optional peer dependency; install the one your
server uses.

## Minimal receiver

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { createPluginHandler } from '@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk'
import { honoHandler } from '@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk/hono'

const handler = createPluginHandler({
  secret: process.env.MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET!,
  on: {
    'report.classified': async (e) => {
      await handleTriaged(e.data)
    },
    'fix.applied': async (e) => {
      await handleFixApplied(e.data)
    },
  },
})

const app = new Hono()
app.post('/mushi/webhook', honoHandler(handler))

export default app
```

`honoHandler` comes from the `/hono` subpath, and `expressMiddleware` from
`@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk/express`. For any other framework, call
`handler({ rawBody, headers })` yourself and send back the `status` and `body`
it returns. Events with no handler (and no `'*'` handler) are answered `200`
and ignored.

  Answer within 8 seconds. Mushi Mushi treats a slower answer as a timeout and retries it, even though the SDK handler's own time limit is 25 seconds. Any non-2xx answer is retried too: up to 5 attempts in all, about 30 s, 2 min, 10 min and 1 h apart. Queue long work instead of awaiting it inline. Retries reuse the same `deliveryId`, so the handler's duplicate check skips work that already succeeded (the default store is in memory; pass a `dedupStore` to share it across instances).

## Typed event shapes

```ts
import type {
  MushiEventEnvelope,
  MushiEventName,
  MushiReportCreatedEvent,
  MushiReportClassifiedEvent,
  MushiReportStatusChangedEvent,
  MushiFixEvent,
  MushiJudgeScoreEvent,
} from '@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk'
```

`parseEvent(raw)` and `isKnownEvent(name)` are there for runtime checks.

Some SDK types promise fields the server doesn't send: fix events other than
`fix.requested` have no `fix.status`, `report.status_changed` has `actor`
rather than `actorUserId`, and the `judge` fields differ. See
[Webhook events](/plugins/events) for the payloads as sent.

## Signature verification

`createPluginHandler` checks the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) headers when they are present: `webhook-signature: v1,` is HMAC-SHA256 over `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${rawBody}`, with the timestamp in seconds. Otherwise it checks the legacy `X-Mushi-Signature: t=<unix-ms>,v1=` header, HMAC-SHA256 over `${t}.${rawBody}`. Both reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes off.

To check by hand, use `verifyStandardWebhooksSignature({ rawBody, webhookId, webhookTimestamp, webhookSignature, secret })` or `verifySignature({ rawBody, header, secret })`. Always pass the exact raw body you received, not re-serialized JSON.

## Publishing to the marketplace

1. Open a PR with a migration in `packages/server/supabase/migrations/` that inserts a `plugin_registry` row. Required columns: `slug`, `name`, `short_description`, `publisher`, and `manifest` (a JSON object with `subscribes`, the default event list, and `config`). Optional: `long_description`, `homepage_url`, `source_url`, `required_scopes`, `category`.
2. Add a doc page at `apps/docs/content/plugins/.mdx`.
3. Once the migration is applied to the database, the listing appears under **Marketplace** for every project.

## Local testing

The SDK ships a `mushi-plugin` command that posts a signed sample event to
your local server:

```bash
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=dev-secret
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_URL=http://localhost:3000/mushi/webhook   # default: http://localhost:3000/webhook
npx mushi-plugin simulate report.classified
```

To test against Mushi Mushi itself, expose your endpoint over HTTPS (for example `ngrok http 3000`), install the plugin with that URL, then press **Test** on it under **Marketplace → Installed**. The test sends a `test.delivery` event with `data: { test: true }`, and the result shows on the **Deliveries** tab.

## Crashlytics

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/crashlytics

---
title: Crashlytics
description: Flag fixed Mushi Mushi reports in Firebase Remote Config so your mobile app can hide stale crash notices. A self-hosted plugin with a Google access token.
---

# Crashlytics plugin

When a Mushi Mushi fix merges, writes a `mushi_resolved_` flag to your
Firebase Remote Config, which your mobile app can read to stop showing a
stale crash notice. It does not create Crashlytics issues.

**Not in the Mushi Cloud Marketplace yet.** The console has no Crashlytics
listing, so you can't install it from there. On a Mushi server you run
yourself, add a `plugin_registry` row for it and install it like any listed
plugin. To bring Crashlytics crashes *into* Mushi, use `@mushi-mushi/adapters`.

## Setup (self-hosted Mushi Mushi)

```bash
npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-crashlytics
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...   # the signing secret set when the plugin is installed
export GCP_ACCESS_TOKEN=...      # OAuth2 access token, firebase + cloud-platform scopes
export FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=...
export FIREBASE_APP_ID=...       # e.g. 1:123456789012:android:abcdef
npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-crashlytics mushi-plugin-crashlytics
```

The plugin takes a ready access token and does not refresh it (tokens last
about an hour). Point the plugin's webhook URL at
`https://<your-host>/mushi/webhook`.

## Package

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-crashlytics`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-crashlytics)

## Events

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `fix.applied` | Set Remote Config `mushi_resolved_` to `"true"` (dashes in the report id become underscores); close the Crashlytics issue only if the event carries `crashlyticsIssueId` (Mushi does not send it today) |

## Cursor Cloud Agent

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/cursor-cloud

---
title: Cursor Cloud Agent
description: Start a Cursor Cloud Agent automatically when a Mushi Mushi report qualifies. It investigates, drafts a fix and opens a draft PR that names the report.
---

# Cursor Cloud Agent plugin

Starts a [Cursor Cloud Agent](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent) run when a qualifying Mushi Mushi event fires. The agent investigates the issue in your repo and, when PR creation is on (the default), opens a **draft** PR titled `fix: … (MUSHI-)`. It is told never to merge; you review and merge.

The **Cursor Cloud Agent** plugin is a first-party plugin (slug: `cursor-cloud-agent`). For the events below, Mushi Mushi calls the Cursor API directly and does not post to the webhook URL in the install form.

You do not need the npm package
[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-cursor-cloud`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-cursor-cloud)
for any of this. Mushi calls Cursor itself; the package is only for running
the same dispatch from your own server.

## Prerequisites

- A [Cursor](https://cursor.com) account with an API key (cursor.com/dashboard/integrations → API Keys).
- GitHub connected on the console's **Integrations** page, so Mushi Mushi knows your repo URL. Without it, no agent starts.
- Your Cursor account connected to GitHub with access to that repo. Cursor clones the repo and opens the PR through its own GitHub connection.

## Setup

1. On the **Integrations** page, open the **Cursor Cloud** card and paste
   your Cursor API key (`crsr_…`). Optionally set a default model (default
   `composer-2.5`) and whether Cursor opens PRs (default on). **Test
   connection** checks the key.
2. That is enough to send a report to Cursor by hand:
   `mushi fix  --agent cursor_cloud`, MCP `dispatch_fix` with
   `agent=cursor_cloud`, or a retry on the **Fixes** page with **Cursor Cloud
   agent** picked.
3. To start agents automatically, go to **Marketplace → Cursor Cloud Agent →
   Install**. The form asks for a webhook URL and signing secret like every
   listing, but for the events below Mushi Mushi calls Cursor directly with
   the key from step 1 and does not post to that URL (only the **Test**
   button and any other event you subscribe it to are posted there). Keep the subscribed events
   (`report.classified`, `qa_story.failed`, `fix.requested`) or narrow them.

Automatic runs on `report.classified` start only for **critical** reports;
the install form has no setting to change that.

## Behaviour

| Event | When the agent runs | What it does |
|-------|---------------------|--------------|
| `report.classified` | Right after triage, for critical reports only | Starts an agent with the report id; it opens a draft PR when PR creation is on |
| `fix.requested` | When the fix worker has already handed a report to Cursor (`mushi fix --agent cursor_cloud`, MCP `dispatch_fix`, a Fixes-page retry) | Nothing: the event names the agent that is already running, so the plugin never starts a second one |
| `qa_story.failed` | Every time a QA story run fails or errors | Starts an agent with a generic investigate-and-fix prompt. The prompt carries no story details. Every QA failure in a project reuses the same agent id, which Cursor rejects as a duplicate, so later failures don't start a new agent |
| `skill_pipeline.step.dispatched` | When a skill pipeline run in `cloud` mode reaches a step | Runs the step's context packet as the agent prompt, stores the agent id on the step, and asks the agent to report back with the `checkin_pipeline_step` MCP tool |

For `skill_pipeline.step.dispatched`, the agent starts even when the marketplace plugin is not installed. The key comes from the **Cursor Cloud** card on the Integrations page, and the repo from your GitHub connection. Without a key or a repo URL the step is marked failed.

## Fixes view integration

Agents started by `mushi fix --agent cursor_cloud`, MCP `dispatch_fix` or a Fixes-page retry with Cursor picked are fix attempts, so the [Fixes page](/admin/fixes) shows them:

- A **Cursor badge** with the agent id, linking to the run in Cursor.
- An **artifact gallery** with any screenshots, logs or files the agent produced.
- The **PR link** once the agent opens a PR.

Agents the Marketplace plugin starts on its own (`report.classified`,
`qa_story.failed`) are not recorded as fix attempts. You find them on the
**Marketplace → Deliveries** tab (the response column shows `agentId=…`) and
in your Cursor dashboard.

## Common tasks

### Which reports start an agent

On `report.classified`, the plugin starts an agent only for critical
reports. To stop automatic runs for triaged reports entirely, remove
`report.classified` from the plugin's subscribed events.

### Triggering manually

You can also dispatch a Cursor Cloud Agent run outside of the Marketplace plugin:

```bash
# CLI
mushi fix <reportId> --agent cursor_cloud --wait

# MCP tool
dispatch_fix reportId=<reportId> agent=cursor_cloud
```

See [`mushi fix`](/sdks/cli) and [`@mushi-mushi/mcp`](/sdks/mcp) for details.

### Reviewing what the agent did

For a fix attempt: open **Fixes**, find the `cursor_cloud` row and expand it. The artifact gallery shows any files the agent produced, and the Cursor badge opens the run in Cursor.

## Troubleshooting

- **Plugin installed but nothing on the Deliveries tab**: no key on the Cursor Cloud card, no GitHub repo URL, or no report triaged as critical yet. In each of these cases the plugin stops before it logs a delivery.
- **Deliveries show an error**: the HTTP code is Cursor's answer. A `401` means the API key is wrong or expired.
- **Agent runs but no PR**: check that PR creation is on in the **Cursor Cloud** card on the Integrations page, and that your Cursor account can reach the repo on GitHub. An agent that changes nothing opens no PR.
- **A fix attempt stays open**: Mushi Mushi checks Cursor runs every 5 minutes and marks an attempt failed when it is still open after 24 hours. Check the run's status in Cursor.
- **Self-hosted Node orchestrator can't read the key from Vault**: set `MUSHI_CURSOR_API_KEY_OVERRIDE` in the orchestrator's environment. Mushi Cloud reads the key from Vault and does not need this.

## Related pages

- [Admin → Integrations → Cursor Cloud](/admin/integrations): the Cursor API key and default model
- [Admin → Fixes](/admin/fixes): Cursor fix attempts, badges and artifact galleries
- [Concepts → Fix orchestrator](/concepts/fix-orchestrator): how agents are chosen and dispatched
- [Concepts → Connecting your orchestrator](/concepts/orchestrator-interop): MCP, CLI, REST and A2A dispatch

## Discord

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/discord

---
title: Discord
description: Post Mushi Mushi report and fix events to a Discord channel. Paste a channel webhook on the Integrations page, or run the self-hosted Discord plugin.
---

# Discord plugin

Posts a message to a Discord channel when Mushi Mushi triages a bug or a fix
lands.

## Setup (Mushi Cloud, no code)

1. In Discord: **Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook**, then copy its URL.
2. In the Mushi console: open the **Integrations** page and paste the URL on the Discord card.

Mushi posts to the channel itself; you do not need the npm package.

## Self-hosted plugin

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-discord`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-discord)
does the same from your own server. The console's Marketplace has no Discord
listing, so you can't install it from the console. On a Mushi server you run
yourself, add a `plugin_registry` row for it and install it like any listed
plugin.

```bash
npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-discord
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...
export DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=https://discord.com/...
export ADMIN_BASE_URL=https://...   # optional: console URL for report links
npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-discord mushi-plugin-discord
```

| Event | Embed |
| --- | --- |
| `report.classified` | Coloured by severity (critical red, high orange, medium yellow, low green) |
| `fix.proposed` | Blue, with the PR link when there is one |
| `fix.applied` | Green, with the PR link |
| `report.status_changed` | Grey, "moved from X to Y" |

The fix embeds also have a "Fix status" field: proposed, applied or failed,
taken from the event.

## Webhook events

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/events

---
title: Webhook events
description: Reference for the webhook events Mushi Mushi plugins receive. The shared envelope, each event's payload, and how to subscribe to only the events you need.
---

# Webhook events

Mushi Mushi sends every plugin event in this envelope (the SDK type is
`MushiEventEnvelope` from `@mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk`):

```ts
interface MushiEventEnvelope<T = unknown> {
  event: string        // e.g. 'report.classified'
  deliveryId: string   // UUID per delivery; use it to drop duplicates
  occurredAt: string   // ISO 8601
  projectId: string
  pluginSlug: string
  data: T
}
```

## Events Mushi Mushi sends today

The `data` column lists what the server puts in the payload today. Treat
every field as optional and ignore fields you don't know: new ones can be
added in a minor release.

| Event | When | `data` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `report.created` | A report is saved | `{ report: { id, status, category, title }, source }`. A regression filed by the status reconciler sends `{ source: 'status-reconciler', regressedActionNodeId, actionLabel }` with no `report` |
| `report.classified` | Triage finishes | `{ report: { id, status, category, severity, title }, classification: { category, severity, confidence, tags } }` |
| `report.status_changed` | A report's status changes (console, API, Slack, fix merge) | `{ report: { id, status }, previousStatus, newStatus, actor }`. `newStatus` equals `report.status` |
| `report.reporter_replied` | The person who filed the report answered in its thread | `{ report: { id }, comment: { id, body, author_kind } }`. `body` is untrusted text from your app's users |
| `fix.requested` | The fix worker has handed a report to a cloud agent (Cursor Cloud or GitHub's cloud agent) | `{ report, fix: { id, status, agent, externalAgentId, externalRunId, statusUrl, branch, pullRequestUrl }, … }`. The agent is already running; don't start another one |
| `fix.proposed` | A fix PR is open | `{ report: { id }, fix: { id, agent, branch, prUrl, pullRequestUrl, commitSha?, summary? } }` |
| `fix.applied` | A fix PR merged | `{ report: { id }, fix: { id, agent, branch, prUrl, pullRequestUrl, prNumber?, commitSha, repository? } }` |
| `fix.failed` | A fix attempt ended without a PR | `{ report: { id }, fix: { id, agent, error, failureCategory? } }` |
| `qa_story.failed` | A QA story run failed or errored (every such run) | `{ story_id, story_name, run_id, status, summary, consecutive_failures }` |
| `qa_story.recovered` | A story that was failing passed again | Same shape as `qa_story.failed` |
| `judge.score_recorded` | The judge graded a report's triage | `{ report: { id }, judge: { model, fallback, score, accuracy, severity, component, repro, classificationAgreed } }` |
| `skill_pipeline.step.dispatched` | A skill pipeline run in `cloud` mode reaches a step | `{ runId, stepIndex, skillSlug, contextPacket, projectId }` |
| `linear.issue.updated` | Linear tells Mushi Mushi an issue was created or changed | `{ linearIssueIdentifier, action, stateType, issueData, … }` |
| `test.delivery` | You press **Test** on an installed plugin | `{ test: true }` |

Whenever a fix event has a PR link, it is sent as both `fix.prUrl` and
`fix.pullRequestUrl` (the name the SDK's `MushiFixEvent` type uses). Every fix
event carries `fix.status`: the status the sender set, or else the one in the
event name (`proposed`, `applied`, `failed`).

## Named in the SDK, not sent to plugins

| Event | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `report.commented`, `report.dedup_grouped`, `sla.breached`, `qa_story.passed` | In the SDK's event list, but nothing in Mushi Mushi sends them yet. A failing story that passes again sends `qa_story.recovered` |
| `reward.points_awarded`, `reward.tier_changed`, `reward.payout_requested`, `reward.payout_paid` | Sent through the project's Rewards webhook, not to plugins. A plugin subscribed to them receives nothing |

## Subscribing to a subset

The install form has a **Subscribed events** field (comma-separated); the API
field is `subscribedEvents`. Mushi Mushi only sends the events listed there.
An empty list or `*` means every event.

For Slack, Discord and Teams plugins, the console's notification settings
also apply: turning off a notification type, or setting a minimum severity
for triaged reports, stops those deliveries too. Other plugins are not
affected by those settings.

## Cursor Cloud Agent events

The **Cursor Cloud Agent** plugin (`cursor-cloud-agent`) handles
`report.classified`, `fix.requested`, `qa_story.failed` and
`skill_pipeline.step.dispatched` by calling the Cursor API directly instead
of posting a webhook. The install form still asks for a webhook URL, but
Mushi Mushi never posts these events to it.

For `skill_pipeline.step.dispatched`, Mushi Mushi starts the Cursor agent
**even when the plugin is not installed**, using the key from **Integrations
→ Cursor Cloud**. Any other plugin subscribed to the same event still gets
its webhook.

See [Cursor Cloud Agent](/plugins/cursor-cloud) for what each event does, and
[Admin → Marketplace](/admin/marketplace) for installing plugins.

## GitHub Issues

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/github-issues

---
title: GitHub Issues
description: Open a GitHub issue for every triaged Mushi Mushi report and close it when the fix lands. Set it up on the Integrations page, or self-host the plugin.
---

# GitHub Issues plugin

Opens a GitHub issue for each bug Mushi Mushi triages, and closes it when the fix
lands.

## Setup (Mushi Cloud, no code)

1. Create a fine-grained token with **Issues: Read and write** on the repo
   that should get the issues (it can be a separate public tracker repo).
2. In the Mushi console: open the **Integrations** page, find **GitHub
   Issues**, and enter the owner, repo and token. **Test connection** checks it.

Mushi opens the issues and closes them itself; you do not need the npm package.

## Self-hosted plugin

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-github-issues`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-github-issues)
does the same from your own server. The console's Marketplace has no GitHub
Issues listing, so you can't install it from the console. On a Mushi server
you run yourself, add a `plugin_registry` row for it and install it like any
listed plugin.

```bash
npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-github-issues
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...
export GITHUB_TOKEN=...     # Issues: write, Metadata: read
export GITHUB_OWNER=acme
export GITHUB_REPO=widget-app
npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-github-issues mushi-plugin-github-issues
```

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `report.classified` | Open an issue labelled `mushi-bug` (the label is created if missing) |
| `fix.applied` | Close the issue |

The report → issue mapping is kept in memory unless you pass your own cache
to `createGithubIssuesPlugin(cfg, cache)`, so after a restart `fix.applied`
can't close issues opened before it.

## Jira Cloud

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/jira

---
title: Jira Cloud
description: Open Jira Cloud issues from Mushi Mushi bug reports and keep their status in step. Set it up on the Integrations page, or self-host the Jira plugin.
---

# Jira Cloud plugin

Opens a Jira issue for each Mushi Mushi bug report and keeps it in step as the
report moves to fixed.

## Setup (Mushi Cloud, no code)

1. At **id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens**, create an API token.
2. In the Mushi console: open the **Integrations** page, find **Jira**, and
   enter your Jira base URL (e.g. `https://acme.atlassian.net`), the
   Atlassian email that owns the token, the token, and the project key
   (e.g. `BUG`).
3. Click **Save**, then **Test connection**.

Mushi opens and resolves the Jira issues itself; you do not need the npm package.

## Self-hosted plugin

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-jira`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-jira)
is a library for doing the same from your own server with Jira OAuth 2.0
(3LO): `buildAuthorizeUrl`, `exchangeCode`, `refreshTokens` and
`createJiraPluginHandler`. See its README for the code. The console's
Marketplace has no Jira listing, so you can't install it from the console. On
a Mushi server you run yourself, add a `plugin_registry` row for it and
install it like any listed plugin.

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `report.created` | Create a Jira issue under `jiraProjectKey`, labelled with category and severity (`unknown` here, since triage hasn't run yet) |
| `report.status_changed` | Run the Jira transition from `statusToTransition` (defaults: pending/classified/grouped → To Do, fixing → In Progress, fixed/dismissed → Done) |
| `fix.applied` | Comment `Mushi fix applied: `. `fix.applied` carries no summary, so none is added |

The report → issue mapping is kept in memory, so after a restart status
changes and fix comments for older reports are skipped.

## Linear

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/linear

---
title: Linear
description: File Linear issues from Mushi Mushi bug reports. Connect Linear on the Integrations page, or run the self-hosted Linear plugin with an API key and team id.
---

# Linear plugin

Opens a Linear issue for each new Mushi Mushi report and updates it once the
report is triaged.

**Most people don't need the plugin.** Connect Linear on the console's
**Integrations** page (OAuth or a pasted API key) and Mushi files Linear
issues and closes them for you. The plugin below is for running the Linear
calls from your own server.

## Setup (self-run plugin)

1. Create a Linear API key: **Settings → Security & access → Personal API keys** → **New key**.
2. Start the server where Mushi can reach it over public HTTPS:

   ```bash
   npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-linear
   export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...      # must match the signing secret in step 3
   export LINEAR_API_KEY=lin_api_...
   export LINEAR_TEAM_ID=...           # the Linear team to file issues under
   npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-linear mushi-plugin-linear
   ```

3. In the console: **Marketplace → Linear Sync → Install**. Set the webhook
   URL to `https://<your-host>/mushi/webhook`. Keep the signing secret Mushi
   generates (or paste your own) and use the same value for
   `MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET`.

## Behaviour

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `report.created` | Creates a Linear issue (title, plus the event JSON in the description) |
| `report.classified` | Updates that issue's title and description |
| `report.status_changed` | Moves the issue to the state in `stateMap[newStatus]`, if you passed a `stateMap` (programmatic use only) |

The report → issue mapping is kept in memory unless you pass your own cache
to `createLinearPlugin(cfg, cache)`, so a restart can lead to a second issue
for the same report.

## Troubleshooting

- **Issues not created**: check the plugin's last delivery status on the
  **Marketplace** page. A `401` from your server means the signing secret
  differs from `MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET`; a Linear error in your server log
  usually means the API key or `LINEAR_TEAM_ID` is wrong.
- **Duplicate issues**: see the in-memory mapping above, and check you have
  not connected Linear both on the Integrations page and through this plugin.

## Microsoft Teams

# Microsoft Teams plugin

Posts a card to a Teams channel when Mushi Mushi triages a bug or a fix lands.

## Setup (Mushi Cloud, no code)

1. In Teams: create a Workflows webhook for your channel (the **Post to a channel when a webhook request is received** template) and copy its URL. Microsoft has retired the old Office 365 **Incoming Webhook** connector, so use Workflows.
2. In the Mushi console: open the **Integrations** page and paste the URL on the Teams card.

Mushi posts to the channel itself; you do not need the npm package.

## Self-hosted plugin

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-msteams`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-msteams)
does the same from your own server with Adaptive Card 1.4 cards. The
console's Marketplace has no Teams listing, so you can't install it from the
console. On a Mushi server you run yourself, add a `plugin_registry` row for
it and install it like any listed plugin.

```bash
npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-msteams
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...
export TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL=https://...
export ADMIN_BASE_URL=https://...   # optional: console URL for report links
npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-msteams mushi-plugin-msteams
```

| Event | Card |
| --- | --- |
| `report.classified` | Coloured by severity |
| `fix.proposed` | With a PR button when there is a PR link |
| `fix.applied` | Green confirmation, with a PR button |

The fix cards also list a "Fix status" fact: proposed, applied or failed, taken
from the event.

## PagerDuty

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/pagerduty

---
title: PagerDuty
description: Page your on-call rotation via PagerDuty when Mushi Mushi triages a bug as critical, and resolve it when the fix lands. Setup with an Events API v2 routing key.
---

# PagerDuty plugin

Pages whoever is on call when Mushi Mushi triages a bug as critical, and resolves
the page when the fix lands.

**Most people don't need the plugin.** Add PagerDuty on the console's
**Integrations** page (paste the Events API v2 routing key) and Mushi pages
and resolves for you. The plugin below is for sending the PagerDuty calls
from your own server.

## Setup (self-run plugin)

1. In PagerDuty, go to **Services → your service → Integrations** and add the **Events API v2** integration.
2. Copy the 32-character **Integration Key** (the routing key).
3. Start the server where Mushi can reach it over public HTTPS:

   ```bash
   npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-pagerduty
   export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...       # must match the signing secret in step 4
   export PAGERDUTY_ROUTING_KEY=...
   export SEVERITY_THRESHOLD=critical   # optional: low | medium | high | critical
   npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-pagerduty mushi-plugin-pagerduty
   ```

4. In the console: **Marketplace → PagerDuty Escalation → Install**. Set the
   webhook URL to `https://<your-host>/mushi/webhook`, and use the form's
   signing secret (Mushi generates one) as `MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET`. The listing subscribes to `report.classified` and
   `sla.breached`; add `fix.applied` and `report.status_changed` so pages
   resolve on their own.

## Behaviour

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `report.classified` with severity ≥ `SEVERITY_THRESHOLD` | Sends a PagerDuty `trigger` |
| `sla.breached` | Sends a `trigger` (Mushi does not emit this event yet) |
| `fix.applied` | Sends a `resolve` with the same `dedup_key` |
| `report.status_changed` to `fixed` or `resolved` | Sends a `resolve` with the same `dedup_key` |

PagerDuty event fields:

| PagerDuty field | Mushi source |
| --- | --- |
| `dedup_key` | `mushi::`, so a re-sent event updates the same incident |
| `summary` | report `title` (or `Mushi: `) |
| `source` | `mushi-mushi` |
| `severity` | `critical → critical`, `high → error`, `medium → warning`, `low → info` |
| `custom_details` | the full Mushi event envelope |

## Troubleshooting

- **No page fired**: check the plugin's deliveries on the **Marketplace**
  page. A `401` from your server means the signing secret differs from
  `MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET`. Check the severity threshold too.
- **Duplicate incidents**: make sure PagerDuty is not set up both on the
  Integrations page and through this plugin.
- **Incident not auto-resolving**: add `fix.applied` and
  `report.status_changed` to the plugin's subscribed events.

## Rollbar

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/rollbar

---
title: Rollbar
description: Copy triaged Mushi Mushi bug reports into Rollbar items and try to resolve them when fixes ship. A self-hosted plugin with an access token and project id.
---

# Rollbar plugin

Copies each bug Mushi Mushi triages into Rollbar as an item, and tries to
resolve the item when the fix merges.

**Not in the Mushi Cloud Marketplace yet.** The console has no Rollbar
listing, so you can't install it from there. On a Mushi server you run
yourself, add a `plugin_registry` row for it and install it like any listed
plugin.
To bring Rollbar errors *into* Mushi, use `@mushi-mushi/adapters` instead.

## Setup (self-hosted Mushi Mushi)

```bash
npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-rollbar
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...      # the signing secret set when the plugin is installed
export ROLLBAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=...     # project access token with post_server_item (or write) scope
export ROLLBAR_PROJECT_ID=...       # required by the server
export ADMIN_BASE_URL=https://...   # optional: console URL for report links
npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-rollbar mushi-plugin-rollbar
```

Point the plugin's webhook URL at `https://<your-host>/mushi/webhook`.

## Package

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-rollbar`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-rollbar)

## Events

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `report.classified` | Create a Rollbar item (environment `production`, level from severity, fingerprint `mushi--`) |
| `fix.applied` | Resolve the item (`PATCH /api/1/item/`, `status: resolved`) |

To resolve, the plugin needs the item id from Rollbar's answer to the create
call and keeps it in memory (pass your own cache to
`createRollbarPlugin(cfg, cache)` to survive restarts). Rollbar documents
that answer as returning an occurrence `uuid`; if it carries no `id`, nothing
is stored and `fix.applied` does nothing. We have not confirmed this against
a live Rollbar account.

## Sentry

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/sentry

---
title: Sentry
description: Two-way Sentry integration. Sentry errors land in the Mushi Mushi queue, merging a fix resolves the issue, and an optional plugin copies triaged reports back.
---

# Sentry plugin

Two-way Sentry integration: Sentry errors flow **into** the Mushi Mushi queue,
and fixes flow **back**. Merging a fix resolves the linked Sentry issue, and
resolving in Sentry resolves the linked report. The outbound plugin below
also copies triaged Mushi reports into Sentry.

## Route Sentry errors into Mushi Mushi (inbound)

No plugin needed. This is built into the hosted API:

1. In Sentry: **Settings → Developer Settings → Custom Integrations → Create
   New Integration → Internal Integration**. Set its webhook URL to the
   **Receive URL** shown on the Mushi Sentry card
   (`/v1/webhooks/sentry?projectId=<your-project-id>`), subscribe to the
   **issue** resource, enable **Alert Rule Action**, and give it **Issue &
   Event: Read & Write**.
2. In the Mushi console, open **Integrations → Sentry** and paste the integration's
   **Client Secret** as the **Webhook secret**, plus your org slug, project
   slug and auth token. Sentry signs every delivery with that secret
   (`Sentry-Hook-Signature`, HMAC-SHA256 of the body); Mushi also requires a
   fresh `Sentry-Hook-Timestamp` and drops a `Request-ID` or body it already
   accepted.
3. To route alerts too: **Alerts → Create Alert Rule** (issue alert) → action
   **Send a notification via** your internal integration.
4. Fire a test alert. The error lands in **Reports** with a `via Sentry` badge,
   a plain-English diagnosis, and a dispatchable fix.

Issues that already exist never fire again. Pull them in with **Import** on
the Sentry card, the `import_sentry_issues` MCP tool, or
`POST /v1/admin/projects//sentry/import` with
`{ "issueIds": ["WEB-12"] }` (ids or short ids, at most 10) or
`{ "query": "is:unresolved", "limit": 5 }`.

For a whole backlog, add `"sinceDays": 30` and `"limit": 10`, then send the
`nextCursor` from each answer back as `"cursor"` until it comes back `null`.
Running it again is safe: issues already imported answer `linked`. If one app
reports to two Sentry projects (say a frontend and a backend), list the second
in `sentry_extra_project_slugs` and pick it with `"sentryProject"`.

In the console, all of this is on the Sentry card:

- **More Sentry projects** (edit the card) takes up to 10 extra project slugs,
  comma-separated. It saves `sentry_extra_project_slugs`; clearing the field
  removes them. Over the API, send a string array to
  `PUT /v1/admin/integrations/platform/sentry`
  (`{ "sentry_extra_project_slugs": ["sbc-be"] }`; `[]` or `null` clears it).
- **Import existing Sentry issues** has a Sentry project picker (shown when
  more than one project is configured) and a **Seen in** choice (any time, or
  the last 7, 14, 30 or 90 days). A windowed search imports 10 at a time;
  **Load next page** repeats the same search from where the last page ended
  until Sentry has no more.

Behavior:

- **Deduped per Sentry issue**: repeat alerts land on the same report;
  re-importing a linked issue returns the existing report.
- **Regressions reopen**: an alert for an already-fixed report flips it to
  `reopened` and bumps the regression counter instead of filing a duplicate.
- **Resolves both ways**: when a Mushi fix PR merges, Mushi resolves the
  linked Sentry issue through the Sentry API (`resolvedInNextRelease`, else
  `resolved`) and comments the PR link; the fix commit also carries
  `Fixes <SHORT-ID>` for Sentry's GitHub integration. A failed resolve shows
  on the fix timeline. `action: resolved` from Sentry resolves the linked
  Mushi report.
- **Fix context**: the files named in an imported issue's stack are indexed
  right away, and codebase sweeps index stack-frame files of open
  Sentry-linked reports first.
- Your Sentry **alert rules are the noise filter**: only alerts you route at
  the webhook are ingested. Sentry User Feedback submissions are also ingested
  on the same endpoint.

## Copy Mushi Mushi reports into Sentry (outbound plugin)

Everything above is built in. The plugin is only for the other direction:
copying the bugs your users report through Mushi into Sentry, so they sit
next to your Sentry errors. You run it on your own server.

1. Start the plugin where Mushi can reach it over public HTTPS:

   ```bash
   npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-sentry
   export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...   # must match the signing secret in step 2
   export SENTRY_DSN=...
   export SEVERITY_THRESHOLD=high   # optional: low | medium | high | critical
   # Optional: resolve the matching Sentry issue on fix.applied
   export SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN=...     # event:admin + project:read
   export SENTRY_ORG_SLUG=acme
   export SENTRY_PROJECT_SLUG=web
   npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-sentry mushi-plugin-sentry
   ```

2. In the console: **Marketplace → Sentry Mirror → Install**. Set the
   webhook URL to `https://<your-host>/mushi/webhook`, and use the form's
   signing secret (Mushi generates one) as `MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET`.

## Package

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-sentry`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-sentry)

## Events

| Event | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `report.classified` (severity ≥ threshold, default `high`) | Capture a Sentry event fingerprinted `['mushi', projectId, reportId]`. The plugin can attach the report as Sentry User Feedback instead when the event carries `report.sentry_event_id` and an auth token is set, but Mushi Mushi does not put `sentry_event_id` in the event today |
| `fix.proposed` | Capture an `info` event, only with `MARK_IN_PROGRESS=true` |
| `fix.applied` | Capture an `info` event tagged `mushi.fixed=true`; with an auth token, resolve the matching Sentry issue. The PR link is attached as the `mushi.pr_url` tag |

## Slack app

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/slack

---
title: Slack app
description: Triage Mushi Mushi bug reports from Slack. Add the app from the Integrations page, and each report posts as a card with buttons to fix, resolve or dismiss.
---

# Slack app plugin

Triage a bug from the channel it lands in. Mushi Mushi posts each classified report
as a Block Kit card carrying the plain-English title, root cause, and evidence
counts. The card's buttons let you dispatch a fix, resolve, or dismiss
without opening the console.

**Why it exists:** the fastest triage is the one that doesn't need a second
tab.

**Who it's for:** teams whose bugs already get discussed in Slack.

## Setup

On Mushi Cloud there is nothing to install or host:

1. In the Mushi console, open the **Integrations** page and click **Add to
   Slack** on the Slack card. Approve the install in Slack.
2. Pick the channel for report notifications.
3. Invite the Mushi bot to that channel.

Running the Mushi backend yourself? Create the Slack app from the manifest
in [`@mushi-mushi/plugin-slack-app`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-slack-app),
point its Interactivity Request URL at `<functions-url>/slack-interactions`,
and set `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`, `SLACK_CLIENT_ID` and `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET`
on the server. The package README lists every URL and scope.

## What's on the card

| Element | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| Header | Severity, category, project, plus `(N×)` when the bug is a repeat |
| Title | The plain-language headline ("Checkout button does nothing"), with the technical summary beneath it |
| 🔍 line | Likely root cause from Stage 2 |
| Context row | Area · component · confidence · reporter · environment · page · release |
| Evidence row | Console errors, failed requests, repro-step count, screenshot, SDK version |
| Footer | Report id and session id |

Rows only render when there's something to show, so a thin report stays a
small card.

## Acting from the channel

| Button | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Triage →** | Opens the report in the console, scoped to the right project |
| **Dispatch fix** | Runs the fix agent and opens a draft PR. Swaps to *Install GitHub App* / *Enable Autofix* when the prerequisites are missing |
| **Resolve ✓** | Marks the report resolved and notifies the reporter |
| **Dismiss** | Marks it dismissed (noise, duplicate, won't fix), behind a confirm dialog |
| **Reply to reporter** | Opens a box for a message the person who reported the bug sees word for word in "Your reports" in your app. Only shown when the report came from your app's widget |

Resolve and Dismiss run the same transition contract as the console (plugin
event, linked-issue resolution, and reporter notification), so acting from
Slack and acting from the web app can't drift apart.

After an action the card rewrites itself in place: the button row is replaced
with an outcome line naming who acted and when, and a threaded reply records
it in channel history.

  **Assign is deliberately absent.** Reports have no assignee column, so an
  "Assign" button would be a UI with nothing behind it.

## Slash commands

Once Slack is added, `/mushi` answers (self-hosted backends point **Slash
Commands → `/mushi`** at `<functions-url>/api/v1/webhooks/slack/commands`):

| Command | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `/mushi list` | The latest 10 open reports, linked to the console |
| `/mushi open ` | One report's summary and console link |
| `/mushi resolve ` | Marks it resolved, the same as the card's **Resolve ✓** |
| `/mushi reply  ` | Answers the person who reported it. Same path as **Reply to reporter**: they see your message word for word in your app, and get an email or push only if they opted in |
| `/mushi voice ` | Voice intake by text; see [Voice intake](/integrations/voice-intake) |

`` is the full report id or its first 6+ characters. Replies are capped at
2,000 characters and only reach reports filed from your app's widget.

The reporter sees a reply from "Developer". Every reply sent from Slack, by
`/mushi reply` or the card's button, also writes a `report.reporter_replied`
entry to the console's audit log naming the Slack user (and, for the command,
the channel) it came from.

## Package

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-slack-app`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-slack-app)

You don't need the package on Mushi Cloud. It holds the pieces for hosting
the Slack side yourself: the slash command router (`list`, `open `,
`resolve `, `help`), `verifySlackRequest`, the OAuth helpers
(`buildInstallUrl`, `exchangeCode`), the app manifest, and
`createSlackPlugin`, which posts `report.classified`, `fix.proposed`,
`fix.applied` and `report.status_changed` to a Slack incoming webhook.

## What gets posted

| Moment | Action |
| --- | --- |
| A report is triaged | Post the Block Kit card to the channel |
| A fix PR opens | Thread with the PR link |
| A QA story fails or recovers | Transition-aware threaded updates |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| Buttons do nothing | Interactivity Request URL not set, or the signing secret doesn't match |
| Cards post but Triage 404s | `ADMIN_BASE_URL` unset on the server, so the deep link can't be built |
| No cards at all | No bot token for the project, and no `slack_webhook_url` fallback configured |

## Zapier

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/zapier

---
title: Zapier
description: Send every Mushi Mushi event to Zapier and on to thousands of apps such as Notion, Google Sheets and HubSpot. Catch Hook setup and event filters.
---

# Zapier plugin

Send every Mushi Mushi event to Zapier and on to the thousands of apps Zapier connects to, such as Slack, Notion, Google Sheets, HubSpot and Jira.

## Setup (no server)

1. In Zapier, create a **Zap** with the **Webhooks by Zapier → Catch Hook** trigger.
2. Copy the webhook URL (e.g. `https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/…`).
3. In Mushi: **Marketplace → Zapier Bridge → Install**.
4. Paste the Catch Hook URL as the webhook URL and keep the signing secret Mushi generates.
5. Optionally narrow the subscribed events (e.g. only `report.classified`, `fix.applied`).

Zapier then receives Mushi's envelope as is: `{ event, deliveryId,
occurredAt, projectId, pluginSlug, data }`, with the report under
`data.report` for report and fix events (see [Webhook events](/plugins/events)
for each payload). The listing subscribes to every event (`*`), including the
`test.delivery` sent by the **Test** button. Zapier does not check the
signature, so anyone who learns the Catch Hook URL can post to it.

## Setup (with the relay package)

[`@mushi-mushi/plugin-zapier`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mushi-mushi/plugin-zapier)
runs between Mushi and Zapier. It checks Mushi's signature and forwards a
flat payload (`event`, `report_id`, `report_status`, `report_severity`,
`report_title`, …, plus the full envelope under `raw`).

```bash
npm i @mushi-mushi/plugin-zapier
export MUSHI_PLUGIN_SECRET=...   # the same signing secret as in the install form
export ZAPIER_HOOK_URL=https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/.../...
export ALLOW_EVENTS=report.classified,fix.applied   # optional: only these
export DENY_EVENTS=test.delivery                     # optional: never these
npx -p @mushi-mushi/plugin-zapier mushi-plugin-zapier
```

Set the Zapier Bridge webhook URL to `https://<your-host>/mushi/webhook`
instead of the Catch Hook URL.

Checking the signature inside a Code by Zapier step is not practical: the
signature covers the exact raw request body, which Zapier does not pass to
the step.

## Common Zaps

| Trigger | Action | Use case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `report.classified` (critical) | Post to a Slack channel | Immediate team alert |
| `report.classified` | Create row in Google Sheets | Bug tracking in a spreadsheet |
| `fix.applied` | Create Notion database entry | Changelog / release notes |
| `report.created` | Create HubSpot ticket | Link product bugs to customer accounts |

## Troubleshooting

- **Zap not firing**: check the plugin's deliveries on the **Marketplace** page in Mushi Mushi.
- **Events arriving out of order**: Mushi Mushi sends each event as it happens and retries failed ones later, so a retried event can arrive after a newer one. Use `occurredAt` to order them, or build one Zap per event type.
- **Payload too large**: Zapier documents a 10 MB limit for webhook payloads (2 MB for a raw hook). Mushi Mushi events are normally far smaller (a `skill_pipeline.step.dispatched` context packet, for example, is capped at 40,000 characters).

## Cursor integration

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/integrations/cursor

---
title: Cursor integration
description: Wire Mushi Mushi into Cursor with one command. Get fix context, lessons and fix dispatch right from the editor.
---

# Cursor integration

**The short setup:**

```bash
npx mushi-mushi setup --ide cursor
# Restart Cursor. It asks you to sign in the first time the agent calls Mushi.
```

## Step-by-step

### Wire Cursor

```bash
npx mushi-mushi setup --ide cursor
```

This writes `.cursor/mcp.json` with a `mushi` entry that points at the hosted
Mushi Mushi MCP URL. No key is written to the file: Cursor opens a browser
sign-in the first time the agent calls Mushi. If the CLI has no saved login
yet, the command signs you in through your browser first. If the file already
exists, the command merges the block without overwriting other entries.

Self-hosted, or a machine with no browser? Log in with a key, then write a
local entry instead:

```bash
npx mushi-mushi login \
  --api-key mushi_xxx \
  --endpoint https://<ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/api \
  --project-id xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
npx mushi-mushi setup --ide cursor --stdio
```

Make that key in the console on **Manage apps → Generate API key** with the
**MCP read-only** preset, or **MCP read + write** if the agent should dispatch
fixes. (**Settings → AI keys** is for your own LLM keys, not Mushi keys.)

### (Optional) Add the evolution-loop coding rules

```bash
npx mushi-mushi setup --ide cursor --with-rules
```

Writes `.cursorrules` with rules telling the agent to:
1. Call `get_fix_context` before writing a fix
2. Check the lesson library for patterns
3. Call `submit_fix_result` after pushing a branch

Download the template to inspect it first:
[cursor.cursorrules](/integrations/cursor.cursorrules)

### Restart Cursor

Reload the window (`Ctrl+Shift+P` → "Developer: Reload Window") or quit
and reopen. The Mushi tools appear in the MCP tools picker.

### Verify

In Cursor chat, ask: **"Use the Mushi MCP to list my recent reports"**.
You should see your most recent bug reports from the dashboard.

## Available tools in Cursor

| Tool | What Cursor can do |
|------|--------------------|
| `get_recent_reports` | "What are users hitting right now?" |
| `get_fix_context` | "Give me a fix brief for report abc-123" |
| `search_reports` | "Find all reports about the login button" |
| `get_blast_radius` | "What else does this component touch?" |
| `dispatch_fix` | "Dispatch the agentic fix for this report" |
| `triage_next_steps` | "What should I fix next?" |
| `run_nl_query` | "How many critical bugs landed this week?" |

## Keep lessons current

```bash
# Pull the latest project lessons into .mushi/lessons.json
npx mushi-mushi sync-lessons
```

Run this in CI after each deploy so Cursor agents always have the most
up-to-date anti-patterns from your project's fix history.

## Connecting GitHub for auto-PR

For Cursor to open draft PRs via `dispatch_fix`, install the Mushi GitHub
App on your repo. In the admin console, open **Integrations** and click
**Install GitHub App**. Turn on **Automatic fixes** on the same page:
`dispatch_fix` is refused while it is off.

## Troubleshooting

**Cursor shows no Mushi tools:** Reload the window and check that
`.cursor/mcp.json` exists. Run `npx mushi-mushi whoami` to verify credentials.

**`[INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE]` error:** Your key needs the `mcp:write` scope to
dispatch fixes. Make one with the **MCP read + write** preset on **Manage apps**
(the hosted sign-in uses your role in the project instead).

**Stale lessons:** Run `npx mushi-mushi sync-lessons` to pull the latest rules.

  See the [MCP quickstart](/quickstart/mcp) for a full tool catalog and
  the [security docs](/security/no-leakage-claim) for what data stays
  in your account.

## Voice intake

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/integrations/voice-intake

---
title: Voice intake
description: Say a bug on your phone and Mushi Mushi files it, or opens a draft PR after you confirm. Works from an iOS Shortcut, Telegram, Slack or the console.
---

# Voice intake

Dictate a bug or a small change request on your phone. Mushi Mushi transcribes it and files a report. For a change request, and only after you confirm the verbatim transcript, it also dispatches the fix and replies with the draft PR link in the same chat.

```
phone voice ──▶ transcript ──▶ sanitise + PII scrub ──▶ refuse privileged verbs
            ──▶ intent (create_report | open_draft_pr | unknown)
            ──▶ report (source = voice)
            ──▶ [open_draft_pr only] verbatim transcript + confirm token ──▶ you confirm
            ──▶ fix dispatched ──▶ draft PR ──▶ reply in Slack / Telegram / push
```

Four inboxes feed the same pipeline. Pick the one that matches your phone.

| Inbox | Best for | Audio leaves the phone? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS Shortcut (Siri dictation) | iPhone, lowest friction | No. iOS transcribes on device; only text is sent |
| Telegram bot | Android (and anything with Telegram) | Yes. The voice note is transcribed server-side, then deleted |
| Slack | Teams already triaging in Slack | Yes. The clip is transcribed server-side, then deleted |
| Installed console (PWA) | Tap-to-talk in the console, or Android share sheet | Yes. Uploaded to a private bucket, transcribed, then deleted |

## Enable it

Voice intake is **off by default** because speech is personal data.

### Turn it on

Console → **Settings** → **Voice reports** tab: turn on **Accept voice reports**, pick the languages you speak, and set **Keep recordings for**. `0` days (the default) deletes every recording the moment its transcript is stored.

### Mint a `voice:write` key

On the same tab, click **Make a voice key**. It opens **Manage apps** with the **Voice intake** preset (`voice:write` scope only) selected; generate the key there. This is the key that lives on your phone. It can call the voice routes and nothing else: not reports, not MCP, not admin.

### Make sure Automatic fixes is on

Draft PRs need **Automatic fixes** turned on (console → **Integrations**) and a connected GitHub repo. Filing reports works without them.

  Transcription and intent classification run on the project's OpenAI / Anthropic keys (BYOK or the hosted wallet). Speech-to-text costs about **$0.0045 per audio minute** (`gpt-transcribe`); the intent call is a few hundred tokens on a small model.

## iOS Shortcut

Two Shortcuts: one to speak, one to confirm.

  
    1. **Dictate Text** — language: your choice, *Stop listening: After pause*.
    2. **Get Contents of URL**
       - URL: `https://.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/intake/voice`
       - Method: `POST` · Request body: **JSON**
       - Headers: `X-Mushi-Api-Key: mushi_…` (the `voice:write` key), `Idempotency-Key: ` (Shortcuts: *Get UUID* action)
       - Body: `source` = `ios_shortcut`, `transcript` = *Dictated Text*
    3. **Get Dictionary Value** — key `session.message`
    4. **Show Result** — Siri reads the message aloud. (*Speak Text* is unreliable inside Siri-invoked runs; *Show Result* is what gets spoken.)

    For a change request the message reads back the verbatim transcript and ends with *"Reply confirm to proceed"*. Save `session.id` and `session.confirm_token` from the same response (two more *Get Dictionary Value* actions into a note or a variable) for the second Shortcut.
  
  
    1. **Get Contents of URL**
       - URL: `https://.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/intake/voice//confirm`
       - Method: `POST` · Body: JSON with `token` = the saved `confirm_token`
       - Header: `X-Mushi-Api-Key: mushi_…`
    2. **Show Result** — `session.message` says *"Draft PR requested"*; the PR link arrives as a push notification, or on the console's **Voice reports** page, once the agent opens it.

    A single Shortcut with an *If Dictated Text contains "確認"* branch works too.
  

The raw request, for reference:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://<ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/intake/voice" \
  -H "X-Mushi-Api-Key: mushi_xxx" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 4d2a…" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"source":"ios_shortcut","transcript":"the login button does nothing on Safari"}'
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "session": {
    "id": "…",
    "status": "created",
    "transcript": "the login button does nothing on Safari",
    "action": "create_report",
    "summary": "Login button unresponsive on Safari",
    "report_id": "…",
    "message": "Filed report: Login button unresponsive on Safari\n\nFrom: \"the login button does nothing on Safari\""
  }
}
```

A change request comes back as `status: "awaiting_confirm"` with a `confirm_token`; `POST /v1/intake/voice/:id/confirm` with `{ "token": "…" }` dispatches, `…/cancel` discards. Tokens are single-use and expire after 10 minutes.

## Telegram (the Android inbox)

### Create a bot

Message [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) → `/newbot` → copy the token.

### Connect it

Console → **Settings** → **Voice reports** tab → **Telegram** → paste the bot token and save. It is stored in Vault, never in plain text. Then click **Connect webhook**.

### Bind your chat

On the same row, click **Make link code** (valid 10 minutes, single use). Open your bot in Telegram and send `/start `. The bot greets you with the project name.

### Talk

Hold the microphone, describe the bug or the change, release. The bot replies with the transcript. Change requests get **Confirm** / **Cancel** buttons; tap Confirm and the draft PR link is posted back into the same chat when the agent opens it.

Plain text messages work the same way. Voice notes are capped at 120 seconds and 20 MB.

## Slack

Two ways in, both need the Mushi Slack app installed with `files:read`, `commands` and `chat:write`:

- **Slash command**: `/mushi voice fix the footer alignment on checkout`. The reply is ephemeral and the confirmation uses the same buttons as fix dispatch.
- **Audio clip**: record a Slack audio clip (or share an audio file) in a channel the app is in. Mushi downloads the clip with the bot token, transcribes it, and replies in a thread. Slack's own transcript is ignored.

## Installed console (PWA)

Install the console to your Home Screen (Chrome on Android: *Install app*; Safari on iOS: *Add to Home Screen*). The **Voice reports** page has a tap-to-talk button (max 120 s) and, on Android, the console appears in the share sheet for audio files; Google Recorder's `.m4a` works. The recording is uploaded through a short-lived signed URL into the private `voice-intake` bucket and deleted after transcription. Confirmation is a button on the page; the PR link arrives as a web push notification when you granted permission.

## What voice intake refuses

Voice text is untrusted **and** lossy: "delete" and "deploy" sound alike, 削除 and 消去 do too. A transcript that mentions any of these is refused outright, before any model sees it, and the verbatim transcript is echoed back so you can see what was heard:

| English | Japanese |
| --- | --- |
| merge, deploy, delete, drop, force push, production / prod, rollback, revert, secret, token, rotate | マージ, デプロイ, 削除, 消去, 本番, 強制, ロールバック, リバート, シークレット, トークン |

Everything else that gets through is still constrained:

- Agents open **draft PRs on a new branch only**. Merging stays a human action in the console.
- The intent is extracted into a strict schema (`create_report`, `open_draft_pr`, `unknown`); the transcript is passed as delimited untrusted data and is never free-texted into an agent prompt.
- Invisible Unicode (zero-width characters, tag characters, bidi controls) and HTML comments are stripped before classification.
- A change request needs an explicit confirmation of the **verbatim transcript**: a single-use HMAC token bound to the session, transcript hash, action and expiry.
- Reporter (end-user) tokens cannot use the voice routes at all.

## Privacy and retention

- Audio is deleted from the bucket as soon as the transcript is stored unless you set a retention window (0–365 days). The daily retention sweep enforces the window.
- Transcripts pass through the PII scrubber (emails, phone numbers, IPs, secret-shaped tokens) **before** they are written to the report.
- The report keeps the sanitised transcript, the detected language and the sha256 of the audio bytes as an audit trail; it never keeps the audio itself unless retention is on.
- Speech-to-text is a vendor hop to OpenAI on the project's key. Mention it in your privacy policy if your users can reach a voice inbox.
- Per-project caps: 30 voice requests per minute, 120 audio minutes per day, plus the normal ingest burst limit.

## API reference

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/v1/intake/voice` | `voice:write` key or admin JWT | Body: exactly one of `transcript`, `audio_path`, `audio_base64` (+ `mime`, ≤ 8 MB decoded). Optional `source`, `external_id`, `languages`, `duration_sec`. Honours `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/intake/voice/upload-url` | same | `{ mime }` → signed upload URL + `path` for the bucket. `400 UNSUPPORTED_STORAGE_PROVIDER` on BYO S3/R2/GCS projects; send `audio_base64` instead. |
| `POST` | `/v1/intake/voice/:id/confirm` | same | `{ token }` → dispatches the fix. `403 INVALID_CONFIRM_TOKEN`, `410 EXPIRED`, `409 CONFLICT` once used. |
| `POST` | `/v1/intake/voice/:id/cancel` | same | `{ token }` → cancels a pending request. |
| `GET` | `/v1/intake/voice/sessions?limit=20` | admin JWT or `mcp:read` | Recent sessions with status, action, report and PR link. |
| `GET` | `/v1/intake/voice/:id` | same | One session. |

`403 VOICE_INTAKE_DISABLED` means the project has not enabled the feature. See the [error catalog](/concepts/error-catalog) for the rest.
