# Mushi Mushi Cloud

## Plans

## Sign-up flow

1. `kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/admin`: email and password, or a GitHub account when that sign-in is offered.
2. Email confirmation (for email sign-up) → sign in → `/onboarding` wizard.
3. Create your first project, mint an API key, run `npx mushi-mushi` to install the SDK.
4. The Billing page in the console shows diagnoses used / limit per app, with an **Upgrade** button
   (**Change plan** once you pay).
5. Stripe Checkout → on success, your subscription becomes active. Overage on monthly plans bills through Stripe meter events.

## Why metered on diagnoses

## Spend controls

Every monthly paid plan has a **hard cap on overage spend** ($50 Builder, $200 Studio by default), set in the console under Billing → Spending Cap. When the cap is reached, Mushi pauses new diagnoses for the rest of the calendar month with an upgrade prompt. Annual plans have no overage and stop at the included diagnoses. You also receive email alerts at 50%, 80% and 100% of your included diagnoses.

## Self-hosting

If you'd rather run Mushi on your own Supabase project, see
[Self-hosting](/self-hosting). The Cloud code is in the public repo: the
server is AGPLv3, and the enterprise features in `packages/server/ee`
(SSO, audit export, retention policies) are source-available and need a
license in production. Cloud also carries its own tuning data (prompt
wording, evaluation sets) as configuration; the repo ships working default
prompts. Self-hosting is free forever; you supply your own LLM keys.

## Self-hosting

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/self-hosting

---
title: Self-hosting
description: Run the whole Mushi Mushi stack yourself with Docker Compose. Your own keys, AGPLv3 server, MIT SDKs, no usage limits.

# Self-hosting

Mushi Mushi is **OSS-first**. Mushi Cloud at `kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/admin` runs the same code as this repo — there is no closed-source plus-tier. Every edge function, migration, and admin SPA you see here is what powers Mushi Cloud. The one difference is data: the hosted service keeps its own tuning (prompt wording, evaluation sets and scoring weights tuned on live traffic) as configuration. The repo ships working default prompts, so your stack has every feature. See [Open source & licensing](/concepts/open-source#what-the-hosted-service-keeps).

  **Prerequisite:** Node ≥ 22, a [Supabase](https://supabase.com) project, and the [Supabase CLI](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development/cli/getting-started).

## What you'll deploy

| Layer | Technology | License |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Database + Auth | Supabase (Postgres 15 + pgvector + pgcrypto + pg_cron) | Open |
| Edge Functions | 50+ Supabase Edge functions (Deno) — run `pnpm docs-stats` for live count | AGPLv3 |
| Admin SPA | React + Vite, deployed to any static host | AGPLv3 |
| Observability | Langfuse + Sentry | MIT / Commercial |
| Sandbox *(optional)* | E2B, Modal or Cloudflare, through `@mushi-mushi/agents` | External |

## Fastest path — Docker Compose

The whole stack (Postgres + Auth + REST + Storage + edge functions + console)
in one command, no managed Supabase project required:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi.git
cd mushi-mushi/deploy
cp .env.example .env   # set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY + Supabase creds
docker compose up -d
```

See [Self-host in minutes](/self-hosting/docker-compose) for the full walkthrough.

## Managed-Supabase path

Prefer a hosted Supabase project? Link it and push the schema:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi.git
cd mushi-mushi
pnpm install                                       # installs all workspaces
cd packages/server                                 # Supabase CLI works relative to this dir
npx supabase link --project-ref <your-ref>
npx supabase db push                               # applies all migrations
```

Then follow the guides in order:

1. [Supabase setup](/self-hosting/supabase) — extensions, RLS, and required seed data
2. [Edge Functions deploy](/self-hosting/edge-functions) — all edge functions + secrets
3. [Admin SPA deploy](/self-hosting/admin-spa) — build and deploy the console
4. [Observability (Langfuse + Sentry)](/self-hosting/observability) — traces and error tracking

## Admin SPA deploy

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/self-hosting/admin-spa

---
title: Admin SPA deploy
description: Build and deploy the Mushi Mushi admin console yourself. A static Vite and React app that talks to your Supabase project, and the env vars it needs.
---

# Admin SPA deploy

The admin console is a Vite + React SPA that talks directly to your Supabase project and the `api` edge function. It has no server runtime — any static host works.

## Build

From the repo root:

```bash
VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://YOUR-REF.supabase.co \
VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=eyJ… \
VITE_API_URL=https://YOUR-REF.supabase.co/functions/v1/api \
pnpm --filter "@mushi-mushi/admin..." build
```

The trailing `...` also builds the workspace packages the console imports (`@mushi-mushi/web`, `@mushi-mushi/mcp` and others) first; a fresh clone has none of their `dist/` folders yet. The output lands in `apps/admin/dist/`.

  `VITE_API_URL` must point to the `api` edge function (`…/functions/v1/api`), **not** your database URL. All console API calls are proxied through that function.

## Deploy options

| Host | Command / workflow |
| --- | --- |
| **Cloudflare Pages** | `wrangler pages deploy apps/admin/dist --project-name mushi-admin` |
| **Vercel** | `vercel apps/admin/dist` |
| **S3 + CloudFront** | See `.github/workflows/deploy-admin.yml` in the repo |
| **Netlify** | `netlify deploy --dir apps/admin/dist --prod` |

## SPA routing

All hosts need to serve `index.html` for every path under the console root. The repo's reference S3 + CloudFront deploy does this with CloudFront functions (`scripts/cloudfront-mushi-spa-router.js` and `cloudfront-mushi-spa-response.js`) in front of a private bucket. For Cloudflare Pages and Netlify, a `_redirects` file or `netlify.toml` with `/* /index.html 200` is sufficient.

## First-run setup

After deploy, open the console and complete the **Onboarding** wizard (`/onboarding`). It will:
1. Generate your first API key.
2. Connect your GitHub OAuth app.
3. Show the SDK snippet for your first project.

If `/onboarding` returns a blank screen, confirm `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are baked into the build — these cannot be injected after build time.

## Self-host in minutes (Docker Compose)

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/self-hosting/docker-compose

---
title: Self-host in minutes (Docker Compose)
description: Self-host the whole Mushi Mushi stack with one Docker Compose file. Postgres, auth, storage, edge functions, the admin console and a Caddy reverse proxy.
---

# Self-host in minutes

The fastest way to run the whole Mushi stack on your own box. One Compose file
brings up Postgres, Auth, REST, Storage, the edge functions, the admin console,
and a Caddy reverse proxy — no managed Supabase project required.

  **Prerequisite:** Docker + Docker Compose, and an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or BYOK
  key) for the classification pipeline. Everything else has a sane default.

## One command

### Clone and configure

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi.git
cd mushi-mushi/deploy
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env` and set at minimum:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...          # the diagnosis engine — no second key needed elsewhere
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key       # generated from your JWT_SECRET
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your-service-role-key
JWT_SECRET=super-secret-jwt-token-with-at-least-32-characters-long
```

### Bring the stack up

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

### Open the console

| Service | URL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admin console | `http://localhost:3000` | React + Vite SPA, served by nginx |
| Edge functions (`api`) | `http://localhost:8000` | Hono on Deno |
| PostgREST | `http://localhost:3001` | the REST surface the SPA talks to |
| Auth (GoTrue) | `http://localhost:9999` | email auto-confirm in local mode |

## What's running

```
deploy/docker-compose.yml
├── postgres          supabase/postgres (migrations auto-applied from initdb)
├── supabase-auth     GoTrue
├── supabase-rest     PostgREST
├── supabase-storage  Storage API (file backend)
├── edge-functions    classify-report, api, fix-worker, … (Dockerfile.edge)
├── admin             admin console SPA (Dockerfile.admin → nginx)
└── caddy             reverse proxy / TLS (Caddyfile)
```

The Postgres container mounts `packages/server/supabase/migrations` into
`/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d`, so a fresh volume applies the full schema on
first boot. To re-apply after a schema change, recreate the volume
(`docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d`) or run `supabase db push`
against the container.

## Production notes

- **TLS / domain** — set `DOMAIN` in `.env` and Caddy will provision a
  certificate automatically.
- **Internal functions** — `classify-report`, `fix-worker`, `judge-batch`, and
  friends authenticate via `requireServiceRoleAuth`. Only the public `api`
  function should face the internet — never expose the others with
  `--no-verify-jwt`.
- **Kubernetes** — for a single-pod cluster deploy, use the Helm chart at
  [`deploy/helm/`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/tree/master/deploy/helm).

## Managed Supabase instead

Prefer to point the console at a hosted Supabase project rather than running
Postgres locally? Skip Compose and follow the
[step-by-step guides](/self-hosting) — [Supabase setup](/self-hosting/supabase),
[Edge Functions deploy](/self-hosting/edge-functions), and
[Admin SPA deploy](/self-hosting/admin-spa).

  Same code, either way. Mushi Cloud runs this exact stack — there is no
  closed-source plus-tier. The hosted service adds only its own tuning data
  (prompts and scoring weights kept as configuration); the repo's default
  prompts give you every feature. See [Open source & licensing](/concepts/open-source).

# Edge Functions deploy

Mushi ships Supabase Edge Functions under `packages/server/supabase/functions/` (run `pnpm docs-stats` for the live count). For a working self-host you only need the **minimal ingest + classification** set below; deploy every function directory except `_shared` (or mirror [`.github/workflows/deploy-edge-functions.yml`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/.github/workflows/deploy-edge-functions.yml)) for a complete instance. Include **`healthz`** for unauthenticated monitoring probes. The repo root guide [`SELF_HOSTED.md`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/SELF_HOSTED.md) remains the authoritative step-by-step.

## Minimal required (ingest + classify)

```bash
cd packages/server

npx supabase functions deploy api --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy fast-filter --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy classify-report --no-verify-jwt
```

Also deploy **`mcp`** if you use the hosted MCP transport, and **`healthz`** for unauthenticated monitoring:

```bash
npx supabase functions deploy mcp --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy healthz --no-verify-jwt
```

  Run every deploy command from `packages/server/` — the Supabase CLI looks for `supabase/functions/` relative to the current directory. Running from the repo root will fail with "entrypoint path does not exist".

## Checking what is deployed

`api` answers `GET /health` and `GET /v1/health` without a key, with the
commit it was built from:

```bash
curl -s "$SUPABASE_URL/functions/v1/api/v1/health"
# {"status":"ok","version":"<commit sha>","deployed_at":"...","region":"us","hosting_region":"ap-northeast-1"}
```

`version` is the sha stamped at deploy time, so it answers "did my deploy
land?" without reading logs — compare it with `git rev-parse HEAD`.
`hosting_region` is where the function actually runs, which matters when the
database lives elsewhere. The standalone `healthz` function reports the same
sha for uptime monitors that should not depend on the API router.

## Common optional functions

```bash
npx supabase functions deploy fix-worker --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy judge-batch --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy intelligence-report --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy generate-synthetic --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy qa-story-runner --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy pdca-runner --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy inventory-crawler --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy inventory-propose --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy inventory-gates --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy drift-walker --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy contract-graph-builder --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy a2a-push-notify --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy test-gen-from-report --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy telegram-webhook --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy cursor-webhook --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy agent-status-poll --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy agent-pr-review --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy recipe-collector --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy radar-scan --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy operator-digest --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy store-review-intake --no-verify-jwt
```

For closed-loop evolution workers (`mistake-clusterer`, `mistake-summarizer`, `release-builder`, `experiment-analyzer`, `anomaly-detector`, …) and cron setup, follow [`SELF_HOSTED.md`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/SELF_HOSTED.md).

## Function inventory (core pipeline)

| Function | Trigger | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api` | HTTP (Hono gateway) | All admin console + SDK API calls — routes under `/v1/` |
| `fast-filter` | Invoked by `api` | Stage-1 cheap triage before full classification |
| `classify-report` | `reports` INSERT | LLM triage: severity, category, blast-radius |
| `mcp` | HTTP | Hosted MCP transport for Cursor / Claude |
| `fix-worker` | Fix dispatch (`POST /v1/admin/fixes/dispatch`, autofix) | Drafts a fix and opens a draft PR, or dispatches a Cursor / GitHub cloud agent |
| `judge-batch` | cron (nightly) | Grades recent classifications; writes `classification_evaluations` and `reports.judge_score` |
| `intelligence-report` | cron / manual | Weekly LLM narrative from KPI trends |
| `drift-walker` | HTTP | Rebuilds the contract snapshot and compares it with the stored `contract_snapshots` baseline |
| `contract-graph-builder` | HTTP | Builds a contract snapshot from the OpenAPI spec, inventory API dependencies and the latest Supabase schema snapshot |
| `pdca-runner` | `pdca_runs` INSERT | Runs one PDCA iteration: fix → judge → promote cycle |
| `qa-story-runner` | cron (every minute) | Runs QA Coverage stories on schedule via Firecrawl / Browserbase |
| `generate-synthetic` | cron | Playwright-based synthetic smoke tests |
| `inventory-crawler` | cron / manual | Crawls app routes to populate `inventory_nodes` |
| `inventory-propose` | manual | Proposes user-story inventory from crawl data |
| `inventory-gates` | manual | Runs gate checks (dead handlers, mock leaks) |
| `a2a-push-notify` | manual / agents | Sends A2A protocol notifications to connected agents |
| `test-gen-from-report` | manual | Generates a Playwright test from a report, opens draft PR |
| `telegram-webhook` | Telegram Bot API | Voice-note inbox: secret-token auth, `/start ` project binding, transcript + inline-keyboard confirmation |
| `cursor-webhook` | Cursor Cloud Agent (v0 callback) | Receives `statusChange` callbacks, writes `fix_attempts.pr_url`, notifies |
| `agent-status-poll` | cron (`5-55/5`) | Polls open Cursor / GitHub cloud-agent runs and closes them (PR URL, failure) |
| `agent-pr-review` | cron (`3-53/10`) + re-run route | Reviews each fix PR with Claude Opus 5.5 on the project's Anthropic key; a merge verdict readies the draft (with no review possible, a fix-worker draft falls back to its own self-check), and a "hold" blocks merging from Mushi without an override |
| `review-followup` | cron (`6-56/10`) | Sends "fix first" findings back to a cloud agent on the same PR (off by default) |
| `fix-verifier` | cron (`4-54/10`) + verify route | Checks the merge gates for a PR's head; merges only when verified auto-merge is on |
| `merge-queue` | cron (`1-56/5`) + queue route | "Merge when ready" and release trains |

The remaining workers (billing, retention, SDK upgrade, skill-sync, rewards payout, …) live alongside these. Full list: `ls packages/server/supabase/functions/` or `pnpm docs-stats`.

## Required secrets

Set secrets before deploying — functions read them at cold-start:

```bash
cd packages/server

npx supabase secrets set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-…
npx supabase secrets set OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-…
npx supabase secrets set LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-…
npx supabase secrets set LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-…
npx supabase secrets set LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com
npx supabase secrets set SENTRY_DSN_SERVER=https://…@sentry.io/…
npx supabase secrets set GITHUB_APP_ID=…
npx supabase secrets set GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat path/to/key.pem)"
npx supabase secrets set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=…
npx supabase secrets set ADMIN_BASE_URL=https://your-domain.example.com/admin
```

Tenants can override `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` per project via [BYOK](/security/byok). `E2B_API_KEY` is read by the Node fix orchestrator in `@mushi-mushi/agents`, not by the edge functions; set it where that runs if you use the E2B sandbox.

## JWT verification

Functions set `verify_jwt = false` in `packages/server/supabase/config.toml`. Auth is enforced **inside** each handler via one of two patterns:

- **Service-role guard** (`requireServiceRoleAuth`) — cron-triggered functions (`intelligence-report`, `pdca-runner`, `judge-batch`, etc.) verify `MUSHI_INTERNAL_CALLER_SECRET` or the Supabase service-role key in the `Authorization` header, so only the scheduler and other server functions can call them.
- **User / API-key guard** — user-facing functions (`api`, `mcp`, `classify-report`, etc.) authenticate via API key or JWT inside the handler.

This two-layer approach lets functions be deployed with `--no-verify-jwt` while keeping security equivalent to the platform default. See `packages/server/supabase/config.toml` for the per-function settings.

## Langfuse + Sentry

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/self-hosting/observability

---
title: Langfuse + Sentry
description: Wire Langfuse LLM tracing and Sentry error tracking into a self-hosted Mushi Mushi server. The Edge Function secrets and what each trace records.
---

# Observability

Mushi Mushi integrates Langfuse (LLM traces) and Sentry (error tracking). Both are optional and configured as Edge Function secrets.

## Langfuse (LLM tracing)

When the Langfuse keys are set, LLM calls are traced to Langfuse with the model, token counts, latency and metadata such as the project and report IDs (string metadata is PII-scrubbed first). Every call is also recorded in the `llm_invocations` table, Langfuse or not.

```bash
cd packages/server
npx supabase secrets set LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-…
npx supabase secrets set LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-…
npx supabase secrets set LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com
```

`LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` is the canonical name (matches root `.env.example`). Docker Compose and older snippets may use `LANGFUSE_HOST` — edge code accepts both.

Replace `LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` with your self-hosted Langfuse URL if needed.

  Which key paid for a call is recorded in `llm_invocations.key_source` (`byok` or `env`), not in Langfuse. See [BYOK](/security/byok).

### What gets traced

| Trace | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Report classification | `fast-filter`, `classify-report` |
| Fix generation | `fix-worker` |
| Classification grading | `judge-batch` |
| Intelligence report | `intelligence-report` |
| PDCA iteration | `pdca-runner` |

### Viewing traces

In Langfuse: **Traces**, then filter by the project ID in the trace metadata. The **Health** page in the Mushi admin console lists recent LLM calls from `llm_invocations`, each with its Langfuse trace ID.

## Sentry (error tracking)

Every Edge Function wraps its handler with `withSentry()` from `_shared/sentry.ts`. Unhandled exceptions are forwarded to Sentry automatically.

```bash
cd packages/server
npx supabase secrets set SENTRY_DSN_SERVER=https://…@sentry.io/…   # SENTRY_DSN also works
npx supabase secrets set SUPABASE_ENV=production                     # Sentry environment
npx supabase secrets set SENTRY_RELEASE=$GIT_SHA
```

### Admin SPA Sentry

The Vite SPA also ships a Sentry integration. Pass the DSN at build time:

```bash
VITE_SENTRY_DSN=https://…@sentry.io/… pnpm --filter "@mushi-mushi/admin..." build
```

## OpenTelemetry

When `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set, `classify-report` exports an OTLP span for each classification, as a child of the ingest request's `traceparent` when there is one. Point it at your collector (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` adds auth headers):

```bash
npx supabase secrets set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://your-collector/v1/traces
```

Spans carry `report.id` and `project.id` attributes so you can join them back to Mushi data.

## Health dashboard

After deploying, open **Mushi health** (`/health`) in the admin console. It shows
the AI calls behind diagnoses and fixes (count, error rate, fallback rate,
latency and cost) and the background jobs' last runs. Integration probes
(Anthropic, OpenAI, Langfuse, Sentry, GitHub) are on the **Integrations** page.

## Supabase setup

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/self-hosting/supabase

---
title: Supabase setup
description: Set up a Supabase project for self-hosted Mushi Mushi. Link the CLI, push every migration, and check the Postgres extensions the server needs.
---

# Supabase setup

```bash
cd packages/server
npx supabase login
npx supabase link --project-ref <your-ref>
npx supabase db push          # applies every migration in supabase/migrations/
```

  Run these commands from `packages/server/` — the Supabase CLI looks for `supabase/` relative to the current directory.

## Required extensions

Enable these extensions in your Supabase project (**Database → Extensions**):

| Extension | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `vector` | Embeddings for dedup + semantic search (commonly called pgvector) |
| `pg_cron` | Scheduled MV refreshes, nightly judge runs, retention cron |
| `pgcrypto` | UUIDs and HMAC |
| `pg_net` | Async HTTP from cron jobs and triggers (plugin dispatcher, edge-function crons) |
| `citext` | Case-insensitive text columns |
| `supabase_vault` | BYOK + plugin-secret storage (on by default in Supabase projects) |
| `age` *(optional)* | Apache AGE graph backend for the knowledge graph |

The migrations run `create extension if not exists` for `vector`, `pgcrypto`, `pg_cron`, `pg_net`, `citext` and `age`. Vault is part of every Supabase project. Report columns are not encrypted with `pgsodium`.

## Required custom functions

The migration sequence creates the following custom Postgres functions:

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `mushi_rls_coverage_snapshot()` | Lists every public table and whether RLS is enabled on it |
| `mushi_apply_retention()` | Applies `project_retention_policies` (also scheduled by pg_cron) |

DSARs are handled via the `data_subject_requests` table + the `api` edge function (`POST /v1/admin/compliance/dsars`), not a stored procedure. SOC 2 evidence is generated by the `soc2-evidence` edge function triggered from the admin console — no `soc2_evidence_snapshot()` RPC exists. Both routes are documented in the [Security & Compliance](/security/soc2) section.

## RLS pattern

Every table ships with RLS enabled and project-scoped policies. The canonical policy pattern is:

```sql
-- Use the subquery form — Postgres caches via initPlan, not per-row
create policy "users see own project data"
on public.reports
for select
using (project_id in (
  select project_id from public.project_members
  where user_id = (select auth.uid())
));
```

Do **not** use bare `auth.uid()`: the subquery form is evaluated once per query instead of once per row, which matters on large tables.

## Seed data

There is no separate seed file. The migrations insert the lookup rows themselves
(pricing plans, the plugin registry, the `mushi_runtime_config` defaults), so
`db push` is enough.

## Verifying the setup

```sql
-- Tables with RLS disabled (should return no rows)
select * from mushi_rls_coverage_snapshot() where not rls_enabled;

-- Check extensions
select name, default_version, installed_version
from pg_available_extensions
where name in ('vector', 'pg_cron', 'pg_net', 'pgcrypto', 'supabase_vault');
```

## Security & compliance

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/security

---
title: Security & compliance
description: How Mushi Mushi protects bug reports. Where data is stored, your own keys and storage, retention sweeps, RLS checks, prompt-injection defence, SOC 2 readiness.
---

# Security & compliance

Mushi Mushi handles raw bug reports: screenshots, console output, sometimes a
user's email. This page is the one-screen summary for whoever has to sign off
on that. Every row links to the page with the mechanism and the evidence.

  **Short version.** Your data is scoped to your project by row-level security,
  you can run diagnoses on your own model keys and keep
  screenshots in your own bucket, old reports are hard-deleted on your plan's
  schedule, and the controls are checked by cron, not by promise. Mushi is
  **not SOC 2 certified**. It collects evidence toward SOC 2; see the last row.

## Posture at a glance

| Control | What it means for you | Status | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Data residency** | Pick a region (US, EU or JP) at project creation | All hosted data is in one Tokyo (`ap-northeast-1`) project today, whatever region you pick. Dedicated US and EU clusters are planned, not live | [Data residency](/security/data-residency) |
| **Bring-your-own-key (BYOK)** | Diagnoses run against *your* Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenRouter account. Keys are stored in Vault, never shown back in plaintext, and nothing is billed to Mushi's provider account | Live | [BYOK](/security/byok) |
| **BYO storage** | Screenshots and crash dumps pinned to your own S3 / R2 / GCS / MinIO bucket; URLs signed server-side | Live | [BYO storage](/security/byo-storage) |
| **Retention sweep** | Reports older than your plan window (Free 14 d · Builder 90 d · Studio 180 d · Enterprise custom) or your per-project policy are hard-deleted daily; legal holds are skipped | Live, daily | [SOC 2 → retention](/security/soc2#data-retention-policies) |
| **Tenant isolation** | Row-level security is enabled on the public tables, and policies scope rows to the projects you own or belong to (`(SELECT auth.uid())`) | Live | [No client data leakage](/security/no-leakage-claim) |
| **Nightly RLS coverage check** | `mushi_rls_coverage_snapshot()` lists every public table and whether RLS is enabled; the `soc2-evidence` job records the result as control CC6.1 | Live, nightly | [SOC 2 → automated controls](/security/soc2#automated-controls) |
| **Prompt-injection defence** | The diagnosis runs in two stages so the main model never reads raw report text; text sent to the fix and review agents passes `sanitizeForLLM()`; screenshots go to an image-only call; an OWASP LLM01-style corpus runs in CI | Live | [Prompt-injection defence](/security/prompt-injection) |
| **Encryption** | TLS in transit; Supabase disk encryption at rest; model and storage keys in Supabase Vault. Report columns are not encrypted separately | Live | [SOC 2 readiness](/security/soc2) |
| **Audit log** | `audit_logs` records admin write actions per project, under RLS | Live | [SOC 2 readiness](/security/soc2) |
| **DSAR tracking** | File and track data-subject requests per project in **Compliance → DSARs**. The row is the audit trail; you fulfil the request yourself | Live | [SOC 2 → DSAR](/security/soc2#dsar-data-subject-access-request) |
| **SOC 2** | **Readiness, not certification.** A nightly job writes evidence snapshots for five controls (RLS, retention, audit-log volume, DSAR lag, availability) that an auditor could start from. No third-party audit has been performed | Evidence collection live · certification not started | [SOC 2 readiness](/security/soc2) |

## Operational transparency

- **Status page:** [updown.io/p/b6lod](https://updown.io/p/b6lod) — live
  availability and history for the API, hosted MCP, console, and docs.
  What is monitored and what we do and do not promise are on
  [Status & uptime](/operating/status).
- **Open source:** the server that enforces all of the above is
  [public](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi) under AGPLv3, so the
  policies, the cron jobs, and the tests can be read rather than trusted.
- **Sub-processors, retention table, and your rights:** on the
  [Privacy Policy](/legal/privacy).

## Report a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue. Use either channel:

1. **GitHub private vulnerability reporting** (preferred):
   [github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/security/advisories/new](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/security/advisories/new)
2. **Email:** [kensaurus@gmail.com](mailto:kensaurus@gmail.com), subject
   prefix `[mushi-security]`

Acknowledgement within 2 days, triage within 7, and a fix for critical and
high findings within 30. The full timeline, safe-harbor terms, and what to
include are in
[SECURITY.md](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/SECURITY.md).

## What we do not claim

- No SOC 2 Type 1 or Type 2 report exists yet.
- Dedicated US and EU clusters are not live; all hosted rows sit in Tokyo
  today, whatever region a project picked.
- No cross-region attestation runs yet, and report columns are not encrypted
  beyond Supabase's disk encryption.
- No uptime SLA on any self-serve plan.
- Prompt-injection defences reduce risk; they do not make model output safe to
  merge unreviewed. Keep the fix agent on draft PRs.

The deeper pages: [BYOK](/security/byok) · [Data residency](/security/data-residency) ·
[BYO storage](/security/byo-storage) · [SOC 2 readiness](/security/soc2) ·
[Prompt-injection defence](/security/prompt-injection) ·
[No client data leakage](/security/no-leakage-claim)

## BYO storage

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/security/byo-storage

---
title: BYO storage
description: Keep Mushi Mushi screenshots and crash dumps in your own storage bucket instead of Mushi's, with credentials in Vault and signed URLs.
---

# Bring-your-own storage

> **Scenario:** Your company policy requires all user screenshots to stay inside your own AWS account, not a third-party storage bucket.

By default screenshots and crash dumps go to a private Mushi-managed Supabase Storage bucket. BYO storage pins them to your own bucket instead: credentials live in Supabase Vault, URLs are signed server-side, and the admin console shows screenshots the same way from either backend.

## Supported backends

| Backend | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| **AWS S3** | `bucket`, `region`, access key ID and secret access key |
| **Cloudflare R2** | S3-compatible; set `endpoint` and `region = auto` |
| **Google Cloud Storage** | `bucket` and a service-account JSON key |
| **MinIO (self-hosted)** | S3-compatible; a custom `endpoint` is required |
| **Supabase Storage** | Default, no configuration needed |

## Setup

In the admin console: **BYO storage** (`/storage`).

1. Select your provider.
2. Fill in the fields for it:
   - **S3 / R2:** `bucket` (exact name) + `region` + access key ID + secret access key
   - **GCS:** `bucket` + service-account JSON
   - **MinIO:** `endpoint` (a public `https` URL, e.g. `https://minio.example.com`) + `bucket` + `region` + credentials
3. Click **Save**. Raw credentials are written to Supabase Vault; the settings row keeps only the Vault references, and the keys are never echoed back.

The bucket must already exist. Mushi never creates buckets.

## What moves (and what doesn't)

- **New reports** ingested after the switch land in your bucket.
- **Existing reports** stay in the Mushi-managed bucket; they are not migrated automatically.
- Edge Functions sign the URLs server-side. For your bucket the lifetime is `signed_url_ttl_secs` (default 3600 seconds, 60 to 604,800 allowed).

## Health check

The BYO storage page has a health check (`POST /v1/admin/storage/:projectId/health`) that uploads a small `_mushi_health_.txt` object and deletes it again. The result is stored as `healthy` or `failing` with the last error, and the page shows it. If an upload to your bucket fails, the report is still saved, without its screenshot, and the error is logged; run the health check after any credential change.

## Permissions required

| Backend | Minimum IAM / policy |
| --- | --- |
| AWS S3 | `s3:PutObject`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:DeleteObject` on `arn:aws:s3:::your-bucket/*` |
| Cloudflare R2 | Object Read, Object Write on the bucket |
| GCS | `storage.objects.create`, `storage.objects.get`, `storage.objects.delete` on the bucket |

---

## Bring-your-own-key

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/security/byok

---
title: Bring-your-own-key
description: Use your own Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter key for a Mushi Mushi project, so diagnosis, fix and grading runs bill to your provider account.
---

# Bring-your-own-key (BYOK)

> **Scenario:** Your company policy requires that all LLM calls use an API key that belongs to your own Anthropic / OpenAI account so usage appears in your own billing dashboard and never routes through a third party.

Mushi Mushi supports project-scoped BYOK. When set, the classifier, judge, fix, review and intelligence-report runs for that project use your key, so usage shows up in your provider console, not Mushi's.

## Setup

In the admin console: **Settings → AI keys**.

1. Find the service's row (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Cursor, Firecrawl, Browserbase or Supabase) and click **Add key**. You can paste `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-…` or a quoted value; Mushi strips the name and quotes.
2. Click **Save & validate**. Mushi checks the key with the provider first (a free call), then stores it in **Supabase Vault**. The database row keeps only the secret's ID, and the key is never returned to the browser.
3. Add more than one key for a service and Mushi moves to the next one when a key is rejected or runs out of quota.

## One key for every app

A new key is used by **All my apps** by default: every app in every organization you own, so you add it once even when your apps live in several organizations. The add form's **Use this key for** picker also offers **This organization** (every app in it) and **This app only**.

- Each app tries its keys in this order: its own key, its old single key from before key pools, its organization's key, the all-apps keys of its organization's owners, then Mushi's own key. A shared key is a fallback or backup, never a replacement for an app's own key.
- An all-apps key reaches only organizations where you are an **owner**, never one you only administer or belong to. Only you can test, turn off, change or remove it; other members see it read-only on the apps it serves.
- A key's row shows where it is used (**All my apps**, **All apps in …**, **This app only**). Change it with the row's **Used by** picker; the move is confirmed first and recorded in the key audit log.
- An organization key is managed by the organization's owners and admins. Turning off or removing an organization or all-apps key affects every app that uses it, so the confirmation says so.
- Supabase access tokens always stay with one app.
- The CLI and MCP `add` commands add a key to one app; organization and all-apps keys are added in the console.

  Keys take effect on the **next** LLM call. No Edge Function redeploy is required. If you rotate a key, update it here — stale keys return `401` from Anthropic/OpenAI and the key shows as rejected on **Settings → AI keys**.

## What uses the key

| Function | Model |
| --- | --- |
| `fast-filter` (first look at each report) | Claude Haiku 4.5, then GPT-5.4 mini |
| `classify-report` (diagnosis) | Claude Sonnet 5.5, then GPT-5.4 |
| `fix-worker` (fix drafts) | Claude Sonnet 5.5, then GPT-5.4 |
| `judge-batch` (fix grading) | Claude Sonnet 5.5, then GPT-5.4 |
| `intelligence-report` (weekly summary) | Claude Haiku 5.5, then GPT-5.4 |
| `agent-pr-review` (review of each fix PR) | Claude Opus 5.5, on your own Anthropic key only (skipped without one) |
| Search, similar bugs, codebase index | OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` |
| Voice reports | OpenAI `gpt-transcribe` |

Your own keys are used first (the app's, then your organization's shared keys, then its owners' all-apps keys); when there are none for a provider, Mushi's platform key is used where the server has one. Set both Anthropic and OpenAI keys to keep every call on your accounts.

## OpenRouter

OpenRouter has its own row. Calls that would go to OpenAI try your OpenAI keys first, then your OpenRouter keys, with OpenRouter's model names (`openai/gpt-5.4`). Speech-to-text and fine-tuning stay on OpenAI, because OpenRouter does not offer them. The OpenRouter row also shows the key's spending limit and usage, read from OpenRouter.

## Audit trail

Key changes write a row to `byok_audit_log`:

```sql
select actor_user_id, action, provider, ts
from public.byok_audit_log
where project_id = 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID'
order by ts desc;
```

`action` is one of `added`, `rotated`, `removed`, `used`, `tested`.

## Rotation

1. Generate a new key in your provider dashboard.
2. Paste it into **Settings → AI keys** and save.
3. The new key is active on the next LLM call.
4. Revoke the old key from your provider dashboard once you confirm calls are flowing.

## Which key a call used

Every model call is recorded in `llm_invocations` with `key_source` set to `byok` (one of your keys) or `env` (Mushi's platform key). The console's cost views count BYOK calls from this column.

## Data residency

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/security/data-residency

---
title: Data residency
description: Where Mushi Mushi Cloud stores data today (Tokyo, ap-northeast-1), how the region picked at project creation works, and what the SDK does about regions.
---

# Data residency

> **Scenario:** Your EU customers' data must stay in the EU. You need to know where report ingestion, embeddings, screenshots, and AI calls actually go today.

Mushi Mushi Cloud is designed for one Supabase project per region with no replication between them. Today all production traffic runs on a single Supabase project in `ap-northeast-1` (Tokyo, `dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj`), whatever region a project picked. The US and EU clusters are planned, not live. Model calls go to the US-based providers listed in the [Privacy Policy](/legal/privacy#5-sub-processors), unless you self-host and choose otherwise.

## Regions

| Region picked at creation | Where the data lives today | Planned dedicated cluster |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **US** (default) | Tokyo (`ap-northeast-1`), the single hosted project | `us-east-1` |
| **EU** | Tokyo, same project | `eu-central-1` |
| **JP** | Tokyo, same project | `ap-northeast-1` |

  Pick the region at project creation. Moving a project that already has data to another region needs an export and restore, so create a new project in the region you want instead.

## How the SDK routes

The browser SDK has no `region` option. It sends everything to `apiEndpoint`,
which defaults to `https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api`,
and every region resolves to that endpoint today. API keys use one `mushi_…`
format in every region.

`@mushi-mushi/core` also exports `resolveRegionEndpoint`, which asks the
gateway which endpoint serves a project and caches the answer in
`localStorage` for 24 hours. Until regional clusters ship it returns the same
endpoint.

```ts
import { resolveRegionEndpoint } from '@mushi-mushi/core'

const endpoint = await resolveRegionEndpoint({
  projectId: 'YOUR_PROJECT_ID',
  apiEndpoint: 'https://dxptnwrhwsqckaftyymj.supabase.co/functions/v1/api',
})
```

## Attestation

There is no cross-region attestation yet. With one hosted project there is nothing to compare against; the region you pick is recorded in `projects.data_residency_region` and mirrored to `region_routing`, which the gateway will use to redirect calls once a second cluster exists. The **Compliance → Residency** tab shows each project's region.

## Self-hosting

If you self-host on your own Supabase project, you control the region entirely — pick any Supabase-supported region at project creation.

## GDPR notes

- Data is encrypted at rest by Supabase's disk encryption. Report columns are not encrypted separately.
- DSARs (data subject access requests) are tracked in the `data_subject_requests` table via `POST /v1/admin/compliance/dsars`; see [SOC 2 readiness](/security/soc2#dsar-data-subject-access-request).
- Transfers from the EEA and UK to Japan rely on the EU's adequacy decision for Japan; transfers to US model providers are covered in the [Privacy Policy](/legal/privacy).

## No client data leakage: what we promise and how we enforce it

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/security/no-leakage-claim

---
title: "No client data leakage: what we promise and how we enforce it"
description: Explicit enumeration of Mushi Mushi's privacy boundaries, the gaps we've closed, and the controls that keep client data isolated.
---

# No client data leakage

This page is the single-source citation for the privacy claims made on the Mushi Mushi landing page. It enumerates exactly what Mushi promises, which controls enforce each promise, and which gaps have been closed or documented as follow-ups.

  **Short version:** Your reports are RLS-isolated per project. Screenshots are behind signed URLs in a private bucket. Common PII patterns are scrubbed before writing to Postgres and before the diagnosis models see a report. Code snippets reach a model only for diagnosis and fixes, and cloud coding agents work in your repo under your own account. With BYOK, model calls run on your provider account instead of ours.

---

## The three promises

### 1. Your data doesn't cross project boundaries

**Control:** Row-Level Security (RLS) is enabled on every customer-facing table. The `reports`, `fix_attempts`, `qa_story_runs`, `llm_invocations`, `byok_audit_log`, and 30+ sibling tables use `project_id IN (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE owner_id = auth.uid())` or the org-member equivalent. The `soc2-evidence` cron snapshots `mushi_rls_coverage_snapshot()` daily and records a failing CC6.1 control if a public table has RLS disabled.

**Verification:** `SELECT schemaname, tablename, rowsecurity FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND NOT rowsecurity;` should return zero rows.

### 2. PII is scrubbed before it reaches Postgres or an LLM

**Control (at-rest, Wave 5 Gap A):** `scrubPii()` from `_shared/pii-scrubber.ts` is called in the ingest path (`api/helpers.ts::ingestReport`) before the `reports` row is inserted. Fields scrubbed: `description`, `user_intent`, `console_logs[].message`, `network_logs[].url` (including query parameters). Patterns cover: SSN, credit-card PAN, AWS/Stripe/Slack/GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic keys, JWTs, IPv4, IPv6, emails, phone numbers.

**Control (client-side, at capture — SDK 1.27+):** The web and Node SDKs now scrub PII *before the report leaves the browser or server process*, so sensitive values never travel the wire in the first place. The web SDK runs `scrubUrl()` over every captured network URL and route-timeline entry; the Node SDK runs `scrubPii()` / `scrubUrl()` over `description`, `environment.url`, and `error.message` / `error.stack` in `captureReport`, the Express handler, and the trace middleware. This is the same pattern set as the server-side scrubber (shared source of truth), so client and server redact identically — the at-rest and pre-LLM scrubs below are now defence-in-depth behind it rather than the first line.

**Control (pre-LLM, defence-in-depth):** `scrubReport()` is also called in `classify-report` and `fast-filter` before building the Anthropic prompt, so even if the ingest scrub is ever bypassed the LLM never sees raw PII.

**Gap not yet closed:** `performance_metrics` and `selected_element` JSONB columns are not yet scrubbed — these fields are unlikely to contain PII but are not covered by the current scrubber. Filed as a follow-up.

### 3. Screenshots are behind signed, time-limited URLs

**Control (Wave 5 Gap B):** The default `SupabaseStorageAdapter` uses `createSignedUrl()` instead of `getPublicUrl()`, and the `screenshots` bucket is private (`public = false`). The stored URL is a signed URL, so flipping the bucket to public later would not turn old URLs into public links. Its lifetime is long (about 7 years) so screenshots keep rendering in the console for as long as the report is kept; treat a stored screenshot URL as a secret.

**BYO storage:** S3/R2/GCS/MinIO adapters use SigV4-presigned GET URLs with TTL from `project_storage_settings.signed_url_ttl_secs` (default 3600s, max 604800s).

---

## BYOK — your API keys run against your account

**What "BYOK" means:** Mushi does not train models on your bug reports. When you add your own Anthropic or OpenAI key (**Settings → AI keys**), the classify, fix and judge calls use your key and your account first. Mushi's platform key is used only for a provider where you have no key.

**What happens without BYOK:** LLM calls fall back to Mushi's platform Anthropic/OpenAI account. Your prompt content (the scrubbed bug description, code context, diff) flows through that account. This is recorded as `llm_invocations.key_source = 'env'`.

**No hard "BYOK only" switch yet (Wave 5 Gap D):** `project_settings.require_byok` exists in the schema, but no edge function reads it today, so it does not block the platform-key fallback. To keep every call on your accounts, add both an Anthropic and an OpenAI key.

**Vault encryption:** BYOK key values are stored as `vault://` references pointing to Supabase Vault (`vault.secrets`). `dereferenceKey()` in `_shared/byok.ts` rejects a raw (non-vault) key reference when the environment is `production`.

---

## Where your code goes

There are two fix paths, and they treat code differently:

- **Mushi's own `fix-worker` model call** reads your codebase through a vector index (`project_codebase_files`) built by `mushi index` or the GitHub indexer. Indexed chunks keep a short `content_preview` for the console plus an embedding for search, are RLS-isolated by `project_id`, and are deleted with the project (`ON DELETE CASCADE`). Only the retrieved snippets go into the prompt, not whole files.
- **Cloud coding agents** (Cursor, GitHub's agent) work directly in your repository under your own key or account, the same as when you run them yourself. Mushi sends them the report and its diagnosis.

---

## Screenshot URL host validation

**Control (Wave 5 Gap G):** `screenshot_url` values are validated at ingest time (`validateScreenshotUrlIngest()` in `api/helpers.ts`). Invalid URLs, non-HTTPS schemes, private/metadata hosts (RFC1918, `169.254.*`, `.local`, `.internal`), and hosts outside the allowlist are rejected and stored as `NULL`. The ingest allowlist defaults to `*.supabase.co`, `*.supabase.in`, `*.supabase.red` — extensible via `MUSHI_SCREENSHOT_HOST_ALLOWLIST`.

---

## Vault secret scoping

**Control (Wave 5 Gap F):** The `vault_store_secret(name, value, project_id)` Postgres function now enforces the naming convention `mushi__*` when `project_id` is supplied. A misconfigured caller cannot overwrite a different tenant's secret. The three-arg form is used by all admin routes that manage BYOK keys.

---

## What we defer (known follow-ups)

| Gap | Description | Status |
|-----|-------------|--------|
| C | SSRF allowlist for self-hosted deployments should auto-derive from `project_storage_settings.endpoint` | Deferred — needs ops coordination |
| H | Sentry Replay in the admin console runs on routes that display customer report data. DOM structure may implicitly reveal topic/count metadata. | Deferred — disable Replay on `/reports/:id`, `/fixes/:id`, `/query` |
| Langfuse tenant isolation | Mushi's Langfuse workspace correlates project IDs with prompt+response payloads. Self-hosted Langfuse per region for "no third-party LLM observability" customers is possible but not yet automated. | Deferred — document opt-out path |

## Prompt-injection defence

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/security/prompt-injection

---
title: Prompt-injection defence
description: How Mushi Mushi defends its LLM pipeline against prompt injection hidden in bug reports, screenshots and PR text, and the regression corpus that runs in CI.
---

# Prompt-injection defence

Bug reports are user-supplied content that ends up in model prompts. That makes prompt injection a real threat: a report could try to override the system prompt, leak data, or steer a fix agent into a harmful change. Mushi Mushi uses several layers. None of them makes model output safe to merge unreviewed.

  `packages/server/src/__tests__/injection.test.ts` runs the injection corpus against `sanitizeForLLM()` in CI (`pnpm test`). A corpus entry that no longer trips a pattern fails the build.

## Defence layers

### 1. Two-stage diagnosis (air gap)

`fast-filter` (stage 1) is the only model that reads the report text, after `scrubReport()` has removed common PII. It extracts structured symptoms and a sanitized evidence summary. `classify-report` (stage 2) receives only that structured JSON, never the raw console lines, network URLs or stack traces, and its system prompt tells it to treat any user-supplied description as data.

### 2. Text sanitizer for agent prompts

Text that goes to the fix and review agents (`fix-worker`, `agent-pr-review`, `review-followup`, `fix-verifier`) and voice transcripts passes through `sanitizeForLLM()` in `packages/server/supabase/functions/_shared/sanitize.ts`. It:

- normalises Unicode (NFKC) and strips invisible and format characters (zero-width joiners, bidi controls, tag characters);
- removes HTML comments, a common hidden-instruction channel;
- removes ASCII control characters;
- decodes base64 blobs that decode to readable text and re-scans them;
- replaces known injection fragments (`ignore previous instructions`, role flips, ``, `[INST]`, `<|im_start|>`, output and tool-call hijacks) with `[BLOCKED_…]` markers;
- collapses long whitespace runs used to bury an instruction.

It does not cap field length; prompt builders apply their own budgets.

### 3. Fenced user content

The PR review prompt puts the report, PR description and diff in labelled data blocks, and `fenceUntrusted()` (`_shared/fix-review.ts`) stops untrusted text from opening or closing one of those blocks. The system prompt tells the model that text inside them is data, not instructions. Review findings handed back to a coding agent are screened as well: only files the PR changed, and nothing that reads as an instruction or carries a foreign URL or shell command.

### 4. Structured output

Classifiers and graders ask for output against a Zod schema. A response that is not valid JSON or does not match the schema throws. Where the caller has a fallback model (for example GPT-5.4 behind Claude), it retries there; otherwise the run fails. Free-form model text is never passed along in place of the structured result.

### 5. Screenshots

Screenshots are never sent alongside user text. After classification, `classify-report` makes a separate image-only call with a fixed system prompt that treats all text in the image as data, copies it into `visible_text_in_image`, and sets `untrusted_image_instructions_detected` when the image tries to give instructions. Because it runs after classification, it can annotate a report but cannot change its diagnosis. The screenshot URL must pass the SSRF host allowlist first, or the vision call is skipped.

### 6. Regression suite

`packages/server/src/__tests__/injection.test.ts` covers:

- `INJECTION_CORPUS` from `sanitize.ts` (19 payloads: instruction hijacks, role flips, system/assistant/INST/ChatML tags, output and tool hijacks, base64-wrapped, control-character, whitespace-burial, zero-width, HTML-comment and tag-character smuggling);
- a local corpus checked against the expected `[BLOCKED_…]` tokens;
- hidden-character filtering for voice intake.

Run it locally with:

```bash
cd packages/server
npx vitest run src/__tests__/injection.test.ts
```

## What this does not cover

- Pattern lists catch known phrasings, not every paraphrase. The air gap and output schemas matter more than the regexes.
- A cloud coding agent reads your repository and the report; keep fix PRs as drafts and review them (or rely on the [agent PR review](/concepts/agent-pr-review)) before merging.

## SOC 2 readiness

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/security/soc2

---
title: SOC 2 readiness
description: Mushi Mushi's SOC 2 readiness, not certification. Nightly evidence for access, retention, DSAR and availability controls, retention per project, DSAR tracking.
---

# SOC 2 readiness

> **Scenario:** Your customer's procurement team asks how bug-report data is controlled. You want to show which controls are checked automatically and where the evidence lives.

Mushi Mushi is **not SOC 2 certified** and no auditor has reviewed it. The server collects evidence toward SOC 2: a nightly job snapshots a small set of controls, retention windows are enforced by cron, and data-subject requests are tracked. This is a starting point for an audit, not a substitute for one.

  All of it is in the admin console under **Compliance** (tabs: Overview, Evidence, Retention, DSARs, Residency). **Refresh evidence** takes a new snapshot on demand.

## Automated controls

The `soc2-evidence` edge function runs daily at 04:30 UTC and writes one row per project and control to `soc2_evidence`, with a `pass`, `warn` or `fail` status and the raw payload.

| Control | What is checked | Frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CC6.1 Logical access | `mushi_rls_coverage_snapshot()` lists every public table and whether RLS is enabled | Daily |
| CC6.7 Data retention | The project has an explicit row in `project_retention_policies` (warns when defaults apply) | Daily |
| CC7.2 Operations | `audit_logs` volume over the last 7 days | Daily |
| CC8.1 DSAR handling | Pending data-subject requests older than 30 days | Daily |
| A1.2 Availability | 7-day uptime ratio from the health probes | Daily |

Other controls rely on the platform rather than on Mushi code:

| Control | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Encryption in transit | TLS on every Supabase endpoint |
| Encryption at rest | Supabase disk encryption; model and storage credentials in Supabase Vault |
| Backup / DR | Supabase backups and point-in-time recovery on the hosted project |

## Audit dashboard

In the admin console: **Compliance**.

- **Evidence**: the latest snapshot per control, with the payload JSON for an auditor.
- **Retention**: each project's windows and legal hold, plus the last sweep.
- **DSARs**: filed requests and their status.
- **Residency**: the region each project is pinned to.

## Generating evidence manually

Click **Refresh evidence** under **Compliance**, or call the edge function with the service-role key:

```bash
curl -X POST https://<your-project>.supabase.co/functions/v1/soc2-evidence \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <service-role-key>"
```

New rows appear in `soc2_evidence` when the call returns.

## Data retention policies

Retention is set per project in **Compliance → Retention** and stored in `project_retention_policies`:

| Column | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reports_retention_days` | 365 | Must be greater than 0 |
| `audit_retention_days` | 730 | Must be greater than 0 |
| `llm_traces_retention_days` | 90 | Must be greater than 0 |
| `byok_audit_retention_days` | 365 | Must be greater than 0 |
| `legal_hold` | off | When on, nothing in the project is deleted |

On Mushi Cloud the daily `retention-sweep` job also applies your plan's window (Free 14 days, Builder 90, Studio 180) when the project has no explicit policy. It hard-deletes expired reports and writes one `audit_logs` row per project with the count.

## DSAR (Data Subject Access Request)

File a DSAR in the admin console (**Compliance → DSARs**) or through the admin API with a signed-in user's access token:

```bash
curl -X POST https://<your-project>.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/admin/compliance/dsars \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <user-access-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"projectId": "<project-id>", "request_type": "access", "subject_email": "user@example.com"}'
# Returns the new data_subject_requests row (status: pending).
```

`request_type` is one of `access`, `export`, `deletion` or `rectification`. The row is the audit trail, not the export: you fulfil the request, then `PATCH /v1/admin/compliance/dsars/:id` with `status: "completed"` (and an optional `evidence_url`) records who completed it and when.

## Privacy Policy

# Privacy Policy

  **Draft, not yet reviewed by a lawyer.** This page is a complete plain-English
  description of how Mushi Mushi handles personal data as of 2026-10-28. Treat
  it as a description of current practice, not a finished legal document.
  Questions: kensaurus@gmail.com.

**Effective date:** 2026-10-29 · **Version:** 4. Version 4 lists Langfuse and Browserbase, which we already used but had left out of section 5; says Sentry also receives errors from Mushi Mushi's own servers; says model providers also receive code snippets for fixes and reviews; describes the request tracker as it is (it records requests, it does not produce a signed export); and corrects the tester ID-check threshold to US$400. (Version 3, 2026-10-28, did not include these corrections; version 2, 2026-10-10, did not list the free production check or the cookieless visit count; version 1, 2026-09-21, did not list the opt-in known-fix search sent to Firecrawl.)

This policy covers **Mushi Cloud** (the hosted service at
`kensaur.us/mushi-mushi`), the **admin console**, the **docs site**, the
**Mushi Bounties** tester marketplace, and the **SDKs** when they send data
to Mushi Cloud. If you self-host the open-source server, you are the operator
and this policy does not apply to your instance.

## 1. Who is responsible

Mushi Mushi is built and operated by **Kensaurus 合同会社**,
based in Japan (the "controller" for the data described in section 3, and the
"processor" for the data described in section 4).

- **Contact for anything in this policy:** [kensaurus@gmail.com](mailto:kensaurus@gmail.com)
- **Subject line that gets the fastest answer:** `[mushi-privacy]`
- **Security reports:** see [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/SECURITY.md) and the [security summary](/security).

There is no separate data-protection officer. The founder answers these
requests personally.

## 2. What data we handle, in one table

| Category | Examples | Where it comes from | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Account data** | Email address, display name and avatar from Google or GitHub sign-in, the "how did you hear about us" answer and `?src=` signup source, plan and billing status | You, when you create a console account | Run your account, bill you, understand which channels bring users |
| **End-user report data** | Screenshot, console and network log excerpts, browser user agent, viewport, page URL, the reporter's free-text description, an opaque reporter token, a hashed device fingerprint (a SHA-256 of browser, screen and time-zone traits, used to spot abuse), any end-user identifier (email, user ID) the host app chooses to pass, voice transcripts when the host app turns on voice intake | The SDK in an app that a project owner built | Diagnose the bug and hand the owner a fix |
| **Fix and repo data** | Repository names, file paths and an index of your code, draft pull requests, MCP tool calls from your editor | The GitHub integration and the MCP server, when you connect them | Produce fixes that fit your codebase |
| **Product usage events** | Console page views, setup-funnel steps (project created, key minted, first report), feature clicks, and a session heartbeat with your browser user agent, tagged with your user ID | The console, through Mushi's own SDK | Improve activation and find dead ends |
| **Docs-site analytics** | Views of the landing, quickstart and pricing pages (route, referring page without its query string, `utm_*` tags), clicks on sign-up and demo buttons, a session heartbeat with your browser user agent, and a random browser ID stored in your browser. These are **pseudonymous, not anonymous**: if you later sign in to the console in the same browser, the console links your earlier docs events to your account | The docs and landing pages, through Mushi's own SDK — only after you accept the consent bar | Measure the funnel from landing to signup |
| **Docs-site page-view count** | For each page view: the page path, the `?src=` campaign tag of the link you arrived by, and the host name of the site that linked to you (for example `news.ycombinator.com`). Stored only as a count per day, path, tag and host. No IP address, cookie, browser ID, user agent or fingerprint is stored, and nothing is written to your browser. To stop one visitor flooding the count, the rate limiter keeps a one-way hash of your IP address salted with a secret and the date, so it cannot be turned back into the address or linked across days, and it is never stored with the counts | The docs and landing pages, without the SDK, before and without consent; skipped when Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control is on | Count how many people each launch post or link brings |
| **Console error telemetry** | Stack traces, browser and OS, the console route you were on when something broke | Sentry, from the admin console | Fix bugs in the console itself |
| **Support and security mail** | Whatever you put in an email to us | You | Answer you |
| **Bounties tester data** | Tester display name, points balance, gift-card redemptions, and KYC details (legal name, jurisdiction, tax ID) once gift-card redemptions reach US$400 in a calendar year | You, on the Bounties marketplace | Pay out gift cards and meet US tax reporting rules |

We do not sell personal data and we do not run advertising.

## 3. Data where Mushi is the controller

This is data about **you**, the person with the console or tester account:
account data, product usage events, docs-site analytics, console error
telemetry, support mail, and Bounties tester data.

**Legal bases (GDPR art. 6(1))**

- **(b) contract** — creating and running your account, billing, delivering
  diagnoses, paying tester bounties.
- **(f) legitimate interests** — keeping the service secure, preventing abuse
  and quota gaming, keeping the console working (error telemetry), and
  understanding which onboarding steps fail. We ran a balancing test on the
  product-usage events: they are scoped to your own account, never shared, and
  expire (section 7).
- **(f) legitimate interests** — the docs-site page-view count: an
  aggregate count per day and page that cannot identify you, with no
  browser storage. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control turn it off.
- **(a) consent** — docs-site analytics. Until you accept the consent bar
  the docs site loads no analytics code, sends no analytics events, and
  stores nothing for analytics except your answer; Do Not Track and Global
  Privacy Control are honoured as a refusal. "No thanks" keeps it that way.
  The only exception is the page-view count above: it is not the analytics
  SDK, sends only the path, the `?src=` tag and the referring host, and
  stores nothing in your browser.
- **(c) legal obligation** — tax records for paid plans and tester payouts.

**Free production check (added 2026-10-28).** The free production check
reads only the public pages of the address you enter (through Firecrawl,
section 5) and stores the address, the findings, a one-way hash of your IP
address for rate limiting (never the IP itself) and, only if you give it, your
email so we can send you the report link once; the email is cleared after that
send. Legal basis: (f) legitimate interests (preventing abuse of a free tool);
the email is (b) contract — you asked for the report.

## 4. Data where Mushi is the processor

End-user report data, fix and repo data, and any voice transcript belong to the
**project owner** — the developer who put the SDK in their app. For that data:

- The **project owner is the controller**. They decide what the SDK captures,
  whether to pass end-user identifiers, whether to enable voice intake, and
  they must tell their own users that screenshots and console output may be
  captured (this duty is in the [Terms](/legal/terms#5-acceptable-use)).
- **Mushi is the processor** and acts only on the owner's instructions: store
  the report, run the diagnosis, produce a fix, delete on schedule or on
  request.
- **Data-processing summary (DPA).** Mushi processes this data only to provide
  the service; applies the security measures on the [security summary](/security);
  uses only the sub-processors in section 5 and gives notice on this page before
  adding one; assists the owner with data-subject requests through the DSAR
  tracking in the console; deletes or returns the data at the end of the
  contract; and makes the SOC 2 readiness evidence available on request. Owners
  who need a signed DPA on their own paper can email us.

End users of a project owner's app should contact **that owner** first. If you
cannot reach them, email us and we will forward the request.

## 5. Sub-processors

Dedicated US and EU clusters are planned; when they ship, a project's data stays in the [region chosen at creation](/security/data-residency) | Row-level security, nightly RLS check |
| **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **OpenRouter** | Report text and logs (after PII scrubbing), screenshots, and code snippets sent for diagnosis, fixes and reviews; audio clips for voice transcription (OpenAI only) | US | **BYOK:** if you add your own model key, calls run against *your* provider account. Nothing is billed to or stored by Mushi's provider account. Hosted keys are used only when you have not added your own |

| **Firecrawl** | Public URLs you point Mushi at (for example your own site) when running inventory, QA-coverage or story-mapping crawls; queries you run on the Research page; and, only if a project turns on **Search the web for known fixes**: the error message of a report with IDs, URLs and long numbers removed (plus the runtime name, such as `node`), searched in Firecrawl's developer index (GitHub issues, pull requests, READMEs, docs) and on GitHub and Stack Overflow after classification or when someone presses **Search again**, and, for a fix dispatch with little code context, the report summary or the first 200 characters of its description | US | Only pages you ask us to crawl. The known-fix search is off by default and set per project (Settings → Web tools) |
| **Tremendous** | Gift-card delivery for Bounties testers: email, amount, and KYC data past the threshold | US | Bounties only |

## 6. International transfers and residency

Mushi is operated from **Japan**, and production data is stored in **Tokyo**.
The EU recognises Japan as providing adequate protection, and Japan
recognises the EEA and the UK in the same way, so EEA/UK ↔ Japan transfers need
no extra safeguard.

Transfers to the US sub-processors above rely on the provider's **EU-US Data
Privacy Framework** certification where it exists, and otherwise on **Standard
Contractual Clauses** in the provider's data-processing terms.

You can pick a residency region at project creation; see
[Data residency](/security/data-residency) for what is live today and what is
reserved.

Legal-hold rows are skipped |

| Backups | Point-in-time recovery, 7 days | Supabase |

## 8. Your rights and how to use them

If you are in the EEA, the UK, or another place with similar law, you can ask
us to **access**, **correct**, **delete**, **restrict**, or **export** your
data, **object** to processing based on legitimate interests, and **withdraw
consent** (the docs consent bar can be reset by clearing site data). You can
also complain to your local supervisory authority.

- **Console accounts:** most of this is self-service in **Settings**. For a
  full export or deletion, email [kensaurus@gmail.com](mailto:kensaurus@gmail.com)
  from the address on the account.
- **Project owners handling requests from their end users:** the console
  has a DSAR tracker (**Compliance → DSARs**) that records each request and
  who completed it, and a host backend can erase one end user's reports
  through `POST /v1/sdk/erase-subject`; see
  [SOC 2 readiness → DSAR](/security/soc2#dsar-data-subject-access-request).
- **End users of someone else's app:** contact the app's owner. If you cannot,
  email us with the app name and we will route the request.

We answer within **30 days**. We will ask you to prove you own the account
or the reporter identity before releasing anything.

- **Provision to third parties (第三者提供):** we do not provide personal

  who act on our instructions under a contract (委託), (b) where required by

| Docs | Release-banner dismissal, theme preference | Hide a banner you closed; light / dark | Until cleared |
| Docs | `mushi:migration::steps` | Your progress through a migration guide's checklist | Until cleared |
| Docs | `mushi:docs:auth`, `mushi:docs:bridge-nonce` (session storage) | Only when you sign in from the docs: a short-lived console session so snippets can show your own project | Until the tab closes |
| Docs, after you accept | `mushi_first_touch_` | Where your first visit came from: `utm_source` / `utm_medium` / `utm_campaign`, the referring page without its query string, the landing path, and the time | Until cleared |
| Docs, after you accept | Mushi SDK keys (see the SDK rows below) | The docs site loads Mushi's own SDK once you accept | As listed below |
| **SDK** (your app, the console, the docs after consent) | `mushi:reporter-token:` (`mushi_reporter_token` when the SDK starts without a project ID) | A random token so repeat reports and analytics events from the same browser group together. It is not an email or a name, but it links events from the same browser | Until cleared |
| **SDK** | `mushi_session_id` (session storage) | Group events from one browser tab session | Until the tab closes |
| **SDK** | `mushi_events_consent_`, `mushi_events_spill_` | The analytics consent state, and analytics events that could not be sent yet (retried on the next visit) | Until cleared or sent |
| **SDK** | `mushi_fingerprint_hash` | The hashed device fingerprint described in section 2, cached so it is computed once | Until cleared |
| **SDK** | Offline report queue (IndexedDB `mushi-mushi`, falling back to `mushi_offline_queue`) and its encryption key (IndexedDB `mushi-mushi-keyring`) | Reports that could not be sent yet, encrypted at rest where the browser allows | Until sent; the key until cleared |
| **SDK** | `mushi:last-run`, cached runtime and SDK-version settings, `mushi_region_v1:` | Technical state: crash-on-last-run detection, cached project settings, and the resolved API endpoint | Until cleared or expired |
| **SDK** | `mushi:lastShown`, `mushi:lastDismiss`, `mushi:consecDismiss`, `mushi::firstSessionShown` | Only when the app turns on proactive report prompts: when a prompt was last shown or dismissed, so it does not keep asking | Until cleared |
| **SDK** | `mushi:tester-jwt:` | Only for a Bounties tester who signs in from the widget: the tester session | Until cleared or expired |

The SDK sets no cookies and reads no third-party cookies.

holders at least **14 days** before the change takes effect. Continued use

## Wave D highlights (shipped)

- **One-click SDK install & upgrade** — `npx mushi-mushi` + `npm create mushi-mushi` wizard, SDK upgrade PRs from the Connect hub
- **Skill-driven triage** — `skill-sync`, `classify-report` Stage 2, pipeline runs, kenji skills integration
- **Codebase Atlas (`/explore`)** — semantic codebase search, ask, tour, and knowledge surface
- **sdk-versions-cron** — daily npm sync keeps SDK freshness chips accurate
- **Backend drift scanner** — daily schema snapshot diff, `gate_findings` of type `schema_drift`
- **MCP tool surface** — `@mushi-mushi/mcp`, `mcp:read` + `mcp:write` scopes, tools grouped into feature groups you switch on (see [`@mushi-mushi/mcp`](/sdks/mcp) for the current, catalog-sourced tool count)

## Completed highlights (Wave C, v0.8.0)

- **Native SDKs** — iOS (Swift), Android (Kotlin) and Flutter implementations in the repo, plus the Capacitor plugin on npm. The three native SDKs are previews: publishing to CocoaPods / SwiftPM release tags, Maven Central and pub.dev is still open
- **A2A discovery** — `a2a-push-notify` edge function; agents can subscribe to Mushi events as A2A peers
- **SOC 2 readiness module** — retention policies, data-subject request tracking and nightly snapshots of five controls (RLS coverage among them). Not a certification
- **Data residency** — a region (US / EU / JP) is picked at project creation, but Mushi Cloud runs one production cluster in Tokyo today; EU and US clusters are reserved, not live ([details](/security/data-residency))
- **BYO storage** — S3, Cloudflare R2, GCS, MinIO, or Supabase Storage per project
- **BYOK** — project-scoped Anthropic + OpenAI keys via Supabase Vault
- **PDCA runner** — closed-loop iteration engine: fix → judge → promote, visible in the Iterate console page
- **Drift scanner** — `drift-walker` + `contract-graph-builder` detect API contract drift against live routes
- **QA coverage stories** — define and schedule user-story tests from the admin console

See [VISION.md](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/VISION.md) (positioning constitution) and [Concepts → Architecture](/concepts/architecture) for the architectural target.

## Mushi Mushi goes AGPLv3: the honest open source story

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/blog/agplv3-relicense

---
title: "Mushi Mushi goes AGPLv3: the honest open source story"
description: Why Mushi Mushi relicensed its server to AGPLv3 while keeping every SDK MIT — the open-core reasoning, what changes for self-hosters, and what stays free.
date: 2026-06-17
---

# Mushi Mushi goes AGPLv3: the honest open source story

*Jun 17, 2026 · Kenji Sakuramoto*

---

We started Mushi Mushi with a BSL 1.1 server license, the "source-available" model HashiCorp moved Terraform to in 2023. The idea was reasonable: let anyone self-host, block unmodified SaaS competitors, and convert to Apache in 2029.

The problem: our README said "open source." Our migration guides said "MIT-licensed." The badges said `BSL 1.1`. Three things, all contradicting each other.

Worse, every time a developer read the license and realized BSL isn't OSI-approved, the credibility hit was worse than just being honest from the start.

## What we actually want

Grafana is AGPLv3. Supabase is Apache 2.0. Langfuse is MIT, with its enterprise folders under a separate license. All three built large developer communities. The common thread: they were clear. Each says what is open and under which license, and you can check it in the LICENSE file. *(Corrected 2026-10-29: this paragraph first said Supabase is AGPLv3. Its main repository is Apache 2.0.)*

We want what they have: trust from developers who can read the license and know exactly what they're getting.

## The decision

The server (`@mushi-mushi/server`, `@mushi-mushi/agents`, `@mushi-mushi/verify`) is **AGPLv3**.

- True OSI-approved open source.
- Self-hosting is and always will be free.
- The AGPLv3 network use provision (Section 13) means if you run a modified server as a SaaS, you publish your changes. This isn't punitive — it's the copyleft that keeps the ecosystem honest.
- The SDK packages (`@mushi-mushi/react`, `@mushi-mushi/vue`, etc.) remain **MIT** — embed them in anything, open or closed.
- Companies that need a non-copyleft path for hosted SaaS can obtain a [commercial license](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md) (dual licensing).

**Self-hosters:** nothing changes operationally. You were already allowed to do everything you're doing. The new license just makes that legally unambiguous and removes the 2029 date anxiety.

## What this changes

**For individual developers and teams self-hosting:** nothing. Fork it, modify it, run it for your own org.

**For companies that want to offer Mushi as a hosted service to third parties:** AGPLv3 applies. Either publish your server modifications or talk to us about a commercial license.

**For Mushi Cloud, the hosted product:** still running the same code. Now provably the same code.

**Update, Oct 22, 2026.** Two changes since this post, both in [Open source & licensing](/concepts/open-source). The console (`apps/admin`) is now AGPLv3 too, so a rebranded console can't ship closed. And we now say it more exactly: Mushi Cloud runs the same code, and carries its own tuning data (prompt wording, evaluation sets and scoring weights tuned on live traffic) as configuration. The repo keeps working default prompts, so self-hosting stays free and complete. One part of the server is not AGPLv3: the enterprise folder `packages/server/ee` (SSO, audit export, retention policies) is source-available, and production use of it needs a license.

## The honest "open source" claim

We can now say "the server is open source" and mean it. The SDKs were always MIT. The distinction is: SDK = embed anywhere; server = copyleft when you SaaS a modified version.

That's the model we committed to — documented in [Open source & licensing](/concepts/open-source).

---

*Questions? Open an issue or start a thread in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/discussions).*
