## Fixes

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/fixes

---
title: Fixes
description: The Fixes page tracks every draft pull request Mushi Mushi opened from a bug report, from the moment a fix run starts until the PR is ready or the run fails.
---

# Fixes

**Route:** `/fixes` (sidebar: **Fixes**)

The Fixes page shows every draft pull request Mushi Mushi opened from a real bug,
from the moment a fix run starts to when a PR is ready to review (or the run fails).
Multi-repo coordination rows appear when one report spans several repos.

---

## The fixes list

Tiles above the list count **Attempts (30d)**, **Reports fixed**, **In flight**,
**PRs open** and, when any exist, **Spec warnings** and why auto-fix stopped.

The table has these columns (Pipeline and CI / Agent are hidden in the compact
layout):

| Column | What it is |
| ------ | ---------- |
| **Status** | Where the attempt is, for example queued, running, completed or failed |
| **Report** | The bug the fix is for |
| **Pipeline** | The fix's stages, from dispatch to PR |
| **CI / Agent** | The PR's CI result and the agent that wrote it (a ◆ chip on Cursor Cloud rows links to the run in Cursor) |
| **Started** | When the run started |

Click a row to expand it: branch, token use, CI sync, the PDCA timeline, the
agent's rationale, the files changed, spec-validation warnings and, for Cursor
Cloud runs, the artifact gallery. The Opus review shows in the merge dialog. Coordination rows expand to the
per-repo child attempts grouped underneath.

---

## Live status

While a dispatch runs, the console follows it over a server-sent event stream
(`GET /v1/admin/fixes/dispatch/:id/stream`) and falls back to polling if the stream
drops. The stream carries run status events (started, status, completed, failed) in
the AG-UI envelope format. The server JSON-encodes every payload
([CVE-2026-29085](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-29085)) so an untrusted
string can't inject extra event frames.

---

## Spec-validation warnings

When the fix-worker runs `validateAgainstSpec()` before opening a PR and finds
soft issues — e.g. the diff doesn't touch any file that references the contract's
required DB table — the warnings land in `fix_attempts.spec_validation_warnings`
and appear under **Spec validation warnings** when you expand the fix row, and in
the **Spec warnings** tile above the list.

Hard errors (removing a json_path field the contract asserts on) abort the run
before the PR opens.

---

## Cursor Cloud Agent runs

When `agent = cursor_cloud`, the fix row shows two additional UI elements:

- **Cursor badge**: a ◆ `bc-…` chip that links to the agent run in Cursor's web interface.
- **Artifact gallery**: screenshots, videos and log files the agent produced during the run, fetched after the run ends.

The artifact gallery is visible in the expanded fix detail when artifacts are present.

### Notes-only pull requests

A cloud agent (Cursor or the GitHub Copilot agent) that cannot find the cause
is told to finish without a pull request. If it opens one anyway, Mushi reads
the PR's changed files before trusting it. A PR whose changes are only notes
is not a fix. Notes are a `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` file, a new markdown file, or
TODO comments. Editing an existing doc page counts as a real change, and so
does any `.txt` file such as `requirements.txt`.

The GitHub Copilot agent opens its draft PR before it pushes anything. So
while an agent is still working, a PR with no files or only notes is attached
to the fix but not judged yet. The report does not move and nobody is
notified. The PR is judged on the files the agent left once the agent
finishes. An empty PR from a finished agent also needs investigation.

When the PR is not a fix:

- the fix row is marked **needs investigation** (`failure_category:
  validation_rejected`) and keeps the PR link so you can read the notes and
  close the PR;
- the report keeps its status instead of moving to **Fixing**;
- your team gets the usual "fix failed" notification.

Mushi reads the files with the project's GitHub token. If it cannot read them
while the agent is still working (GitHub errors, rate limits, a missing
token), the PR waits like an empty one and is read again when the agent
finishes. If the files still cannot be read after the agent has finished, the
PR is trusted and the fix timeline says the contents were not checked.

## Dispatching a fix

You can dispatch a fix from three places:

1. **Report detail** → "Dispatch fix" button (single-repo or auto multi-repo).
   A report with no stack trace, source file or failed request (most web
   vitals and native crashes) leads with "Not a code bug" instead, and the
   button reads "Dispatch anyway": a fix agent usually has nothing to change.
2. **Bugs list** → the **Dispatch fix →** button on a row, which first shows a
   preflight of what is needed.
3. **MCP / A2A / CLI**: `dispatch_fix` tool (`agent=cursor_cloud`), `POST /v1/a2a/tasks`, or `mushi fix  --agent cursor_cloud`.

All paths produce the same `fix_dispatch_jobs` row and emit the same
`fix.dispatched` webhook to subscribed plugins.

When a project has more than one linked repo, pick the repo the PR opens
against: the **Repo** select beside "Dispatch fix" (it starts on the primary
repo), `targetRepoId` on `dispatch_fix` and `POST /v1/admin/fixes/dispatch`, or
`mushi fix  --repo <repoId|owner/name>`. Without it, the fix goes to
the primary repo; another project's repo id is refused with
`400 TARGET_REPO_NOT_IN_PROJECT`.

---

## Webhooks

| Event | When |
| ----- | ---- |
| `fix.requested` | Immediately after a fix dispatch is requested (pre-agent launch) |
| `fix.dispatched` | Immediately after the dispatch row is created and agent has started |
| `fix.proposed` | Orchestrator opens a draft PR (Cursor or standard agent) |
| `fix.applied` | Fix completed and PR is merged |
| `fix.failed` | Orchestrator exhausted retries |

Configure webhook endpoints by installing a webhook plugin on
[Plugins](/admin/marketplace) (`/marketplace`). Each delivery is logged with its
status, latency and the start of the response.

---

## CI feedback on open PRs

When a fix-worker or Cursor agent opens a draft PR, GitHub Actions runs on the branch.
The fix detail card shows a **CI badge** with the latest check-run conclusion
(`success`, `failure`, `pending`, etc.).

| Control | What it does |
| ------- | ------------ |
| **Refresh CI status** | Calls `POST /v1/admin/fixes/:id/refresh-ci` → `ci-sync` edge function. Use when webhooks dropped or the badge is stale. |
| **View GitHub Actions log →** | Deep link to the check run on GitHub. |

A background `mushi-ci-sync-10m` pg_cron also refreshes completed attempts every
10 minutes, but on-demand refresh closes the loop immediately after you push a fix
to the PR branch.

From the CLI:

```bash
mushi fixes refresh-ci <fixId>
```

---

## Merging from the console

After CI passes (or you've reviewed manually), merge the draft PR without leaving
Mushi Mushi. This is **user-confirmed**: Mushi merges only what you merge or queue,
or what passes [verified merge](/admin/verified-merge) when you turned it on.

### Where merge appears

- **Report detail** → fix card → **Merge PR** (confirm popover)
- **Fixes list** → completed row with open PR. The **Opus: merge** filter
  (`/fixes?status=review_merge`) lists only the open PRs whose latest Opus
  review said merge; select them and use the bulk **Merge** action
  (see [Merge when ready](#merge-when-ready)).
- **Pipeline flow** on the report detail page

The UI picks the **primary fix attempt** — if a later retry failed but an earlier
attempt still has an open PR, the merge button targets the mergeable attempt, not
the failed retry.

### Merge flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant Console
  participant API
  participant GitHub
  participant DB

  You->>Console: Confirm squash merge
  Console->>API: POST /v1/admin/fixes/:id/merge
  API->>GitHub: markPullRequestReadyForReview (if draft)
  API->>GitHub: PUT /pulls/:n/merge
  API->>DB: merged_at, report → fixed
  API->>DB: reporter notification + fix.applied webhooks
  Console-->>You: Report status Fixed
```

**Draft PRs:** fix-worker opens PRs as drafts. The PR is marked ready (GitHub's
GraphQL `markPullRequestReadyForReview`, the same as `gh pr ready`) only when the
Opus review says merge on its head, so your CI runs only on an approved commit. A
console merge of a PR that is still a draft marks it ready first.

**Review gate:** while the PR's latest Opus review says **hold**, the merge is
refused unless a team member (not a viewer) overrides it in the console with a
reason. API keys (CLI, MCP) cannot override.

**Merge methods:** squash (default), merge commit, or rebase — chosen in the confirm
popover.

**Already merged:** if GitHub shows merged but the webhook was missed, merge is
idempotent — `finalizeFixMerge()` backfills `merged_at` and report status.

From the CLI (requires `mcp:write` API key):

```bash
mushi fixes merge <fixId>
mushi fixes merge <fixId> --method squash
```

### Merge when ready

The bulk **Merge** action queues the selected PRs by default (ADR 0041). Most
repos require a branch to be up to date before it merges, so merging one PR
leaves the others in that repo behind; the queue does the clicks for you:

1. One PR per repo at a time. A branch that is behind gets GitHub's
   **Update branch**; then the queue waits for CI on the new commit.
2. It merges only when the Opus review of that exact commit says **merge**
   (the update is a new commit, so Opus reviews it again first) and CI is
   green. A hold or fix-first stops the PR until you decide.
3. A merge conflict goes to a Cursor agent on the PR's branch, with your
   review follow-up key and model, only while
   [review follow-ups](/concepts/agent-pr-review#when-the-review-says-fix-first) are on, at most twice per PR.
4. Each merge marks the report Fixed and tells the reporter, as a console
   merge does.

The **Merge when ready** panel on `/fixes` shows each queued PR, what it is
waiting for, and why one is held (red CI, an Opus "fix first" or "hold", no review). **Remove** takes a PR out. You can leave
the page; the queue runs every 5 minutes.

#### Release trains

By default (ADR 0044) approved PRs do not merge one by one. Each merge to
your main branch is a deploy and, for a mobile app, an OTA update, so the
queue batches them into a **release train**:

1. Once every 6 hours, or as soon as 15 PRs are approved, Mushi merges a
   repo's approved PRs into one `mushi/train/…` branch and opens one train
   PR that lists them. A PR that conflicts waits for the next train.
2. CI runs once, on the train. When it is green, Mushi checks each PR's
   Opus review again and merges the train PR with a merge commit. GitHub
   marks every PR in it merged, and each report is marked Fixed.
3. When the train's CI fails, Mushi retries its first half and holds back
   the rest, until it finds the PR that breaks CI. That PR is held, with the
   failing checks named.
4. Fixes for known vulnerabilities and critical bugs skip the wait and merge
   on their own.

In the **Merge when ready** panel, **Release** switches between **Batch**
(trains) and **Each PR**, and the menu sets how often a train leaves. Each
repo shows its train on the way, or when the next one leaves.

If your repo requires a linear history (or has merge commits turned off),
Mushi squash-merges the train instead, then closes each PR in it as shipped
and marks its report Fixed.

**Merge now** (in the same dialog) tries each PR once. The PRs that did not
merge stay listed above the table with GitHub's reason and a
**Merge them when ready** button.

### Prerequisites

| Requirement | Why |
| ----------- | --- |
| Fix status `completed` | Agent finished and opened a PR |
| Open PR (`pr_url`, `pr_number`) | Nothing to merge otherwise |
| GitHub connected | App installation or PAT with merge permission |
| CI green (recommended) | Merge popover warns on failing checks; you can override |

## Full-stack audit

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/fullstack-audit

---
title: Full-stack audit
description: The Full-stack audit in Mushi Mushi runs one health check across RLS gaps, recent backend errors and API contract drift, and returns a readable scorecard.
---

# Full-stack audit

**Route:** `/fullstack-audit` (sidebar: Checks › Full-stack audit)

The Full-stack audit reads your app's Supabase backend and every Mushi Mushi check in one pass.

**First on the page:** one sentence with the exact number of open errors and
warnings (counted on the server, not from the capped list) and **Copy fix prompt
for the top finding**: the check, the file and line, the rule and what to do, ready
to paste into your editor. Every finding in the list has its own **Copy fix
prompt**. The list says "at least" only when it could not get an exact count, and
then says why (only the newest 500 findings were read).

**Known holes in your dependencies** (vuln-watch, [known holes](/concepts/known-holes))
are listed and managed at the end of this page (`#dependency-holes`). Mushi health →
Code size links here instead of repeating them.

> **Scenario:** It's Monday standup. You need a PM-readable health scorecard —
> RLS gaps, recent backend errors, API contract drift — without opening five
> different tabs.

One **Run audit** button calls `POST /v1/admin/projects/:id/audit` and
returns a severity-ranked scorecard.

---

## Scorecard sections

| Check | What it surfaces |
|-------|------------------|
| **Backend link** | Supabase PAT + project ref configured |
| **DB advisors** | Security + performance findings from Supabase MCP |
| **RLS gaps** | Tables without row-level security |
| **Error log** | Recent backend ERROR-level log count |
| **Gate runs** | The newest run of every check in the last 7 days, by name: the eight inventory gates, schema drift, code health, the recipe drift checks (design, CI, deploy, env vars), Mushi setup checks, the app hole checks and the store review checklist |

If a part of the audit could not be read (the settings, the advisors, the logs,
the table list or the gate runs), the page lists it and the verdict reads
**Incomplete**, never **All clear**. A count Mushi could not read is shown as
`—`, not `0`.

---

## Open findings by check

Below the scorecard, every open finding of each check's newest run is listed
with its rule, file and line. This list is available on **every plan**; it
reads `GET /v1/admin/inventory/:projectId/findings`, the same data as the MCP
tool `list_gate_findings`. Running gates, crawls and test generation still need
a plan with the inventory features.

### Mushi setup checks and "Apply suggested caps"

Once a day Mushi checks its own setup for each app (gate `radar`): a provider
key the provider now rejects, a webhook that never delivered, a stale code
index, and **missing spend caps**. The spend-cap check flags a project with no
monthly AI budget, and auto-fix limits that are not set (a warning while
auto-fix is on, a note while it is off).

That finding has an **Apply suggested caps** button. It shows each cap before
anything changes:

- a monthly AI budget of about twice your last 30 days of AI spend, at least
  $10, so it does not stop triage on the day you apply it;
- $2 of auto-fix spend per 30 days and 3 automatic fixes a day.

The suggestion comes from the last daily check, so the button reads your
current settings first, and again when you confirm. A cap someone set since the
check ran is left as it is, and the dialog names it. If every suggested cap is
already set, nothing is sent. If the current settings cannot be read, nothing is
sent either. The button saves the remaining caps through
`PATCH /v1/admin/settings` and needs a signed-in project admin, so an API key or
MCP client cannot apply them. Change or clear them any time in
**Settings → General → Spend limits**. The finding clears on the next daily
check.

---

## Prerequisites

Set the Supabase project ref under **Settings → General → Your database → Supabase project**,
then add a scoped Supabase access token under **Settings → AI keys → Supabase**:
this one project only, with Database, Edge Functions, Advisors and Logs set to
Read, and an expiry. CLI equivalent: `mushi audit`.

---

## CLI

```bash
mushi audit
mushi audit --json
mushi audit --project-id <uuid>
```

## Bug clusters (knowledge graph)

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/graph

---
title: Bug clusters (knowledge graph)
description: The Bug clusters page in Mushi Mushi graphs your bug groups, components, pages and fixes, so you see which bugs share a cause and what one fix might touch.
---

# Bug clusters (knowledge graph)

**Route:** `/graph` (sidebar: **Bug clusters**, under Bugs; the page was called Knowledge graph before)

The Bug clusters page draws the Mushi Mushi knowledge graph for your project: bug groups,
the components and pages they hit, and the fixes made for them. It is the quickest way
to see which bugs share a cause, so one fix can close several reports.

The page has three tabs:

| Tab | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Overview** | A status banner, a summary of the most fragile areas, and how the map relates to Reports and Inventory |
| **Explore** | The map itself, as a **Graph**, a **Surface** (inventory overlay) or a **Table** |
| **Backend** | Apache AGE sync status, ontology tags and node groups, for debugging |

---

## Node types

| Node | What it is |
| ---- | ---------- |
| **Report group** | A group of similar reports |
| **Component** | A component reports were classified against |
| **Page** | A page reports came from |
| **Version** / **App** | The app and the version a report came from |
| **Page (inventory)**, **Element**, **Action** | Nodes from your `inventory.yaml` |
| **API**, **Database** | Backend dependencies from the inventory |
| **Test**, **User story** | Tests and user stories from the inventory |

Edges carry a type such as `causes`, `related_to`, `regression_of`, `duplicate_of`,
`affects`, `fix_attempted`, `fix_applied`, `fix_verified`, and the inventory edges
`contains`, `triggers`, `calls`, `reads`, `writes`, `reports_against` and `errors_on`.
The filters let you narrow both lists. Nodes with no links are hidden, and the canvas
says how many.

---

## Blast radius

Click any node (or focus it with Tab and press Enter or Space) to load its blast
radius: every node it can affect through the graph. The canvas dims everything else,
and the side panel lists the affected nodes along with the node's occurrences and when
it was first and last seen.

---

## Surface view

Choose **Surface** on the Explore tab to overlay your `inventory.yaml` on the bug graph:
user stories, inventory pages, elements, actions, API and database dependencies, tests
and apps, together with report groups.

Surface needs at least one accepted `inventory.yaml` proposal. See
[User stories · Inventory](/admin/inventory) for how to generate one.

---

## Backend tab

The graph is stored in SQL tables and can be mirrored into the Apache AGE Postgres
extension. The **Graph backend** card shows the backend mode (**SQL only**,
**SQL + AGE (dual-write)** or **AGE only**), whether the AGE extension is installed,
how many nodes and edges are not yet mirrored, and when the last drift audit ran.

  There is no Cypher query console in the console. To query the graph by hand, use the
  [SQL query](/admin/query) page (`graph_nodes`, `graph_edges`), or ask a blast-radius
  question there in plain English.

---

## API

```bash
GET /v1/admin/graph/stats
GET /v1/admin/graph/nodes
GET /v1/admin/graph/edges
GET /v1/admin/graph/blast-radius/:nodeId
```

- [User stories · Inventory](/admin/inventory): the inventory that Surface overlays.
- [Bugs](/admin/reports): open the detail view for any report.

## Mushi health

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/health

---
title: Mushi health
description: The Mushi health page shows whether Mushi Mushi itself works (AI calls, background jobs, provider connections), so you catch a degraded integration early.
---

# Mushi health

**Route:** `/health` (the sidebar called it "App health" until October 2026)

This page is about Mushi Mushi itself, not your app: the AI calls behind your diagnoses
and fixes, Mushi's background jobs, and live provider connectivity. Use it to catch
degradation before it surfaces as a user-facing bug. Your own app's uptime and
errors are on **Home**.

The page has four views, picked at the top: **Mushi’s AI & jobs** (described below),
**[Code size](/admin/code-health)**, **[Schema changes](/admin/drift)** and
**[Unusual spikes](/admin/anomalies)**. Inside **Mushi’s AI & jobs**, the tabs are
**Overview**, **AI calls**, **Scheduled jobs** and **Recent traces**.

---

## Time window

Use the **Last hour / Last 24h / Last 7 days** picker to scope the AI-call stats and
charts to a time window. The window is persisted in the URL (`?window=`).

---

## LLM health summary

The top section shows aggregate stats across all LLM-touching pipelines for the selected
window:

| Stat | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Total calls** | Number of `llm_invocations` rows in window |
| **Fallback rate** | % of calls that used a fallback model |
| **Error rate** | % of calls that returned an error |
| **Speed avg / p95** | Average and 95th-percentile response time |

Below the summary, a **per-function breakdown** table shows calls, avg/p95 latency, cost
(USD), fallback count, errors, and last failure time for each edge function
(`fix-worker`, `classify-report`, `judge-batch`, `pdca-runner`, etc.).

A **per-model breakdown** table shows calls, token count, and errors for each LLM model
in use.

---

## Provider probes

On the **Recent traces** tab, two cards test the Anthropic and OpenAI keys set on the
Mushi Mushi server (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`). They do not test the
BYOK keys you add in Settings.

| Provider | What's tested |
|----------|--------------|
| **Anthropic** | A 1-token `POST /v1/messages` call: confirms the key works and can reach the probe model |
| **OpenAI** | `GET /v1/models/`: confirms the key and its access to the model, and costs nothing |

Each card shows a **status badge** (`ok`, `degraded`, `down` or `unknown`), the
**latency**, and the **last probed** time. Click **Probe now** to run the test on demand.

---

## Cron job health

The **Scheduled jobs** tab has a card for each background job: `judge-batch`,
`intelligence-report` and `data-retention`. Each shows:

- **Last run** timestamp and a staleness note when a run is late
- **Run count**, **success rate** and **average duration**, read from the most recent
  100 job runs (not filtered by the time window)

Click **Trigger now** on `judge-batch` or `intelligence-report` to run it immediately.
It spends AI budget, and only admins can use it. `data-retention` has no manual trigger.

---

## Recent LLM calls log

The **Recent traces** tab lists the most recent `llm_invocations` rows for this project,
with the time, function name, model, fallback and error badges, key source (when it is not
the server key), latency, token count, and a link to the Langfuse trace when one was recorded.

Use the **Show** filter (`all / errors / fallbacks`) to isolate problem calls. The URL
param `?recent=` persists the filter. The list auto-updates via a realtime subscription.

---

## Recommended actions

On the **Overview** tab, the summary reads **Critical probes failing**, **Degraded
probes** or **All systems nominal**, from the count of red and amber signals on the page.
When something needs you (error rate, a fallback spike, a failed or late job, or no AI
calls at all in the window), a recommended next step appears with a link.

---

- [Settings](/admin/settings) — configure BYOK keys
- [Improvement runs](/admin/iterate) — the highest per-run LLM cost driver
- [Fixes](/admin/fixes) — fix-worker call detail

## To-do

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/inbox

---
title: To-do
description: The To-do page gathers everything in Mushi Mushi that needs a human decision, like urgent reports, failed fixes, queue failures and health alerts, in one list.
---

# To-do

**Route:** `/inbox` (sidebar: **More pages › Bugs › To-do**, or keep it in the sidebar as a Lab from Settings → Display & sidebar)

> **Scenario:** It's Monday morning. You open Mushi Mushi and want to know in one
> glance what actually needs a human decision right now, without clicking through
> Bugs, Processing jobs and Mushi health separately to piece it together.

To-do is your list across the whole loop: every action that still needs you, in one
prioritised view. It has three tabs: **Overview** (every open card, top to bottom),
**Stages** (filter by step, open and cleared cards together) and **Activity** (the
recent reports and fixes behind the counts).

---

## How it works

The cards come from `GET /v1/admin/dashboard`, and the status line and tab title from
`GET /v1/admin/inbox/stats`. The page stays open (never "All clear") while any critical
or high report is unfixed, including Sentry imports the classifier has already tagged.
Every card you see is a state in the pipeline that Mushi has identified as requiring a
human decision or awareness. A page you opened before shows its last data at once and
refreshes behind it.

---

## Reading an action card

Each card has four parts:

| Part | Example |
|------|---------|
| **PDCA stage chip** | `PLAN` (triage backlog), `DO` (failed fix), `OPS` (dead-letter item) |
| **Page label** | The page that owns the action |
| **Action title** | "2 critical reports need triage", "3 reports still unfixed after an auto-fix attempt" |
| **Reason** | One line on why it matters |

The **primary action button** takes you directly to the page with the relevant item
pre-selected. You never need to search.

---

## Cleared stages strip

Below the open cards, a row of chips shows every pipeline stage that currently has
**nothing pending**, with a ✓ badge. When all chips are checked and there are no open
cards, the page reads **All clear**.

Click any cleared chip to navigate to that page and verify the state yourself.

---

## Filtering by stage

On the **Stages** tab, the filter chips focus on one part of the loop. **All**,
**Open** and **Clear** filter by state; the stage chips appear only for stages that
have cards:

| Filter | Shows |
|--------|-------|
| **All** | Every card, open and cleared |
| **Open** | Cards that still need you |
| **Clear** | Stages with nothing pending |
| **Plan** | Classify and triage |
| **Do** | Dispatch and land fixes |
| **Check** | Verify quality |
| **Act** | Connections and config |
| **Ops** | Health and compliance |

---

## Common tasks

### Morning triage (the fast path)
1. Open To-do. Look at the **Open** count.
2. If it's 0, everything is cleared. Home is the next stop.
3. If not, scan the cards top to bottom; the most urgent comes first.
4. Click the primary action on each card to resolve it.
5. Click **Refresh**: cleared cards disappear as you resolve them.

### When To-do seems wrong
If you resolved an issue but the card is still showing, click **Refresh** to fetch
the counts again.

---

To-do is a read-only view: it doesn't take actions itself. Every primary action
button navigates to the page that owns the action, so actions are logged on their
source page, not here.

---

## Related pages

- [Home](/admin/dashboard): the summary page for one app
- [Bugs](/admin/reports): source of Plan cards
- [Processing jobs](/admin/queue): source of queue-failure cards
- [Mushi health](/admin/health): source of health-probe cards

## Integrations

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/integrations

---
title: Integrations
description: Set up Mushi Mushi integrations on one page. Open fix pull requests on GitHub, send bugs to Linear, Jira or GitHub Issues, alert Slack and import Sentry errors.
---

# Integrations

**Route:** `/integrations/config` (sidebar: **Integrations**, under Connect)

> **Scenario:** You just set up Mushi Mushi and want fix PRs to open on your GitHub repo,
> new bugs to land in Linear, and Sentry errors to flow in, all from one page.

The Integrations page wires Mushi Mushi to the tools your team already uses. Every
integration is optional except GitHub, which fixes need.

The top of the page shows which tools are connected, what is broken, and the next step.

---

## Sections

| Section | Cards |
| --- | --- |
| **Your code** | GitHub (code repo) |
| **Alerts** | Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams |
| **Fix agent** | Cursor Cloud, Claude Code Agent, plus the codebase index, a dry-run panel and **Deployment readiness** |
| **Issue trackers** | Linear, Jira, GitHub Issues, PagerDuty |
| **Errors you already catch (optional)** | Sentry; Langfuse under **Advanced: trace Mushi's AI calls in your own Langfuse** |

At the foot of the page are links to [Editor agents](/admin/mcp), [Agent skills](/admin/skill-pipelines),
[Reporter updates](/admin/notifications) and [Plugins](/admin/marketplace).

---

## GitHub (code repo)

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Repo URL** | The repo Mushi Mushi opens fix PRs against (SSH URLs are normalized) |
| **Default branch** | Base branch for fix PRs; `main` when blank |
| **Installation token** | A GitHub App installation token (preferred) or a fine-grained PAT with Contents: write and Pull requests: write |
| **Webhook secret** | Optional HMAC secret; set the same value on the repo's webhook (events: Check runs, Check suites) |

The **Codebase index** card shows the indexing status for the active project's repo:
`ok`, `stale`, `failed`, `off`, or `never`. The index powers the [Pull requests page](/admin/repo)
and the fix agent's code context. It also shows coverage in files against your plan's
file limit (see [how much of a large repo is indexed](/admin/explore#how-much-of-a-large-repo-is-indexed)).
For a repo connected with a Personal Access Token, it shows the webhook URL that turns on push indexing.

## Fix agents

### Cursor Cloud

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **API Key** | Your Cursor API key (`crsr_…`), stored encrypted in Supabase Vault; never shown again in the UI |
| **Default model** | Optional Cursor model id (for example `composer-2.5`); blank uses your Cursor account default |
| **Auto-create PRs** | On by default: Cursor opens a signed draft PR when the agent finishes. Turn off to review the branch first. |

With a key saved, Mushi Mushi can dispatch a Cursor Cloud agent to fix a classified
report; the agent opens a signed draft PR and the link shows on the [Fixes page](/admin/fixes).
For event-driven dispatch, install the _Cursor Cloud Agent_ plugin from
[Plugins](/admin/marketplace).

The API Key is stored via Supabase Vault. The raw key is never written to any database column. For self-hosted deployments where Supabase Vault is not accessible from the Node orchestrator, set `MUSHI_CURSOR_API_KEY_OVERRIDE` in your Node orchestrator environment as an escape hatch.

### Claude Code Agent

A GitHub Actions workflow for your repo that runs the Claude Code CLI on a fix prompt,
commits a fix branch and opens a draft PR, with your Anthropic key kept in your GitHub
secrets. Mushi Mushi checks the key and gives you the workflow, but it does **not**
trigger the workflow yet: you run it yourself with a `repository_dispatch` event. To have
Mushi Mushi open fix PRs on its own, use Cursor Cloud or the GitHub cloud agent.

## Sentry

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Org slug** | Your Sentry organization |
| **Project slug** | Optional; narrows event search to one project |
| **More Sentry projects** | Optional; up to 10 more projects this app reports to, for import |
| **Auth token** | `project:read` + `event:read` (import, enrichment) and `event:write` (resolve on merge) |
| **DSN (optional)** | Only needed if you want Mushi Mushi reports forwarded as Sentry events |
| **Webhook secret** | The Client Secret of the Sentry internal integration whose webhook URL is the **Receive URL** shown on the card |

## Langfuse (advanced)

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Host** | Langfuse base URL (US cloud, EU cloud, or self-hosted) |
| **Public key** | Langfuse project public key |
| **Secret key** | Langfuse project secret key |

When configured, Mushi Mushi's AI calls send traces to your own Langfuse project.

## Card controls

Each card shows its connection state, when it was last probed, and a short health
sparkline. **Test connection** runs a live probe and reports the result as a toast;
**Edit credentials** (or **Configure integration**) opens the form. Only admins can edit.

---

## Issue trackers

| Destination | What it does |
|-------------|-----------------|
| **Linear** | Creates a Linear issue for a new `critical` or `high` report; when the Linear issue is completed or cancelled, the report is resolved |
| **Jira** | Creates a Jira issue for a new `critical` or `high` report, with severity mapped to Jira priority |
| **GitHub Issues** | Opens a GitHub Issue for a new `critical` or `high` report, with severity and category labels; closes it when the report is resolved |
| **PagerDuty** | Pages on-call (Events API v2) for `critical` reports only; resolves the incident when the report is closed |

Each routing card has **Test connection**, a **Pause / Resume** toggle and **Disconnect**.
While paused, new reports are not forwarded to it.

**Connecting a routing provider:**
1. Click **Connect**.
2. Enter the required credentials (for Jira: base URL, user email, API token, project key;
   for GitHub Issues: PAT with Issues: write, owner, repo; for PagerDuty: routing key).
3. Click **Save**, then **Test connection**.

For more event routing (Discord, Teams, Zapier and more, or your own webhooks), use
[Plugins](/admin/marketplace). The trackers here are pre-built connectors.

---

## Common tasks

### Connecting GitHub so the fix agent can open PRs
1. Install the Mushi Mushi GitHub App on your repo, or create a fine-grained PAT with
   Contents: write and Pull requests: write.
2. On the **GitHub (code repo)** card, click **Configure integration**.
3. Enter the repo URL, default branch and the installation token.
4. Click **Save**, then **Test connection**, and confirm the probe returns green.
5. Open [Pull requests](/admin/repo): the header should show your connected repo.

### Bringing Sentry errors into Mushi Mushi
1. On the **Sentry** card, click **Configure integration**.
2. Enter your org slug, auth token, and optionally the project slug.
3. Click **Save**, then **Test connection**.
4. For live delivery, create a Sentry internal integration whose webhook URL is the card's
   **Receive URL**, and paste its Client Secret as the **Webhook secret**.

### Routing critical reports to PagerDuty
1. In **Issue trackers**, find PagerDuty and click **Connect**.
2. Enter your Events API v2 routing key.
3. Click **Save**, then **Test connection**.
4. The next report classified `critical` pages your on-call.

### Setting up Cursor Cloud auto-fix
1. Create a Cursor API key at [cursor.com/dashboard/integrations](https://cursor.com/dashboard/integrations) → API Keys.
2. Connect **GitHub (code repo)** first: Cursor agents need your repo URL and token.
3. On the **Cursor Cloud** card, click **Configure integration**, paste the `crsr_…` key, then **Save** → **Test connection**.
4. Install the **Cursor Cloud Agent** plugin from [Plugins](/admin/marketplace) (subscribe to `report.classified`) for automatic dispatch.
5. Dispatch a fix on a report: the [Fixes page](/admin/fixes) shows the Cursor agent badge and PR link once the run completes.

## Weekly insights

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/intelligence

---
title: Weekly insights
description: Weekly insights is the Mushi Mushi plain-English bug digest per app, with bug trends, fix velocity and what to check next, in the console and optionally Slack.
---

# Weekly insights

**Route:** `/dashboard?view=insights` (**Home → Weekly insights**). The old `/intelligence`
link redirects there. It was called Intelligence reports before October 2026.

Mushi Mushi writes a **weekly bug digest** for each app: an AI-written summary of the
week's bug trends, fix velocity and areas of concern, with two or three recommendations.
You read it in the console, print it to PDF, and can have it posted to Slack.

The view has three tabs: **Summary**, **Reports** and **Jobs**.

---

## What's in a report

The digest is written from the week's data:

- reports by category, severity and component
- fix attempts and how they ended
- the grader's weekly scores (see [Triage grading](/admin/judge))
- anonymised benchmarks from other projects, only if you opted in and enough projects
  contribute (see below)

The AI writes the summary, so its exact sections vary from week to week.

---

## Schedule and delivery

The `intelligence-report` function runs every **Monday at 06:00 UTC**. Each report is
stored as HTML and listed on the **Reports** tab.

| Channel | How it works |
| ------- | ------------ |
| **In the console** | **Reports** lists every stored digest. Open one to read it |
| **PDF** | Open a report and use the browser's print dialog to save it as PDF |
| **Slack** | Posted when the project has a Slack webhook set |

Mushi Mushi does not email the digest.

---

## Generating on demand

Click **Generate this week** to run the digest for the current app now. The **Jobs** tab
shows each generation job with its status and error, and you can cancel a running job.
Generation is limited to 20 per hour. A run is skipped, with a reason, when no usable AI
key is configured.

---

## Cross-customer benchmarks

Benchmarks are opt-in, from the card on the **Summary** tab. When you opt in, the digest
can compare your app with anonymised aggregates from other Mushi Mushi projects. A
comparison is only shown when at least 5 projects contribute to it (k-anonymity).

---

## Jobs tab

Besides generation jobs, the **Jobs** tab lists pending library modernization findings,
which you can dispatch as a fix or dismiss.

---

## See also

- [SQL query](/admin/query) — ad-hoc questions against the same data.
- [Triage grading](/admin/judge) — the grading trend the digest reads.
- [Self-hosting → Observability (Langfuse + Sentry)](/self-hosting/observability) — trace the AI calls that write the digest.

## User stories · Inventory

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/inventory

---
title: 'User stories · Inventory'
description: The User stories page in the Mushi Mushi console manages inventory.yaml, the pages, actions and stories your app should have, and shows which the gates cover.
---

# User stories · Inventory

**Route:** `/inventory` (sidebar: Checks › User stories)

The **User stories** page in Mushi Mushi is the v2 positive
side of the loop. Where Reports / Graph / Fixes catch what your users
*felt* break, the inventory describes what should *exist* — every page,
every action, every expected outcome — so the gates can fail when the
two diverge.

  User stories needs a plan that includes it. On such a plan it is listed under
  **Checks** in the sidebar; otherwise its card on [Checks](/admin/checks) shows an
  Upgrade pill.

## What you see

With no map yet, the page is one step: **Turn on discovery** (it opens the
Discovery tab with the SDK snippet). Writing the map file by hand is the
other way in.

Once the map exists:

1. **Status sentence** across the top: how many actions are broken (stopped
   working, or no code behind them yet) and how many a test proves, with
   **Check every action** and **Crawl the app**.
2. **Your app, page by page**: one card per page with what a user can do
   on it. Broken actions are red and sort first; pages with a broken
   action come first.
3. **Story cards**: one per user story (`signup`, `pricing`, …) with
   per-story counts and a **⋯** menu for runs scoped to that story.
4. **Action drawer**: click any action to inspect its `expected_outcome`,
   the last walk and its history.

The tabs are **User stories**, **All actions** (the page × element table),
**Code checks** (open findings, `?tab=gates`), **Live probes**
(`?tab=synthetic`), **Out of sync** (`?tab=drift`), **Discovery** and
**Map file** (`?tab=yaml`). The `?tab=` ids are unchanged, so old links work.

## Check every action / Crawl the app

The status line has one **Check every action** and one **Crawl the app**
for the whole project. They call the same server routes the GitHub
Action uses ([`@mushi-mushi/mcp-ci`](/sdks/mcp-ci)):

- **Check every action** runs the server-side checks: status claims, API contract,
  unused backend endpoints and calls to unknown endpoints. Results show on the
  **Code checks** tab.
  It posts nothing to a pull request: the lint checks (dead handlers, mock data)
  need your ESLint report, which only the GitHub Action sends.
- **Crawl the app** crawls every page in the map and reconciles it with
  `inventory.yaml`. Differences land in the *Out of sync* tab.

To run just one story, open the **⋯** menu on its card:

- **Crawl this story's pages** — crawls only the pages linked to that story.
- **Run gates on this story** — runs the gates on that story's actions only.

## SDK-driven discovery

Most teams will never hand-author `inventory.yaml`. Turn on
`capture.discoverInventory` in the SDK config:

```ts
import { MushiProvider } from '@mushi-mushi/react'

<MushiProvider config={{
  projectId: '…',
  apiKey: '…',
  capture: { discoverInventory: true },
}}>
  <App />
</MushiProvider>
```

The SDK quietly observes routes, `data-testid`s, and outbound API paths
in production. Claude drafts a candidate `inventory.yaml` from the
stream every 24 h and the **Discovery** tab surfaces the diff for
review. You accept, edit, or skip — the production payload itself
never contains user data.

## Surface mode in the graph

The same inventory powers a **Surface** toggle on the
[Knowledge graph](/admin/graph) — every Page / Element / Action node
overlaid on the live bug graph so the dead corners (high-traffic
elements with no `expected_outcome`) light up.

## The gates

The GitHub Action rolls these into one composite check. The **Code checks**
tab lists their findings under the names in the first column:

| Gate (console name)            | Id               | What it checks |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------- | -------------- |
| **Dead handlers**              | `dead_handler`   | ESLint `mushi-mushi/no-dead-handler`: buttons and links whose handler does nothing. Needs your ESLint report from CI |
| **Mock data in production**    | `mock_leak`      | ESLint `mushi-mushi/no-mock-leak`: faker or placeholder data in non-test paths. Needs your ESLint report from CI |
| **API contract**               | `api_contract`   | Frontend calls whose request or response does not match the API (server side) |
| **Live route crawl**           | `crawl`          | Every page in the map loaded live; runs through **Crawl the app**, not as part of the composite check |
| **Status claims**              | `status_claim`   | Actions marked `verified` or `wired` in the map whose derived status disagrees |
| **Unused backend endpoints**   | `orphan_endpoint`| Backend endpoints nothing calls |
| **Calls to unknown endpoints** | `unknown_call`   | Frontend calls to endpoints the backend does not have |

## Watch your live site

**Discovery → Watch your live site** asks Firecrawl to crawl your live site once a day, following your site's own links from the address you enter. Mushi files a bug report, before a user finds the problem, for each page that:

- returns a server error (5xx);
- returns a 404 or another 4xx from a link on your own site (sign-in walls and rate limits don't count);
- fails to load;
- changed in a way Firecrawl's checker calls broken: an error message, a blank page, or missing main content. Normal wording and layout edits are ignored.

Pages your `robots.txt` blocks, links that only differ by `?utm_…` parameters, and pages you removed are not reported.

A page has to fail twice before it becomes a report. When a check finds a broken page, Mushi loads that page again, waits about 10 seconds for it to finish loading, and files only if it is still broken. A page caught mid-load (a loading screen, only a "Skip to content" link, a status line waiting on a request) is not a broken page. A server error or a page that won't load also files when two checks in a row see it. If your whole site is down, Mushi files one report within the hour. Two cases file at low severity: a page Firecrawl's checker keeps calling broken that Mushi can't load again to confirm (marked "unconfirmed"), and a server error that keeps coming back but loads fine each time Mushi looks again (3 times in 7 days, marked "intermittent"). These second loads use your app's own Firecrawl key: at most 6 per hourly read, shared across your apps, 1 credit each.

Each broken page files one report. When 5 or more pages break at once (the site is down, or a deploy broke a shared layout), they file one report that lists them all. While a page stays broken, Mushi doesn't file again. When it is no longer broken, it leaves the "Broken right now" list; its report stays as it is for you to close. If it breaks again later, it has to fail twice again before it files.

**Check now** runs a check straight away, and results show in 1 to 3 minutes. Each app can run 6 checks an hour this way; the daily check always runs.

The watch uses your Firecrawl key, or a key shared with all your apps. It costs 1 credit per page per day, about 750 a month for 25 pages. Firecrawl's own estimate is up to twice that, because it holds back 1 credit per page for checking changed pages. **Turn off** deletes the crawl in Firecrawl and needs the key to do so; reports already filed stay. Only public pages are checked; flows behind sign-in belong in [QA stories](/admin/qa-coverage).

The crawler sends `MushiSiteWatch` in its `User-Agent` header (`MushiSiteWatch/1.0 (+https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi)`, after a normal Chrome user agent). Filter that string out of Sentry and your analytics so the daily check doesn't count as visitors or errors, for example by dropping events in Sentry's `beforeSend` when the request's user agent contains `MushiSiteWatch`. The header is on the HTTP request; don't rely on `navigator.userAgent` showing it. A watch turned on before this header was added starts sending it the next time you save it or turn it off and on.

## Synthetic monitor

Mushi re-walks the inventory's `expected_outcome` checks against your
staging URL every 15 minutes once you enable it. The monitor is
**fail-closed by default**: write paths (POST / PUT / DELETE actions)
are skipped unless you turn on **Allow mutations** for the project in
**Map file → Crawler & probes** (the `synthetic_monitor_allow_mutations`
project setting; it is not an `inventory.yaml` key).

Set this only when staging is fully isolated from production and the
write endpoints have an idempotency key or roll back cleanly.

## Spec traceability — every fix carries the originating Action

As of the 2026-05-09 release every fix dispatched against a report that
has been linked to an inventory `Action` (via the `reports_against`
graph edge `classify-report` writes) carries that link end-to-end:

- The dispatch row (`fix_dispatch_jobs.inventory_action_node_id`) and
  the resulting attempt (`fix_attempts.inventory_action_node_id`) both
  store the FK to the `graph_nodes` row for the originating Action.
- The fix-worker LLM prompt includes a Markdown spec-context block
  with the action description, page, story, and every assertion in
  the contract — see
  [Concepts → Spec traceability — read AND write side](/concepts/inventory-and-gates#spec-traceability--read-and-write-side).
- A deterministic `validateAgainstSpec` gate runs before the PR opens.
  Soft warnings (no changed file references the contract's required
  DB table or page route) land on
  `fix_attempts.spec_validation_warnings JSONB` and surface in the
  fix's detail panel under **Spec validation warnings**.
- A targeted post-PR synthetic probe is queued for the originating
  Action immediately after the PR opens. The synthetic-monitor cron
  drains the queue with priority on its next tick — so a fix that
  immediately makes the action `regressed` shows up here within
  minutes of merge, not on the next 15-min reconciler sweep.

External AI agents (Cursor, Claude Code, OpenAI Agents SDK,
LangGraph, CrewAI, A2A v1.0.0) get the same anchor — see
[Connecting your AI agent](/concepts/orchestrator-interop) for the
per-surface details.

## Improvement runs

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/iterate

---
title: Improvement runs
description: The Improvement runs page in Mushi Mushi queues runs where one AI critiques a live URL against your goal and a second scores it, iteration by iteration.
---

# Improvement runs

**Route:** `/iterate` (sidebar: More pages → Fix → Improvement runs; formerly Iterate. It is a Lab: switch it on under **Settings → Display & sidebar → Labs** to keep it in the sidebar)

> **Scenario:** Your app's UX scores have been declining in session recordings. You
> suspect the onboarding flow has friction but don't know where. Instead of spending
> a day manually testing every screen, you queue an improvement run — point it at your live
> URL, describe the goal, and let the producer and judge models critique and
> score it. You come back to a scored report for each iteration.

In Mushi Mushi, the Improvement runs page runs **Plan → Do → Check → Act** scoring loops. The agent
crawls a URL, generates a quality critique across multiple dimensions (UX, performance,
accessibility, etc.), attempts improvements, re-checks the score, and loops until either
the target score is reached or the iteration limit is hit.

---

## Understanding the score

Each run produces a **final score** from 0 to 1. This is the judge model's assessment
of the target URL against the goal you described. A score of 0.85 means the judge
considers the URL 85% of the way to fully satisfying the goal.

The **score timeline** chart in the run drawer shows one bar per iteration. Increasing
bars mean the agent is making real improvements. Flat or decreasing bars mean either
the goal is too vague or the BYOK model is struggling — try a more specific goal or a
stronger model.

---

## Runs table

The left panel lists all runs, newest first. At a glance:
- **Status badge** — `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `aborted`, `failed`
- **Progress** — current / target iterations (e.g. "3/5")
- **Final score** — the bar fills as the score improves across iterations
- **Trigger** appears on a queued row, **Abort** on a queued or running row (Abort asks first)

An **auto-refresh banner** appears at the top when any run is active, polling every
4 seconds so you don't need to manually refresh.

---

## Run detail drawer

Click any run row to open the detail drawer.

### Score timeline

A bar chart with one bar per iteration. Click any bar to jump to that iteration's
detail — its critique text, per-dimension scores, and cost.

### Iterations list

Expand any iteration to see:
- **Overall score bar** for that iteration
- **Per-dimension breakdown** — separate scores for dimensions like UX clarity,
  navigation depth, content quality, error handling
- **Critique text** — the judge model's written assessment of what it found
- **Time elapsed + cost** — how long and how expensive that iteration was

### Succeeded run
When the run succeeds, a **Copy critique to clipboard** button appears. Paste this into
a GitHub issue, Notion doc, or design brief as a structured improvement report.

While a run is queued or running, the drawer reloads itself every 3 seconds. **Refresh**
in the drawer header reloads it at once.

---

## Creating a run

1. Click **+ New Run** (top of page).
2. On the **New Run** tab, fill in:

| Field | Guidance |
|-------|---------|
| **Target URL** | The live URL the agent will crawl — must be publicly reachable |
| **Goal / instructions** | Be specific: *"Improve the onboarding flow for first-time mobile users — focus on step clarity and reducing friction"* is better than *"improve UX"* |
| **Max iterations** | Default 5. More iterations cost more, with diminishing returns |
| **Target score (0–1)** | Default 0.75. 1.0 is rarely reached and will use up every iteration |
| **Producer model** | The model generating improvements: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (default), Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1 or Claude Haiku 5.5 (fastest, cheapest). If Anthropic is down the runner falls back to OpenAI on its own |
| **Judge model** | The model scoring results. Same choices, Sonnet 5.5 by default. Only Claude ids are accepted (`claude-…`) |
| **Critic persona** | The evaluation lens: Nielsen Norman (10 usability heuristics, default), WCAG 2.2 accessibility, Mobile first, Glanceable density, or Tufte data density |

3. Click **Queue run**. The run is saved as `queued`; click **Trigger** on its row in **Runs** to start it.

---

## Common tasks

### Running a UX audit before a release
1. Create a new run: target URL = your staging URL, goal = *"Identify UX friction in the checkout flow"*, max iterations = 3, target score = 0.8.
2. Click **Trigger** and let it run.
3. Open the drawer → read the final critique → **Copy critique to clipboard**.
4. File as a GitHub issue or share with your design team.

### Comparing before and after a change
1. Run a baseline before your change. Note the final score.
2. Deploy your change. Run again with identical config.
3. Compare the final scores and the per-dimension breakdown charts.
4. A higher score on the "UX clarity" dimension confirms your change worked.

### Debugging a failed run
1. Click the failed run row and check which iterations finished and what they scored.
   The console does not show the runner's error message for a failed run; the
   **Last failure** line of the readout only names the URL.
2. Common causes:
   - **LLM key not configured** → go to [Settings](/admin/settings) → **AI keys**
   - **Target URL unreachable** → check the URL returns 200 without authentication
   - **Iteration limit hit with low score** → rewrite the goal to be more specific or increase the target score threshold

---

## API

```bash
GET    /v1/admin/pdca?project_id=<pid>&limit=50
GET    /v1/admin/pdca/<id>
POST   /v1/admin/pdca   { "target_url": "...", "goal": "...", "iterations_target": 5,
                          "target_score": 0.85, "primary_model": "claude-sonnet-5-5",
                          "judge_model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "project_id": "<pid>" }
DELETE /v1/admin/pdca/<id>         (abort)
POST   /v1/admin/pdca/<id>/trigger (manually trigger queued run)
```

- [Fixes](/admin/fixes) — dispatch individual fixes outside the PDCA loop

## Triage grading

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/judge

---
title: Triage grading
description: The Triage grading page in the Mushi Mushi console shows how often a second AI agrees with each diagnosis, week by week, and the worst recent disagreements.
---

# Triage grading

**Route:** `/judge` (sidebar: **Triage grading**, under Verify; formerly Judge)

A second AI grades each diagnosis Mushi Mushi makes: was the category right, the
severity, the part of the app, and were the steps to reproduce usable. This page shows
how often it agrees, so you can tell whether to trust a diagnosis before you merge its fix.

**First on the page:** one sentence with this week's score and how often the grader
disagreed **in the last 14 days** (the window is named; an older server without it
gets "so far", all time), with **See disagreements**. Under it, **How often the grader
agrees** draws the weekly agreement share for 12 weeks, and **Worst disagreements,
last 14 days** lists the 3 lowest-scored disagreements with the grader's reason and a
link to each report. `GET /v1/admin/judge/stats` returns `recentWindowDays`,
`recentEvaluations`, `recentDisagreements` and `agreementWeeks` for this.

---

## Tabs

The page has four tabs: **Overview**, **Trend**, **Grades** and **Prompts**.

- **Trend**: **Score trend (12w)** with a bar per dimension (**Accuracy**, **Severity**,
  **Component**, **Repro**), a **Score distribution**, and a **Weekly history** table
  with the week, each dimension and the number of evaluations.
- **Grades**: **Recent evaluations**, one row per graded report with the model, the
  prompt version, each dimension and whether the grader **Agreed**. Tick
  **Disagreements only** to see the misses.
- **Prompts**: the **Prompt leaderboard** with stage, version, status (`active` or
  `candidate`), score, evaluations and traffic share. Click a row to filter Recent
  evaluations to that version.

**Run judge now** grades recent classified reports straight away. It spends AI budget.
Otherwise the judge runs nightly.

---

## Prompt promotion

You edit and A/B test prompts in [AI prompts](/admin/prompt-lab). The nightly judge
run promotes a candidate prompt on its own once it has at least 30 evaluations and its
mean score is more than 5% above the active prompt's.

---

## Drift alerts

When this week's mean score is more than 10% below last week's, the nightly judge run
records a drift alert and, if the project has a Slack webhook set, posts it to Slack.
The **Week change** figure at the top shows the same comparison.

---

## See also

- [Concepts → Judge & self-improvement](/concepts/judge-loop) — how the nightly judge, A/B testing, fine-tune export, and drift detection work together.
- [AI prompts](/admin/prompt-lab) — edit and A/B test the prompts this page grades.

## Lessons

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/lessons

---
title: Lessons
description: The Lessons page in the Mushi Mushi console turns a bug that keeps coming back into a coding rule your editor agent can read before its next fix.
---

# Lessons

**Route:** `/lessons`

> **Scenario:** Three separate users have reported that the "Save" button on the
> Settings page does nothing on iOS Safari. You've fixed each one individually over
> the past month — but the same root cause (missing `async/await` on the submit
> handler) keeps slipping through PR review. Lessons is the page that stops this
> cycle permanently.

In Mushi Mushi, a lesson is a structured coding rule extracted from a cluster of similar
bug reports. Once promoted, your editor agent can read it before it writes a fix: through
the MCP tools `query_lessons` and `list_lessons`, or from `.mushi/lessons.json` in your repo.

---

## The lifecycle: how a report becomes a rule

1. **Reports arrive** — users submit feedback via the SDK.
2. **Embeddings cluster** — reports with similar semantics are grouped into a
   **mistake cluster** automatically.
3. **Ready to promote** — once at least 3 reports share one cause and Mushi has
   suggested a rule, the pattern is ready. (Behind the scenes a pattern whose reports
   read very alike, coherence 0.75 or more, is promoted for you every 6 hours.)
4. **You promote** — open **Recurring patterns**, read the suggested rule, and click
   **Promote**. The pattern becomes a rule in use.
5. **Retrieval** — when an agent asks for lessons on a change, the best matches are
   packed into a token budget (3,000 by default), ranked by similarity, severity and
   how recent the lesson is.

Mushi Mushi does not commit `.mushi/lessons.json` to your repo by itself. Write or
refresh it with `npx @mushi-mushi/cli sync-lessons` (locally or in CI). Editor agents
read it when their rules tell them to; `mushi setup --with-rules` adds that rule.

---

## Tab: Recurring patterns (`?tab=clusters`)

The page opens here when a pattern is ready. Bugs that keep coming back with the same
cause, most reports first. Each card shows the report count, the suggested rule and
when it was last seen. **Promote** appears only where it can succeed (3 or more
reports and a suggested rule); the first one is the primary button.

**Filter to `Not a rule yet`** to see only patterns that are not rules.

For each pattern, check:
1. **Report count** — 3 or more reports describing the same cause.
2. **Suggested rule** — does it make sense as a coding instruction?
3. **Last seen** — is this still happening? If it's months old and you've shipped a fix, leave it.

A pattern of 2 reports isn't reliable enough to write a codebase rule: it reads
**Still growing** until more reports arrive.

---

## Tab: Rules in use (`?tab=lessons`)

Your active coding rules. Each row shows the severity, how many times it was seen,
the pattern it came from, and the first two lines of the rule text.

**Click any row** to open the detail drawer with the full content:

- **Rule** — the positive instruction (e.g. *"Always await the form submit handler
  before accessing `event.target` values in Safari"*)
- **What to avoid** — the specific code pattern to avoid
- **Summary** — what the original reports described
- **Learned from** — the pattern's name and report count

### When to retire a lesson

Use **Retire** when:
- The affected code has been fully refactored and the pattern no longer applies.
- The rule is generating false positives — the agent is avoiding good patterns.
- A newer, more specific lesson supersedes it.

Retired lessons are hidden from injection but preserved. Use the **Active / Retired**
toggle to review them and restore if needed.

---

## Tab: Try a change (`?tab=query`)

> **Use this when:** You've just promoted a new lesson and want to confirm it will be
> retrieved for a related change. Or you want to check that a retired lesson is no
> longer surfacing.

Paste any code diff or problem description into the textarea, set a token budget (start
with the default 3000), and click **Query lessons**. The results show what `query_lessons` would return to an
agent: rank, similarity score and the full rule text.

**Practical example:**
- Paste the diff of a recent iOS bug fix.
- Check whether the Settings submit-handler lesson appears in the top results.
- If it doesn't, the embedding may not be close enough — consider editing the lesson's
  rule text to include more specific terminology.

---

## Common tasks

### Reviewing new patterns (weekly)
1. Open **Recurring patterns**, filter to `Not a rule yet`.
2. For each pattern marked **Ready to promote**: read the suggested rule. Sensible? Click **Promote**.
3. Patterns marked **Still growing** have only 1–2 reports: leave them to collect more.

### After fixing a recurring bug
1. Open **Recurring patterns** and find the pattern for this bug.
2. If it is ready to promote, promote it.
3. Check with **Try a change** that the rule comes back for a related change.

### Cleaning up stale lessons
1. Open the **Rules in use** tab, toggle to **Active**.
2. Sort by frequency — lessons with frequency 0 in the last 30 days may be stale.
3. Click each → review the rule → **Retire** if the underlying code has changed.

---

## How retrieval works

When an agent calls `query_lessons` (or you use **Try a change**):
1. The pasted change or description is matched against the lesson store by meaning.
2. Matches are scored `0.5 × similarity + 0.3 × severity + 0.2 × recency`.
3. Lessons are packed, best first, until the token budget (default 3,000, allowed
   100 to 8,000) is full.

A lesson raises the odds that the agent avoids the pattern. It is not a guarantee: the
agent still has to read and follow it.

---

## API

```bash
GET   /v1/admin/lessons?limit=100
PATCH /v1/admin/lessons/:id          { "retired": true }
GET   /v1/admin/clusters?limit=100&status=candidate
POST  /v1/admin/clusters/:id/promote
POST  /v1/admin/lessons/query        { "diff": "...", "token_budget": 3000 }
```

- [Fixes](/admin/fixes) — the fix runs a lesson is meant to inform
- [Schema changes](/admin/drift) — a serious finding can become a candidate lesson

## Plugins

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/marketplace

---
title: Plugins
description: The Plugins page in the Mushi Mushi console installs outbound plugins, such as a Zapier bridge or your own signed webhook, that receive events for your project.
---

# Plugins

**Route:** `/marketplace` (sidebar: **Account → Plugins**)

The Plugins page lets you install outbound plugins that receive signed webhook events
from Mushi Mushi, for example when a report is classified or a fix is requested. The
page itself suggests Zapier and your own HTTPS endpoint; for Sentry, Linear, Jira or
PagerDuty it points you to their cards on [Integrations](/admin/integrations) instead.

The `plugins` entitlement is required to install plugins. An upgrade prompt appears if
it isn't active on your plan.

---

## Tabs

The page has four tabs: **Overview**, **Browse**, **Installed** and **Deliveries**.
Overview shows your installed plugins and how their deliveries are doing.

### Browse

A card grid showing all plugins in the catalog. Each card shows:
- Plugin name, publisher, category, short description, version
- **Install status** — installed badge if already active
- **Reliability stats** — total dispatches, ok rate, avg latency (from the dispatch log)

Use the **text search**, **category filter**, and **Installed only** toggle to narrow
the list.

### Installed

The installed plugins list with per-plugin controls (see Actions below).

### Deliveries

A dispatch log table showing the most recent outbound webhook calls. Filterable by
**plugin slug** and **status** (`ok`, `error`, `timeout`). Use this to debug delivery
problems or confirm an event fired.

---

## Installing a plugin

1. Find the plugin on the **Browse** tab.
2. Click **Install**.
3. Fill in the install form:
   - **Webhook URL** — your endpoint that receives events
   - **Signing secret** (HMAC-SHA256): store it, it is shown only once; verify the `X-Mushi-Signature` header in your handler
   - **Subscribed events**: a comma-separated list of event names, or `*` for all
4. Click **Install**.

---

## Managing installed plugins

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Test** | Fires a test webhook event to confirm delivery |
| **Pause / Resume** | Toggle `isActive` — paused plugins skip dispatch |
| **Edit URL** | Update the webhook URL without reinstalling |
| **Rotate secret** | Generate a new signing secret |
| **Uninstall** | Removes the plugin (confirmation required) |

---

## Signing verification

Every outbound webhook includes an `X-Mushi-Signature` header of the form
`t=,v1=`, where `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `` `${t}.${rawBody}` `` with your
signing secret. Deliveries also carry the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/)
headers (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`). Verify the signature
in your handler before processing events:

```ts
import crypto from 'crypto'

function verify(rawBody: string, header: string, secret: string) {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(header.split(',').map((p) => p.split('=')))
  const t = parts.t
  const v1 = parts.v1 ?? ''
  if (!t || Math.abs(Date.now() - Number(t)) > 5 * 60 * 1000) return false
  const expected = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest('hex')
  return expected.length === v1.length &&
    crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected), Buffer.from(v1))
}
```

---

## First-party plugins

### Cursor Cloud Agent

The **Cursor Cloud Agent** plugin (`cursor-cloud-agent`) is a first-party plugin that starts a Cursor Cloud Agent when qualifying events fire. The agent opens a draft PR on your GitHub repo. It still needs your review: see [Fixes](/admin/fixes) for the review and merge gates.

**Subscribes to:** `report.classified` · `fix.requested` · `qa_story.failed` · `skill_pipeline.step.dispatched`

For `report.classified`, only reports at or above the plugin's severity threshold start an
agent (critical when no threshold is set). A `fix.requested` event that the fix worker
already sent to Cursor does not start a second agent.

**Configure after installing:**
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **API Key** | Your Cursor API key |
| **Workspace ID** | Asked for by the install form; the current dispatch code does not read it |
| **Model** | `composer-2.5` (default) or `composer-latest` |
| **Auto-create PRs** | Toggle — enabled by default |

Unlike standard webhook plugins, the Cursor Cloud Agent plugin calls **the Cursor REST API directly**, so there is no outbound webhook URL to configure. If the plugin has no API key, Mushi Mushi falls back to the project's Cursor key; with no key at all, or no GitHub repo URL on the project, the dispatch is skipped.

The dispatch result (agent ID, run ID, PR URL) is visible in [Fixes](/admin/fixes) under the Cursor badge.

## Editor agents (MCP)

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/mcp

---
title: Editor agents (MCP)
description: The Editor agents page connects Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf and other MCP clients to Mushi Mushi and lists the tools your agent can call from the editor.
---

# Editor agents (MCP): ask your editor what broke

**Route:** `/mcp` (sidebar: **Editor agents**, under Connect)

Wire Mushi Mushi into Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, or any MCP client. Once connected,
your agent can read reports, pull fix context, and optionally dispatch fixes —
without leaving the editor.

The page has four tabs: **Summary**, **Setup**, **Catalog** and **Examples**. The
**Catalog** tab mirrors the server registry (**130 tools**, 8 resources, 4 prompts).

---

## Quickstart

The **Setup** tab opens with a 3-step strip, **Get an agent talking in 60 seconds**. Step 1
shows complete when you already have an `mcp:read` key.

### 1. Generate an API key
Mint a key with **MCP read** (to browse) or **MCP read + write** (to dispatch fixes), or use **Add to Cursor**, which creates a key for you. This is separate from your app's SDK ingest key (`report:write`).

### 2. Paste the snippet
Copy the **Stdio (.cursor/mcp.json)** or **Hosted HTTP** block, or click **Add to Cursor** (or the button for your editor on [Connect](/admin/connect)) for a one-click deeplink. The deeplink includes `MUSHI_FEATURES=triage,fixes,inventory,setup,docs` (lean catalog).

### 3. Ask the agent
Restart your IDE, then ask: *"list mushi tools"* or *"call diagnose_setup"*. See [MCP quickstart](/quickstart/mcp) and [Incident loop](/quickstart/incident-loop).

---

## Install snippets

### `.cursor/mcp.json` (stdio — recommended)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mushi-myproject": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@mushi-mushi/mcp@0.30.0"],
      "env": {
        "MUSHI_API_ENDPOINT": "https://<your-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/api",
        "MUSHI_PROJECT_ID": "<your-project-id>",
        "MUSHI_API_KEY": "mushi_...",
        "MUSHI_FEATURES": "triage,fixes,inventory,setup,docs"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

  There is no `--project-id` CLI flag on `@mushi-mushi/mcp`. Pass the project via **`MUSHI_PROJECT_ID`** in `env`. Server names use `mushi-` (admin deeplink) or bare `mushi` for legacy single-project configs.

### Hosted HTTP (no local subprocess)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mushi-http": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://<your-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp?features=triage,fixes,inventory,setup,docs",
      "headers": {
        "X-Mushi-Api-Key": "mushi_...",
        "X-Mushi-Project-Id": "<your-project-id>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Full catalog: append `?features=all` (or set `MUSHI_FEATURES=all` for stdio).
Smallest set: `?features=vibe` lists a dozen tools for the reported-bug loop (reports,
diagnosis, fix context, mark fixed, reply, setup, docs); chat connectors such as
Lovable use it ([guide](/quickstart/lovable-mcp)).

---

## Key status

Two badges next to the strip show whether you have:
- **`mcp:read`** — required for read tools (reports, fix context, lessons, docs search)
- **`mcp:write`** — required for dispatch, merge, QA triggers, and other mutations

  Write tools mutate production data. Store `mcp:write` keys in IDE config or CI secrets — never in a frontend bundle that ships to end users.

---

## Tool catalogue (representative)

See the admin **Catalog** tab for the full list. Names below match `tools/call` exactly.

### Read tools (`mcp:read`)

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `get_recent_reports` | List recent reports with status/category/severity filters |
| `get_report_detail` | Full report payload — logs, screenshot, classification |
| `get_fix_context` | One-shot fix brief — root cause, repro, blast radius |
| `get_similar_bugs` | pgvector nearest-neighbour duplicates |
| `search_reports` | Semantic + keyword search |
| `diagnose_setup` | Unified ingest + MCP + dispatch diagnosis |
| `search_mushi_docs` | Keyword search over Mushi documentation |
| `query_lessons` / `list_lessons` | Evolution-loop learning rules |
| `get_inventory` / `diff_inventory` | Inventory v2 snapshot and gate diff |

### Write tools (`mcp:write`)

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `dispatch_fix` | Dispatch a triaged report to the fix-worker (opens draft PR when configured) |
| `merge_fix` | Squash-merge the fix PR and mark report Fixed |
| `transition_status` | Move a report through triage states |
| `run_qa_story` | Trigger a QA Coverage story run |
| `start_skill_pipeline` | Attach a skill pipeline to a report |

---

## Resources

| URI | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `project://dashboard` | PDCA dashboard snapshot |
| `project://stats` | Report counts and severity breakdown |
| `mushi://activation` | Setup posture — SDK heartbeat, MCP, next action |
| `inventory://current` | Current inventory snapshot with gate status |
| `evolution://history` | Judge scores and lesson inductions (30 days) |
| `privacy://status` | BYOK / retention / region posture |

---

## Prompts

MCP prompts orchestrate multiple tools into a single agent turn:

| Prompt | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `summarize_report_for_fix` | Build a fix plan from `get_fix_context` + blast radius before coding |
| `triage_next_steps` | Five-item priority list from dashboard + queue |
| `explain_judge_result` | Ship / iterate / dismiss from judge scores |
| `mushi_setup` | Diagnose blocked setup via activation + integration health |

---

## Use cases

1. **Incident loop** — `get_fix_context` → `summarize_report_for_fix` → paste into Cursor ([guide](/quickstart/incident-loop))
2. **Morning triage** — `get_recent_reports` + `triage_next_steps`
3. **PR-time lessons** — `query_lessons` before touching files
4. **Setup unblock** — `diagnose_setup` when reports don't appear
5. **Automated dispatch** — CI calls `dispatch_fix` on critical reports (requires `mcp:write`)

## MCP OAuth consent

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/mcp-auth

---
title: MCP OAuth consent
description: The consent page the hosted Mushi Mushi MCP server opens when your editor signs in over OAuth, what you approve, and how the authorization flow works.
---

# MCP OAuth consent

**Route:** `/mcp-auth?txn=`

> **Scenario:** You ran `claude mcp login mushi` (or Cursor / VS Code MCP auth).
> The hosted MCP redirected your browser here to approve access.

The page is titled **Connect an MCP client**. It is the OAuth consent step for MCP
clients of the hosted Mushi Mushi MCP server (MCP auth spec):

1. Hosted MCP `/oauth/authorize` records a pending transaction and 302s here.
2. Page loads `GET /v1/mcp-oauth/request?txn=…`: client name + requested access.
3. Under **Projects this connection can reach**, pick **All my projects** (the default),
   **Only the projects I pick**, or **One project** (one you own or administer).
4. **Approve connection** → `POST /v1/mcp-oauth/approve` mints a revocable key and
   redirects to the client callback with the authorization code. **Deny** sends the
   client a refusal (`POST /v1/mcp-oauth/deny`).

What the key is:

- **One project**: a project API key labelled `mcp-oauth`; revoke it from the project's
  keys.
- **All my projects / Only the projects I pick**: an account key labelled
  `mcp-oauth-`; revoke it from **MCP → Account keys**. In each project it can do
  only what your role there allows.

Sibling flow for the CLI: [CLI device auth](/admin/cli-auth) (`mushi login`).

- [Connect hub](/admin/connect): one-click MCP lane without OAuth
- [CLI device auth](/admin/cli-auth): terminal login approval

## Reporter updates

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/notifications

---
title: Reporter updates
description: The Reporter updates page in Mushi Mushi lists widget messages your reporters see, so you can check they hear back when a bug is diagnosed, fixed and shipped.
---

# Reporter updates

**Route:** `/notifications` (sidebar: **Reporter updates**; formerly Notifications)

When someone reports a bug through your app, Mushi Mushi queues messages for them: when
the report is diagnosed, when it is fixed or the fix failed, when they earn a reward, and
when someone replies to their comment. The SDK widget polls for these messages. This page
lists them so you can check that the loop back to reporters works.

It shows messages to reporters only. Alerts to your team go to Slack, Discord and the
other channels set up in [Integrations](/admin/integrations).

The tabs are **Summary**, **Sent**, **How they hear back** and **Setup**.

---

## Message types

| Type | When it is queued |
|------------|--------------|
| `classified` | The report was diagnosed |
| `fixed` | The report was marked fixed |
| `fix_failed` | A fix attempt for the report failed |
| `reward` | The reporter earned points or a tier |
| `comment_reply` | Someone replied to the reporter's comment |

---

## Sent tab

Each row shows the type, the message, whether the reporter has read it (and when), a
short form of the reporter's key, and a link to the report. Expand a row for the full
JSON payload. Filter by type, or show unread messages only.

**Mark read** on a row, or **Mark all read**, marks messages read once you have checked
them.

---

## If reporters hear nothing

1. Open **Setup**: reporter updates must be on, and **Reporter loop prerequisites** lists
   what else is missing.
2. If reports exist but no messages appear, the updates are off or nothing has been
   diagnosed or fixed yet.
3. If messages stay unread for a long time, check that the widget in your app is running
   a current SDK and can reach Mushi Mushi.

---

- [Tester rewards](/admin/rewards) — where `reward` messages come from
- [Releases](/admin/releases) — publishing a release tells credited reporters their fix shipped
- [Settings](/admin/settings) — project settings
