## Onboarding

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/onboarding

---
title: Onboarding
description: Get your first bug report into Mushi Mushi with the console's Set up page, from naming your project to a report with a plain-English diagnosis.
---

# Onboarding

**Route:** `/onboarding` (sidebar: **More pages › Connect › Set up**)

> **Scenario:** You signed up 5 minutes ago. Your goal: get a real bug report from your
> app into Mushi Mushi before your afternoon standup. The page's own target is a first
> plain-English diagnosis in under 2 minutes.

The **Set up** page is the shortest path from signup to a report in your queue.

---

## First run: two screens

While your project has no report yet, the page shows two screens instead of the full
checklist:

### Name your project
**Step 1 of 2.** Enter a project name and create it. That is the only input: the
create call also makes your report key (`report:write`), so there is no separate key step.

### See your first diagnosis
**Step 2 of 2.** Click **Send test report**. The report goes through the real ingest
path and the diagnosis appears on the same screen. From there, **Install the SDK** to
get the same for real bugs.

Add `?view=all` to the URL, or click **Show all steps**, to see the full checklist
instead.

---

## Full checklist

Once your project has a report (or with `?view=all`), a progress rail tracks four
steps: **App created**, **Key made**, **App connected** and **First bug received**. It
reads "*n* of 4 done. Next: …" with a button for the next step, and "Your app is wired
up" when all four are done.

Below the rail, the page has five tabs:

| Tab | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| **Overview** | Setup status, a diagram of what happens after a report, and what to do next |
| **More to connect** | Optional tools to connect once the app is set up (and the create form in CLI setup mode) |
| **Test it** | **Generate API key**, **Submit test report** / **Send another**, and the **First report in your queue** timer |
| **Install** | The SDK install snippet and a **Go to Dashboard** button |
| **Fix a problem** | SDK heartbeat, version and fix-dispatch checks for one project, with copy-paste commands |

### After you create a project

A **success panel** shows:

- Your **Project ID** (UUID) in a one-click copy chip
- The key that was made for you, and one prefilled
  **`mushi init --project-id … --api-key …`** command
- A **Generate API key** button instead, if the key could not be made automatically

### Generate an API key
**Generate API key** on the **Test it** tab makes an SDK key (`report:write`). The key
is shown in plaintext exactly once, so copy it immediately.

  **Not Settings → AI keys.** That tab holds your own Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor and
  Firecrawl keys. SDK report keys are made here, or on **Manage apps** (`/projects`).

### Test the connection
Click **Submit test report** to send a synthetic report through the ingest pipeline.
A status chip shows `idle` → `running` → `pass` / `fail`. Click **Send another** to send
more. Test reports are limited to 10 per user per hour.

The **Test it** tab also shows a **First report in your queue** timer: how long from
making your first API key to seeing a plain-English diagnosis on a report. The target
is **under 2 minutes**; the card reads "Under the 2-minute target ✓" once you beat it,
or "Target: under 2 minutes" while pending.

### Install the SDK
The **Install** tab shows install snippets per framework (a script tag, React, Vue,
Svelte, React Native, Expo, Capacitor, Node, Express, Fastify, Hono and plain
JavaScript), filled in with your API key and project ID.

Or run the CLI wizard from your app repo: see [CLI ↔ console loop](/quickstart/cli-console-loop).

---

## CLI setup mode (`?setup=cli`)

When you run `npx mushi-mushi` without saved credentials, the wizard can open the console
at:

```
/onboarding?tab=steps&setup=cli
```

| Behavior | Normal onboarding | `setup=cli` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First-run screens | Shown until the first report | Skipped: the full checklist opens on **More to connect** |
| Create form | Hidden if you already have projects | **Always shown**, so you can add another project |
| Banner | None | "Setting up from the CLI?" plus a "Your terminal is waiting" card |
| Success panel | Same UUID + CLI command | Same, meant for pasting back into the terminal |

Use this path when the terminal wizard sent you here, or when you need a **second project**
without leaving the Set up page.

---

## CLI setup strip

Two places reuse the same **1-2-3 CLI setup** strip (`CliSetupGuide`):

- The **Overview** tab of this page, before you have any project
- The empty state on **Manage apps** (`/projects`)

Steps match the [CLI ↔ console loop](/quickstart/cli-console-loop): create → mint key →
`mushi init` or `mushi connect`.

---

## How the loop works

The **Overview** tab includes a static diagram, "What happens after a report", with
outcome copy instead of live counts, so you know what happens after a report lands
before you see live numbers.

---

**One-time key reveal** — the plaintext API key is shown exactly once after generation.
Copy it before clicking away. If you lose it, generate a new key on
[Manage apps](/admin/projects). The old one can't be recovered.

---

## Troubleshooting the test report

If the test report shows `fail`:

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| `401 Unauthorized` | Wrong API key in the SDK install | Re-copy the key from the reveal card |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | You sent more than 10 test reports in an hour | Wait up to an hour (the response's `Retry-After` header says how long), then try again |
| Status stuck at `running` | No AI key the triage can use (self-hosted installs) | Go to [Settings](/admin/settings) → **AI keys** → add an Anthropic key |
| Success but no report on **Bugs** | Wrong project in the SDK snippet | Check `projectId` in your install code |

---

## What happens after setup

Once the SDK sends its first real report from your app:
1. The "waiting for your first report" card on [Home](/admin/dashboard) goes away.
2. The report gets a plain-English read and appears on [Bugs](/admin/reports).
3. The setup rail marks **First bug received** as done.

---

## Setup gaps

Once the app exists, **Setup gaps** lists the configuration that is missing or
broken, before a button fails. Each line has a **Fix** link to the page where you
fix it. Checks that pass fold into one line, and a check Mushi could not read says
so: the page never reads "all fine" while a check is unknown.

| Check | What it reads | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub access, per repo | The Mushi GitHub App's permissions, a classic token's scopes, or a fine-grained token's harmless reads | Pushing fix branches, opening pull requests and re-running CI each need their own permission. Without secrets access, Mushi gives you copy-paste commands instead. |
| Review follow-up key | Your team's follow-up setting and the Cursor key it uses | Mushi turns follow-ups off on its own when that key is deleted. |
| Auto-fix agent key | Whether auto-fix is on and a Cursor key can start an agent | With no usable key, no fix starts on its own. |
| Deploy events | The last deploy Mushi saw | With none in 14 days, reporters are not told when their fix goes live. |
| Slack bot token | The latest Slack check (every 15 minutes) | Slack stops accepting a token when the app is removed from the workspace. |

Mushi only reads to check. It never writes to GitHub to find out whether it may
write, so a fine-grained token's write permissions read **can't tell**. Results are
kept for 10 minutes; **Check again** re-checks.

---

## Restarting the tour

Click **Restart tour** at the bottom of the page to replay the first-run tour of the
console. It opens Home and starts the tour again. It does not reset your setup
progress or delete any projects or data.

---

```bash
GET  /v1/admin/onboarding/time-to-first-diagnosis   → { keyMintedAt, firstDiagnosisAt, ms }
GET  /v1/admin/setup-gaps?projectId=                → { projects: [{ gaps: [{ id, status, title, summary, fixHref }] }] }
```

## Overview (Home view)

# Overview

**Route:** `/dashboard?view=apps` (**Home → Overview**). The old `/overview` link redirects
there. For setup state, hole checks and spend across apps, see [Apps](/admin/portfolio).

> **Scenario:** You manage several connected projects and want a single org-scoped
> glance at 7-day activity and open tickets before diving into any one app.

In Mushi Mushi, Overview covers every app in the active team. Each card is one
connected app (sessions, users, open bugs and a DAU sparkline) with footer links
that switch the active app and open **User activity**, **Bugs** (or **Open bugs**),
**Home**, or **Recipe** when the app has a recipe state.

---

## What you see

| Element | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| **Portfolio totals** | Aggregated 7-day sessions / users and open-ticket counts across projects |
| **Project cards** | Per-project `sessions_7d`, `users_7d`, open + critical reports, last report time |
| **DAU sparkline** | Daily active users for the last week on that project |
| **Health tone** | Critical if any critical reports; then not connected (no SDK heartbeat ever) or silent (heartbeat stopped); warn if open reports &gt; 5; quiet if no sessions in 7 days; otherwise ok |
| **Footer links** | Switch the active app, then open User activity, Bugs, Home or Recipe |

Cards sort so apps that need attention come first.

---

## Data source

```
GET /v1/admin/portfolio
```

Requires a console JWT and `X-Mushi-Org-Id` (set automatically from the org
switcher). Backed by the `org_portfolio_summary` RPC.

Empty state means no apps are linked to this team yet: **Create your first project →**
opens [Set up](/admin/onboarding).

## Pipeline

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/pipeline

---
title: Pipeline
description: The Pipeline page in the Mushi Mushi console shows every bug from report to deploy, where it is stuck and why, with one-click fixes.
---

# Pipeline

**Route:** `/pipeline` (sidebar: Pipeline)

In Mushi Mushi, every bug moves from a report to a fix PR, an Opus review, CI, a release train, a merge and a deploy. This page shows how many items are in each step now, which are stuck, and why. **This app** follows the app you have open. **All apps** reads every project you can see.

## Stages

| Stage | What is in it |
| --- | --- |
| **Reported** | Reports not triaged yet (stuck after an hour, or when triage failed), and reports the API refused at intake. |
| **Triaged** | Triaged reports with no fix started. Stuck after 3 days. |
| **Fix PR** | Apps whose auto-fix cannot dispatch, agents writing a fix, agents that failed without a PR, and drafts whose CI never ran. |
| **Reviewed** | PRs waiting for the Opus review, and PRs Opus held or sent back ("fix first"). |
| **CI** | PRs whose own CI is red, never ran, is still running, or stopped on the test machine. |
| **Release train** | Approved, green PRs in the merge queue, on a train, held, or waiting on a conflict agent. |
| **Merged** | Fixes merged in the last 7 days. |
| **Deployed** | Merged fixes that a deploy recorded after the merge. |

Each stage shows its count, how many are stuck, and how long the oldest item has been in it. The time is counted from when the item entered the stage, not from the last time a worker touched it. Click a stage to see only its groups.

A PR whose own CI is red counts under **CI**, even when it is in the merge queue. A red PR in a release train only makes the train fail. A test machine stop is not a code failure, and a skipped check is not a pass.

## Who opens fixes

One row per app: who opened fixes in the last 7 days (the server, your local `mushi work` lanes, both, or nobody), the server's agent keys, dispatches in 24 hours and last dispatch, and the local lanes' runs, how many are running and the last run. The **Fix PR** stage counts apps by who opened a fix in the last 24 hours.

The server opens fixes on its own only through spend-down, with an active Cursor key that has spend-down on. When an app has auto-fix on but no such key, or its key dispatched nothing in 48 hours, the app is red here and in a stuck group in **Fix PR** that links to the switch on the Spend credits page.

Local lanes are read from the workers you registered (see [Workers](#workers) below), not guessed from past runs. An app with auto-fix on and no agent key is not red while one of its lanes is online and taking new reports.

## Stuck groups

Each group says its reason in plain words, for example "12 PRs: their own CI is red". Open it to see each PR with its report, how long it has waited, the failing checks, the Opus verdict and its findings, and the merge queue's last message. When a setting holds the group (review follow-ups off), the group links to it.

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Send to CI repair** | Sends the PR to an agent that makes its CI green without weakening tests: Mushi's cloud agent when review follow-ups can run (they need a Cursor key on your team), otherwise your local `mushi work --followups` lanes on their next run. Says why when neither can. |
| **Send to follow-up** | The same for an Opus "fix first": an agent fixes the review's findings on the PR's branch. |
| **Re-run CI** | Re-runs the failed CI jobs on the PR's latest commit. |
| **Re-run review** | Asks Opus to review the PR again. |
| **Update branch** | GitHub merges the base branch into the PR. |
| **New conflict agent** | Hands a conflicted PR back to the merge queue, at most 2 agents per PR. Conflict agents are cloud agents: without one, the PR needs a person to resolve the conflict on GitHub, and the page says so with the PR link. |
| **Mark ready** | Takes a draft out of draft so CI runs. |
| **Queue to merge** | Puts an approved, green PR in the merge queue. |
| **Remove from queue** / **Close PR** | Takes it out of the queue, or closes it without merging. The reason is kept as a team note on the report. |
| **Not a code bug** | Closes the report with a reason and tells its reporter. Nothing runs on it again unless someone reopens it. Offered on groups of reports, such as agents that failed without a PR. |
| **Requeue** | Puts a report back at the front of the local lane that ran it, when that lane's machine stopped the run (not the code). Mushi does this once on its own; after that the report waits here for you. It never counts against the report. |

Every action asks first, works on one PR or the whole group, shows each PR's result, and then the page reads again.

## Release trains

One row per repository with the trains of the last 7 days: green merged, red failed, blue on the way. Click a square for that train's detail. The checks that failed the trains most often are listed under the row. **Run merge queue now** checks the queue at once and says whether a train left, and if not, when the next one may leave or why it waits.

## Intake and deploys

Each app shows the reports the API refused (HTTP 400) in the last 7 days, with the first failing field and its check (`fingerprintHash:invalid_string`) and the SDK package that sent them. They also form a red group in **Reported**. An app with none reads **0 rejected since** the day counting began; before anything was ever counted it reads **not recorded yet**, never 0. Each app also shows its last recorded deploy.

## Workers

The **Workers** tab shows your local workers: machines that run `mushi work --daemon` and fix reports with a coding agent on that machine. It replaces `lanectl status` and the queue text files. Set one up with [`mushi worker install`](/sdks/cli#mushi-worker).

| Part | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Machines** | Each registered machine: online or offline, its last heartbeat, what it is doing now (working, idle, waiting for memory, for the GitHub quota, for the Cursor sign-in, or for a free agent space), its load, the Cursor account check and the `gh` sign-in as they last answered, which lane holds each agent space and in which stage, and its guards: how many agents may run at once, the free-memory floor and the GitHub API floor. The machine's owner changes the guards or revokes it. |
| **Lanes** | One app on one machine: its model, mode, how many it runs at once, paused or not, its stop date, and drain (finish what runs, take nothing new). An audit lane also has a second model that may only veto a finding. |
| **Queue** | Reports the lane takes first, in order. Move a report up or down, remove it, or paste report ids (one or many) into **Add reports by id**. A report already being fixed somewhere else waits in the queue until it is free. |
| **Recent runs** | The last 7 days: runs, PRs opened, no change, timeouts, errors, and failures of the machine (infra) kept apart from failures of the code. |

A lane's **mode** says what it does:

| Mode | What the lane does |
| --- | --- |
| Fix reports and follow-ups | Its queue first, then the worst open reports; a draft PR for each |
| Review follow-ups only | Fixes what Opus asked for on PRs a local agent opened |
| Resolve merge conflicts | Merges the base branch into this repository's PRs that wait in the merge queue for a conflict agent. The agent may change only the conflicted files; anything else is refused. It counts toward the 2 conflict agents a PR may have, cloud and local together |
| Audit the code, screen by screen | A model proposes bugs; the machine files only those its own check reproduces, at most 12 an hour per app, into a fix lane for the same app on that machine |
| Run skill runs | Only the rounds of skill runs started on Spend credits with **Run on** set to this lane |

A lane change reaches the machine at its next heartbeat, within a minute. The machine opens no port: it asks Mushi for its settings, and the settings are values (a model id, a number, a date), never a command or a path. Viewers can read this tab but cannot change it.

### When a worker stops doing useful work

Anything that stops a worker from fixing bugs is listed at the top of the tab, worst first, and never folded away. An **agent space** is one coding agent running at a time; each machine allows a set number at once (**Agents at once** in its limits). When every space is taken, other lanes wait.

| Problem | What you see | What fixes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Machine offline | No heartbeat for 3 minutes; how long, and how many queued reports wait | The command that shows the worker's service and its last log lines on that machine |
| Stuck run | A run has held an agent space for over 45 minutes: its stage (getting the repo ready, the coding agent, the repo's **commit hook**, its **pre-push hook**, opening the PR), how long it has been in that stage, and its last few log lines | **Stop this run**, open the report, or the command that finds it on the machine |
| Waiting for an agent space | Lanes waited over 15 minutes, with the runs that hold the spaces and in which stage | Stop the stuck runs, or let the machine run more at once |
| Cursor account | The account check said another account, signed out, not installed, or did not answer in time (with the load on the machine) | **Switch account** (the machine's owner signs it in as the right account from the console: it finishes its runs, then shows a Cursor sign-in link), **Re-check the account**, or the command to sign in on the machine |
| GitHub sign-in | `gh` is not signed in on the machine, so no branch can be pushed | `gh auth login` on the machine |
| Machine waiting | Low memory, the GitHub API quota or a sign-in has held the machine for over 5 minutes | The command that shows what uses the memory or the quota |
| Machine overloaded | Load of 2 or more per core: checks and git hooks time out | The command that lists what runs there |
| Git hooks failing | Two or more runs of a lane failed in the repo's own commit or pre-push check in 24 hours | **Pause this lane**, open the latest report or PR |
| Run outside the worker | A `mushi work` run that no worker claims has run for over 45 minutes: a script started it, so its stage cannot be seen or stopped here | Move that machine to `mushi worker install` |
| Credits idle | No agent has worked for 2 hours while Cursor credits expire within 7 days, with what blocks the work | Open Workers, or Spend credits |

The same problems show above the Pipeline tabs, as a count on the **Pipeline** item in the sidebar, in **Needs you** on Home (for that app), as "credits idle" on [Spend credits](/admin/credits), in `mushi worker status` and in the MCP tool `get_worker_status`.

**Stop this run** (the app's owner or an admin, or the machine's owner; asks first, and is recorded in the audit log) ends the run's claim at once, so the report is free again: the next lane or a cloud agent can take it (it is not put back in a queue). The machine stops the agent at its next heartbeat, within a minute, and commits or pushes nothing more. A git hook that is already running keeps its agent space until git's own time limit (25 minutes); the flag stays up as "a run that was stopped still holds an agent space" until it ends, with the command to end it on the machine. A review follow-up is not a claim: pause its lane and end it on the machine.

Log lines are cleaned on the machine and again by Mushi before they are stored: no keys, tokens or paths, e-mail addresses masked, and no lines a compiler quotes from your code. A machine whose Mushi CLI is older than these checks says so on its card instead of showing a problem.

### Send to my local worker

On a report's page and on a pipeline group, **Send to my local worker** puts the reports at the end of one of your lanes for that app. While a lane holds a report, no cloud agent is sent to it, and the lane does not take a report a cloud agent is already working on.

### Create a worker key

A worker key can only take reports for its lanes and record their fixes. It cannot merge, change settings or read keys. **Create a worker key** makes one for the apps you pick and shows it once; pass it to `mushi worker install --key-stdin` on the machine. `mushi worker install` can also make one with your CLI login. Revoking a machine here revokes its key, and the worker stops at its next heartbeat.

## Apps (all apps)

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/portfolio

---
title: Apps (all apps)
description: The Apps page in Mushi Mushi shows every app in a team, with each app's worst recipe state, hole checks and SDK version, plus fixes that apply across apps.
---

# Apps (all apps)

**Route:** `/portfolio` (sidebar: **Apps**; formerly Portfolio. Also from the team switcher: **All this team's apps**)

> **Scenario:** You run five apps. One has an old Mushi SDK, two have the same
> oversized-file finding, and one never got Sentry set up. You want to see all
> of that in one place and fix each problem once, not five times.

Mushi Mushi only **reads** your apps here. The page builds on each app's [Recipe](/concepts/app-recipe).

---

## What you see

| Section | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Cards** | One per app: the worst recipe state, open reports, the latest release, the Mushi SDK against the latest version, and the hole checks. |
| **Hole checks** | "Not checked yet" means Mushi has not looked. It is never a pass. The checks that read your repo come from one step in your existing CI job: see [One CI step for both checks](/sdks/cli#one-ci-step-for-both-checks). |
| **Fix once** | A problem open in two or more apps. Copy the prompt into your editor to fix it in every repo. |
| **Mushi SDK versions** | Apps behind the latest release of the same package, and apps that never reported. |
| **Missing setups** | An integration most of your other apps have and this one does not. |

In **Advanced** mode each card also shows Mushi's own AI spend for that app over 30 days and its monthly budget.

### When something could not be read

If Mushi cannot read part of the page (the AI spend, the caps, the releases,
the SDK versions, which integrations each app has), a callout at the top names
it and the affected cells read **Could not read**. They never fall back to
`$0`, "Not set", "None yet" or "no missing setups". When there are more rows
than Mushi reads in one go, the total is marked as a lower bound ("at least
$12.40", "40+").

Below the cards:

| Section | What it means |
|---------|---------------|
| **Across your apps** | Problems only visible across apps: a deep link or "more apps" link that no longer opens, a shared login that does not allow one app's domain, apps sharing purchases on different Stripe accounts, many apps posting to one channel, CI cost in two repos. See [One login across your apps](../concepts/shared-login). |
| **Funnel across apps** | One funnel run on every app: the same event names, in the same order, within the same window. Owners and admins pick the steps. An app with product events off, or with no events yet, says so instead of 0%. |
| **Releases** | For each app: what is live and at what rollout, native changes waiting for a store build, and JS-only changes that can ship as an over-the-air update. It suggests one store release per app to save CI minutes. Your own CI builds and submits. |
| **Spend per app** | What each app cost over 30 days, from every source Mushi can read. See [Spend per app](#spend-per-app). |
| **Daily digest** | One message a day across all apps. Off until an owner picks where it goes: an app's Slack channel, Discord or Teams webhook, or Telegram chats, email, or push. Once a week (Monday by default) it adds each app's signups and activations. When there were more reports, AI calls or findings than it reads, it says which numbers are lower bounds. See [Daily digest](#daily-digest). |
| **Shared between apps** | Domains, store apps, Supabase projects and channels two or more apps use. Owners and admins can import what no recipe or source declares from a CSV with the columns `kind, external_id, project` and an optional `role`; each refused row is listed with its line number, and a file is capped at 500 rows and 256 KB. |
| **Accounts and resilience** | Every account your apps depend on (Apple, Google Play, AWS, Supabase, Vercel, your registrar, Stripe…): the owner email, whether 2FA is on, how many people can get in, a recovery contact, and auto-renew for the registrar and each domain. See below. |
| **Payments across apps** | For each RevenueCat project: per app, what it sells (entitlements, offerings, packages, products and their store state) and why a purchase would fail, each with its fix. RevenueCat's headline numbers are shown as context only. A fix with an approved action can be asked for; it runs only after an owner approves it. See the [operator guide](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/docs/operators/monetization.md). |
| **Connected sources** | App Store Connect, Google Play, AI spend, RevenueCat or your own endpoint. Read-only by default. |

---

## Spend per app

One row per app, 30 days, one column per source:

| Column | Where it comes from |
|--------|---------------------|
| **Mushi AI** | Mushi's own AI calls for that app (diagnoses, fixes, store review). |
| **AI provider** | Your own OpenAI or Anthropic bill, from the **AI provider spend** source. An app counts only once it is bound to its OpenAI project or Anthropic workspace. |
| **CI (est.)** | GitHub Actions minutes as money: estimated billable minutes × $0.006, GitHub's Linux price. macOS minutes count 10× and Windows 2×. Public repositories are free, so this is the list price, not your bill. |
| **Supabase** | Supabase bills you import, with egress, invocations and other usage. Mushi reads Supabase read-only and cannot see billing. |
| **Other bills** | Vercel, AWS and other bills you import. |

A source that could not be read says **Couldn't read** and is left out of the
total; the total then ends in `+` because it is a floor. **Not connected**
means there is nothing to read yet. Neither one ever shows as $0.

**Import a bill** (owners and admins) takes a CSV:

- a **FOCUS** export, which both Vercel and AWS Data Exports offer;
- an **AWS Cost and Usage Report** (legacy or 2.0 column names);
- or any CSV with a `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), a `service` and a `cost` column, plus
  optional `quantity`, `unit`, `currency` and `app` columns.

Pick the app the bill belongs to, or let each row's `app` column (or an `app`
or `project` tag) name the app by its name or slug. Rows in another currency
than USD, with a date that is not YYYY-MM-DD, or naming no app of yours are
skipped, and the first few are explained. Importing the same bill again
replaces those days instead of adding to them: each day belongs to the newest
import that has it. **Remove** takes an import out and gives its days back to
the next newest import that has them, so removing a corrected bill brings the
earlier figures back. It says how many rows left the ledger and how many went
back. The file limit is 5 MB: export daily rather than hourly rows.

The ledger shows each member only the apps they can see. An import for one app
is listed to that app's members; an import matched by an `app` column is
listed to the team.

## Daily digest

The digest goes to the places an owner or admin picks. Slack, Discord, Teams
and Telegram each reuse one app's existing connection from
[Integrations](./integrations): its Slack channel, its Discord or Teams
webhook, or the Telegram chats bound to its bot. Nothing new to set up.

On the weekday you pick (Monday by default, in UTC; or never), each app gets
one more line: how many people did the first step of the
[team funnel](#what-you-see) in the last 7 days, and how many of them reached
its last step. An app with product events off gets no line; a funnel that
could not be read says so instead of showing zero. Without a team funnel there
are no weekly lines.

## Accounts and resilience

Losing the only login to your Apple, Google Play or registrar account can end
every app on it. This register keeps, for each account, who owns it and who
else can get in. It holds **names and contacts only**: never passwords, keys or
recovery codes, and anything shaped like a key is refused. Everything in it is
what you declare; Mushi cannot see a provider's own 2FA or renewal settings.

Two checks run on it, and their findings also appear under **Across your apps**:

| Check | When it fires |
|-------|---------------|
| `account_single_owner` | One person can sign in and no recovery contact is recorded. The fix names where that provider lets you add a second owner. |
| `registrar_autorenew_off` | Auto-renew is declared off for a registrar account or a domain. |

**Download as Markdown** saves the whole register as a file to keep offline or
hand to someone you trust. Owners and admins can change the register; other
members can read it.

---

## From your editor

The MCP tools `get_portfolio` and `list_portfolio_findings` return the same
data. They need an **account-level** key (Connect → MCP); a key bound to one
project cannot read its sibling apps. Both return `readErrors`, and each card
an `unreadable` list: a part named there is unknown, not empty.

`get_release_calendar` returns the release calendar: what is live per app, the
merged fixes waiting to ship, and a suggested batch to release now versus next.

The same account-level key can also change the team's funnel definition
(`PUT /v1/admin/orgs/:orgId/funnel`) and import shared resources from a CSV
(`POST /v1/ingest/recipe/csv`), with the `mcp:write` scope. Both still need the
key's owner to be a team owner or admin.

## Who can see it

Members of the team see the team's apps they can reach. A member of another
team gets a 403.

## Manage apps

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/projects

---
title: Manage apps
description: Create a Mushi Mushi project, mint an API key, copy the install snippet for your framework and send a test report, all from the Manage apps page.
---

# Manage apps

**Route:** `/projects` (sidebar: **Apps › Manage apps**)

> **Scenario:** You're setting up Mushi Mushi for a new mobile app. You need to create the
> project, grab an API key, paste the install snippet into your codebase, and send a
> test report to confirm everything is wired up, all before your next PR review.

This page handles the full project lifecycle: create, configure, monitor, and (if
needed) delete. It has three tabs: **Overview**, **Your projects** (one card per
project) and **New project**.

---

## Project card

Each project gets a card showing:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Name** | **Rename** edits it inline. Renaming does not change the slug or any URLs. |
| **SDK version badge** | `ok`, `outdated`, `deprecated`, or `unknown` |
| **PDCA bottleneck** | Chip showing where reports are stuck in the loop (classify → fix → verify) |
| **Repo strip** | Connected repo URL, default branch, index health (`ok` / `stale` / `failed` / `off` / `never`), indexed file count |
| **30-day severity chips** | Count of `critical` / `major` / `minor` / `trivial` reports |
| **7-day report trend** | Arrow indicating whether report volume is rising or falling |
| **Sentry connected** | Badge if a Sentry DSN is wired in |
| **Plan tier + region** | The project's current plan and data-residency region |

---

## Creating a project

Use the **New project** tab here, or [Set up](/admin/onboarding):

1. Enter a name and click **Create project**.
2. A **success panel** appears with your **Project ID** (UUID), the `report:write` key
   that was made for you, and a prefilled `mushi init` command.
3. If no key was made, click **Generate API key**. SDK keys are made here or on Set up,
   **not** in Settings (Settings → AI keys is for your own provider keys).

When the CLI wizard opens your browser, it lands on `?setup=cli` with the same success panel flow.

Local dev console: `http://localhost:6464` after `pnpm dev`. Override with `MUSHI_CONSOLE_URL` in the CLI. See [CLI ↔ console loop](/quickstart/cli-console-loop).

---

## API keys

Each project card lists its API keys:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Prefix** | The start of the key (the full key is only shown once, at creation) |
| **Scopes** | What the key may do (see the presets below) |
| **Created** | Timestamp |
| **Revoke** | Confirmation, then an undo toast for 8 seconds before the key stops working |

**Generate a key:**
1. Pick a scope preset: **SDK ingest**, **MCP read-only**, **MCP read + write**,
   **Voice intake**, **Runner health** or **Local worker**.
2. Click **Generate API key**.
3. Copy the key immediately. It is only shown once in plaintext.

SDK ingest keys are for use in your frontend/mobile SDK. MCP read + write keys grant
write access to Mushi via MCP tools: treat them like a service-role key and store them
only in server-side environments.

---

## SDK install configurator

Each project card includes a live SDK snippet configurator, with the in-widget
assistant settings under it:
- **Framework tabs**: a script tag, React, Vue, Svelte, React Native, Expo,
  Capacitor, Node, Express, Fastify, Hono and plain JavaScript
- **Position picker**: where the feedback button appears on screen
- **Theme**: light / dark / system
- **Copy snippet**: copies the ready-to-paste install code

---

## Send test report

Click **Send test report** on any project card to fire a synthetic report through the
full ingest pipeline. It checks ingest only and does not mark the SDK as installed.
The result appears as a new row on Bugs. Test reports are limited to 10 per user per
hour.

---

## Deleting a project

Delete the project, type its slug in the confirmation dialog, and confirm. An undo
toast gives you 8 seconds to change your mind; only owners and admins can delete.
After that, deletion is irreversible: all reports, fix attempts and QA stories for
the project are removed.

---

## Common tasks

### Connecting a new app (5 minutes)
1. On **New project** (or the first screen of Set up), enter a project name and create it.
2. Copy the **Project ID** and the key from the success panel. If no key was made,
   use **Generate API key** (`report:write`) and copy it immediately.
3. In your app repo run
   `MUSHI_API_KEY= mushi connect --project-id  --endpoint <api-url> --wait`
   (or `mushi init --project-id `). `--project-id` and `--endpoint` are required.
4. Click **Send test report** to confirm reports arrive.

### Sharing with a teammate who only needs read access via AI
1. Select the **MCP read-only** preset → **Generate API key**.
2. Share the key; they configure it in their AI assistant using the snippet on the [Editor agents](/admin/mcp) page.

### Rotating a compromised key
1. Revoke the exposed key and confirm. It stops working once the 8-second undo toast closes.
2. Generate a new key with the same scope.
3. Update the key in your app's environment variables.
4. Click **Send test report** to confirm the new key works.

---

| Action | Where |
|--------|-------|
| Create project | **New project** tab → name → **Create project** |
| Rename | **Rename** → edit inline → Save / Cancel |
| Switch to (set active) | **Switch to** button on the card |
| Jump to Reports | Reports link chip |
| Jump to Integrations | Integrations link chip |
| Jump to Settings | Settings link chip |

## API

```bash
GET  /v1/admin/projects
POST /v1/admin/projects            { name }
PATCH /v1/admin/projects/:id       { name }
DELETE /v1/admin/projects/:id      { confirm_slug }
POST /v1/admin/projects/:id/keys   { scopes?, label? }  (scopes default to ['report:write'])
DELETE /v1/admin/projects/:id/keys/:keyId
POST /v1/admin/projects/:id/test-report
```

## AI prompts

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/prompt-lab

---
title: AI prompts
description: The AI prompts page in the Mushi Mushi console lets you edit and A/B compare the prompts behind each AI step before you promote a new version.
---

# AI prompts

**Route:** `/prompt-lab` (sidebar: **AI prompts**; formerly Prompt lab). `/fine-tuning` redirects here.

AI prompts is a Lab: it is under **More pages** in the sidebar, and Settings → Display & sidebar can keep it in the sidebar. The page
works by URL either way.

**First on the page:** **Versions and their grades**, one row per AI step (Fast
filter, Diagnosis, Grading, Fix writer, …) with the version in use, the best version
being tested, their grades, and a verdict: ahead (consider promoting), behind, or
waiting for grades. A row opens that step's editing table.

> **Scenario:** Your fix-worker has been generating patches that touch the wrong file
> 20% of the time. You suspect the Stage 1 classifier is mislabelling the component
> field — so the fix agent is looking at the wrong area of the codebase. You want to
> try a new prompt, test it on real traffic, and promote it only if the judge confirms
> it's better than what's live.

AI prompts is where you iterate on the prompts behind each Mushi Mushi AI step. You do
not redeploy anything: a version takes effect on the share of traffic you give it.

---

## The 4-step workflow

The **How prompt tuning works** panel lists the steps:

```
1. Build eval dataset → 2. Clone a baseline → 3. A/B at low traffic → 4. Promote when judge ≥ 80%
```

**Step 1 — Build eval dataset:** grades need classified reports. The **Eval dataset**
card shows the recent classified reports the grader can use.

**Step 2 — Clone a baseline:** click **Clone** (the copy icon) on the version in use. The
copy starts at 0% traffic, so it serves no live requests yet. Click **Edit** to change
its template. Steps marked **Built-in** cannot be cloned: no worker reads a project copy
of that prompt yet.

**Step 3 — A/B at low traffic:** use **Set A/B traffic share** to give the copy a small
share (for example 10%). The judge runs nightly and grades both versions. Compare their
**Judge score** columns once each has a fair number of **Evals**.

**Step 4 — Promote:** click **Make this the live prompt** and confirm **Activate at 100%**.
This removes all A/B splits. The nightly judge run also promotes a candidate on its own
once it has at least 30 evaluations and scores more than 5% above the version in use.

The judge runs once per night, so an A/B test needs a few nights of data. Don't promote
after a single night.

---

## Summary tiles

| Tile | What to watch |
|------|--------------|
| **In use** | Prompt versions serving traffic |
| **Being tested** | Candidate versions in an A/B test |
| **Best grade** | The best judge score among the versions |

---

## Steps

Each tab is one AI step. Only steps with prompt rows appear. Start with the one causing
your problem:

| Step | Prompt controls |
|-------|----------------|
| **Fast filter** (`stage1`) | Spam detection: edit if legitimate reports are being dropped |
| **Diagnosis** (`stage2`) | Category, severity and component: edit if labels are wrong |
| **Grading** (`judge`) | The grader: edit if its scores don't match your own judgement |
| **Fix writer** (`fix`) | Code patch generation |
| **Weekly summary** (`intelligence`) | The weekly insights digest |
| **Question to SQL** / **Answer summary** | The SQL query page |
| **Test reports** (`synthetic`) | Generated test reports |

Other steps (for example **Dependency upgrades**, **Prompt tuner**, **Story map audit**)
show up when they have prompt rows.

---

## Prompt table columns

| Column | What it tells you |
|--------|------------------|
| **Version** | The version name, with an **Auto** badge when the weekly prompt tuner drafted it |
| **State** | **Active**, **Candidate** or **Idle**, plus **Global** for a built-in version |
| **Traffic** | What share of live requests this version serves |
| **Judge score** | Higher is better. Uses the rolling 7-day evaluation window |
| **Evals** | How many evaluations the score is based on. A low count means an unreliable score |
| **Updated** | When the version last changed |

---

## Actions per row

| Action | When to use it |
|--------|---------------|
| **Clone** | Starting point for any edit. Built-in versions are read-only; clone first |
| **Edit** | Open the template editor for a project version |
| **Diff** | Compare against the version it was cloned from. Use before promoting |
| **Set A/B traffic share** | Raise a candidate's traffic share gradually |
| **Make this the live prompt** | Activate at 100% and remove all A/B splits |
| **Delete** | Remove a candidate that didn't work out. Its past evaluations stay |

---

## Common tasks

### Fixing wrong component classification
1. Open the **Diagnosis** tab.
2. **Clone** the version in use.
3. **Edit** the template: add explicit examples of the component names your codebase uses.
4. Give it a 10% traffic share.
5. Wait a few nights. Is its **Judge score** above the version in use?
6. If yes: **Diff**, then make it the live prompt. If not: edit and try again.

### Investigating a bad judge score
1. Open the tab for the step with the low score.
2. Check **Evals**. With fewer than 10, the score isn't meaningful yet: wait.
3. With more than 20 and a still-low score, the prompt is likely wrong. Clone and start fresh.

---

## Advanced: fine-tuning & synthetic

This closed panel at the foot of the page holds two rarely used tools:

- **Fine-tuning jobs**: export classified reports and train a small model. See
  [Fine-tuning](/admin/fine-tuning).
- **Synthetic reports**: generate artificial test reports that match your real report
  patterns, to grow the set of reports the grader can score.

---

## API

```bash
GET    /v1/admin/prompt-lab
POST   /v1/admin/prompt-lab/prompts        { stage, name, promptTemplate }
PATCH  /v1/admin/prompt-lab/prompts/:id    { isActive, trafficPercentage, promptTemplate }
DELETE /v1/admin/prompt-lab/prompts/:id
```

- [Triage grading](/admin/judge) — nightly judge scores
- [Fine-tuning](/admin/fine-tuning) — train a small model from your classified reports
- [Mushi health](/admin/health) — check Mushi's AI calls before testing prompt changes

## Scheduled tests

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/qa-coverage

---
title: Scheduled tests
description: Scheduled tests in the Mushi Mushi console turn plain-English user flows into browser tests on a schedule, so you find out when login or checkout breaks.
---

# Scheduled tests

**Route:** `/qa-coverage` (sidebar: Checks › Scheduled tests; formerly QA Coverage)

> **Scenario:** You shipped a login flow last week and want to know automatically
> if it still works — without writing a full Playwright suite from scratch.

Scheduled tests in Mushi Mushi let you describe user flows in plain English, run them on a schedule, and get screenshots plus failure evidence when something breaks.

---

## Story lifecycle

```
Create story (NL prompt or Playwright script)
  → stored in qa_stories (schedule_cron: '0 * * * *' default)
  → pg_cron fires qa-story-runner every minute
  → BYOK key resolution (firecrawl / browserbase / openai)
  → execute via provider
  → write qa_story_runs (status, latency_ms, provider_session_url, assertion_failures)
  → write qa_story_evidence (screenshots, console logs, HAR)
  → on fail/recover → Slack Block Kit (transition-aware) + Discord webhook + dispatchPluginEvent
```

---

## Execution providers

| Provider | Description | When to use |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| **Firecrawl** | Cloud-hosted — no setup required | Default. Good for content checks and basic navigation |
| **Browserbase** | Full Chromium in the cloud | Complex UI interactions, video recording, HAR export |
| **Local** | Playwright on your machine via CLI | Full Playwright access; not schedulable via edge function |

To use Browserbase or Firecrawl, add your key in **Settings → Web tools** first,
then select the provider when creating a story.

---

## Creating a story

1. Click **+ New story** (header or empty state).
2. In the **New QA story** modal, fill in:
   - **Name** — short label for the story card
   - **Target URL** — the page the runner opens first (required for Firecrawl and Browserbase)
   - **Prompt — describe what to verify** — your user story in plain English (e.g. "Open the Reports page, click the first report, verify the classification badge is visible")
   - **Browser provider** — Firecrawl Actions (recommended) / Browserbase / Local Playwright (CLI only)
   - **Run schedule** — every hour (default), every 6 hours, daily, weekly, or a custom cron
3. Click **Create story**.

In the story drawer you can change the target URL and turn the story on or off.

**Generate test** on a bug's detail page creates a story and opens a draft GitHub PR
with a full Playwright test. The story uses the `local` provider and runs weekly
(Mondays 06:00 UTC).

---

## Story cards

The main grid shows one card per story with:
- **Provider badge** — Local / Browserbase / Firecrawl
- **24h pass rate** — colour-coded bar and percentage
- **7 days** — one square per UTC day: red when a run failed that day, green when
  every finished run passed, grey with none. Skipped runs never count as failures.
  From `last_7d` on `GET /v1/admin/projects/:id/qa-coverage` (`null` when the runs
  could not be read).
- **Run count** and **last run** time
- **disabled** / **queued** chip when applicable
- Link to last failure Browserbase replay session

## Story drawer

Click any card to open the story drawer:

- **Story prompt** and **provider** at the top
- **Script** section (collapsible) — the raw Playwright script if one was generated
- **Run history** — newest runs first. Expand any run to see:
  - Meta (status, provider, latency)
  - **Summary** and error message
  - **Assertion failures** table — each failing assertion listed
  - **Evidence** — screenshots, video thumbnail, HAR download
  - **Browserbase replay** link (if Browserbase was used)
- A live indicator and 3-second auto-poll when a run is active

---

## Manual run

Click **Run now** on any story to trigger an immediate execution regardless of its
schedule. The story must be on: a story that is off says "Turn the story on first";
turn it on in the story drawer.

---

## Filters

The chips above the grid filter the stories: **All**, **Failing**, **Passing**,
**No runs in 24h** and **Turned off**. The 24-hour pass rates come from the
`qa_story_coverage_24h` materialised view, refreshed every 15 minutes.

---

## Related pages

- [Mushi health](/admin/health) — verify Firecrawl / Browserbase keys
- [Improvement runs](/admin/iterate) — producer and judge iteration loop
- [Fixes](/admin/fixes) — act on test failures

## SQL query

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/query

---
title: SQL query
description: Ask about your bug data in Mushi Mushi in plain English or in read-only SQL; the SQL query page shows the SQL it ran, the result rows and a short summary.
---

# SQL query

**Route:** `/query` (sidebar: **SQL query**, under Account)

The SQL query page in Mushi Mushi answers questions about your project's bug data. On the
**Ask** tab, pick **Natural language** to type a question in plain English, or **Raw SQL**
to write a `SELECT` yourself. Every run is read-only, sandboxed and logged.

The page has four tabs: **Ask**, **History**, **Schema** (the approved tables) and
**Overview**.

---

## How it works

1. **You type a question**, for example *"How many P0/P1 reports landed this week vs last
   week?"* (press Enter to run). In **Raw SQL** mode you write the query and press ⌘/Ctrl+Enter.
2. **Graph questions go to the graph.** Questions about blast radius or dependencies are
   answered by walking the knowledge graph directly, without writing SQL.
3. **Otherwise the model writes SQL** from a schema description of the approved tables,
   filtered by `project_id = $1` and limited to 100 rows.
4. **The SQL is checked** before it runs: one statement only, no writes or DDL (`INSERT`,
   `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `DROP`, …), no system schemas (`auth`, `storage`, `vault`, …).
   A query without `LIMIT` gets `LIMIT 100` appended. A rejected query returns
   `INVALID_SQL`.
5. **The query runs as a read-only database role** (`mushi_nl_reader`) that can only
   `SELECT` the approved tables and only your project's rows. That role, not the text
   checks, is the real boundary.
6. **You get the result rows as a table**, the SQL that ran (with **Copy SQL**), and, for
   natural-language questions, a short plain-English summary.

Runs are rate-limited to 60 an hour per user; past the limit the API returns `RATE_LIMITED`.

---

## Approved tables

| Table | What's in it |
| ----- | ------------ |
| `reports` | Every incoming report with its classification fields |
| `report_groups` | Groups of similar reports |
| `classification_evaluations` | Judge scores for classifications |
| `reporter_reputation` | Reporter reputation scores |
| `reporter_devices` | Devices tracked by [Spam & abuse](/admin/anti-gaming) |
| `graph_nodes`, `graph_edges` | The knowledge graph |
| `bug_ontology` | Bug category tags |
| `fix_attempts`, `fix_verifications`, `fix_events` | Fix runs, their verification and events |
| `llm_invocations` | Every LLM call, with model, tokens and cost |
| `anti_gaming_events` | Flag and unflag events |

In **Raw SQL** mode, a query that names a table outside this list is rejected before it
reaches the database. The **Schema** tab shows the same list.

---

## Example questions

```
"Which component has the most open critical reports in the last 30 days?"

"Show me the daily report volume trend for the past 3 months."

"How many fix attempts failed vs. succeeded last week?"

"Show reports where severity is critical and status is open, created this week."
```

---

## History and saved queries

Every run, successful or not, is stored with your user, the prompt, the generated SQL,
the row count and the latency. The **Library** panel lists them in three groups:

- **Saved**: runs you pinned with **Pin to Saved**
- **Recent**: your latest runs
- **Team**: recent runs by other people on the projects you can see

You can remove a run from your history.

  Results show as a table only. The page does not draw charts and has no CSV export;
  copy the SQL if you need the data elsewhere.

---

## API

```bash
POST   /v1/admin/query              { "question": "..." }   # natural language
POST   /v1/admin/query/raw          { "sql": "SELECT ..." }  # raw SQL
GET    /v1/admin/query/history?limit=25
PATCH  /v1/admin/query/history/:id  # pin / unpin
DELETE /v1/admin/query/history/:id
GET    /v1/admin/query/team?limit=25
GET    /v1/admin/query/stats
```

---

## See also

- [Admin → Intelligence reports](/admin/intelligence): automated weekly digest built from the same data.
- [Concepts → Knowledge graph](/concepts/knowledge-graph): explore relationships visually instead of via SQL.

## Processing jobs

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/queue

---
title: Processing jobs
description: The Processing jobs page in the Mushi Mushi console shows reports waiting to be diagnosed, retries and dead-letter jobs, and lets you retry failed ones.
---

# Processing jobs

**Route:** `/queue` (sidebar: **Account → Processing jobs**)

> **Scenario:** You open Mushi Mushi on a Monday morning and 14 jobs sit in dead letter.
> Your LLM key hit a rate limit overnight and reports piled up without being
> diagnosed. This page is where you find what broke and replay the affected jobs.

Processing jobs is the operational view of the background jobs that read and sort new
reports (the fast filter and classification stages). Use it to monitor throughput, identify failures, retry stuck
items, and recover from outages.

---

## What "dead-letter" means

An item reaches `dead_letter` status after exhausting all automatic retries. Mushi
won't touch it again until you manually retry it. This is intentional — automatic
infinite retries can amplify a misconfiguration into a cost spiral.

When you see dead-letter items:
1. Read the **Last error** on one of the cards to understand why it failed.
2. Fix the root cause (wrong API key, rate limit, misconfigured repo URL).
3. Click **Retry** per item, or use **Retry page** to replay all failed items on the
   current page at once.

---

## KPI tiles (14-day sparklines)

| Tile | Healthy baseline | Warning sign |
|------|-----------------|-------------|
| **Dead letter** | 0 | Any non-zero number |
| **Failed** | Low — occasional transient failures are normal | Rising trend day-over-day |
| **Pending** | Small queue that clears within minutes | Growing pile-up = processing is slow or stuck |
| **Running** | 1–5 at any time | > 20 may indicate a processing loop |
| **Completed** | Rising trend = healthy throughput | Flat + rising failed = systematic failure |

---

## Throughput chart

The **Daily throughput** chart shows created, completed and failed jobs per day over the
last 14 days. A healthy pipeline completes about as many as it creates, with few failures.

**What to look for:**
- A day where failed > completed → something broke that day. Cross-reference the
  **Audit log** for key changes or deploys.
- Flat completed bars for 2+ days → the pipeline may be paused. Check if your BYOK
  keys expired.

---

## Stage breakdown

Counts per pipeline stage, shown as **Fast filter** (`stage1`), **Classify** (`stage2`),
**Judge** and **Fix suggestion**. If one stage has a disproportionate backlog, that's the
bottleneck. Example:

- **Fast filter has 200 pending** → new reports are not being read. Check the LLM key and
  recent AI calls in [Mushi health](/admin/health), and the prompt in [AI prompts](/admin/prompt-lab).

---

## Item cards

Paginated list (25 per page). Each card shows:
- **Stage and status badge**, and the attempt count (for example `2/3 attempts`)
- A **Waiting** chip when a pending or running job has been waiting a while
- The first 150 characters of the report, linked to the report page
- **Last error**, which often tells you exactly what went wrong
- **Timestamps**: created and last attempt
- A **Retry** button on failed and dead-letter jobs

Use the **Status** and **Stage** dropdowns to filter to just the items you care about.

---

## Bulk actions

| Button | When to use it |
|--------|---------------|
| **Retry page** | After fixing the root cause: replay all retryable jobs on the current page |
| **Flush queued** | After a rate-limit incident: replays reports the circuit breaker parked. Shown only when some are parked |
| **Recover stranded** | Re-runs the fast filter for reports stuck as new or queued for more than 5 minutes (up to 50, fewer than 3 attempts) and re-queues failed jobs that still have retries left. Shown only when something is recoverable |

These buttons need edit rights on the project; viewers see the page read-only.

Use **Recover stranded** only when reports have genuinely been stuck for more than
5 minutes. Running it while a slow function is still working can process a report twice.

---

## Common tasks

### Monday morning: 14 dead-letter jobs
1. Set **Status** to dead letter. Read **Last error** on the first card.
2. Example error: a rate limit or a rejected LLM key → fix the key in [Settings](/admin/settings) → **AI keys**.
3. Come back, filter to `dead_letter` → **Retry page** → watch the status column — items should transition to `running` then `completed`.
4. If they fail again: the root cause isn't fixed. Repeat the diagnosis.

### "Reports have been stuck for 30 minutes"
1. Look for the **Waiting** chip on pending or running jobs.
2. Click **Recover stranded**. It re-runs the fast filter for stranded reports and re-queues failed jobs with retries left.
3. Watch the Failed count: they should retry and (if the root cause is gone) complete.

### Monitoring after a deploy
1. After deploying, open the queue and set a 5-minute mental timer.
2. If the **Pending** tile rises and doesn't fall: your classify function may be
   failing. Check recent AI calls in [Mushi health](/admin/health).

---

## API

```bash
GET  /v1/admin/queue?status=&stage=&page=&pageSize=
GET  /v1/admin/queue/stats
GET  /v1/admin/queue/summary
GET  /v1/admin/queue/throughput
POST /v1/admin/queue/:id/retry
POST /v1/admin/queue/flush-queued
POST /v1/admin/queue/recover
```

---

## Related pages

- [Mushi health](/admin/health): LLM provider errors are a common cause of failed jobs
- [Settings](/admin/settings): the AI keys the diagnosis stages use
- [Audit log](/admin/audit) — cross-reference queue failures with admin actions

## Real-time collaboration

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/realtime

---
title: Real-time collaboration
description: How Mushi Mushi report pages update live, showing who else has the report open and new triage notes as teammates or the reporter post them.
---

# Real-time collaboration

There is no separate page for this. In Mushi Mushi, every report detail page
(`/reports/:id`) shows who else has it open, and its triage thread updates live, so you
can review a bug with a teammate without refreshing.

---

## Presence

The report header shows an avatar stack of the other teammates who have the same report
open. Hover an avatar to see the name and what they are doing (`viewing`, `editing` or
`commenting`).

| State | Indicator |
| ----- | --------- |
| Only you | Nothing shown |
| 1–5 others | One avatar each |
| More than 5 others | Five avatars and **+N** |

Presence is stored in the `report_presence` table. Each open page sends a heartbeat every
20 seconds, and a row expires 60 seconds after its last heartbeat, so a closed tab drops
off within a minute.

---

## Triage thread

The **Triage thread** section of the report holds notes from your team and replies from
the reporter, stored in the `report_comments` table. The console subscribes to the
thread through **Supabase Realtime**, so a new note appears without a refresh.

### Writing a note

Type in **Add a triage note…** and click **Post**. Notes are plain text (line breaks are
kept; Markdown is not rendered), up to 10,000 characters.

Check **Reply to reporter** (or click **Message reporter**) to send the note to the
person who filed the bug. It shows a **visible to reporter** badge and reaches them in the
SDK widget's inbox. Without it, the note stays internal.

Replies from the reporter appear in the same thread with a **reporter replied** badge. A
reply that says the fix did not work also shows a feedback tag, and a regression reopen is
filed automatically.

### Deleting a note

You can delete only notes you wrote (the × on your own note, then confirm). Notes
cannot be edited.

### Timestamps

Each note shows a relative time ("3 minutes ago").

  There is no @mention, no file attachment, no edit window and no Watch toggle on report
  notes. Earlier versions of this page described them, but the console does not have them.

---

## See also

- [Admin → Reports](/admin/reports): the report detail page where this happens.
- [Admin → Teams and Members](/admin/teams): manage who has access to your project.

---

## App blueprint

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/recipe

---
title: App blueprint
description: The App blueprint page in the Mushi Mushi console shows what this app is built from, the state of each part, and the draft pull request a change opens.
---

# App blueprint

**Route:** `/recipe` (sidebar: **App blueprint**, under Verify; formerly Recipe)

**First on the page:** the overall state and **Next step**: the first box in the worst
state, its reason, a button to the page that fixes it and **Show how to fix** for its
side panel. Boxes have a red (check failed), amber (needs attention) or green (OK)
edge; grey dashed boxes are not checked or not set up, never a pass.

> **Scenario:** A fix should follow this app's own tokens and tables, and you are not sure what is connected. Open App blueprint and start with the card marked **Needs attention** or **Check failed**.

App blueprint is the Mushi Mushi console screen for one project's recipe: what the app is made of, and whether each part works. With no project selected it says **No project selected**. How the recipe is stored is on the [App recipe](/concepts/app-recipe) concept page.

---

## Refresh and status

**Refresh** reads the repo again — the recipe file, design tokens, CI builds and environment variable names — and reloads this page. A failure shows the reason. Until the recipe loads, the page says **Composing the recipe…**. A load error names the app recipe and offers a retry.

The status card has two sides:

- **Overall** is the worst state on the page. When that state is a problem, it names those parts. **OK** and **Not set up** are not named as problems.
- **Recipe file** says the page is built from what Mushi already sees when `mushi.recipe.json` is missing, and tells you to add that file at the repo root to declare design tokens, deploy targets and budgets. When the file is present, the card shows its path, the short commit and when it was read. Problems in the file are listed: fix them in the repo, then press Refresh.

---

## Diagram and list

**Auto**, **Diagram** and **List** choose the layout. Auto shows the diagram, and the list below 768 px or when the browser asks for reduced motion. The line beside the control says to click a card for what is wrong and how to fix it.

Both layouts show the same eight parts, in four lanes. A part the server left out still appears, as **Not checked yet**, and says to press Refresh.

| Lane | Cards |
|------|--------|
| **Sources** | Database schema, Design system, Pages and user flows |
| **Build** | Automated checks, CI builds |
| **Deploy** | What is live |
| **Runtime** | Environment variables, Connected tools |

Cards do not move on the diagram. If the column is narrower than the lanes, the page says to drag the diagram sideways or switch to List. Each card shows its state, a one-line reason, when it was last checked, and whether problems are open. List cards also show how that part is checked and up to three facts. A card with a link opens the page that owns that part.

---

## What "not connected" means

The stored state `not_connected` is labelled **Not set up**. Nothing is configured for that part. It is optional, and the card says how to set it up. The check line reads **Nothing to check until it is set up**. It is not a pass and it is not a failure. On **Problems**, Mushi says it cannot say yet whether anything needs fixing.

| Label | What the card means |
|-------|---------------------|
| **OK** | Checked recently, and nothing needs fixing. **OK** with no check time is shown as **Not checked yet**. |
| **Needs attention** | Something does not match what the app expects. The reason says what and how to fix it. |
| **Not checked yet** | Not checked, so this is not a pass. |
| **Not confirmed** | Checked, but the result is out of date or could not decide. Not a pass. |
| **Check failed** | The last check did not finish. |

---

## Side panel

With nothing selected, the panel says to pick a card. A selected card shows the name, state, check time, reason and how it is checked. **Close** clears it.

**What it is** loads the detail. Database schema lists tables (RLS on or off, column count) and what changed since the previous scan. CI builds lists recent workflow runs with their result and estimated minutes. What is live compares each deploy target with the default-branch head; no observation says **Not observed**, and no targets says **Not set up** and points at `deploy.targets` in `mushi.recipe.json`. Environment variables is a matrix of names: **Set**, **Missing**, **Set, not declared**, or **Not checked**. Values are never shown. An empty matrix says **Not set up** and points at the Change tab. Other parts show their fields. Design system also links to the design system page.

**Problems** shows the open count after a check. For **Not checked yet**, **Not set up** and **Check failed** it says Mushi cannot say yet whether anything needs fixing, and links to where those problems are listed.

**Change** is only on Automated checks, Environment variables, and Pages and user flows. You edit the files read from the branch, press **Preview diff**, then **Open draft PR**. The preview writes nothing. Changes ship only as a reviewed draft pull request: one draft with exactly that diff, left in draft so CI does not run until you mark it ready, and nothing on the default branch changes until you merge. An open Mushi draft for the same change has to be finished or closed first. Owners and admins of the project's team can open the PR; anyone else can still preview it.

---

## Risk checks

**Risk checks** sits under the cards: store rules, an expiring domain, a broken privacy link, storage that keeps billing. Problems are listed first. Checks that never ran are under **not checked yet (not a pass)**. Passing checks are in their own disclosure. **Run checks** starts a run and tells you to refresh in a minute. Mushi's own setup checks are linked to [Full-stack audit](/admin/fullstack-audit) instead of being repeated here.

---

## Related

- [App recipe](/concepts/app-recipe) — the concept behind this screen, including `mushi.recipe.json`
- [Full-stack audit](/admin/fullstack-audit) — Mushi's own setup checks

## Releases

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/releases

---
title: Releases
description: The Releases page in the Mushi Mushi console drafts a changelog for each version from the bug reports marked fixed, crediting the users who reported them.
---

# Releases

**Route:** `/releases`

The Releases page in Mushi Mushi drafts changelogs for each version of your app,
crediting the reporters whose bug reports were fixed. Publishing tells each credited
reporter that their fix shipped.

The tabs are **Drafts**, **Published**, **Draft** (generate a new one), **Batch** and
**App stores**.

---

## What it generates

For a new draft, Mushi Mushi:
1. Collects up to 50 reports marked **fixed** in the report window (30 days by default)
   that no earlier published release already shipped.
2. Asks the AI to write a user-facing changelog: a short summary and a **Bug fixes**
   list, each line crediting the reporter.
3. Records a credit for each reporter.

---

## Creating a release

1. Open the **Draft** tab.
2. Enter the **Version** (e.g. `1.2.3`) and, if you like, a **Title (optional)**.
3. Set the **Report window (days)** (30 by default).
4. Click **Generate draft with AI**.
5. Open the draft under **Drafts**, edit the **Changelog** and click **Save draft**.
6. Click **Publish + notify** and confirm.

The same steps work from a script or an agent with an API key: reads
(`GET /v1/admin/releases`, `/stats`, `/:id`) take `mcp:read`; drafting,
editing, deleting a draft and publishing take `mcp:write`. Publishing messages
every credited reporter, so give a key `mcp:write` only where you would let it
do that. A key bound to one project only sees that project's releases. An
account-level key reaches every project you can reach, with your role in each:
it opens any release in those projects, and `/stats` needs the project named
with `project_id` (or the `X-Mushi-Project-Id` header).

---

## Release automatically when you ship

Off by default. Turn on **Release automatically when you ship** on the
Releases overview (project admins only, or
`PATCH /v1/admin/settings { "auto_release_enabled": true }`). From then on,
any of these ships a release on its own:

| Trigger | Where it comes from | Version reporters see |
|---------|---------------------|-----------------------|
| A GitHub release is **published** (not a draft or pre-release) | The Mushi GitHub App on the repo, subscribed to **Releases** | The tag, e.g. `v2.4.1` |
| A **production** deployment succeeds (`deployment_status` = success) | The Mushi GitHub App, subscribed to **Deployment statuses** | The deployed tag, or the short commit sha |
| Your CI posts `release.published` | `POST /v1/ingest/recipe/events` with an agent key (`mcp:write`) kept in CI secrets | The `version` you send |

```bash
curl -X POST "$MUSHI_API_URL/v1/ingest/recipe/events" \
  -H "X-Mushi-Api-Key: $MUSHI_CI_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "events": [ { "type": "release.published", "targetId": "web", "version": "2.4.1" } ] }'
```

For each trigger, Mushi:

1. skips it if a release with that version already exists;
2. skips it if no report was marked fixed since the last published release
   (a deploy with nothing fixed makes no release);
3. skips it while another automatic draft is open (see below);
4. drafts the release from those reports and publishes it, so each reporter
   gets one "your fix is live" message and credits are stamped once
   delivered.

An automatic release is published without anyone reading it first, and report
summaries come from your users. So its notes are not written by AI. Each fixed
report becomes one line, with markdown escaped and links removed.

Only one automatic draft can be open per project, so a GitHub release and the
deploy it triggers cannot both announce the same fixes. If publishing fails
before the release goes live, the draft stays under **Drafts**, and
auto-release pauses until you publish or delete that draft. The
auto-release card on the Releases overview says so and links to it. If the
release went live but messaging reporters failed part-way, the log says the
release is published and some reporters were not told.

The version must be a plain tag, semver or sha (letters, digits, `.`, `_`,
`+`, `-`, at most 64 characters), because reporters see it.

Send `release.published` with an agent key that has `mcp:write`, minted with
`mushi login` or in the console and kept in CI secrets. A key that cannot
release still has its event recorded, and the answer gives the reason:

| Key | `autoReleaseSkipped` |
|-----|----------------------|
| The public SDK key (`report:write`), even one used only from a native app | `key_lacks_mcp_write` |
| An `mcp:write` key that a web page has ever sent | `browser_exposed_key` |

One request releases at most once, for its last `release.published` event. The
answer gives that version in `autoReleaseVersion` and lists any others in
`autoReleaseIgnoredVersions`.

---

## Batch tab: what ships next

The **Batch** tab shows, for each repo, the release train that is running now or
leaves next. A release train collects your approved fix pull requests and merges
them together, so they ship as one deploy. The tab only reads: re-run, merge and
remove fixes from [Pipeline](/admin/pipeline).

- **Each fix** shows whether it rides or waits, the AI review's verdict at its current
  commit (the console labels it **Opus**), its CI, and why it waits.
- **Rules to ride** count how many fixes pass each rule: Opus said merge at the
  current commit, not a draft, its own CI is green, it did not keep failing trains
  at that commit, and it is not urgent (urgent fixes merge on their own).
- **Database migrations** lists migration files in the fixes' changes. Mushi looks
  in the folder your app recipe names (`data.migrationsDir` in
  `mushi.recipe.json`), or else in `supabase/migrations`, `prisma/migrations` and
  `migrations`. Mushi never runs them; apply them when you deploy. If a change could
  not be read, the list says it may be incomplete.
- **Deploy after the last train** says whether the merge commit was seen running, or
  a deploy was seen after the merge. With no deploy in 14 days it links to the
  [setup gap](/admin/onboarding#setup-gaps) that explains why reporters are not
  told.

```bash
GET /v1/admin/release-batch?projectId=   # one app, or every app you can open
```

---

## Release fields

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Version** | Tag or semver string |
| **Title** | Optional title (e.g. "Performance update") |
| **Changelog** | Markdown body (AI-drafted for a manual draft, editable) |
| **Credits** | The reporters credited, with whether each was **notified** or is **pending** |
| **Published at** | When the release was made public |

Published releases are not exposed through an SDK method; reporters hear about them
through the widget's notifications.

- [Pipeline](/admin/pipeline) — re-run, merge or remove fixes in a release train

## Pull requests

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/repo

---
title: Pull requests
description: The Pull requests page in the Mushi Mushi console lists open pull requests in connected GitHub repos, with fix branches, CI status and what each fix agent did.
---

# Pull requests

**Route:** `/repo` (sidebar: More pages → Fix → Pull requests. It is a Lab: switch it on under **Settings → Display & sidebar → Labs** to keep it in the sidebar)

This page shows every open pull request in the GitHub repositories connected to
your Mushi Mushi app, the branch of every fix attempt with its CI status, and a log
of what the fix agents did. It is where code changes land.

---

## Summary

A banner and a snapshot strip come first. The counts are fix attempts:
**Branches** / **PRs open** / **CI passing** / **CI failing** / **Merged** / **Stuck**.
**PR open** counts every attempt with an open pull request, whatever CI says, the
same way the [Fixes](/admin/fixes) page counts.

The page has three tabs: **Pull requests**, **Activity** and **Clean up**.

---

## Pull requests tab

### Open pull requests

Every open pull request in the connected repos, fix or not, grouped by what you can do:

| Group | Shows |
|-------|-------|
| **Mergeable now** | Required checks passed; a Mushi fix also has an Opus **merge** verdict on its latest commit |
| **Needs a fix** | A required check fails, or Opus said **fix first**. Open the fix to send it back |
| **Hold** | Opus said **hold**: a person decides. Merge is disabled here; the fix page shows the findings |
| **Waiting** | CI or a review is still running, or the PR is a draft |

**Merge** asks you to confirm first. Nothing merges from this list on its own.

### Fix attempt branches

A closed panel under the open pull requests lists every fix attempt's branch as a
card. Filter by **All**, **PR open**, **CI passing**, **CI failing**, **Merged** or
**Failed**.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **CI badge** | Passing, failing, running or action required |
| **Branch name** | For a Cursor cloud agent, `/MUSHI--cursor-cloud`, with the prefix taken from the bug category |
| **PR link** | External link to the GitHub pull request |
| **Report summary** | Title and severity of the original report |
| **Files / Lines** | Diff size |
| **Category** | Bug category from the classifier |
| **Timeline** | A small graph of the fix agent's events on this branch |

---

## Activity tab

A log of fix events across the app, newest first. Filter by event type:

| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Dispatched** | A fix run started for a report |
| **Branch** | Branch created |
| **Commit** | Commit pushed to the fix branch |
| **PR opened** | Pull request opened |
| **CI result** | CI checks completed |
| **Opus review** | The agent PR review gave its verdict |
| **Review follow-up** | An agent was sent back to fix the review's findings |
| **Completed** | Fix run succeeded |
| **Failed** | Fix run failed |

---

## Clean up tab

Deletes the branches Mushi made whose pull request merged or closed, closes Mushi's
own stale, replaced or held fix PRs, turns on GitHub's automatic branch deletion,
and restores a branch Mushi deleted. Nothing changes on GitHub from one click:
anyone who can edit the app asks for a list, an owner or admin approves exactly
that list (it expires after an hour) and runs it once, and Mushi checks every item
again when it runs.

---

## Managing the GitHub connection

**Repository settings**, a closed panel near the foot of the page, lists the linked
repos with their default branch, GitHub App and index status, and an **Open on
GitHub ↗** link. Its **Manage** link opens `/integrations/config`, where you
update the GitHub token, repository URL and default branch.
