## Bugs

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/reports

---
title: Bugs
description: The Bugs page is the Mushi Mushi bug list. Filter by status, severity, category and component, and start with the recommended action at the top.
---

# Bugs

**Route:** `/reports` (sidebar: **Bugs**)

The **Bugs** page is your Mushi Mushi inbox: every report, filterable by status,
severity, category, component and free text. A recommended-action card at the top tells
you what needs attention first (for example, critical items waiting for a human look).

## Diagnosis + Fix hero

The top of every report detail leads with the brand promise — *plain-English
diagnosis + a paste-ready fix* — as a single block:

1. **"Here's why it broke"**: a 1–3 sentence plain-English diagnosis (the
   Stage-2 `summary`) with severity, category, and a **confidence chip**
   (`NN% sure`), plus the likely component.
2. **"Fix it with your coding agent"**: **Copy fix prompt** copies one
   self-contained prompt: what broke, why, the suggested fix, how to reproduce,
   the page, browser and OS, the most relevant console and network lines, the
   likely files, what "done" means, and a last step to open a PR that
   references the report. It works pasted into any agent (Claude Code, Cursor,
   Codex, Windsurf) with no MCP setup. **Use with Claude Code**, **Use with
   Cursor** (IDE deeplink or cloud agent) and **Use MCP** (the tool-driven
   prompt for agents with Mushi MCP connected) sit underneath.

**Fail-graceful, by design.** Accuracy matters most for this audience: a
confident-but-wrong diagnosis is worse than none. So when classifier
confidence is **below 0.7** (or the summary is missing), the header flips to
**"Not sure yet — here's what I'd check first"** and lists the most concrete
signals (component, reproduction hint, raw summary) instead of asserting a
single root cause. The detailed sections below are unchanged; the hero just
lifts the answer to the top.

## Compact diagnosis preview

Press **Space** on the focused row in the list to open a preview drawer without
leaving the list. It shows the same confidence-aware label and, when a fix brief is
ready, a **Copy fix prompt** button, so you get the answer before you open the report.

Selecting a report opens the full detail view:

- **Recommended action**: single-sentence guidance derived from the
  report's status, severity and elapsed time, with one button.
- **Description + screenshot + breadcrumbs** captured by the SDK. The
  screenshot is click-to-zoom.
- **Classification panel**: category, severity, confidence, the LLM summary,
  component, reproduction hint, and the model and latency of the triage call.
- **Console / network / performance**: always rendered, with informative
  empty states when the SDK didn't capture data (so silence is visible).
- **Comments + presence**: the header shows **Also viewing:** with anyone else on
  the same report, and comments arrive live.
- **Actions**: change status, dispatch a fix, close as "Not a code bug", and sync
  the report to your tracker (Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues or PagerDuty, whichever
  are connected in Integrations). When the report has no stack trace, source file
  or failed request, "Not a code bug" is the main button and dispatch moves to
  "Dispatch anyway".
- **Fix card + pipeline flow**: when a fix is dispatched, the detail page shows
  the active attempt, CI badge, and merge controls.
- **Related links**: other reports for this component, this reporter's history,
  the knowledge graph, the dispatched PR and the auto-fix pipeline.

---

## Merging a fix from report detail

When a fix attempt completes with an open PR, the report detail page shows:

1. **CI feedback**: check-run status with **Refresh CI status** and a link to
   GitHub Actions.
2. **Merge PR**: confirm popover (squash by default). Disabled when the report
   is already **Fixed** or the PR is merged.
3. **Primary attempt selection**: if a retry failed after a successful PR open,
   the UI surfaces the mergeable attempt, not the failed retry.

The merge goes through the review gate: while the PR's latest Opus review says
**hold**, the merge is refused unless a team member (not a viewer) overrides it from
the console with a reason. API keys (CLI, MCP) cannot override.

After merge, the report status becomes **Fixed**, the reporter widget receives a
resolution notification, and `fix.applied` webhooks fire.

Equivalent CLI:

```bash
mushi fixes refresh-ci <fixId>
mushi fixes merge <fixId>
```

See [Fixes → Merging from the console](/admin/fixes#merging-from-the-console)
for the full sequence diagram and prerequisites.

---

## Research

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/research

---
title: Research
description: The Research page in the Mushi Mushi console runs a web search through your Firecrawl key and lets you attach useful results to a bug.
---

# Research

**Route:** `/research` (a Lab: under **More pages** in the sidebar unless you keep it there)

Research in Mushi Mushi is a web search through your own Firecrawl key. Use it while
reviewing a bug to find release notes, Stack Overflow threads or vendor changelogs, and
attach what helps to the bug. The tabs are **Search** and **History**.

---

## What it's for

- **Debug a library error**: "Why does `react-query` v5 throw on an empty select return?"
- **Find migration paths**: "How do I upgrade from Next.js 14 to 15 App Router?"
- **Check best practices**: "What are the current Supabase RLS performance recommendations?"

Each search is saved as a session for the project, so teammates can open it from
**History** (query, mode, number of results and when) without running it again.

---

## Running a search

1. Type a query of 2 to 500 characters (an error signature, library name or doc topic).
2. Press **Search** or `Enter`.

Each result card shows the page title, its URL and an excerpt of the page text, plus
**Attached** or **Not attached**. Results are not summarised by AI and carry no
relevance score.

If the search fails, the page names the reason:
- **FIRECRAWL_NOT_CONFIGURED**: no Firecrawl key for this project. **Open Firecrawl key**
  takes you to it.
- **FIRECRAWL_AUTH_FAILED**: Firecrawl rejected the key.
- **RATE_LIMITED**: Firecrawl is rate-limiting you. Try again shortly.
- **SEARCH_FAILED**: the search did not complete.

Research sessions are stored in Mushi Mushi's database for your project and are not
shown to other teams. Firecrawl processes queries on their infrastructure using your key;
see their [privacy policy](https://www.firecrawl.dev/privacy-policy).

---

## Attaching a result to a bug

Click **Attach to bug** on a result, pick the bug under **Which bug does this help?**,
and click **Attach to this bug**. The card then reads **Saved on bug** with a link to it.

---

## Automatic results on error reports

When a report carries a real error (a Sentry exception or an error-level console line), Mushi searches for it once after diagnosis and shows the results on the report under **Others who hit this**.

- **Where it looks:** Firecrawl's developer index first (GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs and docs), then GitHub and Stack Overflow web results for any remaining slots. The developer index often finds the pull request that fixed the same error.
- **Search again / Search now:** runs the search from the report page. Only results not already on the report are added. Pressing it twice within 10 minutes searches once.
- **Cost:** about 2 to 5 Firecrawl credits per search, billed to your own key.

---

## Prerequisites

A Firecrawl API key must be configured in **Settings → AI keys** before Research works. A key shared with every app in your organization works too.

---

## Related pages

- [Settings](/admin/settings) — add your Firecrawl key
- [Bugs](/admin/reports) — where attached results and **Others who hit this** appear

---

## Tester rewards

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/rewards

---
title: Tester rewards
description: Set up Mushi Mushi tester rewards from the console, with points for reporter activity, a tier ladder, and the perks your app grants at each tier.
---

# Tester rewards

**Route:** `/rewards` (sidebar: **Account → Tester rewards**)

Tester rewards in Mushi Mushi give the people who report bugs a reason to come back.
Activity your users send through the SDK earns points when a rule (or a built-in
default) covers that action. Points advance tiers. Tiers open perks you configure,
such as a role or a coupon your app grants, and (optionally) monetary payouts via
Stripe Connect.

The page has these tabs: **Overview**, **Bounties**, **Activity rules**, **Tier ladder**,
**Contributors**, **Quests**, **Retention**, **Simulator** and **Settings**. **Bounties**
publishes the app to the Mushi Bounties marketplace so outside testers can find bugs for
a reward; this page does not cover it in detail.

  Configuring rules, tiers and webhooks needs **Builder**, **Studio** or **Enterprise**.
  On Free the page shows a preview with an upgrade link. Monetary payouts need
  **Enterprise**.

---

## How the pipeline works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant App as Your app
  participant SDK as Mushi SDK
  participant API as POST /v1/sdk/activity
  participant DB as Postgres
  participant Admin as Admin console

  App->>SDK: mushi.identify(userId, traits)
  App->>SDK: mushi.submitActivity([{ action: 'page_view' }])
  SDK->>API: batch flush (≤100 events)
  API->>DB: resolve / upsert end_users row
  API->>DB: insert end_user_activity rows
  API->>DB: points per rule (or built-in default), caps applied
  DB->>DB: trigger: apply_activity_points keeps end_user_points totals
  Admin->>DB: GET /v1/admin/rewards/overview
  Admin-->>Admin: live dashboard refreshes
```

The `identify()` call is the gate. Until a user ID is known, activity events
are buffered and tagged with the anonymous `reporter_token_hash`. As soon as
`identify()` fires (typically on auth state change), the SDK flushes the buffer
with the resolved user traits attached, and the server upserts an `end_users`
record that links all future activity and reports to that identity.

---

## Overview tab

The snapshot strip above the tabs shows **Testers (30 days)**, **Points (30 days)** and
**Payouts waiting**. The Overview tab adds:

| Section | What it shows |
|---------|---------------|
| **Top testers** and **Running quests** | Who leads, and which quests are live |
| **Tier distribution** | How many contributors sit at each tier |
| **Activity feed (last 24 h)** | The latest activity events the SDK sent |

---

## One-click recommended defaults

On an empty Activity rules tab, click **Use recommended defaults** (or call
`POST /v1/admin/rewards/presets/apply`). That idempotently installs:

| Action | Points | Max / day | When it fires |
|--------|-------:|----------:|---------------|
| `report.submitted` | 10 | 20 | After ingest links the report to an `end_user` |
| `report.triaged` | 50 | none | After `classify-report` finishes (awarded once per report) |
| `comment_posted` | 8 | 30 | Reporter comments |

Plus a 4-tier ladder: Explorer (0), Contributor (100), Champion (500) and Legend (2,000). Safe to
re-run — existing custom rules/slugs are never clobbered. Full operator guide:
[`docs/REWARDS.md`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/docs/REWARDS.md).

---

## Activity rules tab

Rules define which user actions earn points and what the caps are. The **Point rules**
table has these columns; edit them in place and click **Save rules**.

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Action** | The `action` string the SDK sends (e.g. `report_submit`) |
| **Base pts** | Points awarded per occurrence. Negative values deduct points. |
| **Daily cap** | Cap per user per day. Empty = unlimited. |
| **Lifetime cap** | Lifetime cap per user. Empty = unlimited. |
| **Enabled** | Toggle without deleting. Disabled rules skip evaluation silently. |

Each rule also carries `multiplier_eligible` and `requires_jwt_verification` flags,
set through the API (`PUT /v1/admin/rewards/rules`), not in the table.

**Built-in fallbacks.** When no rule exists for an action, the server uses a built-in
table, for example `report.submitted` 10, `report.triaged` 50, `report_submit` 10,
`report_confirmed` 50, `report_fixed` 25, `comment_posted` 8 and `report_dismissed` -5.
An action with neither a rule nor a fallback earns nothing.

The server computes each award (rule, caps, tier multiplier), then a PostgreSQL trigger
(`private.apply_activity_points`) keeps the `end_user_points` totals in step.

### Custom rules

The table has no add button. To reward an action you define in your own code, send it
from the SDK:

```typescript
mushi.submitActivity([
  { action: 'lesson_complete', metadata: { lessonId: 'l_123', score: 0.9 } }
])
```

Then upsert a rule with `action: 'lesson_complete'` through `PUT /v1/admin/rewards/rules`.
It starts accruing on the next event; no SDK update is required.

---

## Tier ladder tab

Tiers map a point threshold to a named rank with optional perks. Each tier card lets you
edit:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Points threshold** | Minimum `total_points` to reach this tier |
| **Display name** | User-visible name (e.g. "Explorer", "Contributor") |
| **Monetary reward (USD)** | Payout queued when a user reaches the tier (monetary plans only) |
| **Enabled** | Turn a tier off without deleting it |

A tier also has a slug, perks JSON and a host credit payload (what your app grants);
the recommended defaults fill these in.

**Default ladder when you have configured no tiers** (shown as "Using default tiers"):

| Tier | Threshold | Color |
|------|----------:|-------|
| Free | 0 | Grey |
| Explorer | 100 | Blue |
| Contributor | 500 | Purple |
| Champion | 2 000 | Amber |

Edit the ladder to match your own program. Tier evaluation runs inside
`awardPointsForEndUser` after every award; if the new total crosses a threshold, a
`reward.tier_changed` webhook fires.

---

## Contributors tab

A leaderboard of your top reporters, ranked by points. Choose the last 30 days or
all time, filter by tier, and search by name.

**Per-contributor drill-down** (`/v1/admin/rewards/contributors/:id`) shows:

- **Lifetime points** and **Activity events**
- Each `end_user_activity` entry with the action, points awarded, and timestamp
- **Anti-fraud flags**, when there are any
- **Admin actions**: **Award bonus points** and **Override tier**

Export and erasure are SDK routes the end user calls (see [GDPR & consent](#gdpr--consent)),
not console buttons.

  The Contributors tab shows email addresses and display names collected via
  `identify()` traits. Make sure your privacy policy discloses that you collect
  this data through the Mushi SDK before enabling rewards. See the
  [Privacy & GDPR](#gdpr--consent) section below.

---

## Quests tab

Quests are multi-step goals. A user completes a quest by performing a defined
sequence of actions.

**Example quest**, "First Feedback" (each step is one action with a label):
1. `screen_view_unique_per_day`, label "Look around the app"
2. `report_submit`, label "Send your first bug report"
3. `comment_posted`, label "Reply to the team"

Completing a quest awards bonus points in addition to the per-action awards, and
fires a `reward.quest_completed` webhook.

### Quest editor

Click **New quest** to open the editor:

- **Quest name** and **Description (optional)**
- **Bonus points on completion**
- **Expires after (days, optional)**
- **Steps (in order)**: each step has an action and a label (for example "Visit /pricing")
- **Repeatable**: whether a user can complete the same quest more than once

Quest progress is evaluated server-side in `evaluateQuestProgress` after each
activity flush, so no client-side code is needed to track completion state.

---

## Retention tab

The Retention tab (**Retention impact**) compares how long contributors in your highest
tier keep coming back with everyone else: the top tier's median retention in days,
the others' median, and the **Retention lift** between them. It is computed on request
by `GET /v1/admin/rewards/retention-impact`.

---

## Simulator tab

The **Sandbox simulator** previews how an activity log would score against your
current rules, without real data.

1. Type an `action` name and a count for each line; **+ Add event** adds a line.
2. Click **Run simulation**. The server applies your rules and caps and returns
   **Total points**, the **Reached tier**, and a breakdown per action
   (count, points per event, subtotal, note).

Nothing is written: no `end_users` row is created or changed.

Use this to sanity-check daily cap edge cases before you change a rule.

---

## Settings tab

The Settings tab has four sections: **Host webhooks**, **Identity verification**
(JWKS URL, audience and issuer for verifying your users' tokens), **Payout ledger** and
**Disputes**.

Consent and widget display are SDK options, not console settings: `consentMode`
(`explicit`, the default, or `auto`), `showInWidget` and `showNotifications` in the
SDK's rewards config.

### Webhooks

Webhook payloads are sent for these events. Every payload carries `event`,
`end_user_id` and `occurred_at`:

| Event |
|-------|
| `reward.points_awarded` |
| `reward.tier_changed` |
| `reward.quest_completed` |
| `reward.payout_requested` |
| `reward.payout_paid` |

Add endpoints under **Host webhooks** (an HTTPS URL and an optional signing secret of at
least 16 characters; leave it empty and Mushi Mushi creates one and shows it once), and
send a test event from there. `@mushi-mushi/node` exports `createMushiRewardsHandler` to
verify and route these events in your server.

---

## Monetary payouts (P2)

  Monetary payouts require the **Enterprise** plan and a connected Stripe
  account. Each end user onboards through the SDK route `POST /v1/sdk/me/payout/onboard`.

When monetary payouts are enabled:

1. Each contributing user completes a Stripe Connect Express onboarding.
2. A payout is queued when a user reaches a tier that has a **Monetary reward (USD)**.
3. The `reward-payout-aggregator` cron job (monthly, on the 1st at 09:00 UTC) checks
   the user's KYC and anti-fraud flags, then sends the Stripe transfer and marks the
   `reward_payouts` row paid or failed.
4. **Payout ledger** in the Settings tab lists the payouts, so you can top up your
   Stripe balance before the run.

The JWT verification step (`verifyUserToken` in `MushiRewardsConfig`) ensures
that monetary awards are only issued to authenticated users whose identity the
host app can vouch for — preventing anonymous abuse.

---

## GDPR & consent

The rewards pipeline stores:

| Table | Data |
|-------|------|
| `end_users` | `external_user_id`, optional `email` + `display_name`, `last_seen_at` |
| `end_user_activity` | `action`, `points_awarded`, `occurred_at`, metadata |
| `end_user_points` | `total_points`, `points_30d`, `points_lifetime` |

**User rights** are handled by SDK endpoints:

| Endpoint | Right |
|----------|-------|
| `GET /v1/sdk/me/export` | Data portability — returns the full activity log as JSON |
| `DELETE /v1/sdk/me` | Erasure — deletes the end user's activity, sessions and analytics events, zeroes `end_user_points`, anonymises the `end_users` row |
| `POST /v1/sdk/me/consent` | Withdraw / re-grant opt-in; withdrawal stops new award events |

  **These three routes need proof of who is asking.** Since 2026-09-22 each
  one requires either your host JWT (`verifyUserToken`, the same signing key
  the rewards pipeline uses) or a signed `X-Mushi-User-Token` for that end
  user; without one the route answers `IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED`, and a token
  for somebody else answers `IDENTITY_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`. Before that, an
  `identify()` id alone was enough — and those ids are usually guessable, so
  one person could export or erase another person's data. Wire
  `verifyUserToken` (see [Monetary payouts](#monetary-payouts-p2)) before you
  point users at a privacy screen.

If you use `consentMode: 'explicit'` (the default), the SDK surfaces a
one-time prompt before the first `identify()` flush. The user's choice is
persisted server-side in `end_users.opted_in`, so it follows them across
devices.

---

## SDK health

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/sdk-health

---
title: 'SDK health'
description: SDK health in Mushi Mushi lists what stops your app's reports arriving, like a missing install, missing CI keys, an outdated SDK or a blocking CSP, with fixes.
---

# SDK health

**SDK health** is a section of the [Connect](/admin/connect) page
(`/connect#connect-sdk-health`), not a page of its own. Mushi Mushi checks the active
app's repo, keys, CI and live site, and lists the problems that stop bug reports from
arriving, each with a fix. It catches "I installed the SDK two weeks ago and forgot to
ship the deploy".

## What it checks

| Problem | Severity | Fix offered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No GitHub repo is connected | error (warn once the SDK has checked in) | none: connect a repo |
| The SDK isn't in your app yet | error | **File install task** for your fix agent |
| GitHub Actions is missing the Mushi keys | error (warn once seen) | **Write CI secrets** to the repo |
| This app has no working SDK key | error | **Write CI secrets** (mints a key and writes it) |
| The SDK has never checked in | error | none |
| An SDK update is out | warn | **Open upgrade PR**, or a link to the upgrade PR already open with its CI state |
| Your site's security policy blocks Mushi | error | **File CSP task** |
| Cold: no check-in for N days | warn (after 7 days) | none |

A check that could not run (no live site address known, the SDK versions could not be
read, …) is listed under the problems as a note. The section never says "No SDK problems
found" while a check could not run.

**Fix all** runs every pending fix in order: CI secrets first, then the install task,
then the upgrade PR, then the CSP task. Writing secrets to GitHub and **Fix all** ask
you to confirm first. **Check again** re-runs the checks.

## Heartbeat freshness

The same freshness scale is used wherever the console shows the SDK heartbeat (the
project switcher, the Connect snapshot and the key list):

- **Healthy**: last check-in under 1 hour ago
- **Stale**: up to 7 days
- **Cold**: more than 7 days
- **Never**: no check-in yet

## Where it lives

- **Connect page**: the **SDK health** section.
- **Setup checklist**: the "Install the SDK in your app" step's **Fix** button opens the same panel.
- **Project switcher**: each app shows a one-line heartbeat that links to SDK health.

## API

```bash
GET  /v1/admin/projects/:id/sdk-health
POST /v1/admin/projects/:id/sdk-health/tasks
```

- [SDK reference → Overview](/sdks): every published SDK with its
  current latest version.
- [SDK upgrade lockfile helper](/admin/sdk-upgrade-lockfile): make upgrade PRs pass a
  frozen-lockfile install.
- [Concepts → Architecture](/concepts/architecture): where the
  heartbeat data flows in the gateway.

## SDK upgrade lockfile helper

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/sdk-upgrade-lockfile

---
title: SDK upgrade lockfile helper
description: Add one workflow to your repo so Mushi Mushi's SDK upgrade PRs arrive with a refreshed lockfile and pass npm ci or pnpm install --frozen-lockfile.
---

# SDK upgrade lockfile helper

In Mushi Mushi, **Create Upgrade PR** bumps `@mushi-mushi/*` in your `package.json` files. It
does not touch your lockfile, so without help the PR fails a frozen install
(`npm ci`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) until someone runs the package
manager by hand.

Add the workflow below once, and every upgrade PR arrives with the lockfile
already refreshed by your own package manager.

## How it works

1. Mushi sees `.github/workflows/mushi-sdk-lockfile.yml` on your default branch.
2. It pushes the bump as **one commit** to a `mushi/sdk-upgrade-*` branch and
   holds the PR back. The console shows **Refreshing lockfile…**.
3. The push starts your workflow. It runs `npm install --package-lock-only`,
   `pnpm install --lockfile-only` or `yarn install --mode update-lockfile`, always
   with `--ignore-scripts`, and commits the lockfile as `github-actions[bot]`.
4. Mushi checks the branch every 5 minutes. When the lockfile commit is there,
   it opens the PR, so your CI runs on the refreshed lockfile.
5. If no lockfile commit arrives within 30 minutes, the PR opens anyway with a
   **Lockfile not refreshed** note. Check the workflow run on that branch.

Without the workflow, nothing changes: the PR opens at once and its body links
here.

## Add the workflow

Save this as `.github/workflows/mushi-sdk-lockfile.yml` on your default branch.
The console shows the same file under **Upgrade PRs fail `npm ci`? Add the
lockfile helper**, with a copy button.

```yaml
# Mushi SDK lockfile helper. Save as .github/workflows/mushi-sdk-lockfile.yml
# on your default branch. Mushi then pushes each @mushi-mushi/* bump first,
# this workflow refreshes the lockfile, and the upgrade PR opens after it.
# Docs: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/sdk-upgrade-lockfile
name: Mushi SDK lockfile

on:
  push:
    branches: ['mushi/sdk-upgrade-**']

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: mushi-lockfile-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lockfile:
    # Never react to this workflow's own lockfile commit.
    if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5  # v4.3.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e  # v6.4.0
        with:
          # No version file? Replace with  node-version: 22
          node-version-file: .nvmrc  # or .node-version / package.json
          # Nothing is installed here; auto-caching also fails without a root lockfile.
          package-manager-cache: false
      # Private registry? Write ~/.npmrc auth from a secret before this step, e.g.
      #   - run: echo "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}" >> ~/.npmrc
      #     env:
      #       NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
      - uses: kensaurus/mushi-mushi/.github/actions/sdk-lockfile-refresh@master
```

It runs only on `mushi/sdk-upgrade-*` branches, needs only `contents: write`,
stops after 10 minutes, and cancels a superseded run on the same branch.

## What the action does

The action lives at
[`.github/actions/sdk-lockfile-refresh`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/tree/master/.github/actions/sdk-lockfile-refresh).
It is a shell script with no dependencies.

| Step | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Find manifests | `package.json` files changed in the tip commit (`HEAD~1..HEAD`) |
| Find lockfiles | For each one, the nearest lockfile at or above it: the workspace root, or each app's own lockfile in a repo without workspaces |
| Pick the package manager | `packageManager` in `package.json` when its lockfile is there, else the lockfile present (`pnpm-lock.yaml`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`) |
| Pin the version | `corepack enable` for pnpm and yarn. For npm, the major in `packageManager` (via `npx npm@`), which keeps lockfile v3 fields such as `libc` stable; otherwise the runner's npm, with a warning when the lockfile has `libc` fields |
| Regenerate | npm: `install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`, plus `--legacy-peer-deps` when `.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps=true`. pnpm: `install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts --no-frozen-lockfile`. yarn: `install --mode update-lockfile` |
| Commit | Only when a lockfile changed: `chore(deps): refresh lockfile for @mushi-mushi/* bump` as `github-actions[bot]`, pushed with the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` |

  Yarn support is untested; no host we run uses yarn yet. npm and pnpm are
  covered.

## Private registries

The lockfile refresh resolves every dependency, so it needs the same registry
auth your CI install uses. Either write `~/.npmrc` from a secret before the
action (as in the commented step above), or use `actions/setup-node`'s
`registry-url` input with `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` set from a secret. Never commit a
token to `.npmrc`.

## Pinning

`@master` follows the latest action. To pin, replace `master` with a commit
SHA from this repository; the action has no release tags of its own.

## Why Mushi does not write the lockfile or the workflow

- **The lockfile:** only the package manager can write it correctly. A
  hand-edited pnpm v9 lockfile breaks on peer-suffixed keys, and npm cannot run
  inside Mushi's edge runtime.
- **The workflow:** writing files under `.github/workflows` needs the GitHub
  App's `workflows` permission, which Mushi does not request (least privilege,
  ADR 0016). You add the file once; Mushi only reads it.

## Limits

- **Refreshing an open upgrade PR** (the **Refresh** button) pushes to that
  PR's branch. The workflow refreshes the lockfile, but GitHub does not start
  CI for a push made with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so re-run the PR's checks once after
  the lockfile commit lands.
- The PR opens on the next 5-minute check after the lockfile commit, so expect
  a short wait.

## Settings

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/settings

---
title: Settings
description: The Settings page in Mushi Mushi holds every project option, from bug alerts and spend limits to your own AI keys, web tools, voice reports and SDK connection.
---

# Settings

**Route:** `/settings` (sidebar: **Settings**)

> **Scenario:** Your widget copy feels off, you want your own AI keys on the bill,
> and Slack should ping the channel when a critical bug lands. This page holds every
> Mushi Mushi project setting: alerts, keys, widget and developer toggles.

The page has six tabs: **General**, **AI keys**, **Web tools**, **Voice reports**,
**SDK & connection** and **Display & sidebar**. The tab you pick is saved in the URL
(`?tab=`). Old links still work: `?tab=firecrawl` and `?tab=browserbase` open **Web
tools**, `?tab=health` and `?tab=dev` open **SDK & connection**, `?tab=keys` opens
**AI keys** and `?tab=labs` opens **Display & sidebar**.

---

## Tabs

### General

Bug alerts (Slack channel), error tracking (Sentry), an optional read-only link to your
Supabase database, and **Bug sorting**: the AI models for triage, the quick check, the
judge and fixes, the quick-check confidence, grouping of similar bugs and fix branch
names. It also holds daily limits for Firecrawl and test writing, the feedback widget's
"Bug reports by Mushi" line, and, behind **Fixes and CI → Show**, the pull request
review, verified merge, CI cost and CI policy settings.

**Spend limits** (project admins) cap what the project spends. Leave a field
empty for no limit.

| Limit | What happens when it is reached |
|---|---|
| **Monthly AI budget** | Every AI call for the project (triage, fixes, chat) stops until the 1st of next month (UTC). New reports get a short explanation instead of a diagnosis. Calls on your own API keys count too. |
| **Auto-fix spend limit, last 30 days** | Mushi stops starting fixes on its own. Fixes you start yourself still run, and show the 30-day spend. |
| **Automatic fixes per day** | Same, counted per UTC day. A limit of 3 allows 3 automatic fixes. |
| **Ask me before fixes that may cost more than** | A high or critical fix estimated above this waits for your approval, including fixes you start. |

New projects start with $2 per 30 days and 3 automatic fixes a day.

If Mushi cannot read this month's spend (a database error), the AI call goes
ahead and the failure is reported to the operator's error monitoring. A
temporary read failure never stops triage, and it never passes unnoticed.

### AI keys

Your own keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Cursor, Firecrawl, Browserbase and
Supabase. Keys are stored encrypted in Supabase Vault, and after saving the list shows
only a short hint of each key. A key can belong to one app or be shared with your other
apps; an app's own key is tried first. The Cursor row also holds spend-down mode (see
[Spend credits](/admin/credits)).

### Web tools

- **Firecrawl (web pages)**: your Firecrawl key, the websites it may read, and the pages
  per lookup. Firecrawl reads public web pages while Mushi diagnoses a bug.
- **Known fixes on the web**: the **Search the web for known fixes** switch.
- **Browserbase (cloud browser)**: runs [scheduled tests](/admin/qa-coverage) in a cloud
  browser when a story's provider is `browserbase`. Keys go through
  `GET|PUT /v1/admin/byok/browserbase`.

### Voice reports

Report bugs by voice from your phone, Telegram or Slack. See [Voice intake](/admin/voice).

### SDK & connection

**Check the connection** (whether this browser reaches Mushi and where your data
lives), **Install the bug widget** (a link to [Connect](/admin/connect), where the
install snippet lives, and the API address to copy), **Send a test bug**, and **Debug
logging (this browser)**, which logs to the browser console. Debug logging is stored in
this browser only; it is never sent to the SDK or end users.

### Display & sidebar

How the console looks in this browser: theme (system, dark, light), density, table rows
and focus mode (Ctrl/Cmd + . toggles it, Esc exits). The same controls open from your name
at the foot of the sidebar. Below them, choose which extra pages (Labs) stay in the
sidebar. Every other page is under **More pages** in the sidebar. `?tab=labs` links still
open this tab.

---

## Changing a key

1. Open the **AI keys** tab.
2. Add the new key on the provider's row and save it.
3. Open [Mushi health](/admin/health) → **Probe now** to verify the new key works.

Do not paste a Supabase `service_role` key here. That key bypasses all row-level
security and must only be used server-side. The Supabase row asks for a scoped,
read-only access token, as its instructions describe.

# Setup Copilot

**Route:** `/setup-copilot` redirects to `/onboarding?tab=diagnose`, the **Fix a problem**
tab of the **Set up** page. It is no longer a page of its own.

> **Scenario:** SDK and CLI are almost wired, but you want a guided checklist
> that verifies ingest + dispatch with copy-paste commands.

The **Fix a problem** tab in Mushi Mushi checks the active project in four sections:

1. **Connect credentials**: a copy-paste `mushi connect --api-key … --project-id …
   --endpoint … --wait` command, or `mushi init` / `mushi upgrade` in your app repo.
   Wait for the SDK heartbeat.
2. **Install snippet**, plus **CI & store builds**: the environment variables your CI
   and store builds need (for Expo, `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values are compiled in, so rebuild
   after a change).
3. **SDK health**: the heartbeat compared with the console's API host, which catches an
   SDK pointed at the wrong endpoint, the installed SDK version, and **Create Upgrade PR**
   when it is behind.
4. **Verify both tracks**: separate checks for reports coming in and fixes going out.

Use it after [CLI device auth](/admin/cli-auth) and the Connect install, or when
`mushi doctor` reports gaps.

## Agent skills

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/skill-pipelines

---
title: Agent skills
description: Agent skills in Mushi Mushi recommend skills from the kenji skills and skills.sh ecosystem for each classified bug and run them as pipelines during review.
---

# Agent skills (skill pipelines)

**Route:** `/skills` (sidebar: **Agent skills**, under Connect; the page was called Skill Pipelines before)

Agent skills bring the [kenji skills / skills.sh](https://github.com/kensaurus/skills) agent-skill ecosystem into Mushi Mushi bug review. When a bug report is classified, Mushi recommends the most relevant Cursor agent skills — and you can attach a skill chain to any report, visualize it as a live React Flow pipeline, and execute it either as a handoff to your local Cursor agent or automatically via Cursor Cloud.

---

## How it works

```
git repo skills/SKILL.md (kenji skills or any skills.sh-compatible repo)
  → skill-sync syncs SKILL.md files into the agent_skills catalog (daily cron)
  → classify-report Stage 2 recommends top 3 skills per report (pgvector similarity)
  → You start a pipeline run from the Report Detail page (or via CLI/MCP)
  → Mushi composes a "run packet" — skill instructions + full report context
  → Console renders the chain as a live React Flow pipeline
  → Steps update in real-time as your Cursor agent checks them in
```

---

## The three tabs

### Skill Catalog

Browse the full skill catalog grouped by category (`workflow`, `debug`, `test`, `audit`, `enhance`, …). Search by name or description. Open a skill to preview its SKILL.md, then under **Apply to a report** paste a report ID, pick a **Mode** and click **Start pipeline**.

### Pipeline Runs

All pipeline runs for your project — past and active. Click a run to see the live React Flow visualization with step-level status (pending → running → passed / failed). Subscribe to real-time updates without refreshing.

### Sources

Manage the GitHub repos whose SKILL.md files are synced into your project's catalog. A new project starts with no sources; the page suggests adding `kensaurus/skills` (70+ skills). Any [skills.sh](https://skills.sh)-compatible repo works.

---

## Execution modes

| Mode | Description | When to use |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| **Handoff** (default) | Mushi composes a run packet you paste into Cursor | Local development, free, full Cursor IDE experience |
| **Cloud** (opt-in) | Each step dispatches a Cursor Cloud agent run automatically | CI pipelines, async execution, PM-driven automation |

---

## Triage links (`?skill=`)

Share a pre-loaded review link with any team member:

```
https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/admin/reports/<report-id>?skill=workflow-fix-and-ship
```

When opened, the report detail page pre-selects the skill and prompts to start the pipeline. Useful for PMs handing off to devs, or for embedding in Slack/Linear notifications.

---

## CLI quick reference

```bash
# Browse the skill catalog
mushi skills list
mushi skills list --category workflow
mushi skills list --search "fix bug"

# View full skill instructions
mushi skills show workflow-fix-and-ship

# Trigger skill sync (after adding a new source)
mushi skills sync

# Start a pipeline for a report
mushi pipeline start <reportId> --skill workflow-fix-and-ship
mushi pipeline start <reportId> --skill workflow-fix-and-ship --mode cloud

# Watch a pipeline run and print the context packet
mushi pipeline watch <runId>

# Check in a step (report your progress back to Mushi)
mushi pipeline checkin <runId> --step 0 --status passed
mushi pipeline checkin <runId> --step 1 --status failed --notes "Build failed: missing dep"
```

---

## MCP tools

Use these from your Cursor agent to close the loop without leaving the IDE:

| Tool | Scope | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `list_skills` | read | Browse the skill catalog |
| `get_skill` | read | Full skill body + chain |
| `start_skill_pipeline` | write | Attach a skill to a report and get the run packet |
| `get_pipeline_run` | read | Fetch the context packet and step statuses |
| `checkin_pipeline_step` | write | Report step completion — PM sees it live in the console |

---

## Security

Skill catalog content comes exclusively from **allowlisted GitHub repos** configured in the Sources tab. Arbitrary URLs are never fetched. Every SKILL.md body is scanned for leaked API keys before storage.

- Allowlisted sources only — no arbitrary URL ingestion
- Secret-pattern scan before embedding or storing any SKILL.md body
- Skill content flows *into* LLM prompts only — never executed against raw user strings (air-gap preserved)
- Description length enforced at ≤ 1024 chars per the Agent Skills spec
- Run packet capped at 40,000 chars to prevent context overflows

---

## Adding a new skill source

### Go to Agent skills → Sources

Click **Add source** and enter the GitHub `owner/repo` slug (e.g. `myorg/my-skills-repo`).

### Trigger a sync

Click **Sync now** or run `mushi skills sync`. The `skill-sync` edge function fetches all `skills/*/SKILL.md` files, parses frontmatter, embeds descriptions, and upserts the catalog.

### Browse the new skills

Switch to the **Skill Catalog** tab. New skills appear grouped by category prefix.

## Single sign-on

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/sso

---
title: Single sign-on
description: Register a SAML 2.0 identity provider for Mushi Mushi in Supabase Auth, and record OIDC provider details, from the Single sign-on view of the console.
---

# Single sign-on

**Route:** `/team?view=sso` (**Team → Single sign-on**; the old `/sso` address redirects there)

The Single sign-on view (page title **SSO Configuration**) registers identity providers
for the active project in the Supabase Auth instance behind Mushi Mushi. Settings are
stored per project.

SSO is available on the **Enterprise** plan (the `sso` entitlement). Without it the Team tab is
hidden, and opening the address shows which plan includes it. The API also checks the Enterprise license: without one it runs in
evaluation mode, which is licensed for development and testing only.

---

## Supported protocols

| Protocol | Use when |
|----------|---------|
| **SAML 2.0** (self-service) | Your IdP exposes a metadata URL (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) |
| **OpenID Connect** | Saved for audit only. Supabase's Auth Admin API has no OIDC endpoint, so Mushi Mushi cannot register it; the issuer and client ID are kept so you can quote them in a Supabase support ticket |

---

## Registering an identity provider

1. Select **Provider type** — SAML 2.0 or OIDC.
2. Enter a **Provider name** — a human-readable label (e.g. "Acme Okta").
3. For **SAML**: enter the **Metadata URL** (the IdP's XML metadata endpoint) and
   optionally the **Entity ID** if your IdP requires it.
4. For **OIDC**: enter the **Issuer URL** and **Client ID** (the client secret is never stored).
5. Enter the **Email domains** that belong to this provider
   (e.g. `acme.com, acme.io`).
6. Click **Add Provider**.

For SAML, Mushi Mushi saves the row as `pending`, calls the Supabase Auth Admin API, and
on success shows:
- **ACS URL (Reply URL)**: paste this into your IdP's service-provider configuration
- **Audience / Entity ID**: paste this into your IdP as the service-provider entity ID

Copy the ACS URL and Entity ID before navigating away. You'll need them in your IdP's
dashboard to complete the configuration.

---

## Providers table

The table shows all registered providers with:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Provider** | Label you set at registration |
| **Type** | SAML or OIDC |
| **Domains** | The email domains you entered |
| **Status** | `registered`, `pending`, `failed`, `manual_required` or `disabled` |
| **Provider ID** | The Supabase Auth provider ID, for support reference |

If registration failed, an inline error appears below the provider name.

---

## Disconnecting a provider

Click **Disconnect** on a provider row and confirm. This removes the provider from
Supabase Auth and marks the row `disabled`; the row stays for the audit trail.

---

## Signing in

The console's sign-in page does not detect SSO domains and has no SSO button today. A
registered provider exists in Supabase Auth; the console does not yet send people to it.

---

## API

```bash
GET    /v1/admin/sso
GET    /v1/admin/sso/stats
POST   /v1/admin/sso   { providerType, providerName, metadataUrl, entityId, domains, issuerUrl, clientId }
DELETE /v1/admin/sso/:id
```

---

- [Organization members](/admin/teams): manage roles
- [Settings](/admin/settings): other project configuration
- [Billing](/admin/billing): upgrade to Enterprise to enable SSO

## Storage

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/storage

---
title: Storage
description: The Storage view in the Mushi Mushi console chooses where report screenshots and attachments are kept, managed storage or your own bucket, per project.
---

# Storage

**Route:** `/team?view=storage` (**Team → Storage**; the old `/storage` address redirects there)

The Storage view configures where Mushi Mushi writes report screenshots and attachments.
By default it uses managed Supabase storage. You can switch to your own bucket for
data-residency or cost reasons. The view has three tabs: **Overview**, **Configure** and
**Usage** (objects and last write per project).

---

## Providers

| Provider | Notes |
|----------|-------|
| **Supabase Storage** (default) | Managed, no configuration required. |
| **AWS S3** | Needs a bucket, a region, and an access key ID + secret access key. |
| **Cloudflare R2** | Needs a bucket and an R2 access key ID + secret; region `auto` or blank. |
| **Google Cloud Storage** | Needs a bucket and a service-account key (JSON). |
| **MinIO (self-hosted)** | Needs an endpoint URL and an access key ID + secret. |

---

## Configuring a custom bucket

Each project has its own storage config card. The card shows:
- **Health status chip** with the last-check time
- **Last error** if the previous check failed
- **Show debug log**: a toggle that reveals the per-step results of the last health check

To configure:

1. Choose a **Provider** from the dropdown.
2. Fill in the required fields for your provider (see table below).
3. Click **Save & enable** (first save) or **Save** (later changes).
4. Click **Health check** to confirm Mushi Mushi can write to the bucket. Health check needs a saved configuration.

| Field | Required for |
|-------|-------------|
| **Bucket** | S3, R2, GCS, MinIO |
| **Region** | S3 (e.g. `us-east-1`); R2 takes `auto` or blank |
| **Endpoint (S3-compatible only)** | MinIO; must be a public https URL |
| **Path prefix** | All providers (optional subfolder) |
| **Signed URL TTL (seconds)** | All providers |
| **Access key ID** | S3, R2, MinIO |
| **Secret access key** | S3, R2, MinIO |
| **GCS service-account key (JSON)** | GCS |
| **KMS Key ID (optional)** | Server-side encryption |
| **Use signed URLs** | Checkbox: serve uploads via short-lived links |
| **Require encryption** | Checkbox: reject uploads without server-side encryption |

Paste the keys themselves. Mushi Mushi stores them in Supabase Vault under names tied to
the project; the API refuses a Vault name you type (`VAULT_REF_NOT_ALLOWED`). When a key
is saved, its field reads "Saved" and a new value replaces it.

The form blocks **Save** until the provider's required fields are filled: a region for
S3, an endpoint for MinIO, the key pair for S3, R2 and MinIO, and the JSON key for GCS.
These checks run in the console, not on the server.

Storage settings are per-project. Different projects can use different providers.

---

## Required IAM permissions (S3)

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["s3:PutObject", "s3:GetObject", "s3:DeleteObject", "s3:ListBucket"],
      "Resource": ["arn:aws:s3:::YOUR_BUCKET", "arn:aws:s3:::YOUR_BUCKET/*"]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## Required R2 permissions

Create an R2 API token with **Object Read & Write** scope scoped to the target bucket.

---

## Required GCS permissions

Attach the `roles/storage.objectAdmin` role to your service account, scoped to the bucket.

---

## Data residency

For data-residency requirements, use a bucket in the same region as your Supabase instance.
See [Security → Data residency](/security/data-residency) for the full matrix.

- [Settings](/admin/settings): other project configuration

## teams

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/teams

---
description: How teams work in Mushi Mushi. Organizations own projects, billing, invitations and the member roster, and project access comes from membership.
---

# Teams and members

**Route:** `/team?view=members` (Team → **Members**; the old `/organization/members` link opens it)

In Mushi Mushi, teams are modeled as organizations. An organization owns projects, billing, invitations, and the member roster. Every project keeps its existing `project_id`, but access is granted through `organization_members`.

## Plans

Teams are available on Studio and Enterprise.

| Plan | Teams |
| --- | --- |
| Free | Solo workspace, 1 app |
| Builder | Solo workspace, 3 apps |
| Studio | 5 seats (you and up to 4 teammates; pending invitations count) and 10 apps |
| Enterprise | Teams plus SSO and SOC 2 controls, no app limit |

The product enforces this in three places:

- The admin UI hides the invite form and shows an upgrade prompt.
- The API returns `402 feature_not_in_plan` for invitation attempts below Studio.
- The database rejects invitation inserts with the `invitations_plan_gate` trigger.

## Roles

| Role | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Owner | Billing, plan changes, member management, last-owner protected |
| Admin | Invite users, manage project settings and integrations |
| Member | Work in shared projects and review reports |
| Viewer | Read-only access to shared project data |

## Invitation Flow

1. An owner or admin opens **Team → Members** in the admin console.
2. They invite an email with a role.
3. Mushi creates an `invitations` row with a one-time token and sends a Supabase Auth invite email when possible.
4. The invitee signs in and opens `/invite/accept?token=...`.
5. The `accept_invitation(token)` RPC verifies the email, locks the invite row, inserts the membership, and marks the invite accepted.

The accept step is atomic so double-clicks, expired tokens, and email mismatches fail cleanly.

# All users

**Route:** `/users` (sidebar: **Account → All users**, shown to super-admins only)

All users is a super-admin directory of every account that has signed up for
Mushi Mushi. It shows MRR, churn, plan distribution and per-user detail. It is only
accessible to Mushi Mushi operators; other visitors see a not-found page.

This page is visible only to accounts whose `app_metadata.role` is `super_admin`.
Regular org admins cannot use it: the API returns an opaque `404 NOT_FOUND`
(not `403 FORBIDDEN`) so the endpoints cannot be discovered.

| **Signups · 7d** | New signups in the last 7 days |
| **Signups · 30d** | New signups in the last 30 days |
| **Churn · 30d** | Users who cancelled in the last 30 days |

## UX runs

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/ux-runs

---
title: UX runs
description: The UX runs page in Mushi Mushi shows each screen your agent worked on in a mushi ux run, with its plan, attempts, before/after screenshots, and what was kept.
---

# UX runs

**Route:** `/ux-runs` (sidebar: More pages → Fix → UX runs. It is a Lab: switch it on under **Settings → Display & sidebar → Labs** to keep it in the sidebar)

> **Scenario:** You let your coding agent work through every page, tab and dialog of
> your app overnight and want to see, screen by screen, what it changed and whether
> anything got worse.

`mushi ux run` (from the Mushi Mushi `@mushi-mushi/ux` package) runs on your machine. It maps your running app, gives one screen at a
time to the agent you choose (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) in a separate git branch, and
keeps an edit only when accessibility, layout and console measurements did not get
worse. With `--sync` it mirrors the run here as it goes.

```bash
mushi ux ui      # pick the agent, a model from your account, a skill and the pages, then start
# or straight from the terminal:
mushi ux run --dev "pnpm dev --port {port}" --agent claude-code --sync
```

A synced run shows here as it goes: its phase (installing, mapping, working on
"Home, attempt 2"), a progress bar by outcome, and the screen the agent is on.
While an attempt runs you see its step count, the file it last read or edited,
the files changed so far, and the time used out of its time box. A running
run checks in every 30 seconds; when it stops, the page says how long it has
been quiet and how to resume it.

Each screen keeps every attempt's screenshot at phone and desktop width; pick
one to compare it with the baseline. **What the agent did in attempt N** lists
the files that attempt read and edited. The agent's own words and the commands
it ran stay on the machine that ran it. A run only syncs to the project its
app reports to: if your login is for another project, `--sync` says so and
stops.

  Exploring your app never sends a write request: every request that is not a read is
  blocked, forms are not submitted, and buttons such as Delete or Pay are never clicked.

## Run in the cloud

No machine to leave running? **Run in the cloud** starts the same pass on your repo's
GitHub Actions, with a [Cursor Cloud](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints)
agent making the edits. It appears on this page like a local run and ends with one
draft PR. You need, in the app's front end repo:

1. [`.github/workflows/mushi-ux.yml`](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/docs/templates/mushi-ux.yml)
   on the default branch, with `dev-command` set to how your app starts.
2. Secrets `CURSOR_API_KEY` and `MUSHI_API_KEY` (a key with `mcp:write`), the variable
   `MUSHI_PROJECT_ID`, and optionally `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for the review.
3. **Settings → Actions → General → Allow GitHub Actions to create pull requests**, or
   the run ends with a compare link instead of a draft PR.

Pick the model from your Cursor account's list (with its settings, such as
effort and context; this needs a Cursor key under Settings → AI keys) and,
optionally, a skill from the synced skills catalog. Mushi starts it with a
`repository_dispatch` event through your GitHub connection,
at most three times an hour per app. When it cannot (no workflow, no connection,
GitHub refused), the card shows the `gh workflow run` command to start it yourself.

  A cloud run sees your app signed out: screens behind sign-in show as **Could not
  load**. Each attempt is a commit Cursor pushes to `mushi-ux/`; if your CI runs
  on every push, add `branches-ignore: ['mushi-ux/**']` to it.

---

## What you see

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
|--------|---------|------------|
| **Moved by another fix** | A change kept on another screen (often a shared component or token) changed this one. | Check it first. |
| **Rolled back** | Every attempt made a measured problem worse, so it was undone. | File it as a bug, or run again with a different model. |
| **Could not load** | The screen did not render for capture. | Run `mushi ux login` for signed-in screens, or allow the reads your app makes with POST (`--allow`). |
| **Improved** | An edit was kept. | Review it on the run's branch. |
| **No change needed** | The agent made no edit, or nothing visible changed. | Nothing. |

Select a screen to see a before/after slider, the changed pixels, the problems still
measured, each attempt with its commit, and the optional review by a second model.
The review is advisory: it never keeps or reverts anything.

## File as bug

**File as bug** adds the screen to your normal bug queue (source `ux_loop`) with the
measurements and the review's notes. It makes no AI call.

## Audit signed-in screens

`mushi-ux audit` finds UI bugs on the screens behind your sign-in and files them as
reports, without editing code. It reuses a browser profile you are already signed in
with, so it never asks you to sign in again:

```bash
mushi-ux audit --url https://example.com/admin \
  --profile-dir ~/.playwright-cli-profiles/example --file --dry-run
```

It maps the screens under that URL read-only, captures each on desktop and phone, and
files what it measures: serious accessibility rules, a page that scrolls sideways,
console errors, and content that jumps while loading. Add `--review claude-code` for a
model to point out concrete visual defects on whole pages. `--file` files at most 15
reports a run and skips one still open or filed in the last 14 days; `--dry-run` lists
them instead.

## First-time user test

The **First-time user test** page (it was the Fresh eyes tab of this page) tests the path
a stranger takes: a model that has never seen your app tries one goal from your start
page, such as "sign up and start using the app", reading only what is on screen. Code
decides everything else:

- **Time to first value**: how long the app made the visitor wait, plus the time to read
  each new screen, until the goal check passes (a URL, visible text, a selector or an API
  that answers with data). The model's own thinking time is never counted.
- **Where it stalled**: a sign-in it cannot pass, a captcha (never solved), a dead end, an
  error, or a step that needs something outside the app (an inbox, an API key, a
  terminal, another account).
- **What gets filed**: measured problems once a replay of the steps without the model
  shows them again; opinions such as "confusing" only when two sessions agree. Reports
  come in as source `fresh_eyes`, at most 15 a run.

**Run now** starts it from the console. The start page comes from your app (its last
test, its live-site watch or site audit address) and the goal is plain words you can
change. The test runs on your own computer, where its browser and AI run: if Mushi runs
there for this app (`mushi worker install`, shown on Pipeline → Workers), it picks the
test up within a minute and the page follows it live. If not, the page says so and shows
the one thing to set up. Pick **Look around, file nothing** to see where a visitor gets
stuck, or **File what stops them** to turn each problem into a bug report.

From a terminal it is the same run:

```bash
mushi ux fresh-eyes --url https://your-app.com --goal "get my first report" --dry-run
# with a test account for your app, mirrored here and filed:
MUSHI_FRESH_EYES_EMAIL=… MUSHI_FRESH_EYES_PASSWORD=… \
  mushi ux fresh-eyes --url https://your-app.com --goal "get my first report" --sync --file
```

The run is signed out in a clean browser. It may only write to your app's own origins
(`--app-host` adds its API); payments, "Continue with Google/GitHub/Apple", public sign-up
forms and anything labelled delete or revoke are refused. Without an account it stops at
your sign-up page and says so; `--dry-run` never writes to your app.

The page shows each test: time to first value, steps, how many visitors reached the goal,
the trend over tests, and every step with its screenshot and wait. A waiting test can be
cancelled; a failed one says why. Once an app has a finished test, Home shows a
**First-time setup** light with the minutes and steps.

## Where the changes are

Kept edits are commits on the branch shown above the screen list
(`mushi-ux/`). Nothing is merged for you: review the branch and open a draft PR
with **Open draft PR** in the studio (`mushi ux ui`). Once a run has a pull request,
this page shows it with its required checks and a **Merge to &lt;base&gt;** button that asks
you to confirm first. Screenshots are kept for the project's retention window (30 days by default).

See also: [CLI reference](/sdks/cli#ux-pass-over-every-screen).

---

## Verified merge

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/verified-merge

---
title: Verified merge
description: Mushi Mushi merges a cloud agent's fix on its own only with proof, a test that fails without the fix and passes with it, run in your own CI.
---

# Verified merge

Your agents open more fix PRs than you can read. A green CI run does not
prove a fix: an agent can make CI green by editing or skipping a test.
Verified merge asks for proof instead. A cloud agent's fix PR merges on its own only when
**a test fails without the fix and passes with it**, no test was weakened,
the change is small, and two reviews from different model families raise no
problem.

A model's review can stop a merge. It can never approve one on its own
([ADR 0035](https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi/blob/master/docs/adr/0035-verified-fixes-merge-on-proof-not-on-a-verdict.md)).

## The gates

Mushi Mushi checks every gate against the PR's latest commit. A new commit starts
from zero. The fix card in the console shows the list, and so does
`mushi fixes verify `.

| Gate | Passes when | What to do when it does not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Opus review** | The [Opus review](/concepts/agent-pr-review) of this commit says `merge` | Read the findings. `fix_first` and `hold` block. |
| **CI** | Every check on the commit is green | A stopped test machine counts as waiting, never as a pass ([CI runners](/operating/ci-runners)). |
| **Test proves the fix** | The **Mushi verify** check says `fail_to_pass` | Add the workflow below, or ask the agent for a test that reproduces the bug. |
| **No tests weakened** | No test file deleted, no assertions removed, no `.skip`, `.only`, `@ts-ignore` or `eslint-disable` added, no CI config changed, no big snapshot update. A lockfile may change only for a dependency report, beside the manifest it comes from (`package.json` for `package-lock.json`…); for a [known-hole](../concepts/known-holes) report that manifest change must name the package | Undo the change to the test, or merge it yourself. |
| **Small change** | At most 3 source files and 150 changed lines (you can raise both) | A big change needs a person. |
| **Second review** | A model from another family (OpenAI or OpenRouter, on your own key) says `merge` | It runs only after the other five pass. Without a key it reads **unavailable** and blocks automatic merge. |

Each gate reads one of **Passed**, **Failed**, **Waiting**, **Unavailable** or
**Not set up** (`pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `unavailable`, `not_set_up` in the API).

A fix from your own local `mushi work` lane is checked only by its Opus review
and its CI. The other gates run on cloud agents' pull requests.

## Add the workflow

The **Test proves the fix** gate needs one workflow in your repo. Get it with
your runner labels and test command already filled in, in any of three ways:

- Console: **Settings → General → Fixes and CI** (click **Show**) **→ Verified merge →
  Mushi verify workflow → Open a PR that adds it**, or **Copy workflow**.
- Terminal: `mushi verify workflow --out .github/workflows/mushi-verify.yml`,
  then commit it to your default branch.
- By hand: save the file below as `.github/workflows/mushi-verify.yml` and
  change the `runs-on` and `test-command` lines.

```yaml
# Mushi verify. Save as .github/workflows/mushi-verify.yml on your default branch.
# It proves an agent's fix before Mushi merges it on its own: the tests the PR
# adds or changes must pass with the fix, and fail when the PR's other files
# are put back the way they were. The result is a "Mushi verify" check on the
# PR. Mushi reads it with the GitHub access it already has; no secret needed.
# Docs: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/verified-merge
name: Mushi verify

on:
  pull_request:
    # A draft runs nothing; marking it ready runs the check.
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

permissions:
  contents: read
  checks: write

concurrency:
  group: mushi-verify-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    # Agent branches only (cursor/**, mushi/**, copilot/**), and never a fork:
    # `on.pull_request.branches` filters the base branch, so the head is checked here.
    # Never a draft (it runs once the PR is marked ready), a Mushi release train
    # (mushi/train/*, its fixes were proven on their own PRs) or a revert (mushi/revert-*).
    if: >-
      github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      (startsWith(github.head_ref, 'cursor/') ||
       startsWith(github.head_ref, 'mushi/') ||
       startsWith(github.head_ref, 'copilot/')) &&
      !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'mushi/train/') &&
      !startsWith(github.head_ref, 'mushi/revert-')
    # Not "Mushi verify": that name belongs to the check run the action posts.
    name: Mushi verify run
    runs-on: [ubuntu-latest]
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5  # v4.3.1
        with:
          # The commit the agent pushed, not GitHub's merge commit.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # Full history, so the PR's merge base is here.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # Not Node? Swap these two steps for your toolchain's setup action
      # (actions/setup-python, actions/setup-go, …). The verify action itself
      # needs Node 20 or newer on the runner; setup-node gives you that.
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271  # v4.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e  # v6.4.0
        with:
          # No version file? Replace with  node-version: 22
          node-version-file: .nvmrc  # or .node-version / package.json
          cache: pnpm  # npm or yarn for those; remove the pnpm step above
      # Install your dependencies the way your CI does, e.g.
      #   npm ci   |   yarn install --immutable   |   pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - uses: kensaurus/mushi-mushi/.github/actions/fix-verify@master
        with:
          # {files} becomes the test files the PR added or changed, quoted.
          # e.g. "npx jest {files}" or "pytest {files}"
          test-command: "pnpm vitest run {files}"
```

It runs only on PRs from `cursor/…`, `mushi/…` and `copilot/…` branches in
your own repo, needs only `contents: read` and `checks: write`, and stops after
20 minutes. It spends no Actions minutes on:

- a **draft** PR: it runs when the PR is marked ready for review. Mushi opens
  its own fix PRs as drafts and marks them ready once its review says `merge`;
- a Mushi **release train** (`mushi/train/…`): each fix in it was proven on
  its own PR first;
- a Mushi **revert** PR (`mushi/revert-…`): it puts back code that was already
  on your default branch. It never uses `pull_request_target`, so a fork's code never runs
with your secrets. Mushi needs no secret in your repo: it reads the check with
the GitHub access it already has.

  Mushi does not write the file into your repo on its own. Writing under
  `.github/workflows` needs a GitHub permission Mushi does not ask for. The
  **Open a PR that adds it** button opens a pull request for you to merge.

## What the check does

1. It finds the test files the PR **added or changed**. A source file edit
   alone does not count.
2. It runs them with your test command on the PR's commit. They must **pass**.
3. It puts every other file the PR changed back the way it was on your base
   branch, keeps the PR's tests, and runs them again. They must **fail**.
4. It puts the PR's files back and posts the **Mushi verify** check.

| Verdict | Meaning | Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fail_to_pass` | The test fails without the fix and passes with it. This is the proof. | green |
| `no_test` | The PR adds or changes no test. | red |
| `passes_without_fix` | The tests pass even on the old code, so they do not reproduce the bug. | red |
| `fails_with_fix` | The fix does not make its own tests pass. | red |
| `error` | A run timed out, crashed or the command was not found. It says nothing about the fix. | red |

The check's details show the tests it ran, both results, the runner and the
end of the log. Token-shaped strings in the log are masked, and the job's
GitHub token is not passed to your tests.

### The test command

`{files}` becomes the test file paths, each quoted, so a strange file name can
never run as a command. Use your runner's "run these files" form:

| Stack | `test-command` |
| --- | --- |
| Vitest | `pnpm vitest run {files}` |
| Jest | `npx jest {files}` |
| pytest | `pytest {files}` |
| Node test runner | `node --test {files}` |

Set it in the console (**Settings → General → Fixes and CI → Verified merge → Test command**)
so `mushi verify workflow` and the PR button fill it in.

A test file is one under `__tests__/`, `test/`, `tests/` or `e2e/`, or named
`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*_test.go`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*Test.java` or
`*Tests.swift`. If yours look different, add `test-globs` to the action step,
for example `test-globs: "**/*.check.ts"`. A glob without a `/` matches the
file name in any folder.

## Run it on your own machine

The check runs wherever `runs-on` says. To use your own machine (no GitHub
minutes, your own toolchain), set it up as a runner first:

```bash
mushi runner add --repo you/your-app   # prints the label, e.g. mushi-nuc
```

Then add that label under **Settings → General → Fixes and CI → Verified merge →
Where the proof runs** (the console suggests the runners it has seen), and get the workflow
again. The `runs-on` line becomes, for example:

```yaml
    runs-on: [self-hosted, mushi-nuc]
```

See [Add your own machine as a runner](/operating/ci-runners#add-your-own-machine-as-a-runner)
for the safe defaults.

  The check runs the agent's code and tests on that machine, like any CI job.
  Keep self-hosted runners on private repos you trust.

## Turn on automatic merge

Automatic merge is **off** until you turn on **Merge proven fixes automatically**
in **Settings → General → Fixes and CI → Verified merge**. When it is on and every
gate passes, Mushi squash-merges the cloud agent's PR at its exact commit, up to a daily limit per app (5 by default). It never turns
on GitHub's own auto-merge, which merges on green CI alone.

You can still merge any PR yourself, from the console, GitHub or
`mushi fixes merge`, as before.

## After the merge

For 72 hours after Mushi merges a fix, it watches for three signs that the fix
broke something:

| Sign | What Mushi does |
| --- | --- |
| CI fails on the merge commit (not a stopped test machine) | Marks the fix **regressed** and opens a revert PR |
| The report is reopened | Marks the fix **regressed** and opens a revert PR |
| A new report's stack trace names a file the fix changed | Flags the fix for you to look at |

Mushi never merges a revert PR by itself: a person does. If later commits
changed the same files, Mushi opens no revert PR and tells you to revert by
hand. Turn revert PRs off with **If a merged fix breaks something → When it breaks → Off**. A regressed fix also
counts against that app in the spend-down stop-loss, which pauses automatic
fixes for an app whose fixes keep failing.

## Check one fix

```bash
mushi fixes verify <fixId>           # every gate for the PR's latest commit
mushi fixes verify <fixId> --rerun   # check again now
```

## See also

- [Agent PR review](/concepts/agent-pr-review): the Opus review, the first gate.
- [Fix orchestrator](/admin/fixes): the fix card, CI feedback and merging from the console.
- [CI runners](/operating/ci-runners): where your tests run, and a stopped test machine versus a failed fix.

## Voice reports

Source: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/voice

---
title: Voice reports
description: Report a bug by voice from the Mushi Mushi console. Say what is wrong, confirm the transcript, and a draft pull request is started for you.
---

# Voice reports

**Route:** `/voice` (sidebar: **Voice reports**, under Bugs; the feature is also called voice intake)

> **Scenario:** You are away from your desk and something is broken. You say what
> is wrong, read back the transcript the console shows you, tap Confirm, and a
> draft pull request lands while you are still holding your phone.

Voice reports in Mushi Mushi turn a spoken note into a report, and optionally into a dispatched
draft-PR fix. Everything passes through one gate: **you always see the verbatim
transcript before anything is dispatched.**

---

## Turning it on

Voice reports are off until you enable them. Go to **Settings → Voice reports** and
turn on **Accept voice reports**. In the same tab you set:

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Keep recordings for** | Days to keep the clip. `0` deletes it the moment the transcript exists. |
| **Languages** | Hints passed to the transcriber. Leave them all off to let it detect. |
| **iPhone Shortcut or any phone** | **Make a voice key**: a key that can only send voice requests, for a phone Shortcut. |
| **Telegram bot** | Optional. Enables the Telegram inbox described below. |
| **GitHub cloud agent** | Optional token. Needed only for GitHub-hosted cloud agent tasks. |
| **Push to this device** | Get told on this device when a voice request needs you. |

Transcription uses your OpenAI key from **Settings → AI keys**. Without one,
audio intake fails with a message telling you so; typed intake still works.

---

## The ways in

| Path | Where it works |
|---|---|
| **Tap to talk** | The `/voice` page in any browser, best installed to the Home Screen. |
| **Upload a clip** | Anywhere. Accepts ogg, m4a, mp3, webm and wav up to 25 MB. |
| **Type it instead** | Anywhere. Skips transcription entirely. |
| **Share a voice memo** | Android Chrome only, once the console is installed. Share the memo to Mushi Mushi. |
| **iPhone Shortcut** | Dictate on the phone; the Shortcut sends the text with a voice-only key. |
| **Telegram / Slack** | Send a voice note to your Telegram bot, or use the Slack inbox. |

  Install the console to your Home Screen to get the share target, offline shell
  and push notifications. On iOS, notifications only work after installing —
  that is an Apple restriction, and the page says so where it matters.

---

## The confirmation gate

Nothing dispatches on your voice alone. After transcription you see the exact
words that were heard, what Mushi intends to do, and a one-line summary. Then
you choose Confirm or Cancel.

The confirm token is bound to the session, the transcript hash, the intended
action and the expiry. It is single-use and valid for ten minutes. Change any
of those and the token stops verifying, so a replayed or forwarded link cannot
dispatch anything.

Some words are refused outright and never reach a model, in English and
Japanese: merge, deploy, delete, drop, force-push, production (or prod),
rollback, revert, rotate, and anything about secrets or tokens. Voice is a good way to describe a
bug. It is not a way to touch production.

  The transcript is untrusted input. It is wrapped in explicit delimiters before
  any model sees it, and personally identifying strings are scrubbed before the
  text is stored. Read what is on screen before you confirm: that is the whole
  point of the gate.

---

## Getting the answer back

When the draft pull request opens, or a confirmation is needed, or a fix fails,
Mushi tells you on whichever surface you used:

- **Push to this phone** — tap *Notify this device* on the voice page. Uses Web
  Push, so it reaches you with the console closed.
- **Slack** — the transcript card carries Confirm and Cancel buttons.
- **Telegram** — same two buttons, as an inline keyboard.

---

## Telegram

Telegram is the practical Android inbox: a voice memo sent to a bot arrives as a
file the server can fetch.

1. Create a bot with `@BotFather` and paste its token into **Settings → Voice reports → Telegram bot**.
2. Press **Connect webhook**.
3. Press **Make link code** and send `/start ` to your bot, from the chat you want
   to use, within ten minutes.

The binding is per chat and per project, and you can remove any chat from the
same panel.

---

## Recent voice requests

The list below the recorder shows every session with its status, and links
through to the report or the pull request once they exist. It updates live.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Report created** | A report was filed; no fix was requested. |
| **Needs confirmation** | Waiting for you. Shows **Expired** once the ten-minute window has passed. |
| **Confirmed** / **Agent working** | You approved it and the agent was dispatched. |
| **PR ready** | The draft pull request is up and you were notified. |
| **Cancelled** | You declined. Nothing was dispatched. |
| **Refused** | A refused word was in the transcript. |
| **Duplicate** | The same request was already received. |
| **Failed** | Transcription or a cap stopped it. The reason is shown. |

---

## Limits

Voice intake is capped per project so a stuck client cannot spend your
transcription budget: 30 intakes per minute, 120 transcribed audio minutes a
day, and 25 MB per clip. Transcribed minutes
and their cost are recorded per session so you can see what voice actually
costs you.

## Self-hosting

Set `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` and `VAPID_SUBJECT` as edge secrets
before push will work; the page reports push as unavailable until you do. See
[Edge functions](/self-hosting/edge-functions) for the deploy list.
